PREFACE
This Code constitutes a codification of the rules of the Sterling Ranch Community
Authority Board (CAB).
Source materials used in the preparation of the Code were the rules adopted by the
CAB. The source of each section is included in the history note appearing in parentheses
at the end thereof. The absence of such a note indicates that the section is new and
was adopted for the first time with the adoption of the Code. By use of the comparative
tables appearing in the back of this Code, the reader can locate any section of a
rule included herein.
The chapters of the Code have been conveniently arranged in alphabetical order, and
the various sections within each chapter have been catchlined to facilitate usage.
Notes which tie related sections of the Code together and which refer to relevant
state law have been included. A table listing the state law citations and setting
forth their location within the Code is included at the back of this Code.
Chapter and Section Numbering System
The chapter and section numbering system used in this Code is the same system used
in many state and local government codes. Each section number consists of two parts
separated by a dash. The figure before the dash refers to the chapter number, and
the figure after the dash refers to the position of the section within the chapter.
Thus, the second section of chapter 1 is numbered 1-2, and the first section of chapter 6 is 6-1. Under this system, each
section is identified with its chapter, and at the same time new sections can be inserted
in their proper place by using the decimal system for amendments. For example, if
new material consisting of one section that would logically come between sections
6-1 and 6-2 is desired to be added, such new section would be numbered 6-1.5. New
articles and new divisions may be included in the same way or, in the case of articles,
may be placed at the end of the chapter embracing the subject, and, in the case of
divisions, may be placed at the end of the article embracing the subject. The next
successive number shall be assigned to the new article or division. New chapters may

the alphabetical arrangement of chapters is maintained when including new chapters.
Page Numbering System
The page numbering system used in this Code is a prefix system. The letters to the
left of the colon are an abbreviation which represents a certain portion of the volume.
The number to the right of the colon represents the number of the page in that portion.
In the case of a chapter of the Code, the number to the left of the colon indicates
the number of the chapter. In the case of an appendix to the Code, the letter immediately
to the left of the colon indicates the letter of the appendix. The following are typical
parts of codes of ordinances, which may or may not appear in this Code at this time,
and their corresponding prefixes:
CODE
CD1:1
CODE APPENDIX
CDA:1
CODE COMPARATIVE TABLES
CCT:1
STATE LAW REFERENCE TABLE
SLT:1
CODE INDEX
CDi:1
Index
The index has been prepared with the greatest of care. Each particular item has been
placed under several headings, some of which are couched in lay phraseology, others
in legal terminology, and still others in language generally used by local government
officials and employees. There are numerous cross references within the index itself
which stand as guideposts to direct the user to the particular item in which the user
is interested.
Looseleaf Supplements
A special feature of this publication is the looseleaf system of binding and supplemental
servicing of the publication. With this system, the publication will be kept up to
date. Subsequent amendatory legislation will be properly edited, and the affected
page or pages will be reprinted. These new pages will be distributed to holders of
copies of the publication, with instructions for the manner of inserting the new pages
and deleting the obsolete pages.
Keeping this publication up to date at all times will depend largely upon the holder
of the publication. As revised pages are received, it will then become the responsibility
of the holder to have the amendments inserted according to the attached instructions.
It is strongly recommended by the publisher that all such amendments be inserted immediately
upon receipt to avoid misplacing them and, in addition, that all deleted pages be
saved and filed for historical reference purposes.
Acknowledgments
This publication was under the direct supervision of Roger D. Merriam, Senior Code
Attorney, and Amanda Heath, Editor, of the Municipal Code Corporation, Tallahassee,

RESOLUTION NO. 2021-05-02
OF
THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF THE STERLING RANCH COMMUNITY AUTHORITY BOARD
ADOPTING THE CODE OF RULES OF THE STERLING RANCH COMMUNITY AUTHORITY BOARD
Recitals
A.
The Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board (the "CAB") is an authority and separate
legal entity created pursuant to section 29-1-203, C.R.S., and in conformity with
section 29-1-203.5, C.R.S., and that certain Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board
Establishment Agreement, (the "CABEA"), by and between the Sterling Ranch Colorado
Metropolitan District Nos. 1—7 (collectively, the "Sterling Ranch Districts"); and
B.
Pursuant to the CABEA, the CAB Board (the "Board") shall govern the business and affairs
of the CAB and establish the policies, rules and regulations of the CAB; and
C.
Pursuant to Section 32-1-1001(m), C.R.S., CAB has the authority to adopt, amend and
enforce rules and regulations for the carrying on of business and to meet the objectives
of the CAB; and
D.
The CAB has adopted and amended, from time to time, the Utilities, Parks and Open
Space Rules and Regulations dated as being Adopted on November 18, 2020; the Sterling
Ranch Community Authority Board Rules and Regulations (Covenant Enforcement/Design
Review) dated as being Adopted on November 18, 2020; the Amended Sterling Ranch Water
Demand Management Initiatives dated as being Adopted on November 18, 2020; the Sterling
Ranch Residential Property Owners Guidebook dated as being Adopted on November 18,

2020; the Sterling Ranch Book of Fees and Forms dated as Being Adopted on November
18, 2020; the Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board Standards and Specifications
for Potable Water, Sanitary Sewer, and Non-Potable Water dated November 18, 2020;
the Sterling Ranch Water- Wise Tree Lawns at Providence Village dated as being Adopted
on November 18, 2020; and the Sterling Ranch Technology Guidelines and Specifications
dated as being Adopted on November 18, 2020 (the "Rules and Regulations Compilation");
and
E.
The CAB has adopted certain Universal Design Principles and the Ascent Village Design
Principles (the "Design Guidelines") under the authority granted to CAB by the Master
Declaration of Covenants and Restrictions for Sterling Ranch Planned Development recorded
at Reception No. 2015069869 with the Douglas County Clerk and Recorder; and
F.
The CAB has caused to be prepared the Code of Rules for the Sterling Ranch Community
Authority Board (the "Code") to provide a single location for the adopted Rules and
Regulations Compilation and the Design Guidelines of the CAB; and
G.
The Code and any subsequent amendments, modifications, or additions to the Code shall
be the definitive statement of the appliable rules and regulations; and
H.
The Board has determined that adopting the Code is in the best interests of the CAB
and the residents of the Districts.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF THE STERLING RANCH COMMUNITY
AUTHORITY BOARD OF THE COUNTY OF DOUGLAS, COLORADO:
1.
The Code entitled "Code of Rules of the Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board,"
published by Municipal Code Corporation, consisting of chapters 1 through 38, each
inclusive, is adopted.
2.
All rules of a general and permanent nature to the Rules and Regulations Compilation
enacted on or before November 18, 2020, and not included in the Code or recognized
and continued in force by reference therein, are repealed.
3.
The repeal provided for in paragraph 2 hereof shall not be construed to revive any
rule or part thereof that has been repealed by a subsequent rule that is repealed
by this rule.
4.
Additions or amendments to the Code when passed in such form as to indicate the intention
to make the same a part of the Code shall be deemed to be incorporated in the Code,
so that reference to the Code includes the additions and amendments.
5.
All rules, regulations, or changes adopted after November 18, 2020, that amend or
refer to rules that have been codified in the Code shall be construed as if they amend

documents.title: Sec. 1-1. - Title.
documents.text:
This publication shall be known as the "Code of Rules of the Sterling Ranch Community
Authority Board." Such Code may also be cited as the "Sterling Ranch CAB Code."

documents.title: Sec. 1-2. - Definitions and rules of construction.
path: Sec. 1-2. - Definitions and rules of construction.
documents.text:
All words and phrases shall have the meanings provided for them in the master declaration,
unless otherwise defined in this Code. In the event that there is any inconsistency
between the provisions of this Code and the master declaration, the master declaration
shall prevail.
Builder (aka Home builder). The term "Builder" or "Home Builder" means a person, persons, or business that is
responsible for the construction of buildings and/or related improvements, typically
for the purpose of sale to a subsequent owner.
CAB. The abbreviation "CAB" means Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board.
CAB Board or Board. The term "CAB Board" or "Board" means the Board of Directors of the Sterling Ranch
Community Authority Board.
CAB Rules and Regulations. The term "CAB Rules and Regulations" means the CAB Rules and Regulations as outlined
in the Code and as amended from time to time.
CO. The term "CO" refers to a Certificate of Occupancy as defined and issued by Douglas
County permitting occupancy of a unit.
Code. The term "Code" means the Code of Rules of the Sterling Ranch Community Authority
Board as designated in section 1-1 .
Community Authority Board or CAB. The term "Community Authority Board" or the abbreviation "CAB" means the Sterling
Ranch Community Authority Board, a political subdivision and public corporation of
the State of Colorado formed pursuant to C.R.S. §§ 29-1-203 and 29-1-203.5, as created
by the Community Authority Board Establishment Agreement between and among Sterling
Ranch Metropolitan District Nos. 1—7.
County. The term "County" means Douglas County, Colorado.
Design Guidelines. The term "Design Guidelines" means the Design Guidelines for Sterling Ranch as set
forth in the Design Principles, the Water Demand Management Initiatives and the Technology
Guidelines and Specifications and which, collectively with all appendices thereto,
form the Design Guidelines described in the Master Declaration and in the Rules and
Regulations.
Design Principles. The term "Design Principles" means the Design Principles as are adopted by the CAB.
Design Review Committee or DRC. The term "Design Review Committee" and the abbreviation "DRC" means the Sterling
Ranch Design Review Committee, established by the CAB pursuant to the Master Declaration,
the members of which are appointed by the CAB, and who serve at the pleasure of the
CAB, without limitation as to length of term.
Districts. The term "Districts" means Sterling Ranch Colorado Metropolitan District Nos. 1—7.
Dominion. The term "Dominion" means Dominion Water and Sanitation District, a quasi-municipal

documents.title: Sec. 1-2. - Definitions and rules of construction.
path: Sec. 1-2. - Definitions and rules of construction.
documents.text:
corporation and political subdivision of the State of Colorado, the water and sanitation
district that has contracted to produce wholesale water delivery to the CAB.
Dominion Board. The term "Dominion Board" means the Board of Directors of the Dominion Water and
Sanitation District.
Dominion Rules and Regulations. The term "Dominion Rules and Regulations" means the Rules and Regulations adopted
by Dominion and effective as of the date hereof and as they may be amended from time
to time.
General Manager. The term "General Manager" means the Person designated as General Manager by the
CAB Board, who administers and supervises the affairs of and operations and maintenance
of facilities of the CAB or the Person authorized by the CAB Board or the General
Manager to act on his behalf.
Lot. The term "Lot" means a lot, super pad, multifamily parcel, or other portion of the
Property established pursuant to a subdivision plat recorded in the real property
records of the County.
Master Declaration. The term "Master Declaration" means the Master Declaration of Covenants, Conditions
and Restrictions for Sterling Ranch Planned Unit Development, as amended, supplemented
or otherwise modified from time to time.
Owner. The term "Owner" means any record holder of legal fee simple title to a Lot or other
portion of the Property or an interest therein other than a Builder. The term "Owner"
also applies to and includes any person who is permitted to be in the development
by an owner, including, but not limited to, an owner's family, guests, invitees, tenants,
visitors or independent contractors, or the family, guests, invitees, visitors or
independent contractors of an owner's occupants.
Property or Sterling Ranch. The term "Property" or "Sterling Ranch" means the land located in Douglas County,
Colorado, at any time and from time to time subject to the Master Declaration.
Right-of-Way (ROW). The term "Right-of-Way" or "ROW" means a public street, road, alley, motor court,
sidewalk, easement, park, square, plaza, tract, and any CAB-owned or other property
dedicated for public use.
Streetscape. The term "Streetscape" means pedestrian and landscape improvements in the right-of-way,
generally occurring between the curb and the right-of-way. Generally, the term "streetscape"
includes sidewalks, street trees and tree lawns, medians and roundabouts with all
associated landscape and irrigation.
Temporary CO or TCO. The term "Temporary CO" or "TCO" refers to a Temporary Certificate of Occupancy as
defined and issued by Douglas County permitting occupancy of a unit.

documents.title: Sec. 1-3. - Enactment.
documents.text:
These Rules and Regulations are adopted by the Sterling Ranch Community Authority
Board (the "CAB") in accordance with the authority contained in C.R.S. title 32, art.
I, pt. 10 (C.R.S. § 32-1-1001 et seq.) and C.R.S. § 29-1-203, as may be amended.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § 1.1)

documents.title: Sec. 1-4. - Amendments to Code.
documents.text:
(a)
The CAB may amend, supplement, repeal, replace or modify this Code from time to time
as it deems appropriate or convenient.
(b)
Amendments to any of the provisions of this Code may be made by amending such provisions
by specific reference to the section number of this Code in substantially the following
language: "Section ___ of the Code of Rules of the Sterling Ranch Community Authority
Board is hereby amended to read as follows: …." The new provisions should then be
set out in full as desired.
(c)
In the event a new section not heretofore existing in the Code is to be added, the
following language is suggested: "The Code of Rules of the Sterling Ranch Community
Authority Board is hereby amended by adding a section, to be numbered ___, which said
section reads as follows: …." The new section should then be set out in full as desired.
(d)
All sections, articles, chapters or provisions desired to be repealed should be specifically
repealed by section, article or chapter number, as the case may be.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(3), § 5.2)

documents.title: Sec. 1-5. - Supplementation of Code.
documents.text:
(a)
A supplement to the Code shall include all substantive parts of permanent and general
rules adopted during the period covered by the supplement and all changes made thereby
in the Code. The pages of a supplement shall be so numbered that they will fit properly
into the Code and will, where necessary, replace pages which have become obsolete
or partially obsolete, and the new pages shall be so prepared that, when they have
been inserted, the Code will be current through the date of the adoption of the latest
rule included in the supplement.
(b)
In preparing a supplement to this Code, all portions of the Code which have been repealed
shall be excluded from the Code by the omission thereof from reprinted pages.
(c)
When preparing a supplement to this Code, the codifier (meaning the person, agency
or organization authorized to prepare the supplement) may make formal, nonsubstantive
changes in ordinances and parts of ordinances included in the supplement, insofar
as it is necessary to do so to embody them into a unified code. For example, the codifier
may:
(1)
Organize the material into appropriate chapters, articles divisions, subdivisions,
sections or subsections;
(2)
Provide appropriate catchlines, headings and titles for sections and other subdivisions
of the Code printed in the supplement, and make changes in such catchlines, headings
and titles;
(3)
Assign appropriate numbers to sections and other subdivisions to be inserted in the
Code and, where necessary to accommodate new material, change existing section or
other subdivision numbers;
(4)
Change the words "the rules" or the words of the same meaning to "this chapter," "this
article," "this division," etc., as the case may be or to "sections ___ to ___" (inserting
section numbers to indicate the sections of the Code which embody the substantive
sections of the rule incorporated into the Code); and
(5)
Make other nonsubstantive changes necessary to preserve the original meaning of the
sections inserted into the Code; but in no case shall the codifier make any change
in the meaning or effect of material included in the supplement or already embodied
in the Code.

documents.title: Sec. 1-6. - Construction and development.
documents.text:
Notwithstanding anything to the contrary herein contained, normal construction activities
and parking in connection with a Declarant's building of improvements within the Development
or the Declarant's other developmental activities shall not be considered a nuisance
or otherwise be prohibited by this Code.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(3), § 5.3)

documents.title: Sec. 1-7. - Remedies.
documents.text:
All remedies set forth in the Master Declaration and this Code shall be cumulative
of any remedies available at law or in equity, except as limited in the Master Declaration.
The decision to pursue enforcement action in any particular case shall be left to
the CAB's or Enforcement Committee's discretion, except that neither the CAB nor the
Enforcement Committee shall be arbitrary or capricious in taking enforcement action.
Without limiting the generality of the foregoing sentence, the CAB or the Enforcement
Committee may determine that, under the circumstances of a particular case:
(1)
The position is not strong enough to justify taking any or further action;
(2)
The covenant, restriction, or rule being enforced is, or is likely to be construed
as, inconsistent with applicable law;
(3)
Although a technical violation may exist or may have occurred, it is not of such a
material nature as to be objectionable to a reasonable person or to justify expending
the CAB's resources; or
(4)
That it is not in the CAB's best interests, based upon hardship, expense, or other
reasonable criteria, to pursue enforcement action.
Such a decision shall not be construed as a waiver of the CAB's or the enforcement
Committee's right to enforce such provision at a later time or preclude the CAB or
the Enforcement Committee from enforcing any other covenant, restriction, or rule.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(3), § 5.4)

documents.title: Sec. 1-31. - Use of lots and units.
path: Sec. 1-31. - Use of lots and units.
documents.text:
No Lot, Unit or other portion of the Development may be used for any purpose which
is unlawful or which fails to comply with the Master Declaration, Rules and Regulations
or governance policies that the CAB may enact from time to time or which constitutes
a nuisance. Subject to the provisions of the Master Declaration, including Section
4.2 thereof, no part of the Residential Units shall be used for any purpose inconsistent
with the purposes for which the Community was designed. Each Residential Unit shall
be used as a residence for a single family or such other uses permitted by the Master
Declaration or by these Rules and Regulations, and for no other purpose.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(3), § 2.1)

documents.title: Sec. 1-32. - General use restrictions.
documents.text:
(a)
No owner or occupant of a Residential Unit shall operate any machines, appliances,
electronic devices, accessories or equipment in such a manner as to cause, in the
judgment of the CAB, an unreasonable disturbance to others, or cause any damage to
or overloading of any mechanical, electrical, plumbing, or any other system serving
any building within the Community. So as not to disturb other Owners, Owners and Occupants
of Residential Units shall not permit within Residential Units loud noises or playing
of musical instruments, radios, stereos, televisions, etc., in such a manner as to
disturb others and volumes shall be appropriate between the hours of 10:00 p.m. to
8:00 a.m., and at all other times, as determined by the CAB (this provision shall
not be deemed to restrict Commercial Units).
(b)
Each Owner shall maintain his Lot and the Improvements thereon in good condition and
in good order and repair, at the Owner's expense.
(c)
Any accessory business use of a Residential Unit permitted by Section 4.2 of the Master
Declaration must be conducted in accordance with the Master Declaration and these
Rules and Regulations.
(d)
No Lot or Improvement may be used for any use, and nothing may be stored on any Lot
or Improvement, which would constitute an unusual fire hazard, would result in jeopardizing
any insurance maintained on other Lots or Improvements within or on any other portion
of the Property.
(e)
Under no circumstance may Owners or their agents use Residential Units for short-term
lodging, vacation rentals, hotel purposes (i.e., rental or leasing on a day-to-day
or week-to-week basis) or any similar temporary lodging or living quarter arrangements.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(3), § 2.2)

documents.title: Sec. 1-33. - Pets and livestock.
documents.text:
In addition to those provisions set forth in the Master Declaration with respect to
pets and livestock, the following rules shall apply to pets:
(1)
The CAB may prohibit keeping certain breeds or kinds of pets, restrict the size of
such pets, and impose conditions and restrictions upon keeping such pets, based upon
a specific determination that such type or size of pet or that more than one of a
particular type of pet may constitute a safety concern or nuisance to other Owners.
(2)
Pets and livestock shall not be allowed to damage grass, shrubs, trees or any other
portion of the Development or to become a nuisance or annoyance to others. Expenses
and costs incurred by the CAB as a result of damage caused by any pet shall be reimbursed
to the CAB by the owner of the pet responsible for causing the damage.
(3)
Pets shall not be allowed outside of an Owner's Residential Unit unless:
a.
Restrained by a suitable leash and under the direct control of the pet's owner or
his representative; or
b.
In an enclosure expressly permitted by the Design Guidelines set forth in this Code.
(4)
Pets and livestock shall not be leashed, chained or tethered to any building, stake,
sprinkler, fence, trees or other improvements or landscaping contained within the
Development or otherwise left unattended, in each case outside of such Owner's Lot,
except for short durations and in such locations as may be permitted by the owner
of the property upon which it is leashed, chained or tethered. The Owner or Occupant
so leashing, chaining or tethering remains responsible for such pets and livestock,
including any damage they cause.
(5)
Owners agree to comply with:
a.
Current inoculations of pets as required by applicable Department of Health guidelines;
and
b.
All other applicable governmental laws and regulations pertaining to keeping, maintaining
or raising a pet, including, without limitation, registration of pets.
(6)
No animals, livestock, fowl, or poultry of any kind shall be raised, bred or kept
except domesticated birds, fish and other small domestic animals confined indoors
and an aggregate of not more than four domestic animals (e.g., cats and dogs), provided
they are not kept, bred, or maintained for any commercial purpose.
(7)
No animal shall be permitted to make an unreasonable amount of noise or cause any
objectionable odor or become a nuisance.
(8)
All pet waste must be removed from any property immediately and disposed of properly.
This includes Open Space, landscape tracts, commercial properties and residential

documents.title: Sec. 1-33. - Pets and livestock.
documents.text:
properties. All household pets shall be controlled by the Property Owner and are not
allowed off the Property Owner's property except when leashed and accompanied by the
pet Property Owner or pet Caretaker.
(9)
Each Property Owner with a household pet shall be financially responsible and liable
for any damage caused by said pet.
(10)
Pigs, including pot-bellied pigs, are considered livestock, not household pets or
domestic animals.
(11)
If you are trying to solve a problem with a barking dog or clean up after a pet, please
start with communicating your concern to the pet owner or contact the following county
authorities:
a.
Douglas County Animal Services, 303-660-7529, 7:00 a.m. - 6:00 p.m.
b.
Sheriff's Department Dispatch, 303-660-7500 (After 6:00 p.m. if an animal problem
requires immediate attention).
(Rules of 8-26-2020(1), § VI; Rules of 8-26-2020(3), § 2.3)

documents.title: Sec. 1-34. - Signs; flags.
documents.text:
(a)
Except as provided in Section 5.2.1 of the Master Declaration and these Rules and
Regulations, no signs or advertising devices of any nature shall be displayed, hung,
stored or used on any part of any Residential Unit or Lot, in such a manner as to
be visible from any location outside of such Residential Unit or Lot, without the
prior written permission of the Design Review Committee (DRC). Any signs not in conformance
with the Master Declaration and these Rules and Regulations may be removed by or on
behalf of the CAB, and any damage caused by the placement and removal of such nonconforming
sign shall be paid for by the Owner responsible for the placement of such sign.
(b)
Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in these Rules and Regulations or the Master
Declaration, an Owner may display flags or political signage, subject to the following
restrictions:
(1)
An Owner or Occupant may display a flag on a unit owner's property, in a window of
the unit, or on a balcony or patio adjoining the unit or on a DRC approved flagpole.
No flag shall be prohibited or regulated on the basis of their subject matter, message,
or content; except that flags bearing commercial messages are prohibited. No flag
shall exceed four feet by six feet in size.
Also see Sec. 21-22 (b)(36) and (37) for additional guidance.
(2)
An Owner or Occupant may place political signs promoting or opposing a candidate for
office or a ballot issue in the window of such Owner's or Occupant's Unit, or within
the boundaries of an Owner's Lot, not earlier than 45 days prior to the applicable
election day, and shall remove any such signs within seven days after such election.
Not more than one sign per candidate, office or issue may be so displayed and, subject
to applicable law, no such sign shall exceed 36 inches by 48 inches in size.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(3), § 2.4; Res. No.
2022-08-02
, § 1, 8-26-2022)

documents.title: Sec. 1-35. - Trash.
documents.text:
(a)
No Owner or Occupant will permit any refuse, garbage, trash, lumber, grass, shrubs
or tree clippings, plant waste, metal, bulk materials, scrap, or debris of any kind
to be kept, stored, accumulated on his Lot, nor will such items be deposited on a
street, unless placed in a suitable, tightly covered container that is suitably located
solely for the purpose of garbage pickup, recycling or composting. Further, no Owner
or Occupant will permit any trash or materials to accumulate in such a manner as to
be visible from any Lot or Unit. Owners and Occupants will keep all equipment for
the storage or disposal of refuse in a clean and sanitary condition. No garbage or
trash cans or receptacles or trash bags shall be placed outside earlier than 4:00
a.m. the morning of trash pickup day due to wildlife and shall be kept within garages
or suitable enclosures or locations approved by the DRC at all other times. Trash
cans must be placed back within suitable enclosure or garage same day of trash pick
up.
(b)
Trash removal and recycling shall be organized by, and be performed by, companies
engaged by the CAB. All Owners shall be obligated to use such trash removal and recycling
services in accordance with any rules and regulations in connection therewith, except
with the approval of the CAB. Except as permitted by such companies, disposal of hazardous
waste or large items, such as, but not limited to, building materials and large quantities
of landscape materials, furniture, appliances, or hot water heaters, shall not be
permitted, and removal of these items from the property is the responsibility of the
Owner.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(3), § 2.5(a), (b); Res. No.
2022-08-02
, § 1, 8-26-2022)

documents.title: Sec. 1-36. - Flammable, incendiary or explosive substances or devices.
path: Sec. 1-36. - Flammable, incendiary or explosive substances or devices.
documents.text:
(a)
Owners, tenants, occupants or guests shall not store any flammable, combustible, odorous,
explosive, or other inherently dangerous fluids, chemicals or substances anywhere
within the Community, except those reasonably required for normal household and business
use and in accordance with these Rules and Regulations.
(b)
The term "incendiary or explosive device" includes, but not by way of limitation,
any device consisting in whole or in part of flammable material or other material
having the capability of exploding, igniting or burning.
(c)
Gasoline or fuel for a lawn mower, snow blower, and the like may be maintained on
an incidental basis on or in a Lot or Unit if the amount so kept does not exceed five
gallons and is kept in UL-approved containers. Gasoline or other volatile or incendiary
materials or devices shall be stored only in a manner that strictly complies with
all Applicable Laws.
(d)
Reasonable supplies for the operation of grills, smokers or similar implements may
be maintained including propane tanks (no larger than 20 pounds), charcoal briquets,
smoking pellets or similar materials so long as appropriately stored, maintained and
used.
(e)
No fireworks or firearms may be fired or discharged within the Development, except:
(1)
In any areas specifically designated therefor and in compliance with all Applicable
Laws;
(2)
With the permission of the CAB; and
(3)
Firework displays performed by professional pyrotechnics companies/persons approved
by the CAB.
(f)
The CAB reserves the right to require Owners to promptly remove any such materials
that the CAB believes might constitute a hazard. Owners agree to remove such contents
upon receipt of written notice from the CAB.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(3), §§ 2.5(e), 2.6, 2.8(b))

documents.title: Sec. 1-37. - Vehicles; parking.
documents.text:
(a)
Commercial vehicles, tractors, mobile homes, recreational vehicles, trailers (either
with or without wheels), campers, camper trailers, motorcycles, scooters, boats and
other watercraft, golf carts and boat trailers must be parked only in enclosed garages
and may not be parked on the street. Motor vehicles are prohibited from parking on
any landscaped area at any time, and any portion of a driveway apron in the alley.
Notwithstanding the foregoing, recreational vehicles and motor homes may be temporarily
parked for a maximum of 72 consecutive hours in the driveway of a Lot. All types of
recreational vehicles, including, but not limited to, truck, trailer, motor home,
mobile home, detached camper unit, utility trailer, boat trailer, snowmobile, jet
ski, race car, watercraft, and ATV, are prohibited from parking anywhere within the
community unless they fit entirely within an enclosed garage. A temporary expedient
for loading, delivery, maintenance or emergency is granted. In any event the maximum
amount of time a Recreational Vehicle is allowed to be parked is three overnights
(e.g., 72 hours) during any seven-day period. Periodic movement of the vehicle for
the purpose of circumventing this standard shall not qualify the vehicle for exception
from this standard. Recreational vehicles are allowed to temporarily park for 72 consecutive
hours without DRC approval. This restriction does not prohibit:
(1)
Recreational vehicles, trailers (either with or without wheels), campers, camper trailers,
motorcycles, scooters, boats and other watercraft, golf carts, and boat trailers must
be parked only in enclosed garages and may not be parked on the street. Motor vehicles
are prohibited from parking on any landscaped area at any time, and any portion of
a driveway apron in the alley. Notwithstanding the foregoing, recreational vehicles
and motor homes may be temporarily parked for a maximum of 72 consecutive hours in
the driveway of a Lot. All types of recreational vehicles, including, but not limited
to, truck, trailer, motor home, mobile home, detached camper unit, utility trailer,
boat trailer, snowmobile, jet ski, race car, watercraft, and ATV, are prohibited from
parking anywhere within the community unless they fit entirely within an enclosed
garage. A temporary expedient for loading, delivery, maintenance, or emergency is
granted. In any event the maximum amount of time a Recreational Vehicle is allowed
to be parked in the driveway is three overnights (e.g., 72 hours) during any seven-day

shall not qualify the vehicle for exception from this standard. Recreational vehicles
are allowed to temporarily park for 72 consecutive hours without DRC approval. For
commercial vehicles, tractors, oversized vehicles, and emergency vehicles please go
to Section 21-22 (b)(20).
(2)
Reserved.
(3)
Standard motor vehicles (i.e., less than or equal to one ton) with advertising logos;
or
(4)
Vehicles parked by Property Owners while on vacation or during a period of illness.
Temporary moving of the vehicle around Sterling Ranch shall not relieve a vehicle
from these rules, though an impacted individual may apply for permission to park for
a longer time with the DRC.
(b)
No vehicle may be parked in such a manner as to impede or prevent ready access to
any entrance or exit of a building or parking space, nor shall any vehicle be parked
on any grass, sidewalks or patios, block garbage trucks from access to any dumpsters,
or be parked in a fire lane or designated "no parking" area.
(c)
All vehicles parked in the Development which are required by law to have license plates
must have current license plates. Inoperative, abandoned, unlicensed or stored vehicles
(as defined in the Master Declaration) may not be parked on any street. Vehicles shall
be deemed to be abandoned or inoperative if they meet one or more of the following
criteria:
(1)
The vehicle has a flat tire or other condition rendering it inoperable.
(2)
The vehicle does not have current license plates.
(3)
The vehicle is in an obvious state of disrepair, such as a missing tire, damaged window,
missing or damaged body panel or other parts, or the vehicle is on jacks or blocks.
Inoperative, unused, or unregistered vehicles shall only be stored, parked, maintained
or kept within a 100 percent secured-from-view facility, such as a garage. This applies
to any automobile, truck, motorcycle or motorbike which has not been driven under
its own propulsion or has not been moved for a period of 72 consecutive hours or longer.
(d)
Vehicles in violation of parking regulations are subject to being towed and stored
at the owner's expense. Inoperative, abandoned, unregistered, or unused vehicles are
subject to ticketing or towing at the Property Owner's expense or as provided herein
by applicable law.
(e)

Recreational vehicles, trailers (either with or without wheels), campers, camper trailers,

documents.title: Sec. 1-38. - Household items.
documents.text:
(a)
Rugs, clothing, or other household items may not be hung from any window, balcony,
fence, or facade of the buildings. Temporary clotheslines are permitted so long as
they are not up for longer than 24 hours.
(b)
All roadways and walkways shall be clear for emergency traffic. No furniture, electrical
cords, bicycles, barbecues, toys, or other items of personal property shall be stored,
left or parked on a roadway, walkway, or any other place within the Community other
than an Owner's Lot; provided, however, that bicycles may be stored in designated
bicycle parking areas within the Community, if any.
(c)
The CAB assumes no liability for any loss or damage to articles left or stored in
any portion of the Community.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(3), §§ 2.5(c), (d), 2.8(a); Res. No.
2022-08-02
, § 1, 8-26-2022)

documents.title: Sec. 1-39. - Wiring; air conditioning.
documents.text:
No Owner or Occupant may install exterior wiring for electrical or telephone installation
or for any other purpose, nor shall any items, including, but not limited to, television,
cable, or radio antennae, furnace or other vent, machines or air conditioning unit
vents, be installed on the exterior of a Unit or protrude through the walls or the
roof of Improvements, except with the approval of the DRC. Notwithstanding the foregoing,
the foregoing restriction shall not apply to any satellite dish or antennas used to
receive video programming, broadband radio or wireless data service and Internet access
except in compliance with Section 207 of the Telecommunications Act of 1996 and the
rules and regulations promulgated thereunder.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(3), § 2.9)

documents.title: Sec. 1-67. - Construction/alteration of improvements.
documents.article: ARTICLE III. - DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE; DESIGN GUIDELINES; DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE PROCEDURES
path: ARTICLE III. - DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE; DESIGN GUIDELINES; DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE PROCEDURES
documents.text:
Per the Master Declaration and adopted Design Guidelines, construction of all Improvements
on a Lot, and any alterations or modification of such Improvements (other than changes
the interior thereof), must be approved, in writing, by the DRC. The submittal requirements
and procedures for the DRC are set forth in this article. Except as expressly provided
to the contrary in the Master Declaration or the Design Guidelines, no Improvement
shall be constructed without the prior written consent of the DRC, and no changes
or deviations in or from the plans and specifications consented to by the DRC shall
be made without the prior written consent of the DRC. The approval rights of the DRC
extend to aesthetic considerations as well as issues of design consistency and quality.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(3), § 3.1)

documents.title: Sec. 1-68. - Approval request; plans and specifications.
documents.article: ARTICLE III. - DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE; DESIGN GUIDELINES; DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE PROCEDURES
path: ARTICLE III. - DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE; DESIGN GUIDELINES; DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE PROCEDURES
Sec. 1-68. - Approval request; plans and specifications.
documents.text:
Each request for DRC approval (an "Approval Request") at the conceptual design submittal
and final design submittal phases described in Section 1-69 shall be accompanied by such plans and specifications of the proposed Improvement
as are set forth in the applicable Design Guidelines that show, to the extent applicable
to the Improvement for which the approval is requested, the design and other characteristics
thereof as are set forth in the applicable Design Guidelines and a review fee as established
by the DRC (the "Review Fee"). The DRC will submit a schedule of proposed review fees
annually to the CAB for review and approval. The DRC may postpone review of any material
submitted until it has received all required or requested Plans and Specifications
and other information. The DRC shall notify the Owner in writing upon receipt of all
required Plans and Specifications and that the Owner's Approval Request is complete.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(3), § 3.3)

documents.title: Sec. 1-69. - Review procedure.
documents.article: ARTICLE III. - DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE; DESIGN GUIDELINES; DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE PROCEDURES
path: ARTICLE III. - DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE; DESIGN GUIDELINES; DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE PROCEDURES
documents.text:
The DRC review process for Improvements generally consists of three stages: a pre-design
meeting with the DRC, a conceptual design submittal and a mandatory final design submittal.
While final design submittal is the only mandatory step, final design submittal applications
made without prior completion of the pre-design meeting and conceptual design submittal
have a significantly increased probability for denial by the DRC. Therefore, applicants
are strongly encouraged to complete the pre-design meeting and the conceptual design
submittal prior to submittal for final design approval, unless otherwise directed
by the DRC. The DRC shall strive to approve, approve with conditions or deny a complete
Approval Request within the later to occur of 30 days after its receipt or ten days
after the first meeting of the DRC following its receipt. The DRC's failure to approve,
approve with conditions or deny a complete Approval Request within such period shall
be deemed a denial of such Approval Request. Approval of a majority of the members
of the DRC, either at a meeting or in writing, shall be required to approve any Approval
Request. If DRC approval is granted subject to conditions, the Owner shall revise
his Plans and Specifications to incorporate such changes and shall deliver the required
number of complete sets of revised Plans and Specifications (reflecting responses
to all items) to the DRC, which shall again be reviewed in accordance with and in
the timeframe described above. The DRC has 30 days from receipt of all acceptable
materials to give a ruling. In the event the submittal is extensive in nature, the
DRC may require more review time than the normal 30-day turnaround.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(3), § 3.4; Rules of 8-26-2020(1), §§ III, VI)

documents.title: Sec. 1-70. - Modifications to approved plans and specifications.
documents.article: ARTICLE III. - DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE; DESIGN GUIDELINES; DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE PROCEDURES
path: ARTICLE III. - DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE; DESIGN GUIDELINES; DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE PROCEDURES
Sec. 1-70. - Modifications to approved plans and specifications.
documents.text:
Any modification or change to an approved set of Plans and Specifications must again
be submitted to the DRC for its approval in the same manner as for initial approval
of Plans and Specifications.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(3), § 3.5)

documents.title: Sec. 1-71. - Appeal of DRC decision.
documents.article: ARTICLE III. - DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE; DESIGN GUIDELINES; DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE PROCEDURES
path: ARTICLE III. - DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE; DESIGN GUIDELINES; DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE PROCEDURES
documents.text:
If the DRC disapproves any part of the Plans and Specifications submitted (or approves
the same subject to conditions), the Owner may, within ten days after the DRC's disapproval
or deemed disapproval, make a written request for a hearing before the CAB, or any
appeals board established by the CAB in accordance with the Master Declaration, to
reconsider the Plans and Specifications. A form of a request for a hearing for an
Owner's use is on file in the CAB offices. If the Owner requires a hearing in accordance
with the foregoing sentence, the hearing shall be held in executive session of the
CAB or such appeals board, affording the Owner a reasonable opportunity to be heard.
The Owner shall be notified in writing of the decision within ten days after the hearing.
The decision of the CAB or the appeals board, as applicable, shall be final and binding
upon the Owner.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(3), § 3.6)

documents.title: Sec. 1-72. - Prosecution of work; notice of completion; notices of noncompliance.
documents.article: ARTICLE III. - DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE; DESIGN GUIDELINES; DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE PROCEDURES
path: ARTICLE III. - DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE; DESIGN GUIDELINES; DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE PROCEDURES
Sec. 1-72. - Prosecution of work; notice of completion; notices of noncompliance.
documents.text:
All work approved by the DRC in an Approval Request must be diligently prosecuted
to completion, and a Notice of Completion delivered to the DRC in connection therewith,
in accordance with and within the time allotted in Article 3 of the Master Declaration.
In addition, the DRC shall have the powers to inspect the work and issue Notices of
Noncompliance as set forth in the Master Declaration.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(3), § 3.7)

documents.title: Sec. 1-73. - Variances.
documents.article: ARTICLE III. - DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE; DESIGN GUIDELINES; DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE PROCEDURES
path: ARTICLE III. - DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE; DESIGN GUIDELINES; DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE PROCEDURES
documents.text:
Exceptions from the provisions of the Design Guidelines are considered by the DRC
on a case-by-case basis for specific applications only, and shall not establish a
precedent for any other project or future development. Typically, a technical criteria
variance is submitted with and reviewed concurrently with plans for the improvement
pursuant to the Design Guidelines.
(1)
Submittal requirements for technical criteria variance.
a.
Criteria from which the variance is sought.
b.
Identification of the alternative design, improvement, construction technique or material
proposed to be used.
c.
Supporting documentation, including justification for variance including how the intent
of the criteria is still being achieved, related calculations, details, exhibits,
etc.
d.
The variance request shall be signed by the owner or design professional.
(2)
Review criteria for technical criteria variances. A technical criteria variance may be approved if one or more of the following criteria
are met, provided that no variance shall impose a detriment or injury to other property
or improvements within the Property and will not militate against the general intent
and purpose of the Design Guidelines and the Master Declaration:
a.
The standards may be met by an alternative method that is demonstrated to have an
equivalent or better function and meet the same objective.
b.
Physical constraints exist, such as steep topography or other natural hazards, which
limit the ability to install the improvement, would limit healthy plant growth, or
could cause safety concerns.
c.
Site conditions, including geology, topography, indigenous soils, or issues related
to water demand, may be better addressed through the alternative proposal.
(3)
Documentation of a technical criteria variance. Technical criteria variances shall be documented on drawings for construction and
inspection purposes, including: the variance number, description of the variance,
any conditions of approval, and the approval date.
(4)
Appeals of denials to the CAB. If the DRC denies a request for a variance, it shall provide notice thereof within
ten days after such denial. Notice shall include the reason for the action and shall
be delivered to the address of record. The Owner requesting such variance may appeal
such decision to the CAB. The forms for filing a written appeal are on file in the
offices of the CAB. The procedure for appeals shall be as follows:
a.
Within ten days after the notice of denial has been delivered to the Owner, the Owner

must complete a Request for a Hearing form substantially similar to the Request for
a Hearing form which is on file in the CAB offices.
b.
Upon receipt of a valid request for hearing, the CAB shall set a time, date, and place
of the hearing, which shall be conducted at a CAB Board meeting no later than 60 days
after receipt of the Request for a Hearing, and so notify the Owner.
c.
The Owner or other interested parties may provide testimony at the scheduled hearing.
The CAB shall provide the applicant or registrant with written findings and a ruling
by certified mail, within 15 days after the completion of the hearing.
d.
Any decision rendered by the CAB shall be final.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(3), § 3.9)

documents.title: Sec. 1-93. - Owner complaints.
documents.article: ARTICLE IV. - ENFORCEMENT COMMITTEE AND ENFORCEMENT
path: ARTICLE IV. - ENFORCEMENT COMMITTEE AND ENFORCEMENT
documents.text:
Any complaint by an Owner which alleges a violation of the Master Declaration or any
other Document shall be made in writing and shall contain substantially the same information
as that set forth in the form of Witness Statement on file in the CAB offices and
in the Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board Book of Fees and Forms on file in
the offices of the CAB. At a minimum, the complaint shall set forth:
(1)
The name, unit number and phone number of the complaining witness.
(2)
The name, if known, and unit number of the violator.
(3)
The specific details or description of the violation, including the date, time and
location where the violation occurred.
(4)
A statement by the complaining witness that he will cooperate in the enforcement procedures
and will provide testimony at any proceedings, hearings or trial which may be necessary.
(5)
The signature of the complaining witness and the date on which the complaint is made.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(3), § 4.2)

documents.title: Sec. 1-94. - Notification of alleged violation.
documents.article: ARTICLE IV. - ENFORCEMENT COMMITTEE AND ENFORCEMENT
path: ARTICLE IV. - ENFORCEMENT COMMITTEE AND ENFORCEMENT
documents.text:
(a)
If an investigation or inspection reveals that any part or portion of a Lot or Unit
is not in compliance with the Documents, the DRC has submitted a Notice of Noncompliance
with respect to a Lot or Unit, or another Owner has submitted a complaint in accordance
with Section 1-93 , the Owner shall be notified of the complaint and alleged violation by the Enforcement
Committee or its duly authorized agent, and the Owner shall have the opportunity to
correct or cure the violation, except that certain violations constituting a nuisance
or a threat to the health, safety, or welfare of another resident may require immediate
correction or cure. If the complaint is based on conduct of the Owner's Occupant,
the Occupant shall also be notified of the alleged violation. In addition, if the
alleged violation is due to an Owner complaint, the complaining Owner will also be
copied. The notification shall be in a manner prescribed by the Enforcement Committee
in a form on file in the CAB offices.
Noncompliance notification to a lot or unit owner will be issued with the following
schedule:
(1)
Notice of Noncompliance - Courtesy Notice. A written notice will be sent notifying the Owner of the nature of the alleged violation
and providing seven days to remedy the identified violation.
(2)
Notice of Noncompliance - Stage 1. If the violation is not corrected or cured within seven days, a Stage 1 notice letter
will be sent to Owner, notifying the Owner of the continued violation, and providing
30 days to correct or cure the violation. A Stage 1 Fine will be issued on the thirty-first
day after the Stage 1 notice is sent if the violation is not cured.
(3)
Notice of Noncompliance - Stage 2. If the violation is not corrected or cured on the thirty-first day after the Stage
1 notice is sent, a Stage 2 notice will be sent to the Owner, notifying the Owner
of the continued violation and providing 14 days to correct or cure the violation.
A Stage 2 Fine will be issued on fifteenth day after the Stage 2 notice is sent if
the violation is not cured.
(4)
Notice of Noncompliance - Stage 3. If the violation is not corrected or cured following the fifteenth day after the
Stage 2 notice is sent, a Stage 3 notice will be sent to the Owner, notifying the
Owner of the continued violation and providing 14 days to correct or cure the violation.
A Stage 3 Fine will be issued on fifteenth day after the Stage 3 notice is sent if
the violation is not cured.
(b)
The following violation of the Documents and the Sterling Ranch CAB Code are deemed
Nuisances:
(1)

documents.title: Sec. 1-94. - Notification of alleged violation.
documents.article: ARTICLE IV. - ENFORCEMENT COMMITTEE AND ENFORCEMENT
path: ARTICLE IV. - ENFORCEMENT COMMITTEE AND ENFORCEMENT
documents.text:
Vehicle parking pursuant to Section 1-37 ;
(2)
Basketball hoops pursuant to Section 21-22 (b)(11);
(3)
Equipment storage pursuant to Section 21-22 (b)(31);
(4)
Holiday Displays pursuant to Section 21-22 (b)(46);
(5)
Seasonal Decorative Lighting left on after 10:00 p.m. or displayed outside of permitted
periods pursuant to Section 21-22 (b)(55)
(6)
Outdoor decorative lighting left on after 10:00 p.m. pursuant to Section 21-22 (b)(55);
(7)
Play equipment pursuant to Section 21-22 (b)(69);
(8)
Trash and recycling can storage pursuant to Section 21-22 (b)(100) and 21 - 22(b)(101); and
(9)
Weed growth in planting beds, rock beds, breezeway paths, driveways, sidewalks, and
turf areas pursuant to Section 21-22 (52)(b).
(c)
Notice and Cure Process for Nuisance Violations; Nuisance Violation Fees and Charges.
(1)
Notice of Non-Compliance - Courtesy Notice. A written notice will be sent notifying
the Owner of the nature of the alleged violation and providing seven days to remedy
the identified violation.
(2)
Notice of Non-Compliance - Stage 1. If the violation is not corrected within seven
days, a Stage 1 notice will be sent to the Owner notifying them of the continued violation
and providing seven days to correct or cure the violation. If the violation is not
corrected or cured, a Stage 1 nuisance fine will be issued on the eighth day following
the Stage 1 notification letter.
(3)
Notice of Non-Compliance - Stage 2. If the violation is not corrected within seven
days, a Stage 2 notice will be sent to the Owner notifying them of the continued violation
and providing three days to correct or cure the violation. If the violation is not
corrected or cured, a Stage 2 nuisance fine will be issued on the fourth day following
the Stage 2 notification letter.
(4)
Notice of Non-Compliance - Stage 3. If the violation is not corrected within three
days, a Stage 3 notice will be sent to the Owner notifying them of the continued violation
and providing 24 hours to correct or cure the violation. If the violation is not corrected
or cured, a Stage 3 nuisance fine will be issued.
(5)
More than three violations will be deemed habitual offenders and will receive a written
notice and be given 24 hours to cure or correct the violation.
(6)
Fees and charges for violations as specified herein shall be as set out in Chapter 13 , Article II, Section 13-22 .
(Rules of 8-26-2020(3), § 4.3; Res. No.
2022-08-02
, § 1, 8-26-2022)

documents.title: Sec. 1-95. - Opportunity for a hearing before the Enforcement Committee.
documents.article: ARTICLE IV. - ENFORCEMENT COMMITTEE AND ENFORCEMENT
path: ARTICLE IV. - ENFORCEMENT COMMITTEE AND ENFORCEMENT
Sec. 1-95. - Opportunity for a hearing before the Enforcement Committee.
documents.text:
Any Owner receiving a Notice of Alleged Violation and who has not corrected or cured
the violation within the permitted time is entitled to an opportunity for a hearing.
If the Owner desires a hearing, the Owner must proceed as follows:
(1)
Within ten days after the Notice of Alleged Violation has been delivered on the Owner
and the time for correction or cure of the violation has expired, the Owner must complete
the Request for a Hearing form, in the form attached to the Notice of Alleged Violation
(a copy of which form is on file in the CAB offices in the Sterling Ranch Community
Authority Board Book of Fees and Forms), and return it to the Enforcement Committee
or CAB staff.
(2)
If a request for a hearing is timely filed, a hearing on the complaint shall be held
before the Enforcement Committee. The Owner shall be notified of the date and time
of the hearing, which shall be conducted no later than 30 days after receipt of the
Request for a Hearing, as determined by the Enforcement Committee. The hearing shall
be conducted in accordance with any rules and procedures therefor promulgated by the
CAB or the Enforcement Committee.
(3)
At any such hearing, the Enforcement Committee shall hear and consider arguments,
evidence or statements regarding the alleged Violation. Following a hearing, the Enforcement
Committee shall issue, within ten days, its determination regarding the alleged Violation.
(4)
Notification of the Enforcement Committee's determination shall be made in writing
and transmitted to the Owner. Where the Lot or Unit is determined to be in Violation
of the Documents, the notification shall be considered a notice of violation (a "Notice
of Violation"), and shall include the time period, which may be immediate and may
not exceed 30 days, in which the Violation is to be corrected, remedied or otherwise
removed, as well as any fines or other sanctions imposed. Fines may be imposed according
to the fine schedule set forth by the CAB from time to time.
(5)
At any time prior to the Enforcement Committee's final determination of Violation,
an Owner may notify the Enforcement Committee in writing that any Violation has been
corrected, remedied or removed. Following inspection of the Lot or Unit by the Enforcement
Committee and confirmation that the Lot or Unit is in compliance; the Enforcement
Committee may suspend or dismiss all actions to enforce its remedies.
(6)
If no Request for a Hearing is filed within ten days after a Notice of Alleged Violation,
a hearing will be considered waived, the allegations in the Notice of Alleged Violation

Sec. 1-96. - Opportunity for a hearing before the CAB.
documents.text:
Any Owner who has received a decision from the Enforcement Committee of a Notice of
Violation that desires to appeal to the CAB is entitled to an opportunity for a hearing
before the CAB. If the Owner desires such a hearing, the Owner must proceed as follows:
(1)
Within ten days after the Owner's receipt of the Notice of Violation with the Enforcement
Committee decision, the Owner must complete the Request for a Hearing form for a hearing
before the CAB, which is attached to the written decision (a copy of which form is
on file in the CAB offices in the Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board Book of
Fees and Forms), and return it to the CAB staff.
(2)
If a request for a hearing is timely filed, a hearing on the complaint shall be held
before the CAB at its next regularly scheduled Board meeting. If the next occurring
CAB Board meeting is less than two weeks from the date on which the request for appeal
is received, the appeal shall be added to agenda for the meeting subsequent to the
next occurring CAB Board meeting to allow time to gather the appropriate documents
and generate the necessary reports. The Owner shall be notified of the date and time
of the hearing. The hearing shall be conducted in accordance with any rules and procedures
therefor promulgated by the CAB.
(3)
At any such hearing, the CAB shall hear and consider arguments, evidence, or statements
regarding the Notice of Violation. Following a hearing, the CAB shall issue, within
ten days, its determination regarding the Notice of Violation.
(4)
Notification of the CAB's determination shall be made in writing. Where the Lot or
Unit is determined to be in Violation of the Documents, the notification shall be
considered a confirmed Notice of Violation (a "Confirmed Notice of Violation"), and
shall include the time period, not to exceed 45 days, in which the Violation is to
be corrected, remedied or otherwise removed, as well as confirmation of the fines
or other sanctions imposed by the Enforcement Committee.
(5)
At any time prior to the CAB's issuance of the Confirmed Notice of Violation, an Owner
may notify the CAB in writing that any Violation has been corrected, remedied or removed.
Following inspection of the Lot or Unit by the Enforcement Committee and confirmation
that the Lot or Unit is in compliance, the CAB may suspend or dismiss all actions
to enforce its remedies.
(6)

Community Standards Committee decision, a hearing before the CAB will be considered

documents.title: Sec. 5-19. - Scope.
documents.text:
(a)
The enduring character of Sterling Ranch is sustained through the design principles
and standards presented in this article. Within these pages are guidelines for community
principles, residential architecture, landscape, fencing and signage that, together,
ensure a cohesive community. Community principles that play a role throughout Sterling
Ranch are articulated to instill in each home state of the art structural and systematic
foundations regarding sustainability.
(b)
This article contains architectural principles for traditional and modern Colorado
designs, including a description of the design style and renderings of each design
component. To maintain the flow of Sterling Ranch's aesthetic, signage program standards
are presented as regulations for builder representation within villages under construction.
(c)
Through the implementation of these Design Principles set forth in this article, Colorado's
rich heritage and its destiny find a home in harmony throughout the Sterling Ranch
community.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(9), § 1.1)

documents.title: Sec. 5-20. - Community statement.
documents.text:
(a)
Colorado's rich heritage and its destiny find a home in harmony at Sterling Ranch.
(b)
This mixed-use, master-planned community of authentic Colorado architecture and treasured
natural surroundings will be vitalized by mindful, sustainable and forward-thinking
technologies. All brought together in a shared experience: the quality of nature and
the quality of a promising new day come together as one.
(c)
Sterling Ranch will soon be home to over 10,000 new residences, spaciously sweeping
across eight unique villages all radiating outward from an amenity-rich town center.
Pedestrian-friendly planning and design focused on connectivity offers approximately
30 miles of trails, beautiful open space, two state parks and three regional parks.
(d)
Surroundings that celebrate the natural beauty of the land, and innovation that ensures
the promise of tomorrow; that is the Nature of Sterling Ranch.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(9), § 1.2)

documents.title: Sec. 5-21. - Site description.
documents.text:
Nestled into the foothills of Colorado's Front Range and situated southwest of Denver,
Sterling Ranch's land is composed of rolling hills, ravines and gullies. Throughout
the dips and high points, the site boasts spectacular views of the mountains and southern
foothills. The site location offers a variety of open space options including easy
access to adjacent Roxborough and Chatfield State Parks, trail entrances to Sharptail
Ridge and Pike National Forest. To the south, the Sterling Ranch Open Space protects
Colorado's wildlife corridors. Carefully conceived, this master-planned community
provides eight distinct villages.
Site Plan Map
(Rules of 8-26-2020(9), § 1.3)

documents.title: Sec. 5-46. - General overview.
documents.text:
(a)
The homes at Sterling Ranch are all integral parts of this innovative, smart community
that is unlike any other, anywhere. In support of the high tech nature of this community,
each home is required to have and/or offer specifications for lifelong learning, energy
efficiency, healthful materials, outdoor lifestyles, safety systems, technology integration,
and water sustainment. Working in concert, each of those elements come together to
create a sustainable, forward-thinking community that is one to emulate.
(b)
Listed here are required and optional specifications that must be provided or offered
by each builder to home buyers. The optional specifications shall be presented to
home buyers as discretionary add-ons for homeowner selection.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(9), § 2(intro. ¶))

documents.title: Sec. 5-47. - Education.
documents.text:
(a)
Education is a cornerstone of the Sterling Ranch Community, and lifelong learning
is an ongoing amenity for all residents.
(b)
Required education specifications. Builders will be responsible to pay a one-time
supplemental fee of $1,500.00 per single-family detached dwelling unit to the Douglas
County School District (DCSD); or $750.00 per single-family attached units. This payment
contributes to the overall Sterling Ranch Planned Development's education ecosystem.
It is a commitment to the Douglas County School District to assist in building schools
and facilities. The stewardship related to the combined focus for, attention to and
support of Sterling Ranch's educational opportunities offers continued personal development
for all residents in every phase of life.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(9), § 2.1(A))

documents.title: Sec. 5-48. - Energy.
documents.text:
(a)
Power sustainment. The power of Sterling Ranch is harnessed through each home's ability for energy sustainment
and conscientiousness.
(b)
Energy specification categories. The required and optional energy specifications listed below support the uniqueness
and resourcefulness of homes at Sterling Ranch and maintain the sustainable component
of this community:
(1)
Required energy specifications.
a.
HERS score. Each builder will be responsible for obtaining a Home Energy Rating Score (HERS)
for each home. The HERS score will be posted for each home and the anticipated utility
costs shall be made aware to the home buyer.
b.
EnergyStar. Each builder will be responsible to design each home in compliance with the EPA's
most current EnergyStar program. The specifications for EnergyStar can be found at
www.energystar.gov.
c.
Solar ready.
1.
Pre-wired. Every home shall be pre-wired for solar installation. This includes, but is not limited
to, every home having conduit placed from the roof to the electrical load center or
panel.
2.
Solar Made Simple program. Builders shall participate in the Solar Made Simple program that makes solar standard
on every home. The builder may allow homeowners the option to opt out of zero down
payment lease options for residential solar by utilizing the CAB provided form. Builders
will work with CAB approved solar providers in order to increase efficiency and improve
value to homeowners.
Builders and homeowners may contact CAB for a list of currently approved solar providers.
If a homeowner does not opt out, each builder shall allow an approved solar provider
to install a solar system on the roof of a home. If a homeowner elects to opt out,
the homeowner shall be provided the option to participate in Xcel offsite renewable
energy programs.
d.
Energy reading equipment. Builders must install in each home energy-reading equipment that digitally displays
readouts from the Xcel Energy gas and electric meters. For additional information
refer to Section 5-219.
e.
Electric vehicle ready. Every home shall be pre-wired for electric vehicle charging. This includes, but is
not limited to, every home shall have a NEMA 14-50 electrical outlet, located in the
garage per electrical plan.
f.
Dark Sky compliance. All exterior lighting shall be Dark Sky compliant with adequate shielding.
(2)
Optional energy specifications.
a.
LED lighting package. Each builder shall offer an LED lighting package for each home.
b.
Solar system purchase. Builders shall offer a solar system that homeowners can purchase from the solar company

documents.title: Sec. 5-48. - Energy.
documents.text:
offering the solar opt out program.
c.
Electric vehicle charging station. Each builder shall offer an electric vehicle charging station for the garage.
d.
Energy storage. Each builder shall offer a battery storage option for each home.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(9), § 2.1(B); Res. No.
2023-07-01
, § 1, 7-19-2023)

documents.title: Sec. 5-49. - Health.
documents.text:
Permeating throughout each home is the crispness of air that is inherent to living
in Colorado. To ensure each home supports the quality and healthfulness of life at
Sterling Ranch, the following are required and optional specifications:
(1)
Required health specifications.
a.
Low volatile organic compound paints. Each builder shall use low volatile organic compound (VOC) paints, carpets and adhesives.
(2)
Optional health specifications.
a.
Healthy ventilation. Each builder shall offer an HVAC system designed to accommodate minimum MERV 8 filters
and ANSI 62.2 ventilation standards.
b.
Indoor airPlus certification. Each builder shall offer a home that can be Indoor airPlus certified. The standards
for Indoor airPlus certification can be found at www.epa.gov/indoorairplus.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(9), § 2.1(C))

documents.title: Sec. 5-50. - Lifestyle.
documents.text:
(a)
Commitment to community and home design. Sterling Ranch is committed to ensuring its community and home design components
align with the multitude of lifestyle attributes of prospective residents. This includes
a concentration in resourcefulness and conscientiousness of the community's natural
surroundings, and how that impacts outdoor lifestyles.
(b)
Wildlife habitats. The importance of outdoor lifestyles is associated with the protection of local wildlife
and longevity of its habitats. Landscape Design Principles will secure native and
naturalized landscaping that promotes the integration of wildlife habitats that exist
in the community's natural surroundings. See section 5-131 .
(c)
Outdoor living space integration. Due to Sterling Ranch's attention to outdoor lifestyles, outdoor living spaces integrated
into the houses are encouraged to allow residents the enjoyment and immediate access
to its natural beauty.
(d)
Required lifestyle specifications; backyard landscaping. Each builder shall offer backyard landscaping plans for each residential unit.
(e)
Optional lifestyle specifications.
(1)
Outdoor living spaces. Each builder shall offer an outdoor living option. The outdoor living option should
include one or more of the following features:
a.
Covered deck/patio;
b.
Fire pit;
c.
Fireplace;
d.
Integrated grill with outdoor kitchen area;
e.
Outdoor seating area;
f.
Backyard planter boxes.
(2)
Wildlife friendly. Each builder shall have a wildlife-friendly landscaping package for the backyard.
Refer to section 5-131 .
(3)
Edible landscaping. Each builder shall offer an edible landscaping package for the backyard that promotes
homegrown food and a healthy environment.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(9), § 2.1(D))

documents.title: Sec. 5-51. - Safety.
documents.text:
(a)
Generally. The safety and security of Sterling Ranch goes beyond the intelligent planning of
its interconnected community. It is showcased in the security of each home and leads
to peace of mind for every homeowner. When leaving on vacation, homeowners know their
investment is protected.
(b)
Safety specification categories. The following are required and optional specifications to ensure a safe, secure and
worry-free community from the front door:
(1)
Required safety specifications.
a.
Security system. The Siemens system includes a basic security system, which must be
installed by the builder on the main floor of each home. Refer to sections 5-215 and
5-216.
(2)
Optional safety specifications.
a.
Cameras. Each builder shall include a security upgrade option to the home automation analytics
management system that includes interior and exterior cameras. Refer to sections 5-215
and 5-216.
b.
Upgrade packages. Each builder shall offer additional security upgrade packages that complement the
Siemens system. The packages should include automated door locks, motion sensors and
additional window and door sensors. Upgrade options are available through Siemens
as well as other vendors.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(9), § 2.1(E); Res. No.
2023-04-02
, § 1, 4-19-2023)

documents.title: Sec. 5-52. - Technology.
documents.text:
(a)
Generally.
(1)
The homes of Sterling Ranch are smart, from the inside out. With some of the nation's
fastest Internet speeds per home, and the interconnectedness of the entire community,
each home requires features to enable this technology.
(2)
Below are required and optional specifications to allow the technology of Sterling
Ranch to function optimally. For additional information, refer to division 8 of this
article.
(b)
Required technology specifications.
(1)
CAT 6 drops. Each builder shall have a minimum of three CAT 6 drops and one coaxial drop housed
in Smurf Tube.
a.
One CAT 6 drop must be to a central location on the main floor where a WAP/router
can be installed as the home's wireless network.
b.
One CAT 6 and one coaxial drop must be to an entertainment location within the home.
(2)
Home automation analytics management system. Each builder shall install a home automation analytics management system within each
home. This system must meet the detailed requirements specified in section 5-216.
(3)
ONT and router. Each builder shall give an Internet service provider access to the property to install
an optical network terminal (ONT) and a high bandwidth wireless router (WAP).
a.
It is the builder's responsibility to have both fiber and power to the ONT and CAT
6, and power to the WAP.
b.
Each builder shall also provide a state-of-the-art Wi-Fi system in order to provide
homeowners with whole-home Wi-Fi coverage. For additional information, refer to section
5-218.
(c)
Optional technology specifications.
(1)
Home automation analytics management system upgrades. Each builder shall offer a minimum of three upgrade packages for the home automation
analytics management system. These upgrade packages may include options for automated
lighting, thermostats, HVAC/ventilation systems, security and video system, and garage
door openers.
(2)
Fiber optics. Each builder shall offer an interior fiber optic upgrade in which bendable fiber
optic cables are run throughout the home. Bendable fiber can also be procured through
Corning, Inc.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(9), § 2.1(F); Res. No.
2023-04-02
, § 1, 4-19-2023

documents.title: Sec. 5-53. - Water.
documents.text:
The elements of water sustainability are key components for maintaining Sterling Ranch's
proper usage of resources now and well into the future. Provided here are required
and optional specifications that ensure a water-conscious community.
(1)
Required water specifications.
a.
Toilets. Toilets shall be WaterSense® labeled (and use less than or equal to 1.28 gallons
per flush (gpf)).
b.
Lavatory faucets. Lavatory faucets shall be WaterSense® labeled (and have a flow rate of less than
or equal to 1.5 gallons per minute (gpm)).
c.
Kitchen faucets. Kitchen faucets shall have a flow rate of less than or equal to 2.2 gpm.
d.
Showerheads. Shower heads shall be WaterSense® labeled (and use less than or equal to 2.0 gpm
per shower head).
e.
Clothes washers. Each clothes washer shall be EnergyStar labeled with a water factor of less than
or equal to 6.0 gallons per cycle per cubic foot.
f.
Hot water recirculation. Any installed hot water recirculation systems shall be demand initiated. Builders
are encouraged to construct to the EPA Version 1.1 WaterSense® new home specification
in order to minimize wasted water while waiting for hot water. The WaterSense® specification
requires that no more than 0.6 gallons of water shall be collected from the hot water
fixture before hot water is delivered.
g.
Water meters.
1.
The CAB will require builders to install an IP-based residential dual water-metering
package that is pre-assembled. The package measures the indoor and outdoor water usage.
2.
This solution will only require one main water tap and will be installed in the home
between wall studs. Utility grade data for billing and community analytics is the
outcome of this solution.
h.
Irrigation controllers. The CAB has an approved irrigation controller that is WaterSense® certified and ties
into the home system. For additional details, refer to section 5-217.
(2)
Optional water specifications.
a.
WaterSense® certification. Each builder will be required to offer a home WaterSense®
certification as an option.
b.
The specifications for WaterSense® can be found at www.epa.gov/watersense.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(9), § 2.1(G))
