documents.title: Sec. 5-383. - Overview.
documents.article: ARTICLE III. - ASCENT VILLAGE DESIGN PRINCIPLES
path: ARTICLE III. - ASCENT VILLAGE DESIGN PRINCIPLES
documents.text:
Residential fencing provides community identity, and delineates boundaries. The design
(color, scale, materials and detail) of fencing has been selected to enhance the appearance
of individual lots and to complement the character of Sterling Ranch.
(1)
A standard fence has been developed for Ascent Village to help establish a cohesive
character throughout the community.
(2)
The Ascent Village Fence for all lots adjacent to open space has been developed to
create visual consistency within open space areas and to help transition individual
lots into open space in an aesthetically pleasing way.
(3)
Fencing on Icon Lots may be subject to additional design requirements not included
in these standards, dealt with on a case-by-case basis.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(10), § 6.1)

documents.title: Sec. 5-384. - Ascent Village single family.
documents.article: ARTICLE III. - ASCENT VILLAGE DESIGN PRINCIPLES
path: ARTICLE III. - ASCENT VILLAGE DESIGN PRINCIPLES
documents.text:
(a)
All on-lot fencing shall be three-rail fence. Setting the Wing Fence on all lots a
minimum distance from the front of the building facade (interior lots ten feet, corner
lots 20 feet) allows for a larger landscaped area between homes. Builders are required
to install Wing Fencing; the rear and side lot line fencing may be installed with
the rear yard landscape. Corner lots will have fencing on the side. Open and park
lots will have side and rear as an open space.
(b)
Requirements are as follows:
(1)
Wing fencing: Minimum of ten feet back from front of building facade, or at an appropriate
architectural feature, perpendicular to the house.
(2)
Wing fencing on corner lot: Minimum of 20 feet back from the front building facade,
or at an appropriate architectural feature, perpendicular to the house.
(3)
Rear yard: Inside property line if adjacent to open space. It will be on the property
line if it is on the interior lot.
(4)
Side yard: On property line.
(5)
Side yard on corner lot: Minimum of two feet setback from property line.
(6)
Height: 54 inches.
(7)
Materials: Concrete.
(8)
Finishes: Color to be Solomon Dry Pigment #338 'Earthen.'
(9)
Pet Mesh (Optional): Rectangular grid pattern, 14 gauge, welded wire mesh, attached
to private side of fence.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(10), § 6.2)

documents.title: Sec. 5-385. - Ascent Village four-pack cluster product.
documents.article: ARTICLE III. - ASCENT VILLAGE DESIGN PRINCIPLES
path: ARTICLE III. - ASCENT VILLAGE DESIGN PRINCIPLES
Sec. 5-385. - Ascent Village four-pack cluster product.
documents.text:
(a)
All fencing shall be three-rail fence and match specifications. See Section 21-23 , Fencing standards.
(b)
Builders are required to install three-rail concrete fence along property lines adjacent
to open space, parks or street corners.
(c)
Any additional fencing if wanted by homeowners requires DRC approval.
(1)
Fencing submittals shall include a scaled site plan with the location of the fencing
clearly marked, include dimensions.
(d)
Setting the Wing Fence a minimum distance from the front of the building facade of
three feet or at an appropriate architectural feature, perpendicular to the house
is required.
(e)
Fencing on Enhanced or Icon Lots may be subject to additional design requirements
not included in these standards, dealt with on a case-by-case basis.
(f)
Any fencing which was installed by the Builder or Developer shall not be removed or
modified without DRC approval.
(g)
Gates require DRC approval, will be considered on a case-by-case basis, and must match
specifications. See Section 21-23 , Fencing standards.
(h)
Nothing may be attached to a fence to increase the height or screening capability,
such as but not limited to, lattice, temporary fencing, chain link, extra fence pickets,
etc.
(i)
Two fences cannot be built side-by-side on the same property line. Fences may not
be installed in a manner that creates a "double fence" with a fence on a neighboring
property. Double fences, even if multiple feet apart, can create spaces that are difficult
to maintain.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(10), § 6.3; Res. No.
2022-08-02
, § 1, 8-26-2022)

documents.title: Sec. 5-386. - Ascent Village retaining walls.
documents.article: ARTICLE III. - ASCENT VILLAGE DESIGN PRINCIPLES
path: ARTICLE III. - ASCENT VILLAGE DESIGN PRINCIPLES
documents.text:
(a)
All retaining walls shall be Allan Block Europa collection, Abbey Blend Pattern, Grey
Blend color. Setting the retaining walls on all lots a minimum distance of two feet
from the side and rear lot line allows for a larger landscaped area between homes
and away from fencing. Builders are required to install retaining walls if the required
slope from Douglas County is not achievable; additional retaining walls installed
by homeowners will require approval of the county and a revised drainage survey plan.
Final approval of retaining walls are up to the discretion of the Design Review Committee
after county approval. Retaining walls for cluster, town home, alley load and like
product will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis.
(b)
Requirements are as follows:
(1)
Minimum two-foot setbacks from side lot lines.
(2)
Walls will not be allowed in easements without the consent of the utility or the owner.
(3)
Any change from the original drainage plan will require new survey and drainage report
from a licensed surveyor.
(4)
Height: 48 inches max. Additional height will need to be engineered by a licensed
engineer.
(5)
Finishes: Allan Block Europa collection, Abbey Blend Pattern, Grey Blend color.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(10), § 6.4)

documents.title: Sec. 9-1. - Tree lawn maintenance.
documents.text:
(a)
Every Owner shall be responsible for the irrigation and maintenance of the Tree Lawn
between their property edge and the street along the perimeter of their property ownership.
The amount of water required for maintenance of the tree lawn will be included in
the outdoor water budget calculated in accordance with the Water Demand Management
Initiative.
(b)
The maintenance responsibility shall also include the cutting of the grass and replacement
of any grass and plant materials as necessary to keep the tree lawn in substantially
similar condition to its original approved installation design plan unless and until
a subsequent design plan is approved by the CAB.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § XI)

documents.title: Sec. 9-12. - Definitions.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
path: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
documents.text:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the
meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates
a different meaning:
Artificial Turf means non-living material typically in place of living turf/lawn. The appearance
is intended to mimic green, living turf during the growing season.
BMPs means Best Management Practices.
CAB Rules and Regulations Utilities, Parks, and Open Space means the CAB Rules and Regulations Utilities, Parks and Open Space adopted by the
CAB, as set forth in this Code and as amended from time to time.
Drought Tolerant means a plant with the capability of withstanding drought conditions without dying.
Enhanced Landscaping means additional landscaping requirements on corner lots, lots adjacent to open space,
and Icon Lots. Example requirements include additional trees/plantings and treatment
in Transition Zones.
Establishment Period means a period of time required for a plant to seed, germinate, and establish a healthy
root system, which promotes long-term health and growth which for purposes of the
Initiative is assumed to be 45 days from the date of installation to the development
of a healthy root system; with the assumption that all installations will not happen
on the first day of a billing cycle, the Establishment Period will begin on the first
day of the billing cycle in the month of installation and will continue through the
last day of the next billing cycle.
Evapotranspiration (ET) means a measure of water depletion from the soil due to evaporation from the soil
surface and transpiration through plant foliage.
GPM means gallons per minute.
GreenCO means Green Industries of Colorado.
Hardscape means non-living site improvements such as buildings, pavement, walkways and parking
areas.
Hydrozone means areas within the landscape area defined by similar water needs. For the purpose
of this document, hydrozones are subdivided into high, moderate, and low categories.
Icon Lot or Enhanced Lot means lots that are identified as such in the Design Principles for Sterling Ranch
set forth in chapter 5 .
Initiatives means the Water Demand Management Initiatives for Sterling Ranch set forth in this
article.
Landscape and Irrigation Plan means a plan drawn to scale that shows the layout of all landscape and irrigation
system components and their specifications for a development site.
Landscape and Irrigation Professionals means a landscape and/or irrigation plan designer, and/or installer, and/or maintenance

documents.title: Sec. 9-12. - Definitions.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
path: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
documents.text:
contractor that possesses the qualifications, and is registered with the CAB, to perform
design, installation, and maintenance of landscaping and irrigation work at Sterling
Ranch.
Landscaping Standards means those standards as they are as set forth in the Design Principles and the Initiatives.
Outdoor Annual Water Budget means the same as the term is defined in the CAB Rules and Regulations.
PSI means pounds per square inch.
Sight Triangle means a triangle formed at roadway intersections that must be kept clear of obstructions
as required by Douglas County or the CAB.
Transition Zone means landscaped areas located between developed landscapes and open space. The intent
is to visually blend open space and yards.
Tree Lawn means the landscaped space between the street and sidewalk. The Builder will complete
this area with sod, shrubs, street trees, and an irrigation system. The property owner
is required to maintain this area in accordance with this design. Tree Lawns provide
a safety zone for pedestrians as well as improving the visual aesthetics of the streetscape.
Variance means a design, or portion of a design, that is a diversion from the Initiatives
contained herein, or acceptance of a landscape professional different than that specified
in Section 9-190 . Any approved variance shall meet the intent of these Initiatives. A variance requires
formal approval by the DRC and/or CAB in accordance with the process described in Section 9-142 .
Water Budget means the Outdoor Annual Water Budget as set forth in the Rules and Regulations and
this article.
Water Factor means the quotient of the total weighted per-cycle water consumption divided by the
capacity of the clothes washer. Lower numbers indicate more efficient use of water.
(Rules of 11-18-2020, § 2)

documents.title: Sec. 9-13. - Intent.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
path: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
documents.text:
The Water Demand Management Initiatives contained in this article constitute the framework
for "watersmart" development. With respect to water demand management set forth in
the Design Principles, it is the intent of this article to provide for appropriate
water use management within Sterling Ranch through the regulation of the design, installation
and operation of interior and exterior water fixtures, landscaping, and irrigation
systems. The CAB may at any time and from time to time amend, supplement or otherwise
modify this article, or implement additional Initiatives and specifications, as CAB
deems necessary and advisable.
(Rules of 11-18-2020, § 1(intro. ¶))

documents.title: Sec. 9-14. - Compliance with plumbing or building requirements.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
path: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
Sec. 9-14. - Compliance with plumbing or building requirements.
documents.text:
Nothing provided herein shall be deemed to relieve any Owner from compliance with
the plumbing code or building code of Douglas County or any other federal, state or
local plumbing or building requirements.
(Rules of 11-18-2020, § 1.1)

documents.title: Sec. 9-32. - Applicability.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
path: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
documents.text:
The Nonresidential Water Demand Management Initiatives in Section 9-32 and Subdivisions II and III of this Division apply to all Nonresidential Improvements
(as defined in the Master Declaration) at Sterling Ranch. Nonresidential land uses
include commercial, industrial, schools, parks, streetscapes, open space, and any
other uses not associated with a dwelling unit.
(Rules of 11-18-2020, § 4(intro. ¶))

documents.title: Sec. 9-33. - Metering and leaks.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
path: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
documents.text:
(a)
Metering. All indoor and outdoor uses shall each be independently metered, submetered, or equipped
with an alternate technology capable of tracking water used. All water meters shall
be specifically approved by the CAB.
(b)
Leaks. There shall be no detected leaks pertaining to the initial or subsequent installation
of any water-using fixtures, appliances, equipment, or the irrigation system.
(Rules of 11-18-2020, § 4.1)

documents.title: Sec. 9-34. - Dual metering and monthly billing.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
path: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
Sec. 9-34. - Dual metering and monthly billing.
documents.text:
(a)
Metering systems shall be capable of separately measuring indoor and outdoor nonresidential
water use. All outdoor faucets (e.g., hose bibb) water usage shall be metered as outdoor
use. Each Builder shall purchase and install the CAB's specific approved water meter
in every building. These water meters have been designed to be read remotely through
the Internet; as such, each building must have an Internet connection for the meters
to be read remotely. Any Owner replacing the Builder-installed water meter (other
than with a CAB-approved water meter) or terminating the Internet connection within
his building must provide the CAB with written authorization to enter such building
to manually read the water meter and pay the CAB a monthly or other fee established
by the CAB from time to time in order to do so. Failure to do so will be deemed a
violation of this article and shall entitle the CAB to all remedies under the Master
Declaration and this Code.
(b)

documents.title: Sec. 9-47. - Specifications.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
path: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
documents.text:
Nonresidential spaces at Sterling Ranch shall be constructed according to the following
indoor specifications. The indoor specifications are largely based on the U.S. Environmental
Protection Agency's WaterSense New Home Specification; however, the values may be
periodically adjusted to reflect revisions to the WaterSense program and other statutory
requirements, new technology and concepts, and/or to provide different demand management
measures as the CAB deems necessary or advisable as described in Section 9-13 .
(1)
Toilets.
a.
Tank-type toilets shall be WaterSense labeled.
b.
Flushometer-valve toilets shall be WaterSense labeled. For maximum water savings and
performance, the flushometer valve and bowl should be purchased in hydraulically matched
combinations that are compatible in terms of their designed flush volume.
(2)
Urinals. Urinals shall be WaterSense labeled. Waterless urinals should be considered as appropriate.
(3)
Lavatory faucets.
a.
Private-Use Lavatory Faucets (e.g., offices) shall be WaterSense labeled.
b.
Public-Use Lavatory Faucets (e.g., recreation center) shall be WaterSense labeled.
Consider installing automatic-shutoff faucets that use a maximum of 0.25 gal/cycle.
(4)
Kitchen faucets. Kitchen faucets shall use less than or equal to 2.2 gpm. Consider installing temporary
shut-off or foot-operated valves for kitchen faucets in commercial facilities.
(5)
Showerheads.
a.
Single Shower Stalls shall be WaterSense labeled.
b.
Communal Shower Stalls may have multiple showerheads that are each WaterSense labeled.
(6)
Laundry equipment. Commercial clothes washers shall be Energy Star labeled.
(7)
Dishwashers. Private-use dishwashers shall be Energy Star labeled.
(8)
Commercial kitchen equipment. Pre-Rinse Spray Valves shall be WaterSense labeled.
(9)
Mechanical systems. Single-pass cooling systems are prohibited.
(Rules of 11-18-2020, § 4.2)

documents.title: Sec. 9-70. - Maintenance standards.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
path: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
documents.text:
(a)
Generally.
(1)
Maintenance requirements shall be noted on landscape and irrigation plans.
(2)
Regular maintenance shall be consistent with the needs of the plant material and may
include pruning, mowing, fertilization, and weeding.
(3)
CAB staff shall meet periodically with maintenance teams responsible for parks within
Sterling Ranch to evaluate historical evapotranspiration, weather forecasts, and data
from weather stations.
(4)
Insect infestations are treated quickly and effectively to prevent spreading.
(b)
Irrigation.
(1)
Irrigation systems shall be maintained to ensure proper operation and function for
water use efficiency.
(2)
A regular maintenance schedule shall include, but not be limited to, routine inspection,
auditing, adjustment and repair of the irrigation system and its components. Operation
of the irrigation system outside the normal watering window is allowed for auditing
and system maintenance.
(3)
Repair of all irrigation equipment shall be done with the originally installed components.
If equipment components with greater efficiency are used in replacement, the entire
zone must be changed to maintain consistency.
(c)
Turf and woody plants, and fertilization.
(1)
Turf.
a.
Turf shall be maintained in a manner consistent with its growth characteristics and
intended use. It shall optimize sustainability through maintenance practices that
encourage root development and overall plant health.
b.
Preferred mowing height is 3.5 inches, but does not exceed 4.0 inches.
c.
Adjust mowing frequency throughout the growing season to remove between one-quarter
and one-third of the grass height per mowing.
d.
Maintain mowing equipment by sharpening mower blades, or checking reel-type mowers
for proper blade to bed knife adjustment.
e.
Thatch build-up shall be addressed for plant health purposes and to reduce runoff.
f.
Spring and fall aeration is recommended.
g.
Turf is green and has been treated to prevent weed growth.
(2)
Woody plant material. The mature size of woody plant material shall be considered during the design process
so that pruning should only be necessary due to damage or health conditions, and to
encourage a natural growth habit for hedges and topiaries.
a.
Pruning practices shall be consistent with type of tree or shrub. It is recommended
to not remove more than one-third of the branch growth.
b.
Eliminate dead and diseased plant material. If this causes significant disfigurement,
replacement is necessary.
c.
Encourage naturalistic habit and reduce crowding, while controlling scale related

will have a water budget of 20 gal/sf, ten gal/sf, and six gal/sf, respectively. Non-irrigated

documents.text:
(a)
Landscape and irrigation plans for each outdoor service connection at Sterling Ranch
must be submitted for review and approval by the DRC. Each application for plan review
shall be accompanied by the review fee established by the DRC from time to time. The
DRC, in its discretion, may waive fees for the review of plans.
(b)
As a part of the Landscape and Irrigation Application, the Landscape Verification
Checklist (on file in the offices of the CAB) must be submitted to the DRC to ensure
that the water demand of the landscape plan complies with the Water Budget provided.
(c)
The Landscape and Irrigation Application (on file in the offices of the CAB) and Landscape
Verification Checklist must be updated and submitted for approval by the DRC any time
15 percent or more of the irrigated area is being modified.
(d)

for Indoor and Outdoor Water Demand Initiatives (on file in the offices of the CAB)
to be delivered to the CAB prior to conveyance of the Lot or Lots that are the subject
of such certification to an Owner.
(e)
The landscape water demand will be calculated based on the water use for selected
vegetation, as noted on the Landscape Verification Checklist. High, moderate, and
low water use zones described in the Water Budget section will be considered.
(f)
High water use zones will include all irrigated turf, vegetables, fruits/vines, annual
beds, and water features including water fountains. All other approved plantings are
considered medium and low water users.
(g)
Plantings must be selected from the recommended Plant List contained in Section 9-231 , or approved by the DRC. Planting native grasses, flowers, shrubs, and trees that
produce seeds, nectar, fruit and nuts is encouraged to attract birds to the property.
(h)
The DRC will only respond to requests made in writing. The DRC review process is more
fully set forth in the Rules and Regulations.
(i)
The CAB reserves the right to require changes to landscape plans that are outside
normal parameters.

documents.title: Sec. 9-74. - Waste of water prohibited.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
path: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
documents.text:
(a)
Waste of water is prohibited at Sterling Ranch, as defined by noncompliance with this
article or any of the following measures:
(1)
Water shall be used only for beneficial purposes and shall not be wasted. Prohibited
water waste includes, but is not limited to:
a.
Applying more water than is reasonably necessary to establish and maintain a healthy
landscape. Routine watering of turf shall be limited to three days per week, except
for watering during the Establishment Period. Car washing is permitted; however, water
is not to be wasted and allowed to run into the flow line of the curb. An outside
hose with a shut-off mechanism must be used so that water does not continue to run
during non-wash or non-rinse activities. Water used for this purpose is part of the
outdoor Water Budget.
b.
Watering with spray irrigation between the hours of 10:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m. during
the period from May 1 to September 30, except for the following uses:
1.
Watering during the Establishment Period.
2.
Watering new plant material such as flowers, trees and shrubs on the day of planting.
3.
Watering essential to preserve turf subject to heavy pedestrian use.
4.
Operating an irrigation system for installation, repair or reasonable maintenance,
so long as the system is attended throughout the period of operation.
c.
Continuous irrigation to any area resulting in ponding or pooling of water or runoff
of water not absorbed into the ground or soil which flows away from the area being
irrigated.
d.
Failure to repair any irrigation system that is leaking.
e.
Excessive application of water intended for irrigation to an impervious surface, such
as a street, parking lot, sidewalk, or driveway or using water to wash down outdoor
impermeable surfaces. Periodic cleaning of streets, parking lots, sidewalks, decks,
patios, driveways, or windows, etc., is allowed as long as such cleaning does not
become excessive, and will count against the annual Water Budget.
f.
Letting water run unrestricted from a hose or faucet to drainage.
g.
Any unapproved usage of reclaimed water.
h.
Watering landscaped areas during rain or high wind.
i.
Washing vehicles with a hose that lacks an automatic shut-off valve.
(2)
Violations of the foregoing prohibitions will subject the Owner to additional fees
and fines, in accordance with a fee schedule and fine schedule adopted by the CAB.
In addition, the CAB shall also have the power to require continuing violators to
install a flow restrictor or suffer termination of outdoor water service, at the CAB's
discretion.
(b)

These prohibitions on water waste are not related to drought response, insufficient

a.
Maintenance or testing of an irrigation system can be performed at any time, provided
there is active observation of a zone while it is operating, and each zone is turned
off prior to leaving the location.
b.
Hand watering is allowed at any time with a hand-held hose with an attachment such
as a shut-off valve or water conserving method such as a drip, trickle, micro-spray,
or deep root watering system.

Car washing is allowed at any time. If a hose is used, rather than a bucket, it must
also be equipped with a shut-off device that prevents uninterrupted water flow.

Additional Outdoor Water Restrictions may be implemented by the CAB, including, but
not limited to, day-of-week limits, additional limits on hours of watering, and/or

In the event these Restrictions are violated, fees assessed and actions taken are

documents.title: Sec. 9-125. - Water budget.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
path: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
documents.text:
(a)
The indoor water budget per single-family residence is a combination of usage factors.
New owners are provided with a base rate of 8,000 gallons per month. In April of each
year, indoor water use will be totaled from the previous December, January, and February,
and then averaged. This is called the Average Winter Consumption ("AWC"). The AWC
is then your Tier 1 water rate for the next 12 months. The Interior Water Budget is
adjusted annually in April based on the AWC for each year. This allows for changes
in family circumstances to vary each year and still meet Tier 1 requirements.
(b)
For single-family residences, the Tier 1 minimum threshold is 4,000 gallons/month
and the maximum is 6,000 gallons/month. For example, if the owner's AWC is less than
4,000 gallons/month, Tier 1 is zero to 4,000 gallons/month. If the AWC is over 6,000
gallons/month, Tier 1 is zero to 6,000 gallons/month. Volume rates are applied to
actual monthly usage. Accounts without an AWC history will be assigned 6,000 gallons/month
as an initial AWC.
(c)
For multifamily residences, the Tier 1 minimum threshold is 3,500 gallons/month and
the maximum is 5,500 gallons. For example, if the owner's AWC is less than 3,500 gallons/month,
Tier 1 is zero to 3,500 gallons/month. If the AWC is over 5,500 gallons/month, Tier
1 is zero to 5,500 gallons/month. Volume rates are applied to actual monthly usage.
Accounts without an AWC history will be assigned 5,500 gallons per month as an initial
AWC.
(d)
When a home is sold to a new owner, the Interior Water Budget cycle starts over with
a base rate of 6,000 gallons per month until the next full AWC can be established.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(1), § V(2))

documents.text:
The residential outdoor specifications contained in this subdivision apply to the
entire landscaped area of a Lot. Builders are required to design and install landscaping
and irrigation systems in the front yard. The "front yard" is defined as the Tree
Lawn, including any Tree Lawn on a corner lot wherein the Tree Lawn on the street
side of the Lot is not owned or maintained by the CAB or other entity, and the portion
of the Lot from the sidewalk to the edge of the residence and to the edge of the wing
and side lot (for corner lots) fence. Builders are not required to design and install
landscaping and irrigation systems in the back yard; however, Builders must make landscape
and irrigation plans for each model home type, as well as installation services, available
to home buyers as an optional upgrade. Owners electing to design and install landscaping
and irrigation systems on their Lot by themselves are required to follow all requirements
in this division, except for those related to professional registration. All hose
bibbs must be connected to the irrigation system, not the indoor water system, so
that water usage from a hose bibb is considered a part of the outdoor water budget.
Following BMPs for low water use landscaping and gardening is strongly recommended,
as found on the GreenCO website: http://www.greenco.org/.
(Rules of 11-18-2020, § 3.3.1)

documents.title: Sec. 9-143. - Water budget.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
path: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
documents.text:
(a)
Customized Water Budgets are provided to allow flexibility to meet individual landscaping
styles while still achieving water usage reductions. Water Budgets are based on lot
size; larger lots have higher Water Budgets than smaller lots. Water rates and billings
are based on the Water Budget for a given Lot, so it is critical for the installed
landscape and irrigation system to be capable of supporting a healthy landscape within
the Water Budget.
(b)
The total Water Budget for a given Lot size is shown in Table 9-1 set forth in subsection (c) of this section. Note the Lot size does not include the
Right-of-Way (ROW)/Tree Lawn area between sidewalks and streets; however, the Water
Budget for the lot applies to the entire landscape area including the ROW/Tree Lawn.
(1)
Dominion and/or the CAB are required to, and have implemented, tiered water use rate
structures that provide for increased rates for water consumption. Outdoor water use
in excess of the water budgets set forth in this section may result in significant
increases in utility charges. Builders are required to educate home buyers on Sterling
Ranch's water use rate structure and clearly identify the water budget remaining for
portions of the landscape not installed by the builder.
(2)
The First Tier of Fee rate per 1,000 gallons applies to the use of up to 100 percent
of the customer's Water Budget. The Tier Fee rate per 1,000 gallons for use over 100
percent of the Water Budget increases based upon the amount over 100 percent that
is used by that customer. Notwithstanding the tiered rate structure, water used during
the Establishment Period shall be billed at the First Tier fee rate. In addition,
the amount of water delivered during the Establishment Period shall not count against
the Water Budget.
(c)
Water budget standards.
(1)
Outdoor Water Budgets are based on lot size. Larger lots have higher Water Budgets
than smaller lots do. The total Water Budget by lot size is shown in Table 9-1 . Good landscape and irrigation design will support a healthy landscape within the
limits of the Water Budget. Please note the lot size does NOT include the Tree Lawn.
Tree Lawns are technically rights-of-way and are not included in the square footage
of a lot. However, the Water Budget applies to the ENTIRE landscaped area, including
the Tree Lawn.
(2)
Steward
TM
, your home automation system, is connected to the water meters in your home, and
can show your water use in real time. This allows you to monitor where you are in
relation to your Water Budget.
(3)

documents.title: Sec. 9-144. - Soil amendment and mulch.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
path: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
documents.text:
(a)
Prior to the installation of plant materials and/or the beginning of landscape improvements
beyond soil preparation, a minimum of four cubic yards of soil amendment per 1,000
square feet of landscaped area must be applied over the existing ground surface and
rototilled to a depth of at least six inches. The soil amendment itself must be a
combination of ground-aged manure and organic compost. The graded site shall be free
of rock, debris, and dirt clods over three-quarter inch in diameter. Existing topsoil
should be salvaged and stockpiled for use as soil amendments or topsoil.
(b)
All exposed soil shall be covered with mulch at a rate of one cubic yard per 80 square
feet, or a depth of three inches, and as appropriate to each species. Inorganic mulches
such as rock, pebbles, and gravel shall have a minimum depth of two inches; rock mulch
of 1½ inches in diameter is preferred. Preferred mulch materials are described in
the Landscaping Standards. Bird-friendly landscapes can be encouraged by avoiding
the use of mulch or weed barrier, and instead opting for the use of pea gravel with
larger "squeegee"-size rock, which provides improved oxygenation and infiltration.
(Rules of 11-18-2020, § 3.3.5)

documents.title: Sec. 9-145. - Completion/installation dates.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
path: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
documents.text:
(a)
Front yard landscaping must be completed by the Builder no later than 30 days after
the issuance of CO or a Temporary CO on a residential unit, with the following exception:
A winter deferral period is granted for closings, TCOs, or COs that have been issued
from November 1 to April 30. Builders have a grace period of 30 days (until May 31)
to catch up and complete landscaping on homes closed, TCOs, COs that have been issued
during the winter deferral period.
(b)
Rear yard landscaping must be completed within 120 days after closing, with the following
exception: A winter deferral period is granted from November 1 to April 30. The 120-day
completion window begins on the day of closing, a TCO, or a CO has been issued. This
completion window is suspended during the deferral period, and begins again on May
1.
(Rules of 11-18-2020, § 3.3.7)

documents.title: Sec. 9-146. - Landscape maintenance standards.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
path: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
documents.text:
(a)
All landscaping is to be kept healthy. Generally, this means the following rules are
applicable:
(1)
Turf is mowed and does not exceed four inches in height;
(2)
Planting beds, driveways, sidewalks, and turf areas are weed free;
(3)
Turf is green and has been treated to prevent weed growth;
(4)
Dead branches are pruned out of shrubs and trees; dead plants are removed and disposed
of properly; dead trees must be replaced;
(5)
Trees are maintained in a natural shape after pruning;
(6)
Insect infestations are treated quickly and effectively to prevent spreading.
(b)
Plantings on corner lots must meet safety requirements for Sight Triangles. If plants
are not located on that portion of the Lot outside of the Sight Triangle, then branches
are to be removed up to an eight-foot height on trees, and shrubs shall be trimmed
so as to not exceed three feet in height.
(c)
Trees in Tree Lawns, as they grow towards maturity, are required to have branches
removed up to eight feet above the ground. This provides an open visual corridor so
pedestrians can be seen on walks or crossing the street. Tree Lawns are expected to
be maintained in the same configuration as when planted by the Builder. Any variance
to this configuration must be submitted to the DRC and specific approval received.
(d)
Irrigation systems shall be maintained to ensure proper operation and function for
water use efficiency.
(e)
A regular maintenance schedule shall include, but not be limited to, routine inspection,
auditing, adjustment and repair of the irrigation system and its components. Operation
of the irrigation system outside the normal watering window is allowed for auditing
and system maintenance.
(f)
Repair of all irrigation equipment shall be done with the originally installed components.
If equipment components with greater efficiency are used in replacement, the entire
zone must be changed to maintain consistency.
(Rules of 11-18-2020, § 3.3.8)

documents.title: Sec. 9-147. - Outdoor water features.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
path: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
documents.text:
(a)
Swimming pools and other water features. Owners wishing to install a swimming pool or other water feature (e.g., a fountain
or pond) holding in excess of 3,000 gallons of water must pay a Pool Tap Fee as set
forth in this Code. Upon the payment thereof and the provision of written notice to
the CAB Manager, an Owner will be allowed to clean and fill the pool at the First
Tier Fee rate, and the water delivered in the billing cycle in which the pool is cleaned
and filled shall not be counted against the Water Budget. Pool covers are recommended
when not in use to reduce evaporation.
(b)
Hot tub or spa. Water used to fill and clean a hot tub or spa will be counted as part of the Water
Budget. It is strongly recommended that the fixture be covered when not in use to
reduce evaporation.
(c)
Fountains, ponds, and artificial streams. Water features must be recirculating. Subject to the provisions of subsection (a),
water used to fill, clean, and re-fill these facilities will be counted as part of
the Water Budget.
(Rules of 11-18-2020, § 3.3.4.4)

documents.title: Sec. 9-160. - General irrigation requirements.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
path: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
documents.text:
(a)
Manual shut-off valves (such as a gate valve, ball valve, or butterfly valve) shall
be required, as close as possible to the point of connection of the water supply and
to isolate sections of mainline on larger systems, to minimize water loss in case
of an emergency (such as a main line break) or routine repair.
(b)
Designs should utilize state-of-the-art water-efficient irrigation technologies such
as precision spray heads, rotary nozzles, and pressure-compensating drip systems.
(c)
Spray sprinkler bodies shall be WaterSense labeled.
(d)
Irrigation systems shall be hydrozoned, meaning that plantings with similar water
demands shall be grouped by irrigation zone (e.g., a single zone cannot be used to
irrigate high and moderate use plantings).
(e)
Overhead irrigation is not allowed in areas less than eight feet in width, or on slopes
greater than 4:1. Drip or other subsurface irrigation is required in these narrow
and steep areas.
(f)
Large Subsurface drip irrigation systems are cautioned against in large irrigated
turf areas on residential lots due to the need for more active management.
(g)
In general, only turf grass and native species may have overhead irrigation. Trees,
shrubs, perennials, and groundcovers shall be irrigated with a form of drip technology.
(h)
If an irrigation system is installed in a multifamily building, the system shall be
independently metered, submetered, or equipped with an alternate technology capable
of tracking water used for outdoor irrigation.
(Rules of 11-18-2020, § 3.3.6.1)

documents.title: Sec. 9-161. - Irrigation system design.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
path: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
documents.text:
(a)
Pop-up or rotor heads shall utilize high efficiency spray nozzles designed with head-to-head
coverage. This may include conventional rotors, stream rotators or high efficiency
pop-up spray nozzles.
(b)
Backflow prevention devices shall be required to protect the potable water supply
from contamination by the irrigation system and comply with local plumbing codes.
(c)
Irrigation systems shall be designed and installed to achieve a distribution uniformity
of 0.75.
(d)
Pop-up spray height shall be consistent with the mature height of the plant material,
and shall be a minimum of six inches in height.
(e)
Sprinkler bodies shall have built-in pressure regulating stems and check valves.
(f)
Maximum spacing for sprinkler heads to be head-to-head at 90 percent of the maximum
spray radius.
(g)
Turf areas shall use pop-up spray heads on areas 25 feet wide or less and may use
a combination of pop-up spray and short-to medium range rotors in areas greater than
25 feet wide.
(h)
Traditional fixed and variable arc spray nozzles are not allowed.
(i)
Pop-up spray heads cannot be zoned together with rotator or rotor heads.
(j)
Drip or other subsurface irrigation systems shall be used in all shrub bed areas,
with the following minimum requirements:
(1)
Pressure compensating emitters.
(2)
Pressure regulation at the control valve assembly (minimum of 30 psi, maximum 40 psi).
(3)
Filtration at the control valve assembly (minimum 200 mesh).
(Rules of 11-18-2020, § 3.3.6.2)

documents.title: Sec. 9-162. - Irrigation controllers.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
path: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
documents.text:
(a)
WaterSense certified irrigation controllers that are compatible with the Siemens Desigo
TM
CC system are mandated. Smart controllers must be either weather based (ET) or soil-moisture
based, that automatically adjust irrigation in response to changes in plants' needs
as weather conditions change.
(b)
Weather-based (ET) controllers without integral rain sensors or communication systems
that account for local rainfall shall have a separate wired or wireless rain sensor
which connects or communicates with the controller.
(c)
Soil-moisture based controllers are not required to have rain sensors.
(d)
Controllers shall have a minimum of three programs or schedules and minimum of three
start times per schedule or program.
(e)
Controllers shall be specified on landscape plan submittals in order to be approved
by the CAB.
(Rules of 11-18-2020, § 3.3.6.3)

documents.title: Sec. 9-174. - Submittal required.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
path: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
documents.text:
(a)
Landscape and irrigation plans for each residence at Sterling Ranch must be submitted
for review and approval by the DRC. Each application for plan review shall be accompanied
by the review fee established by the DRC from time to time. The DRC, in its discretion,
may waive fees for the review of plans submitted on behalf of one applicant for multiple
systems of similar configuration to be installed by the applicant.
(b)
Builders are encouraged to submit landscape and irrigation plans for non-custom homes
(e.g., model or tract), for both front and rear yards, to the DRC for pre-approval
to expedite the review process.
(c)
Owners electing not to purchase a preapproved rear yard completion plan from the Builder
are required to submit a detailed landscape and irrigation plan to the DRC, and pay
the required fees on file in the offices of the CAB.
(Rules of 11-18-2020, § 3.3.4.1)

documents.title: Sec. 9-175. - Submittal requirements.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
path: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
documents.text:
(a)
A Builder or Owner, as part of the Landscape and Irrigation Application, must submit
the Landscape Verification Checklist to the DRC to ensure that the water demand of
the landscape plan complies with the Water Budget provided.
(b)
A Builder must submit the completed Landscape Verification Checklist (on file in the
offices of the CAB) for the area being installed by such Builder. A maximum of 30
percent of the total Water Budget may be utilized for the front yard and Right-of-Way
to ensure that an adequate Water Budget remains to landscape the backyard.
(c)
The Landscape and Irrigation Application (on file in the offices of the CAB) and Landscape
Verification Checklist (on file in the offices of the CAB) must be updated and submitted
for approval by the DRC any time 15 percent or more of the irrigated area is being
modified.
(d)
The landscape water demand will be calculated based on the water use for selected
vegetation, as noted on the Landscape Verification Checklist (on file in the offices
of the CAB). Three water use zones (high, moderate, and low) will be considered.
(e)
High water use zones will include all irrigated turf, vegetables, fruits/vines, annual
beds, and water features including hot tubs and water fountains. All other approved
plantings are considered medium and low water users.
(f)
Plantings must be selected from the recommended Plant List contained in section 9-231 , or approved by the DRC. Planting native grasses, flowers, shrubs, and trees that
produce seeds, nectar, fruit and nuts is encouraged to attract birds to the property.
(g)
Example landscape plans for common lot sizes are provided in section 9-233 , which also includes an example of a Transitional Zone.
(h)
The DRC will only respond to requests made in writing. The DRC review process is more
fully set forth in this Code.
(i)
The CAB reserves the right to require changes to landscape plans based on individual
Lot and home configurations that are outside normal parameters but do not qualify
as Icon or corner lots.
(Rules of 11-18-2020, § 3.3.4.2)

documents.title: Sec. 9-176. - Required landscape materials.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
path: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
documents.text:
(a)
Minimum front yard tree installation. Minimum tree installation for front yards:
(1)
The term "front yard" includes the area of a yard extending across the full width
of a lot between the front lot line of the lot and the front wing fence.
(2)
One deciduous tree (minimum two-inch caliper, measured six inches above ground);
(3)
One evergreen tree (minimum six feet in height); or one ornamental deciduous (minimum
1½-inch caliper); and
(4)
One street tree in tree lawn (minimum two-inch caliper, measured six-inches above
ground). Street tree designations are shown in the plant list contained in section 9-231 .
(5)
A variance may be granted to allow for one required front yard tree for smaller lot
product when irrigated area is restrictive.
(6)
Trees should be planted a minimum of three feet from concrete driveways and sidewalks,
four feet is preferred.
(b)
Rear yard landscaping. Rear yard landscaping also must include two trees:
(1)
The term "rear yard" includes the area of a yard extending across the full width of
a lot between the rear lot line of the lot up to the front wing fence.
(2)
One deciduous tree (minimum 1½-inch caliper, measured six-inches above ground); and
(3)
One evergreen tree (minimum six feet in height).
(4)
A variance may be granted to allow for one required rear yard tree for smaller lot
product when irrigated area is restrictive.
(c)
Wood planter boxes. No wood planter boxes are permitted in the front yard. See section 21-22 (b)(42), Gardens; vegetable, for additional requirements.
(d)
Artificial turf. Artificial turf will be considered for the front and/or the rear yard on a case-by-case
basis. Specific guidelines for artificial turf installation are provided in section 21-22 .
(Rules of 11-18-2020, § 3.3.4.3; Res. No.
2022-08-02
, § 1, 8-26-2022; Res. No.
2023-04-02
, § 1, 4-19-2023)

documents.title: Sec. 9-188. - Registration required.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
path: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
DIVISION 6. - LANDSCAPE AND IRRIGATION PROFESSIONAL REGISTRATION
documents.text:
(a)
Registration with the CAB is required to conduct the following residential landscape
and irrigation services within the boundaries of Sterling Ranch, whether installation
is by a builder or contracted for by an owner:
(1)
Landscape design;
(2)
Irrigation design;
(3)
Supervision of landscape or irrigation installation.
(b)
Registration requirements apply to individuals, not to companies or organizations.
The registered individual is responsible for all work completed on a project under
their supervision. Professional registrations may be granted via reciprocity to individuals
holding registrations in other Colorado municipalities, on a case-by-case basis as
deemed appropriate by the CAB. The CAB may delegate to the DRC all or any part of
the registration power and process described herein.
(Rules of 11-18-2020, § 3.3.2.1)

documents.title: Sec. 9-189. - Professional classifications.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
path: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
DIVISION 6. - LANDSCAPE AND IRRIGATION PROFESSIONAL REGISTRATION
documents.text:
(a)
Landscape design professional. To be qualified for registration as a Landscape Design Professional, an applicant
must demonstrate that they meet the requirements for landscape plan preparation by
providing current proof of professional qualifications. Colorado law governs the sizes
and types of projects that unlicensed individuals can design, and is independent from
this article. For those projects that are exempt from State licensure, a GreenCO Best
Management Practice Certificate of Completion is required before registration will
be issued by the CAB.
(b)
Irrigation design professional. To be qualified for registration as an Irrigation Design Professional, an applicant
must certify that they are qualified to prepare the type of plan submitted by providing
proof of their active professional qualifications. One of the following qualifications
is required to become registered as an Irrigation Design Professional:
(1)
Irrigation Association (IA) Certified Irrigation Designer (CID);
(2)
Qualified Water Efficient Landscaper (QWEL) Certified Professional;
(3)
Registered Professional Civil Engineer (PE);
(4)
Licensed Landscape Architect (LA) with a minimum of five years of demonstrable irrigation
design experience.
(c)
Landscape and irrigation installation and maintenance professional. To be qualified for registration as a Landscape/Irrigation Installation and Maintenance
Professional, an applicant must certify that they are qualified to install and maintain
landscape and irrigation systems, by providing proof of their active professional
qualifications. One of the following qualifications is required to become registered
as a Landscape and Irrigation Installation and Maintenance Professional:
(1)
IA Certified Irrigation Contractor (CIC);
(2)
Qualified Water Efficient Landscaper (QWEL) Certified Professional;
(3)
Associated Landscape Contractors of Colorado (ALCC) Certified Landscape Technician
(CLT);
(4)
GreenCO Best Management Practice Certification of Completion;
(5)
Additional industry-related certification or registration as approved by the CAB.
(Rules of 11-18-2020, § 3.3.2.2)

documents.title: Sec. 9-190. - Registration process, expiration, and renewal.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
path: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
DIVISION 6. - LANDSCAPE AND IRRIGATION PROFESSIONAL REGISTRATION
Sec. 9-190. - Registration process, expiration, and renewal.
documents.text:
(a)
Applications for registration as a Professional shall be made by filing completed
Applications for Registration of Landscape Professional (on file in the offices of
the CAB). All information requested on the application shall be provided. Failure
to provide required information may result in non-issuance or revocation of registration.
Each application shall be accompanied by the registration fee relative to the type
of registration being sought. The applicant will be notified of approval or denial
of registration within 30 days of submitting a fully completed application, including
all required supporting materials.
(b)
It is the responsibility of the registered professional to promptly inform the CAB
of any change in the registrant's contact information or registration status. All
registrations are valid for a period of three years. Registration renewals for professionals
in good standing may be issued upon receipt of acknowledgment of revisions to policies,
criteria, or other applicable codes. Noncompliance with this article may deem an applicant
ineligible for renewal.
(Rules of 11-18-2020, § 3.3.2.3)

documents.title: Sec. 9-191. - Denial, suspension, revocation, or restriction of registration.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
path: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
DIVISION 6. - LANDSCAPE AND IRRIGATION PROFESSIONAL REGISTRATION
Sec. 9-191. - Denial, suspension, revocation, or restriction of registration.
documents.text:
(a)
Authority. The CAB shall have the authority to deny, suspend, revoke, or place restrictions
on a registration under any of the following circumstances:
(1)
False or misleading information was provided on the registration application or permit
application.
(2)
The applicant or registrant fails to provide reasonable information or documentation
of knowledge and experience required by the registration classification applied for.
(3)
The registrant provides false or misleading information on permit applications.
(4)
The registrant fails to comply with the Design Guidelines or the Rules and Regulations.
(5)
The registrant knowingly allows the registrant's registration to be used by another
person, firm, or corporation.
(6)
The registrant commits any conduct constituting fraud in or connected with any activity
relating to construction that is governed by the Design Guidelines or the Rules and
Regulations.
(7)
The registrant fails or refuses to correct or remove work, material, equipment, or
appliances that are in violation of the Design Guidelines or the Rules and Regulations.
(8)
The registrant provides false or misleading permit fee charges to a customer or to
the CAB.
(b)
Procedure. When the CAB deems that such registration shall be denied, suspended, revoked or
restricted, the procedures set forth below shall be followed:
(1)
The applicant or registrant shall be notified in writing and by certified mail, at
least seven calendar days prior to the denial, suspension, revocation or restriction.
Notice shall include the reason for the action and shall be delivered to the address
of record.
(2)
The applicant or registrant may request a hearing in accordance with the procedures
set forth for variances in this Code. Such hearing shall be conducted, and the findings
thereof reported, in accordance with the procedures set forth for variances in this
Code.
(3)
Any decision rendered by the CAB shall take effect immediately.
(c)
Emergency suspension. If the CAB finds that an emergency cause exists for suspension or revocation of a
registration, it may enter an order for immediate suspension of such registration,
pending further investigation. The registrant, upon notice of such suspension, may
request an immediate hearing before the CAB.
(d)
Period of suspension. The suspension of a registration shall be for the period stated in the suspension,
but no longer than six months.
(e)
Effect of revocation. If a registration is revoked, the applicant shall not be eligible to register with
the CAB for a period of six months after the revocation.
(f)

DIVISION 7. - INSPECTIONS, WATERSMART HOME CERTIFICATION AND RE-SALE AUDITS
documents.text:
The CAB has developed the following procedure to assess compliance with the water
demand management measures outlined in this article:
(1)
Indoor water demand management certification. Each Builder shall certify to the CAB that all homes being constructed by the builder
are in compliance with the general and indoor specifications outlined in Sections 9-100 and 9-124 .
(2)
Outdoor water demand management certification.
a.
The Builder and/or Owner, or their designated landscape and irrigation professional,
shall certify to the CAB that the landscape and irrigation systems are in compliance
with the outdoor specifications outlined in division 3 of this article.
b.
The responsible party (Builder or Owner) is required to submit detailed information
to the DRC that verifies the landscape and irrigation systems meet or exceed the outdoor
residential specifications. A sample Verification Checklist is provided in the offices
of the CAB.
c.
The Builder must include the Verification Checklist in the packet provided to Owners
as part of the education requirements outlined in Section 9-101 .
(3)
New construction inspection program and inspection fees.
a.
Landscape and irrigation plans for every residential lot shall be submitted to the
DRC for review and approval as described above in division 3, subdivision III, of
this article. The plan review and approval process is a component of the inspection
program. Builders are encouraged to submit plans for non-custom homes (e.g., model
and tract), for both front and rear yards, to the DRC for pre-approval to expedite
the review process.
b.
A sampling program will be used to inspect non-custom homes that are constructed by
an approved Builder. All inspection fees shall be paid by the Builder for landscape
installed by the Builder. The DRC, in its discretion, may waive fees for the inspection
of multiple systems installed by Builders in accordance with preapproved plans and/or
of similar configuration.
1.
Three of the first seven homes or units constructed by a Builder shall be inspected.
2.
After three of the first seven homes or units are inspected and approved, the DRC
will randomly select one home or unit for sampling, as determined by the DRC and/or
the CAB.
3.
Unless otherwise determined by the DRC upon the request of a Builder or Owner, a formal
inspection to assess compliance with this article, to be paid for by the Builder or
Owner at the fee rate therefor established by the DRC (provided that the DRC may waive
fees for the inspection of multiple systems of similar configuration installed by

(i)

c.
When an inspection is required in any of the foregoing instances, a two-step inspection
process will be completed to ensure that landscape and irrigation installations are
consistent with the approved plans. The applicable fee shall include both inspections.
1.
The first inspection shall be prior to the installation of plant material to document
adherence to the soil amendment and tilling requirements.
2.
The second inspection will be completed within the Establishment Period to document
that the installed landscape is consistent with the approved plan and that the irrigation
system functions properly.
d.
The CAB will utilize metered water use data and analytical techniques to assess ongoing
compliance with the indoor and outdoor water budgets.
e.
The CAB reserves the right to revise the sampling program and/or institute additional
inspection requirements at any time.
f.
Every Builder for every lot shall cause a completed and executed Builder certification
for Indoor and Outdoor Water Demand Initiatives to be delivered to the CAB prior to
conveyance of the Lot or Lots that are the subject of such certification to an Owner.
(4)
Remodel inspection program. Owners are required to submit plans for remodeling or addition of outdoor water-using
features to the DRC for review and approval. Any landscape remodeling in excess of
15 percent must also be submitted to DRC for review and approval.
(Rules of 11-18-2020, § 3.5.1)

documents.title: Sec. 9-208. - Watersmart home design standards.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
path: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
DIVISION 7. - INSPECTIONS, WATERSMART HOME CERTIFICATION AND RE-SALE AUDITS
documents.text:
All residences in compliance with the residential indoor and outdoor water demand
management criteria listed in this article meet the CAB's watersmart home design standards.
Compliance shall be achieved prior to occupancy for indoor water use and shall be
sustained thereafter, and outdoor water use compliance is to be established and sustained
subject to the provisions of section 9-145 .
(Rules of 11-18-2020, § 3.5.2)

documents.title: Sec. 9-209. - Voluntary audit.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
path: ARTICLE II. - WATER DEMAND MANAGEMENT INITIATIVES
DIVISION 7. - INSPECTIONS, WATERSMART HOME CERTIFICATION AND RE-SALE AUDITS
documents.text:
Upon request of an Owner, including in connection with the re-sale of the Owner's
home, and payment of such fee therefor as may be established from time to time, the
CAB and/or DRC shall perform an audit to verify the presence and continued operation
of water demand management measures and determine if the home does not meet, meets
or exceeds the CAB's watersmart home design standards.
(Rules of 11-18-2020, § 3.5.3)

documents.title: Sec. 9-251. - Plant material and water demand overview; predetermined water budgets.
documents.article: ARTICLE III. - WATER-WISE TREE LAWN GUIDELINES AT PROVIDENCE VILLAGE
path: ARTICLE III. - WATER-WISE TREE LAWN GUIDELINES AT PROVIDENCE VILLAGE
Sec. 9-251. - Plant material and water demand overview; predetermined water budgets.
documents.text:
(a)
An essential component of natural resource stewardship and responsible water management
is specifying a significant portion of plant material that is native, naturalized,
or adapted to the semi-arid high plains prairie ecosystem in which Providence Village
is located. By incorporating the native or naturalized plantings of this geographic
region in a way that meets the aesthetic character of the community, tree lawns in
Providence Village can be a showcase of water demand management and a successful blending
of nature and development. Tree lawns by definition refer to the landscape area between
the sidewalk and street-curb.
(b)
Customized water budgets have been predetermined for varying lot sizes in Providence
Village. There is flexibility in using these water budgets to meet individual landscaping
styles. For example, tree lawns planted with shrubs, grasses, and perennials and irrigated
with a drip system will have a lower water demand than the same area planted entirely
with turf and irrigated with a spray system. The water savings from the tree lawns
can be applied towards additional planting elsewhere in the front yard or backyard
landscape.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(7))

documents.title: Sec. 9-253. - Sample tree lawn plans.
documents.article: ARTICLE III. - WATER-WISE TREE LAWN GUIDELINES AT PROVIDENCE VILLAGE
path: ARTICLE III. - WATER-WISE TREE LAWN GUIDELINES AT PROVIDENCE VILLAGE
documents.text:
The following Sample Tree Lawn Plans illustrate a matrix of landscape design alternatives
for tree lawns arranged by relative amounts of water use. The sample water use calculations
provided are based on a typical 6,600-square-foot corner lot with a water budget of
32,000 gallons per season. (Actual water usage will vary from lot to lot based on
lot shape and the size of the home, driveways, patios, etc.) The Sample Plans for
which the water use calculations are provided all have the same front yard and backyard
landscape design. Only the treatment of the tree lawn changes with each alternative
to demonstrate how the different tree lawn treatments work within the overall water
budget for the lot. While four of these six sample tree lawn plans are offered to
the user as a kit of tools, two have been provided to illustrate tree lawn plans that
are not encouraged. Sterling Ranch encourages the implementation of some plans over
others to balance the goals of conserving water and creating an aesthetically pleasing
tree lawn.
Tree Lawn Alternative
(1)
The 'perennial border.' This tree lawn design essentially substitutes all of the turf typically found in
a tree lawn with low water use perennials, grasses, and shrubs. The planting in this
approach takes advantage of vertical layering and massing that virtually fills the
tree lawn. Plantings consist of spreading groundcovers and a densely planted mix of
low water use shrubs, grasses, and perennials; reminiscent of a perennial border garden.
(2)
Planting bed with turf accents. This alternative can be thought of as a toned-down version of the Perennial Border.
Approximately 75 percent of the tree lawn is comprised of planting beds with groundcovers,
shrubs, grasses and perennials, and it is accented with panels of turf (approximately
25 percent of the tree lawn).
(3)
The half and half. This tree lawn alternative is a 50/50 split of manicured turf and planting beds.
As in the previous alternatives where plant material is incorporated into the tree
lawn, the wood or rock mulch below is essentially covered by grouping plants together
or by using spreading groundcovers. In some instances plant height is vertically layered
and a variety of texture and color is provided; in others, a single type of ground
cover creates a clean, unifying ground plane.
(4)
Turf with planting bed accents. This tree lawn design is essentially a reverse of the Planting Bed with Turf Accent
treatment. The tree lawn is comprised of approximately 75 percent manicured lawn,

documents.title: Sec. 9-253. - Sample tree lawn plans.
documents.article: ARTICLE III. - WATER-WISE TREE LAWN GUIDELINES AT PROVIDENCE VILLAGE
path: ARTICLE III. - WATER-WISE TREE LAWN GUIDELINES AT PROVIDENCE VILLAGE
documents.text:
punctuated with planting beds (approximately 25 percent of the tree lawn area).
(5)
The typical (not encouraged). This alternative reflects what one would see in the majority of suburban neighborhoods
across Colorado; tree lawns comprised completely of turf. While this treatment is
certainly typical for the State, the Sterling Ranch community encourages forward-thinking
landscape designs that reallocate the large water resource normally spent on turf
in tree lawns to more functional areas in the front and backyards of our homes. A
tree lawn comprised of all turf is not an encouraged tree lawn treatment.
(6)
The rock mulch minimum (not encouraged). While this approach achieves the lowest water use of all the alternatives presented,
it does not meet the desired community aesthetic and, as such, it is not an encouraged
tree lawn treatment. While this approach may technically meet the minimum design requirement
to break up continuous mulch areas greater than eight feet in width, it still exposes
large spans of uninterrupted rock mulch which can have a detrimental effect on the
intended community aesthetic, particularly if the same treatment is applied across
numerous adjacent lots.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(7))

(a)
It goes without saying that the most intensive water using alternative is one that
is not encouraged, The Typical, which would use an estimated 38,180 gallons of water
per year. The second highest water using alternative at 35,072 gallons per year is
the Turf with Planting Bed Accents. Both of these designs as shown exceed the 32,000-gallon
water budget for the lot. Reduced planting and/or turf area in the front and backyards
or the use of artificial turf in the rear yard would be needed to bring the landscape
into conformance with the budget.
(b)
The other tree lawn alternatives (The Perennial Border, The Half & Half, Planting
Bed with Turf Accents) all are within the 32,000-gallon water budget and are encouraged
tree lawn design alternatives at Sterling Ranch. The Rock Mulch Minimum is the lowest
water using tree lawn alternative; however, it does not achieve the secondary goal
of creating an aesthetically pleasing tree lawn. Unlike the design approaches above
that use spreading groundcovers or a mix of layered and massed plant materials, The
Rock Mulch Minimum exposes large spans of uninterrupted rock mulch which, when compounded
over the length of a street block, can create an undesirable aesthetic effect.

documents.text:
CAB Community Facilities include the Sterling Center, Parks, Open Space, Clubhouses
and Pools. The following Fees and Charges shall apply to the use and rental of those
Facilities subject to the Facilities Rules and Regulations:
(1)
CAB Clubhouse and Pool Membership Fees.
a.
CAB residents. Individuals who own or have as their primary residence property that is within the
boundaries of one of the Sterling Ranch Colorado Metropolitan Districts Nos. 1—7 shall
not be assessed any fees for use of the Clubhouse or Pool.
b.
Nonresident members. Individuals who do not own or have as their primary residence property that is within
the boundaries of one of the Sterling Ranch Colorado Metropolitan Districts Nos. 1—7
do not pay for or support the operations and maintenance of the Clubhouse or Pool
and shall pay a Membership Fee in the following amounts reasonably calculated to offset
the costs of usage. In order to ensure the Clubhouse and Pool are not overused and
thereby damaged or degraded, total Nonresident Annual Memberships shall be limited
to 120:
Annual Membership, (up to 2 Individuals) .....$850.00
c.
Guest charges. The CAB Facilities Rules and Regulations set daily and annual limitations on the
number of guests CAB Residents may bring with them. Additional guest passes are available
for the following charge:
25 guest passes .....$100.00
d.
Caregiver membership passes. CAB Residents and Property Owners may obtain one caregiver pass per household for
a non-family member who provides caregiver services to the household. This pass permits
access only in conjunction with the supervision of minor children or dependents who
are otherwise permitted to use the Clubhouse or Pool:
Annual Child Care Provider Pass .....$300.00
e.
Replacement membership card fee. Any replacement membership cards are subject to a fee of $5.00.
(2)
Rental Charges and Fees. Certain CAB Facilities are available for reservation and rental as provided in Chapter 17 , Article IV. All fees and charges for rental shall be as specified in the CAB Facilities
Rules and Regulations.

facility rentals. Effective January 1, 2023, the rates for rentals shall be as follows

documents.article: ARTICLE I. - FEES AND FORMS RELATED TO FACILITIES, LANDSCAPING, WATER AND SEWERS
path: ARTICLE I. - FEES AND FORMS RELATED TO FACILITIES, LANDSCAPING, WATER AND SEWERS
documents.text:
(a)
Residential Facilities Fee. Residential Facilities Fees are to be paid on all residential property within the
Sterling Ranch Districts at or prior to the date of issuance of a building permit.
Residential Facilities Fees paid through December 31, 2022 are (i) $10,600.00 per
single-family attached and detached residential unit, and (ii) $9,300.00 per multifamily
residential unit, and thereafter as may be further adjusted by the Board. Effective
January 1, 2023, Residential Facilities Fees are due in the amount of (i) $11,130.00
per single-family attached and detached residential unit, and (ii) $9,765.00 per multifamily
residential unit.
(b)
Commercial Facilities Fee. Commercial Facilities Fees are to be paid on all commercial property within the Sterling
Ranch Districts at or prior to the date of issuance of a building permit. Commercial
property is any property that is zoned or planned for any use other than residential
property. Commercial Facilities Fees shall be assessed proportionately at the rate
of four times the rate of the applicable single-family detached Residential Facilities
Fee per acre at the time of building permit issuance.
(c)
Payment. All Facilities Fees shall be paid to the CAB. The CAB may impose penalties for noncompliance
as permitted by law. Upon collection of a Facilities Fee by the CAB and provision
of an adequate legal description of the subject property, the CAB shall cause a release
of its lien, applicable to the subject property. Without limiting the foregoing, a
late charge on any past-due amounts shall accrue from the date due at a rate of $150.00
per month, or up to five percent per month, not to exceed 25 percent of the amount
due, whichever is greater. Nothing herein shall prevent any party from prepaying a
Facilities Fee at any time with the consent of the CAB.
(d)
Modification. The Facilities Fee policy adopted herein and the rate thereof have been established
based on projected budgetary requirements of the CAB using various assumptions regarding
the cost of public improvements, bond issues and interest rates therefor, together
with operations expenses and maintenance expenses. Actual costs may differ from projections,
and the CAB may determine to modify the Facilities Fee imposed hereunder from time
to time.
(e)
Status as Lien/Foreclosure. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 32-1-1001(1)(j), the Facilities Fee shall, until paid, constitute
a perpetual lien on and against the property subjected to the Facilities Fee hereunder
from and after the date of adoption by the Board of Directors of the CAB, which lien

documents.text:
(a)
Voluntary energy usage, predictive analytics, and predictive billing services fees.
(1)
Customers who agree to share their energy usage information with the CAB will be given
predictive analytics on their energy usage patterns relative to the community, predictions
about anticipated monthly usage, and anticipated monthly energy bills.
(2)
The fee for predictive analytics for energy consumption is $12.00 per month.
(b)
Manually reading indoor and outdoor water meters.
(1)
Customers who do not have an Internet connection to the home, or chose not to have
the CAB's Water Meters, or chose not to connect their water meter to the Internet
will be subject to a monthly charge in order for a technician to manually read the
meters.
(2)
The fee for manual water meter reading is $25.00 per month.
(c)
Residential trash collection (excluding multi-family and commercial properties), recycling
and disposal charge. The CAB provides its residents with non-hazardous municipal solid waste residential
trash collection, recycling and disposal services. Effective January 1, 2023, the
Trash Collection, Recycling and Disposal Charge will be a fixed quarterly fee that
accompanies the water and sanitary charges and that will be invoiced to all residential
customers at the beginning of each quarter (January, April, July, and October). The

Sec. 13-72. - CAB maintenance of shared driveways and alleys.
documents.text:
Throughout the community CAB maintains certain shared driveway and alley improvements
that specifically serve individual homes or groups of homes. CAB maintenance obligations
include snow plowing as well as regular repair and replacement of these improvements
in order to ensure efficient and cost effective service to residents. However, the
work performed by CAB benefits these residents specifically and not the community
generally making it appropriate to charge a fee for the services provided and the
benefits received by the benefited lots. CAB shall set these fees based on the reasonable
costs of providing annual service and the expected long-term repair and replacement
costs.
(Res. No.
2022-10-03
, § 1, 10-19-2022)

documents.text:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the
meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates
a different meaning. Except as may be otherwise noted, all capitalized terms shall
have the meanings defined in the Utilities, Parks and Open Space regulations of the
Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board (the "CAB"), as may be amended and as set
forth in chapters 17 and 29 :
Applicant means the person or entity that files an Application.
Application means an application form, as designated by the Utility Director of the CAB to provide
the necessary information for evaluating water or sanitary sewer service. The party
filing the Application shall be the Applicant.
CAB and Dominion. All property and facilities owned by the CAB and Dominion Water & Sanitation District
("Dominion") shall be exempt from the payment of any and all Tap Fees described herein
for property and facilities in Sterling Ranch Filing No. 1 ("Filing 1"). For any property
and facilities owned by CAB and Dominion in any Filing other than Filing 1, Tap Fees
and all rates and charges described herein shall apply.
Customer means any person, firm, corporation, association or agency who is authorized, or
who desires to obtain services from the CAB and is a connector to or user of the CAB
Facilities.
General Manager means the Person designated as General Manager by the CAB Board, who administers
and supervises the affairs of and operations and maintenance of the facilities of
the CAB or the Person authorized by the CAB Board or the General Manager to act on
his behalf.
Hydrant Permit means a permit issued by the CAB for temporary construction water or temporary delivery
of nonpotable water. When applying for temporary delivery of nonpotable water for
use outside the CAB service area boundaries, applicants must, in writing, and as part
of the application:
(1)
Affirm that they are experiencing water supply circumstances constituting an emergency,
which may include but are not limited to failing wells;
(2)
Submit for the CAB's approval a plan to address their emergency circumstances after
their access to such water delivery is terminated, with such plans including an estimated
time frame for terminating use of the temporary nonpotable water;
(3)
Affirm that they will use such water delivery for existing uses only, not for any
new or expanded uses; and
(4)
Acknowledge that the permit allows for the delivery of temporary nonpotable water
and that the CAB makes no warranties, guarantees, or representations concerning the

A permit for water use outside the CAB service area boundaries shall be for a period
not to exceed three years and requires approval by the Board of Directors. All fees
and provisions herein concerning construction water shall also apply to temporary
delivery of nonpotable water.
Multifamily Residential Dwelling Unit Service means a residential dwelling unit located in a single structure containing three
or more residential dwelling units on a single lot.
Nonpotable Irrigation Service means service provided to any user who has been approved to use nonpotable water
for irrigation purposes by the CAB. The rate may be a result of either contracting
for use of nonpotable or reuse water.
Nonresidential Service means service to any nonresidential use, including, but not limited to, the following:
retail, office, hotel, motel, restaurant, service facility, manufacturing, warehouse,
recreation uses and various institutional uses such as museums, convention centers,
hospitals, schools, places of worship, etc. A separate meter is required for each
nonresidential structure requiring service. In order to be considered a single structure,
the structure must have a common foundation; a common wall; a common roof; and common
ownership. If any of the above is missing, the structure will be classified as multiple
structures and require payment of Tap Fees for each structure.
Residential Dwelling Unit means a structure or part of a structure containing one or more rooms and a single
kitchen arranged, designed and intended as a unit for occupancy by one family living
independently of others, including panelized, prefabricated, modular or other factory-produced
buildings and mobile homes; but excluding therefrom hotels and motels.
Sports Field Service means an area of turfgrass used and managed for organized sporting activities. The
CAB recognizes that sports fields experience significant usage outside of our normal
irrigation season of April 15 to October 15. These activities can require supplemental
irrigation water in order to keep fields in good condition and safe. Classification
as a Sports Field Customer will provide the customer with an annual irrigation budget
rather than a defined budget for each monthly billing cycle.
Sterling Ranch Districts means Sterling Ranch Colorado Metropolitan District Nos. 1 through 7.
Water Budget means the Budget established for water use by each customer service type as shown
in section 13-104 .
