documents.title: Sec. 13-105. - Water conservation measures.
documents.article: ARTICLE V. - UTILITY RATES, CHARGES AND RESTRICTIONS/WATER CONSERVATION MEASURES
path: ARTICLE V. - UTILITY RATES, CHARGES AND RESTRICTIONS/WATER CONSERVATION MEASURES
documents.text:
(a)
Water use. Consistent with the Water Demand Management Initiatives, as set forth in chapter 9 , article II, wasteful use of water is prohibited at all times. Examples of wasteful
water use include:
(1)
Excess water flowing in street gutters from irrigation or other outdoor uses.
(2)
Unrepaired leaks or fixture malfunctions that lead to excess water use.
(b)
Mandatory outdoor water restrictions. Consistent with the provisions of chapter 9 , article II, concerning Mandatory Outdoor Water Restrictions, the following restrictions
apply at all times:
(1)
Outdoor irrigation is prohibited between the hours of 10:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m. from
May 1 to September 30 with exception of prior approved daytime watering permits.
(2)
Operation of an irrigation system for maintenance is allowed at any time. Maintenance
is defined as actively observing an irrigation zone while it is operating to ensure
that it is functioning properly. A person must be visible at the location of the zone
while it is running. Each zone must be turned off prior to leaving the location and
not left running until the completion of a cycle.
(3)
Hand watering of landscape materials is allowed at any time. Hand watering is defined
as the application of irrigation from a hose held in the hand with a shut-off valve;
or a water-conserving method such as a drip, trickle, micro spray, deep root watering
device or watering can.
(4)
Car washing is allowed at any time. However, if water for car washing is coming from
a hose rather than a bucket, a hose end shut off device must be in use to prevent
uninterrupted water flow.
(c)
Changes to mandatory outdoor water restrictions. The Mandatory Outdoor Water Restrictions imposed by this Code may be changed at any
time by declaration of CAB Board of Directors at a regular or special board meeting.
Such changes may include, but are not limited to:
(1)
Mandatory day-of-week limits on irrigation.
(2)
Mandatory limits on the hours of watering.
(3)
Mandatory limits on the allowed run times of irrigation systems.
(4)
Mandatory prohibitions of all outdoor water use under severe water supply shortages.
(d)
Required water conservation devices.
(1)
The irrigation system of any Nonresidential Irrigation Customers (Nonresidential,
industrial, combination, governmental or HOA common area irrigation system) that receives
water from the CAB must be equipped with rain-sensing shut-off devices approved as
to number and type by the CAB.
(2)
All rain sensors shall be installed, adjusted and set as follows:
a.

documents.article: ARTICLE V. - UTILITY RATES, CHARGES AND RESTRICTIONS/WATER CONSERVATION MEASURES
path: ARTICLE V. - UTILITY RATES, CHARGES AND RESTRICTIONS/WATER CONSERVATION MEASURES
documents.text:
A surcharge may be charged to Customers that discharge wastewater with higher oxygen
demand or solids loadings than those found in typical domestic wastewater. These charges
will cover the additional costs incurred to treat the wastewater. The surcharge is
calculated using a formula specified below:
SC = V (8.34) [(AOD) x (UCo) + (TSS-300) x (UCs)]
SC = surcharge in dollars and cents
V = volume of wastewater discharged in units of million gallons
8.34 = conversion factor (gallons to pounds)
AOD = additional oxygen demand in units of milligrams per liter
UCo = cost of treating a pound of additional oxygen demand (AOD). The cost is $0.07
per pound of AOD.
TSS = total suspended solids in units of milligrams per liter. (Typical domestic wastewater
contains less than 300 mg/l TSS).
UCs = cost of treating a pound of total suspended solids (TSS) in dollars and cents.
The cost is $0.03 per pound of TSS.
Note: for use in the formula above, first determine if BOD (Biochemical Oxygen Demand)
or COD (Chemical Oxygen Demand) should be used in the determination of AOD by using
the following determination:
(1)
If the ratio of COD to BOD (as mg/l) is less than AOD = (BOD - 250) (Typical domestic
wastewater contains less than 250 mg/l BOD).
(2)
If the ratio of COD to BOD (as mg/l) is greater than or equal to 3.0, then AOD = (COD
- 500). (Typical domestic wastewater contains less than 500 mg/l COD).
(Rules of 8-26-2020(5))

path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
Sec. 17-21. - Applicability; rules supplemental to sign code, Master Declaration, and covenant enforcement.
documents.text:
These sign rules and regulations set forth herein apply to all properties managed
by the CAB and the adjacent road right-of-way. Temporary signs are any and all signs
that are not permanently installed. These rules are in addition to sign rules contained
in the Douglas County Sign Code, as may be amended, and sign rules adopted in the
Master Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions for Sterling Ranch Planned
Development, as may be amended, and the Sterling Ranch Rules and Regulations for Covenant
Enforcement, as set forth in chapter 1 , as may be amended.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § 13.1)

documents.title: Sec. 17-22. - Temporary sign rules.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.text:
(a)
Temporary sign categories and rules.
(1)
Private Citizen Event Signs. Temporary signs for private citizen events such as garage sales, open houses, and
religious services are permitted on the day of the event or as otherwise indicated
here.
(2)
Signs Advertising the Sale of Goods and Services. Signs advertising the sale of goods and services by businesses or other commercial
entities are not permitted.
(b)
Placement of temporary signs.
(1)
Temporary signs may be placed on landscaped areas or on sidewalks as long as they
are not compromising the safety of pedestrians or motorists. Temporary signs of any
kind, as defined above, are prohibited on medians.
(2)
Temporary signs cannot be placed within 150 feet of intersections of four-lane to
four-lane, and four-lane to six-lane roads.
(3)
Temporary signs must be freestanding. Signs cannot be staked in to the ground or attached
to trees, light poles, traffic signals or signs, utility boxes or fences.
(4)
Temporary signs that compromise public safety, are damaging or have the potential
to damage public property, are not permitted on any land owned or managed by the CAB,
Dominion or Districts or the adjacent road right-of-way.
(c)
Time of placement of temporary signs.
(1)
Garage Sale Signs may be placed on the day of a sale and must be removed on the last
day of the garage sale by sunset.
(2)
Open House Signs can be placed and must be removed on the day of the open house by
sunset.
(3)
Religious Services Signs may be placed the day before the service and must be removed
the day of the service.
(4)
Sizes of signs are limited to the following:
a.
Garage Sale Signs: a maximum size of two feet by two feet.
b.
Open House Signs: a maximum size of two feet by two feet.
c.
Religious Service Signs: a maximum size of 16 square feet.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § 13.2)

documents.title: Sec. 17-23. - Community event/service signs.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.text:
(a)
Community event/service signs may be used by any group or organization that is offering
an event or service open to the general public. These signs may be used by governmental
entities, the CAB and non-commercial organizations (i.e., nonprofit 501(c)(3)) to
advertise public events and services.
(b)
Community event/service signs may also be used to promote certain community services
that are offered periodically which benefit the Sterling Ranch community and/or a
worthy or charitable cause. Examples of these services include recycling programs,
hazardous materials collection events and election voting notifications.
(c)
Community Event Sign Locations. Community event signs must be placed at locations
designated by the CAB and Douglas County. Prior to placing such signs, the sponsor
must apply for and obtain a permit through the CAB and provide the CAB with the name
of the sponsor and the name of the individual who will be responsible for maintaining
and removing the signs.
(d)
Time of Placement of Signs. Signs may be posted at the locations designated by the
CAB up to ten days before an event and must be removed the day after the event by
10:00 a.m.
(e)
Directional Signs. Freestanding sandwich board signs directing the public to the event
site and parking may be placed on immediately adjacent parkways the day of the event
and must be removed the day after the event by 10:00 a.m.
(f)
Content of Signs. Community event signs posted at designated locations may include
the event name, dates, times, location, fees (if applicable) for the event, the logo
of the organization operating the event and contact information. These signs may include
the logo of one title sponsor not to exceed one square foot. It is strongly recommended
that event signs contain as few words as possible to allow letters to be large enough
to read from a vehicle using a four- and six-lane road with a speed limit of 45 miles
per hour.
(g)
Size/Material of Signs. Community event signs must be four feet by four feet and made
of corrugated plastic or other weather-resistant material.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § 13.3)

documents.title: Sec. 17-54. - General rules.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.article: ARTICLE III. - PARK AND OPEN SPACE RULES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
ARTICLE III. - PARK AND OPEN SPACE RULES
documents.text:
(a)
The control of dogs in Parks and Open Space is regulated by Douglas County Resolutions
R-998-100 and R-999-177, as may be amended, and violations are punishable as set forth
in the applicable resolutions.
(b)
Dog owners must leash and have physical control of their dog at all times. Dog owners
shall pick up and dispose of their dog's excrement.
(c)
Motorized vehicles are prohibited in parks, trails, and open space.
(d)
Glass containers, littering, dumping and misuse of public property are prohibited.
(e)
Fires are only permitted within charcoal burning grills provided at park shelters,
or within liquid-fueled or gas-fueled grills/stoves on CAB or District owned or managed
developed park sites and parking lots when no fire restrictions apply. Fires in Open
Space areas are strictly prohibited.
(f)
Firearms are defined as any pistol, revolver, rifle, or other weapon of any description
from which a shot, projectile, arrow or bullet may be discharged. This includes, and
is not limited to, compressed air guns, CO
2
and battery-operated guns, BB guns, pellet guns, air soft pellet guns, paintball guns,
and slingshots. Archery equipment is defined as any bow, including, but not limited
to, a crossbow, longbow or compound bow, which shoots arrows or other projectiles.
Model rockets and airplanes are defined as any craft that is propelled off the ground
by a gas or electric engine, CO
2
, compressed air or any other form of power. Only model gliders propelled by humans
and airplanes propelled by elastic bands are permitted.
(g)
Possessing fireworks, firearms, archery equipment, model rockets and airplanes on
any CAB owned or managed properties is prohibited, except as provided by C.R.S. §
18-12-201 et seq.
(h)
Firing or shooting any firearm or archery equipment in or into any CAB, Dominion or
District owned or managed properties is prohibited.
(i)
Swimming or the use of watercraft and/or floatation devices is not permitted on CAB
ponds and open water. Use of model, or remote-controlled toy boats on CAB, Dominion
or District owned ponds and open water may not interfere with or disturb fish, wildlife
and fishing activities.
(j)
Parks and Open Space are open from 5:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m. daily.
(k)
Hitting golf balls in or into CAB, Dominion or District owned or managed property
is prohibited.
(l)
Amplified sound systems are prohibited unless specifically authorized in writing by
the CAB.
(m)
Disorderly conduct as defined in C.R.S. § 18-9-106 is prohibited.
(n)
Relocating or releasing animals, fish, birds or insects on CAB, Dominion or District

documents.title: Sec. 17-54. - General rules.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.article: ARTICLE III. - PARK AND OPEN SPACE RULES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
ARTICLE III. - PARK AND OPEN SPACE RULES
documents.text:
owned or managed property is prohibited.
(o)
Fishing is permitted in CAB ponds and is governed by the Colorado Division of Wildlife's
fishing regulations. CAB, Dominion and District owned and managed ponds and water
bodies are regulated by both statewide rules and the CAB's posted site rules. A CAB
fishing permit shall be required by any Person fishing in CAB ponds. The CAB fishing
permit shall be applied for by completion of an application.
(p)
Harassment of wildlife, as defined in C.R.S. § 33-6-128, is prohibited. All of this
statute is incorporated herein except C.R.S. § 33-6-128(3).
(q)
Camping in any CAB Park, Open Space, tract or public area is prohibited except for
during designated community events that may be planned and hosted by the CAB at designated
times, dates, and locations. For purposes of this provision, the term "camping" shall
mean sleeping or staying in any CAB Park or Open Space past the designated closure
time or the erection of tents, shelters, or other equipment that is not being used
as a temporary sunshade during permitted day use. Any items left unattended at any
time may be disposed of without further notice or warning.
(r)
Public bathing, urination, defecation, or other personal sanitation activities, such
as dishwashing, laundry, etc., are prohibited in CAB Parks, Open Space, tract or public
areas.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § 12.1; Res. No.
2022-01-02
, § 1, 1-19-2022)

documents.title: Sec. 17-55. - Land use rules; open space.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.article: ARTICLE III. - PARK AND OPEN SPACE RULES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
ARTICLE III. - PARK AND OPEN SPACE RULES
Sec. 17-55. - Land use rules; open space.
documents.text:
(a)
Dumping and littering of any kind is prohibited. This includes grass clippings, sod,
soil, trash, debris, landscape materials, and dog waste.
(b)
Permanent recreation amenities such as playgrounds, tetherball, volleyball courts,
ball fields, trampolines, horseshoe pits, treehouses, rope swings and archery ranges
not constructed by the CAB or Districts are prohibited.
(c)
Extended Landscaping. Mowing and weed whipping is permitted between the residential
fence line and the outer edge of the CAB's mow line. Improvements including irrigation,
landscape materials, shrub and tree planting, gardening, structure of any kind or
retaining walls are prohibited on CAB, Dominion or District owned or managed properties.
Tree and shrub growth extending onto CAB, Dominion or District owned or managed property
that interferes with maintenance practices is prohibited.
(d)
Storage or staging of any type of equipment or materials is prohibited.
(e)
Dog Off-Leash Areas (DOLAs) hours are from 7:00 a.m. until sunset year-round.
(f)
Damage or misuse of CAB, Dominion or District property is prohibited. This includes,
but is not limited to, applying herbicide, digging and erosion caused by drainage
from adjacent property.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § 12.2(b)—(g); Res. No.
2022-08-02
, § 1, 8-26-2022)

documents.title: Sec. 17-56. - Fence rules.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.article: ARTICLE III. - PARK AND OPEN SPACE RULES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
ARTICLE III. - PARK AND OPEN SPACE RULES
documents.text:
(a)
Owners of property adjacent to fences maintained by the CAB shall not place any landscaping
or other materials in such a manner as to cause damage to the CAB's fence. The CAB
may remove any such materials as provided in Section 17-60 .
(b)
Any person causing any damage to any fence maintained by the CAB shall promptly repair
such damage.
(c)
No Person shall install a gate in a fence on their property that abuts the CAB property
without the prior written approval by the CAB.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § 12.3)

documents.title: Sec. 17-57. - Operation of motorized vehicles and equipment.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.article: ARTICLE III. - PARK AND OPEN SPACE RULES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
ARTICLE III. - PARK AND OPEN SPACE RULES
Sec. 17-57. - Operation of motorized vehicles and equipment.
documents.text:
(a)
Private property may not be accessed through CAB or District open space.
(b)
The operation of any motorized vehicle or equipment on or through parks and open space
owned and maintained by the CAB or Districts is prohibited except for the following:
(1)
CAB and Dominion service vehicles and equipment.
(2)
Law enforcement, fire, rescue, and emergency vehicles and equipment, including the
Douglas County Sheriff, South Metro Fire Rescue Authority, Colorado Division of Wildlife,
and Animal Welfare.
(3)
Vehicles and equipment operated at the direction of public agencies, such as the Denver
Water Board, the City of Aurora, Urban Drainage and Flood Control District, Douglas
County Department of Public Works, when being used by such entities to install or
maintain facilities located in their easements or rights-of-way.
(4)
Vehicles and equipment operated by contractors of the CAB or Dominion, provided the
contractor has obtained an access permit from the CAB or Dominion, as appropriate.
(5)
Power-Driven Mobility Devices which are classified as wheelchairs under the Americans
with Disabilities Act Part 35.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), §§ 12.2(a), 12.4)

documents.title: Sec. 17-58. - Parks and open space water management.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.article: ARTICLE III. - PARK AND OPEN SPACE RULES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
ARTICLE III. - PARK AND OPEN SPACE RULES
Sec. 17-58. - Parks and open space water management.
documents.text:
(a)
Park adjustments. A representative of the CAB shall meet periodically with maintenance teams responsible
for parks within its service area to evaluate historical evapotranspiration, weather
forecasts, and data from weather stations.
(b)
Irrigation system inspections. The CAB staff will visually inspect irrigation systems periodically to ensure proper
adjustment (e.g., to reduce overspray on roads, fix leaking heads, etc.). The CAB
staff will also use analytics of its system to determine opportunities to increase
system efficiency.
(c)
Routine lawn and plant care. The CAB will implement best management practices such as:
(1)
Aerating and fertilizing parks on a routine basis.
(2)
Applying surfactant to older areas as needed to help the soil better receive moisture.
(d)
Additional landscape and irrigation regulations. The CAB will adopt Parks and Open Space Technical Specifications that include evapotranspiration/soil
moisture sensors, smart controllers, rain gauges, sprayer requirements, scheduling
specifications and other additional irrigation controller requirements for the CAB
owned and operated Parks and Open Space.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § 12.5)

Sec. 17-60. - Other remedies of the CAB.
documents.text:
(a)
Any violation of Sections 17-55 (a)—(e) and 17-56 (a) and (b) adjacent to private property shall be deemed to have been placed by the
owner of the adjacent property and that property owner shall be responsible for the
correction of the violation.
(b)
In addition to any penalties provided by the Colorado Revised Statutes, the CAB may
correct violations of Sections 17-54 (b)—(e) and 17-56 at the expense of the responsible party.
(c)
Prior to correcting any violation, the CAB shall give the party responsible ten days'
written notice.
(d)
In the event the CAB corrects any such violation, the responsible party shall be assessed
a fee equal to the amount required to correct the violation plus 20 percent for administrative
expenses. Any such fee shall be collected by the CAB.
(e)
Any party aggrieved by this section may appeal as provided in Section 29-43 .
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § 12.7)

documents.title: Sec. 17-81. - General purpose and scope; rules supplementary to CAB rights.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
Sec. 17-81. - General purpose and scope; rules supplementary to CAB rights.
documents.text:
(a)
The CAB has adopted the Facilities Rules and Regulations, as set forth in this article
("Rules and Regulations"), to provide for the orderly and efficient conduct of management,
operation and control of certain public facilities of the CAB, including, but not
limited to, the Sterling Center, Parks, Open Space, the Clubhouse and Pool (collectively
the "Facilities" and each a "Facility").
(b)
The CAB expressly reserves the right to make any lawful addition and/or revision to
this article when and as they may become advisable to properly operate and maintain
the Facilities and provide related services and to promote the peace, health, safety,
and welfare of the people residing in the area under the CAB's authority pursuant
to that certain Second Amended and Restated Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board
Establishment Agreement between Sterling Ranch Colorado Metropolitan CAB Nos. 1 through
7, dated and effective as of March 18, 2020. The Rules and Regulations contained in
this article are supplementary to, and are not to be construed as, any abridgement
of any lawful rights of the CAB as outlined in the Colorado Revised Statutes, as applicable.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), intro. ¶)

documents.title: Sec. 17-106. - General authority of public access.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
DIVISION 2. - ACCESS TO AND USE OF THE FACILITIES
Sec. 17-106. - General authority of public access.
documents.text:
The Facilities of the CAB are open to the public, subject to the Rules and Regulations
set forth in this article. The CAB retains the right to limit access to each Facility
based upon the safe and reasonable capacity as determined by the Board of Directors
in its discretion. Use of the Facilities shall be allowed on a first-come, first-served
basis in the event of any such limitations.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 1.1)

documents.title: Sec. 17-107. - Attire.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
DIVISION 2. - ACCESS TO AND USE OF THE FACILITIES
documents.text:
Proper and appropriate attire should be worn by all persons when utilizing any Facility.
Nudity is strictly prohibited. Shirts and shoes are required to be worn at all times
in the Sterling Center and the Clubhouse.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 1.2)

documents.title: Sec. 17-108. - Children.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
DIVISION 2. - ACCESS TO AND USE OF THE FACILITIES
documents.text:
(a)
For safety and health reasons, children 11 years of age and younger must be accompanied
and actively supervised by a parent, legal guardian, or, if authorized by a parent
or legal guardian, another adult 15 years of age or older, when utilizing the CAB
operated facilities at the Sterling Center.
(b)
The CAB staff shall not be held responsible for the safety of unsupervised children
under age 18 in any of the Facilities.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 1.3; Res. No.
2022-08-02
, § 1, 8-26-2022)

documents.title: Sec. 17-109. - Event and program registration and fees.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
DIVISION 2. - ACCESS TO AND USE OF THE FACILITIES
Sec. 17-109. - Event and program registration and fees.
documents.text:
Persons may register for various activities, programs, special events and classes
taking place at or within the Facilities by contacting the CAB. Such persons may be
required to sign additional waivers or forms and pay a fee for such activities. Fees
are nonrefundable except in the event that the subject activity, program, special
event, or class is cancelled for reasons, including, but not limited to, inclement
weather.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 1.4)

documents.title: Sec. 17-110. - Hours of operation.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
DIVISION 2. - ACCESS TO AND USE OF THE FACILITIES
documents.text:
Generally, the Facilities shall be open seven days a week subject to seasonal limitations.
Hours of operation shall be posted on the CAB website and at each facility. The Board
of Directors, in its sole discretion, may make seasonal adjustments or changes to
the hours of operation, and date and time of opening of the Facilities as it deems
necessary and appropriate for CAB programming. People may contact the CAB to obtain
up-to-date information relating to the hours of operation for any of the Facilities.
Additionally, the CAB reserves the right to close any Facility due to weather conditions,
maintenance, preparation for major events, temporary staffing problems, or other reasons.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 1.5; Res. No.
2022-01-02
, § 1, 1-19-2022; Res. No.
2022-08-02
, § 1, 8-26-2022)

documents.title: Sec. 17-111. - Lost articles.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
DIVISION 2. - ACCESS TO AND USE OF THE FACILITIES
documents.text:
The CAB is not responsible for any lost or stolen articles or for accidents on the
premises of the Facilities. All personal articles should be locked or secured as appropriate
to avoid loss to the owner. There will be a collection spot for all lost articles
designated in the Facilities. All lost articles which are not claimed shall be deemed
abandoned and donated or otherwise disposed of on a monthly basis as determined by
the CAB in its sole discretion.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 1.6)

documents.title: Sec. 17-112. - Limitation of liability of CAB.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
DIVISION 2. - ACCESS TO AND USE OF THE FACILITIES
Sec. 17-112. - Limitation of liability of CAB.
documents.text:
Use of all Facilities shall be at the sole risk of any person using same. Except as
provided by the Colorado Governmental Immunity Act, C.R.S. § 4-10-101 et seq., the
CAB shall not be responsible for any claims for damages by reason of any action or
inaction of the CAB or its agents or representatives in connection with any of the
Facilities.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 1.7)

documents.title: Sec. 17-113. - Equipment.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
DIVISION 2. - ACCESS TO AND USE OF THE FACILITIES
documents.text:
All items, furniture, and equipment located on or around the Facilities are the property
of the CAB and shall not be taken from the premises without prior written consent
of the CAB. Any violations shall result in criminal prosecution by the CAB. Windows
and doors shall not be left propped open by any member of the public.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 1.8)

documents.title: Sec. 17-114. - Food and drink.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
DIVISION 2. - ACCESS TO AND USE OF THE FACILITIES
documents.text:
Food and drink are permitted in designated areas within the Facilities. Glass containers
are prohibited in all Facilities unless authorized during special events by and in
the sole discretion of CAB Management. People consuming food and/or drink must clean
up after themselves. Food and/or drink may not be consumed in the pool.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 1.9; Res. No.
2022-08-02
, § 1, 8-26-2022)

documents.title: Sec. 17-115. - Smoking, vaping and drugs.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
DIVISION 2. - ACCESS TO AND USE OF THE FACILITIES
documents.text:
Smoking of any kind, including, but not limited to, tobacco and marijuana, and the
use or possession of illegal drugs shall not be permitted on or around the Facilities
and is strictly prohibited. Smoking includes the use of electronic smoking or vaping
devices.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 1.10)

documents.title: Sec. 17-116. - Alcohol.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
DIVISION 2. - ACCESS TO AND USE OF THE FACILITIES
documents.text:
The consumption of alcohol in the Facilities is permitted as follows:
(1)
The Sterling Center. Adults over the age of 21 years may only use alcohol in the Sterling Center if the
alcohol is purchased therein. All people using alcohol or otherwise within the Facilities
must comply with all applicable rules, regulations, policies, ordinances, and laws
promulgated by the CAB and other local, municipal, State, and Federal governmental
entities.
(2)
Parks and open spaces. Adults over the age of 21 years may only use alcohol in the Parks or Open Spaces
when permits or other documentation, if required, have been obtained from the County
and/or other applicable governmental entities.
(3)
Clubhouse and pool. Adults over the age of 21 years may use alcohol in designated areas in and around
the Clubhouse and on the deck of the Pool.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 1.11; Res. No.
2022-08-02
, § 1, 8-26-2022)

documents.title: Sec. 17-117. - Animals.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
DIVISION 2. - ACCESS TO AND USE OF THE FACILITIES
documents.text:
Pets are allowed in parks and open spaces. Animals are not allowed in the Sterling
Center, the Clubhouse or the Pool except those specially trained to assist a person
with a disability as permitted by State or Federal Law. All animals must be on a leash
at all times, and people must immediately pick up and properly dispose of any waste
produced by animals under their ownership or control. No animal shall at any time
be left unattended inside or outside the Facilities unless left in a Designated Area
within the applicable Hours of Operation of the nearest Facility. If animals are left
in a Designated Area outside of the applicable Hours of Operation, or are left unattended
within the Facilities, the CAB reserves the right to contact Douglas County Animal
Services to report a lost animal. People leaving their animal in a Designated Area
are responsible for any damages to their animal, others' animals, people, or property
caused by the pet.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 1.12)

documents.title: Sec. 17-118. - Solicitation policy.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
DIVISION 2. - ACCESS TO AND USE OF THE FACILITIES
documents.text:
Sales, solicitations, distribution and posting of materials, and for-profit activities
are prohibited within the Facilities and other CAB property unless the CAB gives its
prior written approval. The CAB may, within its sole discretion, designate certain
areas outside the Facilities for sales, solicitations and distribution of materials.
Activities may be further restricted to specific times and dates as determined by
the CAB. People may not use the Facilities for commercial or business purposes, including,
but not limited to, personal training sessions, athletic lessons, advertising, home
business party sales (i.e., cosmetics, candles, etc.), solicitation of business, or
promotions unless the CAB gives prior written approval on any terms or conditions
required by the CAB.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 1.13)

documents.title: Sec. 17-119. - Community bulletin board.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
DIVISION 2. - ACCESS TO AND USE OF THE FACILITIES
documents.text:
Upon sending a request to info@sterlingranchcab.com, and if the CAB gives written
approval of the request, a person may post content on the Community Bulletin Board.
Such content may include business cards and flyers no larger than four inches by six
inches. All content will be removed from the Community Bulletin Board and disposed
of each January 1, April 1, July 1, and October 1. The CAB reserves the right to ask
for additional information to determine whether to grant a request, and to charge
a fee for posting content on the Community Bulletin Board.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 1.14)

documents.title: Sec. 17-120. - Media wall.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
DIVISION 2. - ACCESS TO AND USE OF THE FACILITIES
documents.text:
The Sterling Center contains a media wall that is owned not by the CAB, but by SR
Civic Center, LLC, and its successors and assigns ("SR Civic Center"). The Media Wall's
content and use is governed by a lease agreement between SR Civic Center and the CAB.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 1.15)

documents.title: Sec. 17-121. - Complaints.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
DIVISION 2. - ACCESS TO AND USE OF THE FACILITIES
documents.text:
Complaints from residents should be directed to the CAB at info@sterlingranchcab.com,
feedback collection process, or work order system adopted by the CAB, and the CAB
will make reasonable efforts to promptly resolve the conflict. Under no circumstances
will anyone interfere with, attempt to discipline, request special treatment from,
or otherwise direct employees in the course of CAB business. People shall not request
special personal services from CAB employees.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 1.16; Res. No.
2022-08-02
, § 1, 8-26-2022)

documents.title: Sec. 17-122. - Photography.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
DIVISION 2. - ACCESS TO AND USE OF THE FACILITIES
documents.text:
Photography of any kind is not permitted inside the Facilities' restrooms. When using
photographic equipment of any kind in or around the Facilities, people should take
care not to inadvertently include in the photo or video any person who has expressed
a wish not to be so included. Photographic equipment is permitted at the Facilities
for personal use. From time to time, the CAB may cause photos to be taken at the Facilities
to be used for marketing purposes. Persons not wishing to be in such photos should
take care to avoid having their photo taken.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 1.17)

documents.title: Sec. 17-123. - Audio devices.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
DIVISION 2. - ACCESS TO AND USE OF THE FACILITIES
documents.text:
Personal audio equipment must be used in compliance with the rules, regulations, and
policies of the CAB and any applicable noise ordinances or other laws. In parks and
open space, small personal amplified sound systems, such as a Bluetooth speaker or
similar, are permitted so long as such use does not bother other users or residents.
Any amplified sound system other than a small personal amplified sound systems are
prohibited unless specifically authorized in writing by CAB. In all other Facilities,
sound emanating from personal audio equipment must be contained through the use of
personal headphones unless the CAB has given prior consent.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 1.18; Res. No.
2022-08-02
, § 1, 8-26-2022)

documents.title: Secs. 17-124—17-144. - Reserved.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
DIVISION 2. - ACCESS TO AND USE OF THE FACILITIES
documents.text: Secs. 17-124—17-144. - Reserved.

documents.title: Sec. 17-145. - General composition.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.text:
The Clubhouse consists of the Great Hall, Pavilion No. 1, Pavilion No. 2, and the
Fitness Center. The Pool consists of the pool deck and surrounding grounds and the
swimming pool itself.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 2.1)

documents.title: Sec. 17-146. - Membership to clubhouse and pool.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
Sec. 17-146. - Membership to clubhouse and pool.
documents.text:
(a)
Open access to members. Access to the Clubhouse and Pool shall be open to the following classifications of
members:
(1)
CAB residents. These are individuals who either own, or have as their primary residence, property
that is within the boundaries of one of the Sterling Ranch Colorado Metropolitan Districts
No. 1—7 and their permitted Guests.
(2)
Non-resident members. Individuals who do not own or have as their primary residence property within the
boundaries of one of the Sterling Ranch Colorado Metropolitan Districts No. 1—7, but
who have purchased a Non-Resident Membership.
(3)
Caregiver members. One Caregiver Membership per CAB Resident household will be available only to CAB
Residents at a rate determined by the CAB. This membership permits the identified
non-family member caregiver access only in conjunction with the provision of caregiver
services to the CAB Resident household.
(b)
Designation of members, guests. Collectively, CAB Residents, Non-Resident Members and Caregiver Members are referred
to as "Members." Collectively, Members and Guests are referred to as "Users."
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 2.2)

documents.title: Sec. 17-147. - Guests of CAB resident.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.text:
(a)
Each CAB Resident household is permitted up to six guests per day. If the Clubhouse
and Pool is not at capacity, additional guests beyond six will be permitted for a
fee of $5.00 per guest. CAB Residents are encouraged to call and verify capacity before
arrival. Each CAB Resident household receives 25 complimentary guest passes per calendar
year.
(b)
Guests must be accompanied by a CAB Resident at all times during their use of Clubhouse
and Pool facilities. If you are unable to accompany your guest, then you need to fill
out an online form. This form is good for one day only. Guests are the responsibility
of the Resident.
(c)
Additional fees for Guest use may be adopted by the CAB at its discretion.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 2.3; Res. No.
2022-01-02
, § 1, 1-19-2022; Res. No.
2022-08-02
, § 1, 8-26-2022)

documents.title: Sec. 17-148. - Cards required for access.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.text:
All Members will be provided a membership card which must be used to enter the Facility.
A picture of a membership card may be used in lieu of the physical card. Membership
cards shall only be used by the designated Member. Lost cards or replacement cards
will be subject to a replacement fee as determined by the CAB.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 2.4; Res. No.
2022-01-02
, § 1, 1-19-2022)

documents.title: Sec. 17-149. - General behavior standards.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.text:
(a)
As a condition of use of the Clubhouse and Pool, all Users shall adhere to the rules
and regulations as stated herein. In addition, no User shall:
(1)
Interfere with or act in a physically or verbally abusive manner towards any Clubhouse
or Pool staff.
(2)
Interfere with any other User's use and enjoyment of the Clubhouse or Pool or act
in a physically or verbally abusive manner towards any other User.
(3)
Engage in any behavior that is, or threatens to be, criminal, tortious, or resulting
in bodily harm or property damage.
(b)
Users that, in the sole discretion of Clubhouse or Pool Staff, are being disruptive,
unruly, using any equipment or area of the facility in a manner for which it was not
intended, or are posing a health or safety threat to themselves or to others may be
asked to leave the Facility and may be subject to disciplinary action as provided
in division 5 of article.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 2.5)

documents.title: Sec. 17-150. - Personal trainers and swimming instructors.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
Sec. 17-150. - Personal trainers and swimming instructors.
documents.text:
Personal trainers and swimming instructors may be available for a fee at such rates
as may be set by the CAB. Independent contractors may offer personal training or swimming
lessons with approval of the CAB and execution of an Independent Contractor Agreement
on the CAB-approved form on file in the offices of the CAB. Outside trainers or instructors
who have not completed the CAB Independent Contractor Agreement will not be allowed.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 2.6)

documents.title: Sec. 17-151. - Commercial use.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.text:
Commercial activities or other private business enterprise is forbidden except as
specifically provided for in this division. Events of a commercial nature may be held
at the Clubhouse provided the User first submits an Application for Facility Use and
completes a Clubhouse Rental Agreement in accordance with this division. Exterior
signage and advertising of any kind shall not be permitted. Events held at the District's
Clubhouse are intended for invited guests only and under no circumstances shall commercial
activities be solicited to or made open to the public. Any person desiring to hold
an event at the Clubhouse which is contrary to this division must submit a request
in writing at least 30 days prior to the date of such event to the CAB for its consideration.
The User must indicate how all safety requirements and other provisions of this division
have been satisfied. The Board shall make a determination regarding such event at
its next regularly scheduled meeting and shall inform the User in writing of its determination.
All such requests are subject to the District's discretion.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 2.7)

documents.title: Sec. 17-152. - Supervision of children.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.text:
Children under the age of 11 years must be accompanied and actively supervised by
a parent, legal guardian, or if authorized by a parent or legal guardian, another
individual of 15 years or age or older, while using the Clubhouse or Pool.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 2.8; Res. No.
2022-01-02
, § 1, 1-19-2022; Res. No.
2022-08-02
, § 1, 8-26-2022)

documents.title: Sec. 17-153. - Equipment.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.text:
All equipment, supplies, furnishings, or other amenities located in or around the
Clubhouse and Pool are the property of the CAB and shall not be taken from the premises
without authorization.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 2.9)

documents.title: Sec. 17-154. - Lost articles.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.text:
The CAB is not responsible for any lost or stolen articles. All personal articles
should be locked or secured as appropriate to avoid loss to the owner. Lost items
may be turned in to Clubhouse or Pool staff. Any items which are not claimed may be
donated to a nonprofit collection agency on a monthly basis at the CAB's sole discretion.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 2.10)

documents.title: Sec. 17-155. - Food and drink.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.text:
User-provided food and drink shall only be allowed in designated areas of the Clubhouse
grounds, the Clubhouse, and the Pool. Glass containers are forbidden in the Pool area.
All Users must clean up after themselves.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 2.11)

documents.title: Sec. 17-156. - Weapons.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.text:
All weapons, including the open carry of firearms, are strictly forbidden in or around
the Clubhouse, the Pool and the Pool deck.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 2.12)

documents.title: Sec. 17-157. - Pets.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.text:
Pets are not allowed in the Clubhouse or on the Pool deck except service animals or
companion animals as defined by the Americans with Disabilities Act and the laws of
the State of Colorado. No animals are permitted in the Pool with the exception of
CAB Sponsored Events.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 2.13; Res. No.
2022-08-02
, § 1, 8-26-2022)

documents.title: Sec. 17-158. - Clubhouse-specific rules.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.text:
All Clubhouse Users shall adhere to the following rules concerning use of the Clubhouse:
(1)
Fitness Center Rules.
a.
All use of the fitness equipment is at the User's own risk. Users should consult a
physician before engaging in a new physical exercise routine. Clubhouse Staff may
be available for an equipment orientation upon request.
b.
All equipment must be used in the manner for which it was designed. Users may be restricted
from utilizing the fitness center or specific equipment based on safety considerations,
including recommendations of equipment suppliers or manufacturers.
c.
Slamming or dropping weights is prohibited. All weights and equipment must be re-racked
or returned to its proper location after use.
d.
After use all equipment shall be wiped down with sanitizing solution.
e.
Appropriate attire must be worn at all times within the clubhouse. Proper athletic
shoes shall be worn when using fitness equipment. Sandals, "Crocs" style shoes, or
open-toed shoes are not allowed.
f.
All bags and personal items must be stored appropriately and out of areas of User
traffic to ensure a clean and safe environment in which to exercise.
g.
Personal electronic devices must be used with headphones.
h.
Talking on a cellphone while using fitness equipment is prohibited.
i.
Violation of these rules may result in being asked to leave the fitness center.
(2)
Grills. No personal grills may be used in the Clubhouse or Pool deck area. On-site grills
are available on a first-come, first-served basis. Users must clean grills after use.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 2.14; Res. No.
2022-08-02
, § 1, 8-26-2022)

documents.title: Sec. 17-159. - Pool-specific rules and regulations.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.text:
The following rules apply to the Pool and Pool deck area:
(1)
Swimming any time where a lifeguard is not on duty is at the User's sole risk.
(2)
All users must take a cleansing shower before entering the pool. Showering after using
the pool is recommended.
(3)
Users must wear appropriate swimwear at all times. Street clothing, including basketball
shorts, jean shorts, or cargo shorts, undergarments, sports bras, or similar attire,
is prohibited in the pool. White T-shirts or tank-tops are permitted in the pool if
worn over appropriate swim attire. Pool staff will make the final determination of
if swimwear is appropriate. Nudity is strictly prohibited.
(4)
Non-swimmers must be accompanied by a swimmer in the water and be within arm's reach
at all times.
(5)
Glass Containers are prohibited in the Pool and Pool Areas.
(6)
Users who are ill, have experienced vomiting or diarrhea in the past 24 hours, have
open sores, or ear or nasal discharge should not use the pool.
(7)
Any incontinent user must wear approved swim diapers when using the pool. Rubber or
plastic swim pants are recommended in addition to a diaper.
(8)
Users shall immediately report any fecal or vomit incident in the Pool to a lifeguard
or staff.
(9)
Horseplay, running, diving into the pool and hanging on, swinging from or pulling
on aquatic equipment or features is prohibited. Repeat violators will be asked to
leave the pool.
(10)
Lane ropes and stair railings are installed to assist and guide pool users. Standing
or sitting on these items is prohibited.
(11)
When lap lanes are present, those areas are to be used for lap swimming or water walking
only.
(12)
During busy times, lap swimmers may be asked to share lanes, circle swim, or limit
swim time to ensure all have an opportunity to use the facilities.
(13)
The pool deck is reserved for walking, safety and emergency purposes. No obstruction
of any kind will be permitted in this area.
(14)
Inflatable pool toys, flotation aids, or similar items are only allowed under the
following conditions:
a.
Only transparent circular inflatables no larger than 42 inches in diameter, infant
inflatables, water wings with an attached chest piece and pool noodles are permitted
in the pool.
b.
Mesh infant inflatables may be no larger than 33 inches by 38 inches.
c.
Pool mattresses or other inflatables are prohibited.
d.
Users with noncompliant inflatables or flotation devices will be asked to remove them
from the pool.
(15)
Personal sound equipment such as stereos or wireless speakers are permitted so long

documents.title: Sec. 17-159. - Pool-specific rules and regulations.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.text:
as they do not disrupt others' enjoyment of the Pool. If any complaints are received,
Users will be asked to turn down their music, use headphones, or, upon repeated complaint,
asked to turn off the device or leave the Pool.
(16)
The Pool must be cleared during thunder and lightning storms or other inclement weather
events that present a danger to Users. The Pool will be cleared if lightning strikes
within ten miles of the Pool, or at the discretion of Clubhouse or Pool staff. All
Users must follow staff directions and safety instructions. Staff will determine when
it is safe to reopen the Pool.
(17)
Chemicals are used to ensure a sanitary and safe water environment. Conditions are
tested and documented on a regular basis. If unacceptable conditions occur, including
a vomiting or fecal event, staff will determine if the Pool must be closed to preserve
the health, safety and well-being of all Users.
(18)
Chemicals used in the pool may damage swimwear. CAB is not responsible for any such
damage.
(19)
CAB furniture in the Pool area shall not be removed. Users may bring additional portable
lounge chairs, umbrellas, or other similar items to the Pool area, provided they do
not present a safety concern or unreasonably interfere with others' use and enjoyment
of the Pool as determined by staff.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 2.15; Res. No.
2022-08-02
, § 1, 8-26-2022)

documents.title: Secs. 17-160—17-186. - Reserved.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.text: Secs. 17-160—17-186. - Reserved.

documents.title: Sec. 17-187. - Rental policy of facilities.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.text:
The CAB may, from time to time and within its sole discretion, rent the Facilities
as provided herein. Rental of the Facilities are subject to the CAB's Code, all federal,
state, and local laws and ordinances, and any other conditions imposed by the CAB.
The CAB may, in its discretion, decline rental of any Facility for any event it deems
to jeopardize the safety, health or welfare of the public.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 3.1)

documents.title: Sec. 17-188. - Reservation process.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.text:
To make a reservation, any interested person shall:
(1)
Submit the Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board Facilities Rental Application
and Agreement ("Rental Agreement") which is on file in the offices of the CAB;
(2)
Pay the applicable rental fee, security deposit and any other required fees or charges
adopted by the CAB as specified by the Rental Agreement. All fees and charges are
due at the time of submission of the Rental Agreement.
(3)
Rentals in some circumstances may require approval from the CAB's Board of Directors.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 3.2)

documents.title: Sec. 17-189. - Limitations.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.text:
(a)
Private rentals for the following year will be made available on December 1 of each
year.
(b)
CAB programming, meetings and community events will be scheduled before private rental
dates will be made available. CAB programming, meetings and community events take
priority over private rental requests. Confirmed reservations will not be displaced
for CAB use.
(c)
Rental requests are reviewed on a "first-come, first-served" basis,
(d)
CAB limits private rentals reserved by the same person to no more than one rental
per day and no more than two rentals per calendar month, except for properly approved
"Recurring Rentals."
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 3.3; Res. No.
2022-01-02
, § 1, 1-19-2022)

documents.title: Sec. 17-190. - Recurring facilities rental.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.text:
People may reserve the Facilities on a recurring basis for a maximum of one time per
week, three hours per rental during regular operating hours ("Recurring Rentals").
Recurring Rental requests can be made at the discretion of the CAB Staff. Recurring
rentals depend on the availability of space and CAB programming. CAB personnel will
review Recurring Rental requests on a first-come, first-served basis, and will have
the discretion to create a rotating list in order to provide equal access to all rental
applicants. CAB programming will take priority over all Recurring Rental requests.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 3.4; Res. No.
2022-08-02
, § 1, 8-26-2022)

documents.title: Sec. 17-191. - Fees and costs.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.text:
All rental fees and costs will be determined by the CAB and shall be specified on
the Rental Agreement. All deposits, fees, and charges are due at the time the reservation
is received by the CAB.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 3.5)

documents.title: Sec. 17-192. - Security deposit.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.text:
The security deposit is collected to ensure the Facilities are returned to CAB in
the same condition in which they were rented. The security deposit will be returned
only after inspection by CAB staff. If the security deposit is insufficient to pay
for any cleaning, repairs, theft or other damage to CAB property, the renting party
is liable for any additional amounts as provided in the Rental Agreement.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 3.6)

documents.title: Sec. 17-193. - Capacity.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.text:
Any Person renting a Facility shall ensure that the number of attendees during the
rented period does not exceed the permitted rental capacity imposed by the CAB. In
no case will attendance beyond the maximum capacity as determined by South Metro Fire
Protection District be permitted.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 3.7)

documents.title: Sec. 17-194. - Security.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.text:
Security personnel may be required at the user's expense for all rentals at which
50 or more persons will be present. CAB management shall provide a list of approved
providers, or permission to use an alternate provider may be requested in writing.
CAB management may, in its sole discretion, waive the requirement for security personnel
upon request.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 3.8; Res. No.
2022-08-02
, § 1, 8-26-2022)

documents.title: Sec. 17-195. - Vendors.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.text:
Vendors are defined as any person, business, or entity providing a service at the
Facilities on behalf of a Renter. Examples include, but are not limited to, caterers,
bands, DJs, entertainment, and rental supply companies. All vendors must be approved
in advance by the CAB, and provide certificates of insurance listing the Sterling
Ranch Community Authority Board and the CAB Managing Agent as provided in the Rental
Agreement. CAB reserves the right to refuse the use of Vendors at its discretion.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 3.9)

documents.title: Sec. 17-196. - Cancellation and refund policy.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.text:
Refunds for cancellations of facility rentals shall be made in accordance with the
terms of the Rental Agreement.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 3.10)

documents.title: Sec. 17-197. - Specific facility rental rules.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.text:
(a)
Sterling Center Exhibit Hall.
(1)
The Sterling Center's Exhibit Hall is a Facility leased by the CAB. Rental of this
Facility includes ONLY the Exhibit Hall and does not include the office section of
the Sterling Center.
(2)
This community amenity is available for rent for events, including birthdays, anniversary
parties, etc. Events in this Facility may have a maximum of 200 people unless otherwise
authorized in writing by the CAB. If a greater number of attendees is requested, the
CAB may require additional conditions, including, but not limited to, an increased
security deposit and additional on-site security.
(b)
The Clubhouse. The Clubhouse or the portions described herein may be rented by any Member. Areas
of the Clubhouse available for rent include the Great Hall (which includes the kitchen,
balcony and outside fireplace patio), Pavilion 1 and Pavilion 2.
(1)
Capacity of the Great Hall is limited to 169 people on the main level and 31 people
on the lower level.
(2)
The Great Hall is limited to three private rental days per month, and no more than
two private rentals in a given week.
(c)
Pool rental and reservation policy. The Pool and Pool deck area are not available for reservation or rental except as
explicitly authorized by the CAB. Any request for reservation or rental shall be submitted
in writing to CAB management at least 30 days in advance and shall be considered at
the next occurring CAB meeting. All such requests are subject to the CAB's discretion
and subject to terms to be determined by the CAB.
(d)
Parks.
(1)
CAB-owned parks, including the shelters and benches, are available for rental. Playgrounds
and grassy areas within any Park are not part of any Park rental.
(2)
Petting zoos, farm or livestock animals are not allowed on turf areas, including both
manicured and native turf, at any time.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 3.11; Res. No.
2022-08-02
, § 1, 8-26-2022)

documents.title: Sec. 17-218. - Disorderly conduct.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.text:
The CAB Staff or authorized representatives, including the Managing Agent, may request
any person to cease conduct that is:
(1)
In violation of any of the Rules and Regulations in this article or other rules, regulations,
or policies of the CAB.
(2)
Interferes with, or is abusive toward, any of the CAB's representatives in the normal
operation of the Facilities.
(3)
Interferes with any person's use or enjoyment of the Facilities, or is abusive to
any such person.
(4)
Misusing or damaging real property and fixtures or personal property such as furniture
and equipment.
(5)
Criminal, tortious, intimidating or threatening, or any behavior that might result
in bodily harm or property damage.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 4.1)

documents.title: Sec. 17-219. - Remedies available for disorderly conduct.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
Sec. 17-219. - Remedies available for disorderly conduct.
documents.text:
In the event that the offending party fails to cease such conduct after being requested
and warned to do so, the CAB is authorized to use all reasonable means necessary to
stop such conduct, including, but not limited to, contacting local law enforcement,
having the offending party removed from the Facility and/or suspending the offending
party's Facility privileges for 48 hours without the necessity of action or consent
by the CAB. Any person refusing removal from the Clubhouse or attempting to enter
or remain on the premises of the Clubhouse after their privileges have been revoked
may be subject to arrest and prosecution for criminal trespass under Colorado law.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 4.2)

documents.title: Sec. 17-220. - Review and disciplinary action by CAB general manager.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
Sec. 17-220. - Review and disciplinary action by CAB general manager.
documents.text:
The CAB General Manager will have 15 working days to investigate the incident and
to make a decision on disciplinary action. The General Manager shall notify the offending
party in writing of their decision regarding discipline. The following disciplinary
measures may be imposed by the General Manager without the necessity of Board Action:
(1)
First Offense:
a.
Issuance of written warning that future conduct will result in suspension.
b.
In the case of actual physical altercation or property damage as a First Offense,
the District Manager may apply the sanction of a Second Offense.
(2)
Second Offense: Suspension from the Facility for two weeks.
(3)
Third Offense: Suspension from the Facility for one month.
(4)
Fourth Offense: Suspension from the Facility for one year.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 4.3)

documents.title: Sec. 17-221. - Appeal to board.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.text:
The CAB Board of Directors shall be notified of all disciplinary measures. Any person
may appeal the disciplinary action imposed by the CAB General Manager by requesting
a written hearing before the CAB within five days of receiving the General Manager's
decision. Such appeal shall be heard at the next occurring regular meeting following
receipt of the request for hearing.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 4.4)

documents.title: Sec. 17-222. - Discretion of CAB.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.text:
The CAB, in hearing an appeal, shall have the authority to:
(1)
Uphold the discipline imposed by the General Manager.
(2)
Reduce the suspension imposed by the General Manager.
(3)
Increase the suspension imposed by the General Manager.
(4)
Impose other disciplinary measures it deems appropriate which may include revocation
of Facilities privileges for a person and/or that person's family members. The person
involved in a disciplinary matter shall receive notice of the violation and disciplinary
measures that may be imposed by the Board.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 4.5)

documents.title: Sec. 17-223. - Restitution for damage or costs.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
Sec. 17-223. - Restitution for damage or costs.
documents.text:
If any person commits an act or omission that constitutes a violation of the Rules
and Regulations contained in this article, and the violation causes the CAB to incur
damages or expenses, the person who commits the violation, or who is responsible for
the person who commits the violation, shall be liable to the CAB for all such damages
and expenses and shall repay the same to the CAB upon request. Such expenses may include,
but shall not be limited to, reasonable attorneys' fees incurred as a result of the
violation, as well as reasonable costs and/or attorneys' fees incurred in obtaining
and collecting a judgment against a person who commits a violation or is responsible
for a person who commits a violation.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 4.6)

documents.title: Sec. 17-224. - Record of violations.
documents.chapter: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
path: Chapter 17 - PARKS, FACILITIES AND OPEN SPACES
documents.text:
Violations and disciplinary measures taken related to any Violations will be recorded
in writing and kept on file by CAB personnel.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(6), § 4.7)

ARTICLE V. - POLICIES, PROCEDURES, FEES AND FORMS FOR COLORADO PARKS AND WILDLIFE
Sec. 17-273. - Colorado Parks and Wildlife Parks Pass Program.
documents.text:
(a)
Parks Pass Program Agreement. The CAB has entered into a Parks Pass Program Agreement, dated August 15, 2017, as
may be amended from time to time (the "Parks Pass Agreement") with the Colorado Parks
Foundation, Inc., a Colorado nonprofit corporation ("CPF"), to purchase Colorado Parks
and Wildlife ("CPW") annual state parks passes (each, an "Annual Pass" and together,
the "Annual Passes") for certain residents of the Community (the "Parks Pass Program").
(b)
Annual pass distribution. The Parks Pass Program is subject to the following Policies, Procedures, Fees, and
Forms:
Table 17-273 . Distribution of Annual Passes
Event
Distribution Method
The first 100 closings of real estate purchase agreements for "Qualified Residences"
(any single-family residence, townhome or condo located within the Community)
A Voucher ( on file in the offices of the CAB) to obtain an Annual Pass will be included
in a welcoming packet and/or gift that will be given to the property owner of record.
The Voucher must be brought to the Sterling Ranch Information Center and exchanged
for an Annual Pass.
Closings for initial owners of Qualified Residences, other than the first 100 closings
A Voucher to obtain an Annual Pass will be mailed to the property owner of record
and/or will be given to the real estate agent to give to the property owner. The Voucher
must be brought to the Sterling Ranch Information Center and exchanged for an Annual
Pass.
Closings of Qualified Residences other than for initial owners (transfer of ownership
of Qualified Residences)
The property owner of record must submit an Application (on file in the offices of
the CAB) and submit it to the CAB at the Sterling Ranch Information Center. Once the
Application is approved, the CAB will provide an Annual Pass to the Qualified Residence.
Expiration of Annual Pass
Each Annual Pass is issued for a period of one year. Owners of Qualified Residences
may submit an Application for a new Annual Pass upon expiration of the initial or
immediately preceding Annual Pass. Once the Application is approved, the CAB will
provide an Annual Pass to the Qualified Residence.
Note: Before the CAB provides an annual pass (whether in exchange for a voucher or
following an approved application), the CAB will require presentation of government-issued
photo identification and documentation of ownership (discussed below).
(c)
Rules, regulations, and conditions.
(1)
Parks pass agreement controls. In the event these Policies, Procedures, Fees and Forms for the Colorado Parks and

Annual pass terms, conditions, limitations and restrictions. The Annual Passes are issued by CPF and may be subject to additional terms, conditions,

(6)
Documentation of ownership. The CAB will require presentation of documentation showing that the individual presenting

documents.title: Sec. 21-21. - The design review process.
documents.text:
(a)
Generally.
(1)
Any change to the exterior of the home or on the lot must be submitted to the DRC,
and approval obtained before any work is started. The submittal address (USPS, hand
delivery, courier) is:
STERLING RANCH DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE
8220 PINEY RIVER AVENUE
LITTLETON, CO 80125
VIA EMAIL:
submit@sterlingranchdrc.com
(2)
The DRC has up to 30 days to review a submittal from the date it was RECEIVED. If
you have NOT been notified, in writing, by the 31st day after the receipt date, the
submittal is deemed to be DENIED. It is the responsibility of the Applicant to contact
the DRC to determine the status of the submittal.
(3)
There are consequences for failure to obtain DRC approval before making changes to
the exterior of your home or lot, and for not adhering to approved plans. This includes,
but is not limited to, fines, removal of unapproved materials, and/or legal actions.
NOTE: The DRC does not evaluate changes to grading or drainage. Applicants are to
seek approval from the County and/or other appropriate governing bodies. The DRC is
not responsible in any way for changes made to grading and/or drainage while installing
landscaping or other improvements.
(b)
What to submit; for general architectural change. The DRC may require additional information if the submitted materials do not adequately
demonstrate what will be constructed.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(1), § III)

documents.title: Sec. 21-22. - General community standards.
documents.text:
(a)
Generally.
(1)
An alphabetical list of common improvements and restricted uses is set forth in subsection
(b) of this section, with pertinent information for each. Unless specifically stated
as "PREAPPROVED," all improvements must be submitted to the DRC, and approval obtained
prior to installation of any materials. Likewise, any contemplated improvement not
listed here must also be submitted to the DRC and prior approval obtained before any
work is done.
(2)
No additions, alteration or renovations shall be allowed if the resulting impact materially
adversely affects neighboring properties and/or community areas. All project requests
are considered on a case-by-case basis including a variety of factors, such as the
available space on the lot, site conditions, proximity to neighbors, and compatibility
with neighboring properties. The DRC reserves the right to limit the size and location
of certain modifications.
(3)
As a condition of approval, the DRC may require that the homeowner requesting a lot
improvement obtain written consent/agreement of all other property owners whose lots
may be impacted by the improvement. Neighboring property owner approval will be on
a case-by-case basis as requested by the DRC. The DRC may allow an improvement even
if neighboring owners object to the improvement.
(4)
Some structural improvements may require a separate building permit from Douglas County.
Please check with the Douglas County building department before starting any improvements
on your property. The DRC is not responsible for compliance with building codes or
matters related to safety.
(5)
All attachments, improvements, construction, landscaping and alterations to residences
or other structures and property, or on the Common Elements within the Properties,
which have not been approved in writing by the DRC must be removed at the direction
of the DRC upon receiving its notification. A reasonable period of time for this action
to be accomplished by the homeowner is 14 days. Removal of non-approved items shall
be at the Owner's expense, and noncompliance will subject the Owner to further remedies
allowed the CAB by its governing documents.
(6)
In making improvements to the Property, homeowners are responsible for locating all
water, gas, sewer, electrical, cable television or other utility lines or easements.
Homeowners should not construct any improvements over such easements without the consent
of the utility involved and homeowners will be responsible for damage to any utility
lines. Call 811 for a utilities/wire locate before digging in your yard.
(7)

documents.title: Sec. 21-22. - General community standards.
documents.text:
Special note. Home builder representatives do not have authority to approve submittals.
Approvals are only granted by the DRC.
(b)
List of standards.
(1)
Accessory buildings. DRC approval is required. An accessory building is a freestanding structure, not
connected to the home. Any structure attached to the home or immediately adjacent
to the home is considered as an addition or expansion of the home and is guided by
the principles below. Materials, including roofing, shall match the home unless otherwise
approved. In general, accessory buildings should not exceed eight feet, six inches
in height.
a.
Utilities to an accessory building must be underground.
b.
Then-existing grading conditions shall be taken into account when placing an accessory
building and excavation may be needed to meet height restrictions.
c.
A playhouse that is less than 24 square feet and less than six feet in height shall
not be considered as an accessory building.
d.
Dog House. See subsection (b)(27) of this section, Dog House/Dog Run.
e.
See also subsection (b)(9) of this section, Backyard Utility Sheds and subsection
(b)(44) of this section, Gazebo/Pergola/Casita/Ramada.
(2)
Additions or expansions of home. DRC approval is required.
a.
Submittals must include two sets of detailed plans and specifications, including exterior
elevations of the existing structure, and any changes to roof lines.
b.
Plans shall be at a minimum scale of one inch equals 20 feet, and/or one-quarter inch
equals one foot for elevations.
c.
A plot plan must be included showing the revised footprint of the home and setbacks
to all property lines.
d.
All materials must match the existing materials on the home, or be of a complementary
nature.
(3)
Address numbers. DRC approval is not required if the following conditions are met: Numbers shall be
a contrasting color to the surface on which they are mounted, shall be readable from
the street, and shall not exceed eight inches in height.
(4)
House cooling equipment (A/C and window fans). DRC approval is not required before house cooling equipment can be installed.
a.
Window units installed at street level can only be located in a side yard or rear
yard, and must be screened from adjacent properties or view from the street.
b.
Installation of air conditioning equipment above street level is not permitted unless
totally concealed from view.
c.
Air conditioning units installed on-grade must be screened from adjacent properties
or view from the street. Units installed behind the front wing fence in a side yard
is considered appropriately screened from view.
d.

documents.title: Sec. 21-22. - General community standards.
documents.text:
Evaporative coolers must also be screened from adjacent properties or view from the
street. Exterior roof top installation is not permitted.
e.
See subsection (b)(54) of this section, Landscape screens.
(5)
Animals. See section 1-33 (6)—(11).
(6)
Antennas/satellite dish.
a.
Not more than two small satellite antennas may be installed and maintained on any
single property.
b.
Each antenna must be less than 40 inches in diameter and be placed as unobtrusively
as possible without compromising the availability of a signal. No guarantee or warranty
is made by the DRC that an adequate signal will remain undisturbed by vegetation or
improvements located on surrounding properties.
c.
Satellite antennas are restricted to the personal use of the property owner or lessee
of the individual residential property on which it is placed.
d.
Preferred locations of antennas are as follows:
1.
Inside the home, not visible from the street;
2.
Rear or side yard, below the level of a fence;
3.
Rear or side yard, mounted on the house, in the least visible location near roofline
eaves.
e.
Cabling to the device shall be installed as unobtrusively as possible, securely attached,
and painted to match the color of the structure where it is installed.
DRC approval is required only if the satellite dish is to be installed on the front
fascia of a home, regardless of use.
(7)
Artificial turf. All installations require DRC approval and will be considered on a case-by-case basis.
a.
The DRC will evaluate the use of artificial turf in the landscape design and consider
the square footage of artificial turf in combination with the square footage of live
coverage.
b.
Submissions must include the following materials and information:
1.
Plot plan with location of turf including distances to property lines, easements,
sidewalk, driveway and drainage ways, square footage of turf installation and percentage
of artificial turf coverage in yard.
2.
Product specification sheet that includes details on color, materials, pile height,
face weight of backing and infill requirements.
3.
Product specifications for all aggregate base materials, infill materials, seaming
materials and adhesives.
4.
Copy of manufacturer's warranty for all materials, workmanship, and installers warranty
statement for workmanship for construction for a minimum of one year workmanship warranty.
5.
Detailed product photos are required and DRC reserves the right to request a 12-inch
by 12-inch sample of the exact artificial turf if photos are not clear.
c.
Please note that all installations must appear natural at all times.
d.

documents.title: Sec. 21-22. - General community standards.
documents.text:
Any deviation from a natural look due to improper installation or lack of maintenance
will be in violation of these rules and require repair or removal.
e.
As Colorado water laws and product market availability change over time, DRC reserves
the right to revisit guidelines.
f.
Product improvements may occur at any time. The Design Review Committee reserves the
right to review new products and solutions as they become available and may modify
the artificial turf specifications and guidelines as needed.
g.
Artificial turf is not allowed in tree lawns.
h.
Turf may not contain lead or PFAS chemicals.
i.
Specialized surfaces for putting greens, play areas, bocce ball and other uses are
allowed in rear yards only.
j.
Artificial turf may not be placed in drainage swells or near discharge from sump pumps.
k.
Antibacterial infill required for areas intended for pet use. Silica sand allowed
in non-pet areas.
l.
Six inches of compacted native soil topped with weed barrier is required.
m.
A minimum of a four-inch sub-base aggregate on top of the weed barrier and compacted
