to 95 percent is additionally required.
n.
For the sub-base aggregate, two inches of larger aggregate topped with two inches
of compacted breeze is preferred for optimal drainage.
o.
Infill per square foot should be a minimum two pounds per square foot, worked halfway
into depth of turf.
p.
Seam tape and glue is required on all seams. Seams may not be readily visible.
q.
Front yard installations.
1.
Artificial turf cannot exceed 30 percent of the square footage of the front yard and
the front yard must still include a combination of grasses, shrubs, perennials, annuals,
and required trees.
2.
Artificial turf must be interior to the lot and buffered with live plant material.
3.
Live plant material must be included between house foundation and turf.
4.
Turf pile is required to have color variation (field green/olive, green/clover, green/tan,
field green/apple, etc.).
5.
Pile height must be a minimum 1.75 inches.
6.
Face weight (density of the fibers on top of the backing) must be a minimum 60-ounce.
7.
Artificial turf backing required to have minimum hole punches every four inches for
drainage, completely perforated backing preferred.
8.
Required to have an element of "thatch" and needs to be brown or beige, or tan, or
a color that is different from the turf piles.
9.
Artificial turf is required to be a minimum of five feet from side property lines,
three feet from back of sidewalk, and may not be installed over trench drains.
10.

documents.title: Sec. 21-22. - General community standards.
documents.text:
Turf must be installed so that the tips of the piles face toward the primary street
frontage of the lot.
11.
15-foot maximum width preferred to reduce seams.
12.
Fix turf down around the perimeter with edging, bend-a-board or similar product. Secure
a minimum of every six inches with five-inch or six-inch nongalvanized nails or turf
staples—recommend every four inches at edges adjacent to concrete to avoid lift at
edges and tripping hazard.
r.
Rear yard installations.
1.
Artificial turf cannot exceed 30 percent of the square footage of the rear yard and
the rear yard must still include a combination of grasses, shrubs, perennials, annuals,
and required trees.
2.
Artificial turf must be interior to the lot and buffered with live plant material
to ensure adequate visual screening toward community.
3.
Turf pile is required to have color variation (field green/olive, green/clover, green/tan,
field green/apple, etc.)
4.
Artificial turf backing required to have minimum hole punches every four inches for
drainage, completely perforated backing preferred.
5.
Required to have an element of "thatch" and needs to be brown or beige, or tan, or
a color that is different from the turf piles unless turf is specialized surface for
putting greens, bocce ball and other similar type uses.
6.
Artificial turf is required to be a minimum of five feet from side and rear property
lines.
s.
Artificial turf maintenance.
1.
Artificial turf will fade over time. Faded turf will require replacement. Color fade
between older product and replacement product may not be visible.
2.
Power broom maintenance is required when artificial turf becomes matted. Recommend
power broom and power wash once a year to stand fibers up and deep clean product.
(8)
Awnings. DRC approval is required.
a.
In general, awnings must be an enhancement to the architectural style of the home
and of a color and material complementary with the home.
b.
Awnings are not permitted to become faded, tattered, torn, or otherwise fall into
disrepair.
(9)
Backyard utility sheds. DRC approval is required.
a.
Backyard utility sheds will be considered based on size, height, color, relationship
to size of lot, relationship to landscaping, and setbacks from property lines.
b.
Material, style and color, including roofing, are appropriate for the architectural
style of the home unless otherwise approved.
c.
In general, backyard utility sheds should not exceed an overall height of eight feet,
six inches. The shed footprint maximum is 150 square feet. If the shed footprint is

documents.title: Sec. 21-22. - General community standards.
documents.text:
150 square feet or less and the roof pitch is at a slope of 4:12 and the eight-foot,
six-inch height is exceeded, the DRC will evaluate on a case-by-case basis for approval.
d.
Then-existing grading conditions shall be considered when placing an accessory building
and excavation may be needed to meet height restrictions.
e.
Utilities to a backyard utility shed must be underground.
f.
Backyard utility sheds must be screened with landscape plantings that at full growth
reach a minimum of half the shed wall height. Evergreen plantings are strongly recommended
for four-season screening and visual interest.
g.
Backyard utility sheds are strongly recommended to be located outside easements.
h.
No variances will be granted on high visibility lots, icon lots or enhanced lots.
i.
See subsection (b)(54) of this section, Landscape Screens.
(10)
Balconies. The term "balcony" means a horizontal extension of an adjacent floor cantilevered
outside the exterior enclosure of a building that is not a roof, roof terrace, plaza,
porch or deck and is typically not enclosed except for a railing. DRC approval is
required for all balcony additions, alterations or renovations.
a.
All requests are considered on a case-by-case basis including a variety of factors,
such as the available space on the lot, site conditions, proximity to neighbors, and
compatibility with neighboring properties. The DRC reserves the right to limit the
size and location of certain modifications.
b.
Balconies are open to public view and shall be kept neat and clean.
c.
No balcony shall be enclosed, covered or altered from the design originally approved
for installation by the builder.
d.
Balconies shall not be used as storage areas. Items such as household appliances,
household furniture, mechanical equipment, tires, paint, cleaning supplies shall not
be stored on the balcony. Bicycles may be stored as long as contained behind the railing
and not immediately visible from the community.
e.
Unless permitted elsewhere in these rules, nothing is allowed to be hung, displayed
or exposed on the exterior of balcony railings. No personal belongings can protrude
over the edge of the balcony. This prohibition includes without limitation flags,
laundry, clothing, rugs, signs, awnings, canopies, shutters, planter boxes, or any
other items.
f.
Furniture that is deemed appropriate for outdoor use is permitted on balconies. Such
furniture shall be of sufficient durability and structural integrity that its continued
exposure to the elements will not degrade the appearance of the unit.
g.

documents.title: Sec. 21-22. - General community standards.
documents.text:
Animal feeders and facilities shall not be placed on balconies. Bird feeders and animal
facilities, such as litter boxes, feeding devices, shelters on balconies are prohibited.
h.
No pet shall be left unattended on a balcony. Pet excrement must be disposed of immediately
or Animal Services will be called.
i.
Portable BBQ grills, unless disallowed by any rental agreement or other document are
permitted and shall be covered when not in use and kept in good working condition.
(11)
Barbecue grills, portable and permanent.
a.
PORTABLE, freestanding grills do not require DRC approval provided they are kept in
rear yards for primary use. They may be used at the front of the home temporarily,
but must be returned to the rear yard or garage after each use.
b.
PERMANENT outdoor grills require DRC approval. Built-in outdoor cooking facilities
of any kind must be submitted to the DRC and must include specifications as to size,
height, location, materials, colors, and fuel supply.
(12)
Basketball backboards, portable and permanent. DRC approval is not required provided the following conditions are met:
a.
Portable hoops in front of the home.
1.
Free passage of vehicles and pedestrians must be maintained at all times. Portable
hoops cannot be placed in the public right-of-way, on streets, sidewalks, alleys,
or placed so as to impede access to a garage or driveway.
2.
Portable hoops are not allowed to fall into disrepair, such as a ripped or missing
net, chipped paint, or similar unsightly conditions.
b.
Permanent mounted backboards and hoops.
1.
A separate, freestanding pole is preferred, black in color, with a coupler release
that would allow the pole to be removed.
2.
Basketball backboards mounted to a garage or other portion of the home may void your
home warranty and are strongly discouraged.
3.
Permanently mounted hoops are not allowed to fall into disrepair, such as a ripped
or missing net, chipped paint, or similar unsightly condition.
Exception. Rear yard basketball courts require DRC approval and must be submitted similar to
a landscaping plan, showing the size, location, setbacks, and impact to rear yard
landscaping. No lighted rear yard courts are permitted.
(13)
Birdbaths. DRC approval is not required provided no more than one birdbath is placed in the
front or rear yard, is not greater in height than three feet, and is a color complementary
to the home.
(14)
Birdhouses and birdfeeders. DRC approval is not required for rear yard installation provided all the following
conditions are met:
a.

documents.title: Sec. 21-22. - General community standards.
documents.text:
The number of birdhouses is limited to three, and the maximum size of any one birdhouse
does not exceed one foot by two feet by two feet.
b.
If the birdhouse is pole-mounted, the height of the pole does not exceed six feet.
c.
All birdhouses and the ground surrounding them shall be kept in a clean and sanitary
condition.
Exception: DRC approval is required for any front yard installation of a birdhouse.
(15)
Boats. See subsection (b)(76) of this section, Recreational vehicles, and subsection (b)(108)
of this section, Watercraft.
(16)
Business activity from a residence. Home-based businesses are permitted provided the following conditions are met:
a.
No external evidence of the business can be discerned.
b.
No unreasonable inconvenience is created for neighboring properties.
c.
No more than one vehicle at a time is parked at the residence by a person using the
in-home business services.
Exception: No residential property is allowed to be used for short-term, vacation
property commonly referred to as VRBO (Vacation Rental By Owner) or other similar
acronym, or for "bed and breakfast" type lodgings. See also subsection (b)(55) of
this section, leasing/rental of properties.
(17)
Camper, mounted and tow-behind. See section 1-37 .
(18)
Car covers. DRC approval is required. Garages are intended to house vehicles, including any vehicle
that is not being used for any significant length of time or for which a cover is
required to protect its finish. In general, the cover must be of a neutral color,
well maintained, and specifically manufactured for the vehicle it is covering.
(19)
Carports. Carports are not permitted.
(20)
Clothes lines, clothes dryers. DRC approval is not required provided the following conditions are met:
a.
Clothes lines or clothes drying structures must be temporary and taken down after
each use.
b.
Such facility is only permitted in a rear yard, and shall be placed a minimum of five
feet away from any side or rear property line.
c.
Clothing and other materials shall be taken in as soon as dry and, in any event, not
permitted to hang longer than 24 hours.
(21)
Commercial vehicles, oversized vehicles, emergency service vehicles. It is understood that some residents may use a company-owned vehicle as a condition
of their employment. It is the intent of this subsection to provide a framework in
which certain vehicles may be parked within the community at a residence and which
types of vehicles will not be permitted to be parked or stored at a residence:
a.
An "oversized vehicle" is one that cannot be parked inside the garage.
b.

documents.title: Sec. 21-22. - General community standards.
documents.text:
A "commercial vehicle" is somewhat objective but generally includes trucks with one
or more of the following: towing capacity in excess of one ton, significant commercial
lettering on its exterior, materials or tools exposed in the back of a truck bed,
any truck with a "flat bed" or "stake bed," any vehicle intended as a "bus" for transport
of people on a commercial basis, and any vehicle falling under the Colorado Department
of Highways definition of a commercial vehicle.
c.
An "emergency service vehicle" is defined as a vehicle with one or more of the following:
used by the property owner who is a bona fide member of a fire department (volunteer
or otherwise) or law enforcement agency, used by a property owner who is employed
by an emergency service provider (as defined by C.R.S.), or a vehicle which bears
an official emblem or other visible designation of an emergency service provider.
The emergency service vehicle must be able to be parked without obstructing emergency
access or blocking an adjacent property owner from accessing their property in a normal
manner.
d.
Oversized, commercial, and emergency vehicles parked at a residence must meet the
following conditions:
1.
Only one such vehicle is permitted to be parked at the residence.
2.
The vehicle must have a gross weight of 10,000 pounds or less.
3.
Exposed tools, racks, ladders, equipment, and all other similar materials must be
removed from the vehicle daily if the vehicle is parked outside the garage.
4.
No vehicle with more than a conventional two-axle configuration is permitted to be
parked at a residence, with the exception of a "dually" which may have a wider rear
axle than a conventional pick-up truck.
5.
Any vehicle wherein the top of the cab or truck bed exceeds six feet, six inches from
the ground is prohibited from being parked at a residence with the exceptions of temporary
loading or unloading of materials at the residence, or of an emergency vehicle providing
aid to residents.
(22)
Compost. DRC approval is not required if the following conditions are met:
a.
Containers are only permitted in rear yards and must be at least five feet from any
side or rear yard property line.
b.
Underground composting is not permitted.
c.
Compost containers should be commercially available plastic containers designed for
the home composter, be no greater than 48 inches in any dimension, and have a secure
lid.
d.
Open-topped wire or board pens are not permitted.
e.
Composting odors shall be controlled and not allowed to become a nuisance to adjacent
property owners.
(23)

documents.title: Sec. 21-22. - General community standards.
documents.text:
Decks. A "deck" is an unenclosed structure attached or adjacent to the exterior wall of
the building and which is supported by the grade below. DRC approval for all new deck
construction and deck expansion is required. Some structural improvements may require
a separate building permit from Douglas County. Please check with the Douglas County
building department before starting any improvements on your property.
a.
Decks shall not appear tacked on and consideration shall be given to the connection
of a deck extension and the existing architecture. Decks must maintain the overall
form and be a natural extension of the architecture. Decks and balconies must be integrated
into the building using similar materials and detailing.
b.
Deck supports must have a substantial scale that visually anchors the deck to the
ground.
1.
Stair landing supports are required to be a minimum of six inches by six inches and
shall be finished to match the architectural style of the house.
2.
On Enhanced and Icon lots, deck support columns are required to be a minimum of 18
inches by 18 inches and at a minimum, lower-level deck columns need to be full stone
wrapped to match architectural style and color palette of the house. Column may transition
from stone to other materials when it reaches the main level.
c.
Upper deck expansions should not exceed two-thirds of the width of the home.
d.
Natural wood decks shall be permitted (provided the wood is sealed or stained and
maintained to prevent discoloration or degradation). The use of synthetic recycled
decking material such as TREX® decking is encouraged.
e.
Deck expansions shall not be closer than ten feet from the rear property line and/or
five feet from the side property line when adjacent to another single-family lot.
"Adjacent" shall also include properties with a shared rear property line. Consideration
may be give if the deck extension is not more than 24 inches from ground level at
any point, and is not covered.
f.
Deck expansions shall not encroach upon any easement or setback without a variance
and written permission from the applicable easement holder(s) and/or Douglas County.
Refer to Douglas County for easement and setback requirements.
(24)
Deck covers. DRC approval is required. The submittal must include the type of materials, color
of materials, truss system if applicable, height, amount of deck to be covered, and
photos or renderings demonstrating compatibility with the architectural style of the
home.
(25)
Deck, enclosed. DRC approval is required. The submittal must include the type of materials, color

documents.title: Sec. 21-22. - General community standards.
documents.text:
of materials, height of walls, amount of deck to be enclosed, door and window materials,
and photos or renderings demonstrating compatibility with the architectural style
of the home.
(26)
Disability accessibility. DRC approval is required. This shall include such items as ramps, railings, landings,
lifts, and hard surface alterations. Review of the items shall take into consideration
such things as integration into the landscape and compatibility with the architecture
of the home, colors and materials of the improvement, and potential screening if necessary.
(27)
Doghouses and outdoor pet areas.
a.
DRC approval is required for all outdoor pet areas, except as noted below.
1.
All outdoor pet areas must be located in the side or rear yard, abutting the home
and located behind yard fencing. Outdoor pet areas located in a side yard adjacent
to a corner sidewalk, street, common area or open space are not preferred, and may
require additional screening if no other location on a property is suitable.
2.
All outdoor pet areas must be substantially screened from view by evergreen plantings
and grasses to provide four-season screening.
3.
All outdoor pet areas are required to be kept in a clean, sanitary condition, and
not allowed to fall into disrepair.
4.
Sonic pet barriers are not permitted.
b.
Dog runs are fenced, open-top areas that may not exceed 200 square feet or 25 percent
of the rear yard, whichever is less.
1.
Dog runs must be constructed of fencing material that matches the lot-line fencing
and is stained to match lot-line fencing or black powder-coated steel not to exceed
48 inches in height from grade at any one point.
2.
Pet mesh screen is required to be two-inch by four-inch galvanized welded wire mesh
used on the inside of the fence and not exceeding the top rail in height and reaching
ground level.
3.
Metal chain link enclosures or covers (tarps, blankets, sheets, etc.) are not permitted.
Dog runs are limited to one dog run per property.
c.
Kennels are free standing panel system kennels and may not exceed 50 square feet and
are a maximum of 48 inches in height.
1.
All kennel panels must be either painted to match the body color of the house or black
ornamental steel framed with wood painted to match the body color of the house for
a custom look.
2.
Dog kennels are limited to one dog kennel per property and are not allowed for commercial
purposes.
d.
One doghouse per yard does not require DRC approval provided the following conditions
are met:
1.
It does not exceed 48 inches in any direction;
2.
It is a color compatible with the home;
3.

documents.title: Sec. 21-22. - General community standards.
documents.text:
It is kept in a clean, sanitary condition, and not allowed to fall into disrepair.
4.
Required to be a minimum of ten feet for all property lines.
e.
Invisible fencing is allowed. All wiring must be buried no less than six inches inside
the lot line. Regardless of the method of restraint used, pet owners are responsible
for assuring that their pets do not run free. Pet owners are liable for any damage
to persons or property caused by their pets.
(28)
Doors and windows.
a.
DRC approval is not required if the following conditions are met:
1.
An exact replacement in design, size, and color is being installed to replace existing;
2.
No modification to framing is needed; and
3.
Storm doors that are "full view" or "split door" styles with the frame color neutral
to match the architectural style of the home and trim color.
b.
All other exterior doors (pedestrian, security, garage) and window changes or additions
require DRC approval.
1.
Considerations for approval include but are not limited to neighborhood consistency,
window/door design, color, style, etc.
2.
Security doors should minimize vertical bars, preference is no more than two, and
must compliment the architectural style of the house.
3.
All windows shall be trimmed with a material appropriate to the architectural style
of the home on all building elevations.
4.
Replacement windows must be full glass or match the architectural style of the window
being replaced.
5.
Window trim design and color on all building elevations must match.
(29)
Drainage, general.
a.
Sterling Ranch Master Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions requires
that there be no interference with the established drainage pattern on any property.
The established drainage pattern means the drainage pattern as engineered and constructed
by the home builder prior to (or in some cases, immediately following) conveyance
of title from the home builder to the individual homeowner.
b.
Any owner or resident who changes the existing grading or drainages may void warranties
applicable to affected components of the home and shall be liable for all costs and
expenses of repairing such changes, or any costs, liabilities, damages or causes of
action arising out of such changes.
c.
When installing your landscaping, it is very important to ensure that water drains
away from the foundation of the house (but not onto neighboring properties) and that
the flow patterns prevent water from flowing under or against the house foundation,
walkways, sidewalks, and driveways into the street.
d.

documents.title: Sec. 21-22. - General community standards.
documents.text:
Landscaping should conform to the established drainage pattern.
e.
Adverse effects to adjacent properties will not be tolerated.
f.
The DRC is not responsible in any way for changes made to grading and/or drainage
while installing landscaping or other improvements. All County and State code requirements
are to be followed and are the sole responsibility of the homeowner. Any change to
the drainage pattern that causes damage to any downstream party is totally and solely
the responsibility of the property owner who made the grade change or who permitted
the grade change to be made by a contractor, vendor, or other entity working on the
property.
g.
The DRC may require a report from a Colorado registered civil engineer with a P.E.
stamped plot plan and letter stating that drainage will not be changed in an adverse
way as part of landscaping or improvement plan approval for plans, including, but
not limited to:
1.
Patios;
2.
Covered decks;
3.
Sport courts;
4.
Raised or bermed planting beds.
(30)
Drainage, downspouts. Tip downs or downspout extensions are to be kept in good working order, and kept
in the down position at all times except when maintenance activities are taking place.
If a property owner wishes to bury the downspout extension and move the discharge
point, DRC approval is required. The applicant will need to demonstrate how the changed
drainage pattern will affect adjacent property owners or how it will affect open space
or landscaped tracts. The DRC will require a report form a Colorado registered civil
engineer describing the changes to drainage and alternate drainage patterns to be
established.
(31)
Driveways. DRC approval is required for expansion, modification, or resurfacing of any driveway.
a.
Expanding a driveway to provide additional parking spaces on the property will not
be approved.
b.
Extension or widening of the driveway may not be within setbacks or easements, must
be attached to the driveway, and cannot alter drainage.
c.
In a case for side turn in garage entry, extensions will be considered on a case-by-case
basis. Extensions are not permitted in easements, setback, and/or swales.
d.
Additional landscaping will be required to screen the neighboring views as deemed
necessary by the DRC.
(32)
Equipment storage. Lawn maintenance equipment, or other maintenance tools and equipment (including but
not limited to snow shovels, pooper scoopers, lawn mowers, etc.), shall be in stored
in the garage, a backyard utility shed, or out of community sight in the backyard
behind the wing fence.
a.

documents.title: Sec. 21-22. - General community standards.
documents.text:
Bags of ice melt, mulch, potting soil, seeds, and other garden hoses should be stored
neatly when not in active use. Options for storing garden hoses include placing them
in a container, on a reel, neatly coiled behind shrubbery, in the garage or in the
backyard behind the wing fence.
b.
Garden hoses should be stored neatly when not in active use. Options for storing garden
hoses include placing them in a container, on a reel, neatly coiled behind shrubbery,
in the garage or in the backyard behind the wing fence.
c.
Recreational equipment (including but not limited to paddle boards, kayaks, canoes,
hockey goals, soccer goals, etc.), shall be kept stored out of sight when not in active
use, preferably in the garage or backyard utility shed.
(33)
Evaporative cooling systems. See subsection (b)(4) of this section, Air conditioning equipment.
(34)
Fencing, styles and maintenance.
a.
A general statement. The CAB has adopted, or may adopt in the future, certain fence
styles appropriate to specific uses, including, but not limited to, village theme
fencing, perimeter fencing, lot line fencing, arterial fencing, park fencing, and
others of a similar nature. In addition, approved fence colors have been determined
for each type of fencing.
b.
Residents are required to keep fencing in good repair and to use the approved fence
color in the process of maintaining any fence.
c.
Interior lot-line fencing is not required.
d.
Please review section 21-23 , Fencing standards. Any proposed fence type that varies from the fence standards
described in section 21-23 , Fencing standards, requires DRC approval.
e.
Fencing may have been constructed inside certain property boundaries. In general,
residents are responsible for maintenance and repair on any fence located INSIDE their
property lines, and are jointly responsible with other parties if fencing is placed
ON property lines.
(35)
Firewood. Outdoor fire pits, chimeneas, grills and similar equipment occasionally use wood
as a fuel source. No wood or other stockpile is allowed if visible from a street or
from any other lot. DRC approval is not required for storage of one cord of firewood
or less, which is kept neatly stacked, does not interfere with drainage patterns,
and is not visible from a street or from any other lot. Property owners are cautioned
to determine the source of firewood so that insects (pine beetles, ash borers, etc.)
are not imported into the community, thereby causing irreparable damage. If any such
insect infestation is discovered, the property owner is required to treat it immediately.
(36)

documents.title: Sec. 21-22. - General community standards.
documents.text:
Fire pits. DRC approval is required for any permanent outdoor fireplace or fire pit. Portable,
commercially available fire pits, chimeneas, etc., located in the rear yard a minimum
of five feet from any property line do not require DRC approval. Outdoor gas fire
pits must be installed and operated in accordance with all applicable local and state
safety standards and guidelines. If the gas fire pit utilizes natural gas, all applicable
permits and permissions for the installation of the natural gas line must be obtained
from Douglas County and the appropriate utility provider.
(37)
Flags. The only flags allowed to be displayed on the front of the home are the United States
flag, the Colorado flag, and certain permitted military service flags. The maximum
size of any one flag shall not exceed four feet by six feet.
(38)
Flag holders, flagpoles. Bracket flag holders installed on the surface of the home do not require DRC approval
provided that the size of the bracket holder is commensurate with the size of the
flag permitted in the subsection (b)(37) of this section. DRC approval is required
for freestanding flagpoles and any separate nighttime illumination of a flag.
(39)
Garage sales. Up to three garage sales per year, not exceeding two days for each event, may be
conducted at any one residence. All materials to be sold at a garage sale must be
the private property of the property owner (e.g., not items acquired for the purposes
of resale). Garage sales shall be held in compliance with all municipal requirements.
Signage advertising a garage sale is permitted provided it complies with temporary
sign rules.
(40)
Garbage containers. See subsection (b)(101) of this section, Trash containers, and subsection (b)(102)
of this section, Trash enclosures.
(41)
Gardens; flowers. Must meet the criteria of sections 9-74 and 9-143 .
(42)
Gardens; vegetable. DRC approval is required and will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis with consideration
of location, lot conditions, size, materials, and views from neighboring properties.
a.
Vegetable gardens and raised beds of reasonable size and height relative to yard size
are encouraged and must be located in the rear or side yards.
b.
Vertical gardens will be considered on a case-by-case basis.
c.
Vegetable garden boxes shall:
1.
Complement the architectural style of the house;
2.
Be screened from view of adjacent homes and public areas;
3.
Not cover more than 50 percent of the rear or side yard;
4.
Be maintained in good condition and have all dead growth removed at the end of the
growing season; and
5.

documents.title: Sec. 21-22. - General community standards.
documents.text:
Be located a minimum of five feet from all property lines.
(43)
Gates.
a.
Additional gates are considered on a case-by-case basis and require DRC approval.
Homeowners will be responsible for the cost of mitigating any damage to the open space
caused by the installation of such a gate, including, but not limited to, that caused
by concentrated foot traffic. Gates must meet all community gate specifications and
be kept in good repair. No modifications to open space or common areas are permitted,
including, but not limited to, mowing of vegetation or placement of pavers, rock,
crushed granite or similar materials in order to create a path from the common area
to the owner's yard. Additional gates within side and rear property line concrete
fencing that are street facing are not allowed.
b.
Requests will only be considered for additional gates located within:
1.
Front wing fencing;
2.
Interior perimeter fencing between two homes if both neighbors are in agreement (signatures
required on submittal plan drawings); or
3.
Rear perimeter fencing when adjacent to CAB-owned common space with CAB permission.
(44)
Gazebos, pergolas, casitas, ramadas, etc. DRC approval is required. Maximum height is ten feet, six inches from floor level,
or 11 feet, six inches from grade level. The structure must be integrated into the
landscape plan. The DRC will require information regarding the location of the structure,
its proximity to adjacent properties, setbacks from lot lines and utility easements,
and the square footage of the structure. Submittals must include material and color
specifications, dimensions of the structure, a plan showing dimensions from the structure
to property lines and the house, and renderings or photos of a finished structure.
(45)
Grading and grade changes. See subsection (b)(29) of this section, Drainage, general, and (b)(30) of this section,
Drainage, downspouts.
(46)
Greenhouses. DRC approval is required. See subsection (b)(1) of this section, Accessory buildings.
(47)
Holiday displays. Holiday displays (which excludes lighting) should be tasteful in nature, with consideration
for your neighbors. This includes limiting roof top displays and excessive noise.
a.
Holiday displays (which excludes lighting) shall be:
1.
Holiday and seasonally appropriate;
2.
Permitted 30 days prior to a holiday and must be removed within 30 days after the
holiday;
3.
Turned off between the hours of 10:00 p.m. and 8:00 a.m. for any noise or sound effects,
such as music, generators, inflation systems, or similar items.
b.

documents.title: Sec. 21-22. - General community standards.
documents.text:
For rules and regulations regarding seasonal decorative lighting refer to section 21-22 (b)(56), Lighting, seasonal decorative lighting.
c.
At the sole discretion of the CAB, removal dates of holiday displays may be extended
due to extreme weather conditions or other factors.
(48)
Hot tubs, outdoor spas, outdoor saunas. Hot tubs, outdoor spas, outdoor saunas. DRC approval is required.
a.
These items should be designed as an integral part of a deck, patio area and/or the
landscaping, are only permitted in rear yards, may not be located in utility easements,
and must be a minimum of five feet from all property lines.
b.
These items should be installed in a way so as not to be openly visible to adjacent
property owners. Screening of the facilities is required at time of installation.
Preference is for landscape screens combined with live plant material that reaches
a minimum height equivalent to the height of the facility. See subsection (b)(54)
of this section, Landscape screens.
c.
Preference is that these items not be located in a side yard adjacent to a corner
sidewalk, street, common area or open space, and may require additional screening
if no other location on a property is suitable.
(49)
Inoperable vehicles. See section 1-37 .
(50)
Irrigation systems. See sections 9-74 and 9-143 .
(51)
Kennels. See subsection (b)(27) of this section, Doghouses and dog runs.
(52)
Landscaping submittals. See chapter 5 , article II.
(53)
Landscape maintenance standards. Landscaping is to be kept healthy. Generally, this means the following practices
are applicable:
a.
Turf is mowed regularly and does not exceed four inches in height.
b.
Planting beds, driveways, sidewalks, and turf areas are weed free, and turf is green.
c.
Dead branches are pruned out of shrubs and trees; dead plants are removed and disposed
of properly. Dead trees must be replaced in order to maintain the minimum requirements.
d.
Trees in tree lawns, as they grow towards maturity, are required to have branches
removed up to eight feet above the ground. This is for safety of passers-by and provides
an open visual corridor so pedestrians can be seen on walks or crossing the street.
e.
Trees are maintained in a natural shape after pruning.
f.
Insect infestations are treated quickly and effectively to prevent spreading.
g.
Areas not covered by plant materials remain covered by mulch materials.
(54)
Landscape screens. DRC approval is required.
a.
Five-foot maximum overall height for exposed landscape screen from grade. We encourage

documents.title: Sec. 21-22. - General community standards.
documents.text:
plantings around base of screens and, therefore, will allow a six-foot maximum overall
height from grade if plantings are installed around the screen base.
b.
Eight-foot maximum overall width for landscape screens. Multiple screens may not be
attached at corners, at edges, to sheds, or to the house. Must be freestanding in
the rear or side yard.
c.
Landscape screens are only allowed in rear or side yards and are not allowed in easements.
A maximum of three screens are allowed if lot square footage permits. The DRC will
review on a case-by-case basis.
d.
Landscape screens must have 30 percent required transparency.
e.
Materials must be constructed of a minimum of 50 percent top grade redwood or cedar,
or high grade Trex material or an equivalent in a color complementary to the home.
If other materials like masonry or metal are used, they must match the architectural
style of the house. Vinyl is not permitted.
f.
Landscape screens may be either painted or stained. Paint colors must match or complement
house colors. Stain must match fence stain (Sherwin Williams #3002 Belvedere Tan)
or a natural stain. Wood grain is allowed to show through.
g.
If stained with a natural stain, the homeowner must sign an agreement that the stain
will be reapplied every two years or the homeowner will be required to take down the
landscape screen.
h.
Landscape screens may be used to screen hot tub areas on two sides only.
i.
All screens must be maintained and kept in good condition or will be required to be
taken down.
(55)
Leasing/rental of properties. Leasing or renting a residential property for less than 30 consecutive days is prohibited.
All leases and rental agreements must be written and the lessee/renter must be advised
that the property is subject to documents and to the standards contained within this
article, as they may be amended from time to time. The property owner shall provide
written notification to the CAB of a current mailing address in the event the property
owner does not occupy the home.
(56)
Lighting.
a.
General. DRC approval is required to modify or add exterior lighting. This includes, but is
not limited to, motion detector spotlights, security lighting, landscape lighting,
architectural accent lighting, decorative lighting, ballasted fixtures, additional
lighting at doors or windows, etc. "Cut sheets" (product description, specifications
and illustrations) must be submitted to the Design Review Committee for each type
of fixture proposed for review.
1.
All exterior lighting must be compliant with these Rules and Douglas County's "Dark

documents.title: Sec. 21-22. - General community standards.
documents.text:
Skies" guidelines (https://www.douglas.co.us/planning/development- review-regulations/development-info-assistance/development-outdoor-lighting/).
To minimize effects of light pollution, lighting should:
•
Only be on when needed;
•
Only light the area that needs it;
•
Be no brighter than necessary.
2.
Lighting techniques that "up light" buildings or landscape and shine light into the
sky shall not be permitted.
3.
Exterior light fixtures must be fully shielded so that the lamp bulb or LED cluster
is not visible from property lines or the street, have a warm white light with a color
temperature of 3,000 Kelvin or less (2,700 Kelvin is preferred).
4.
Exterior lighting must be directed downward, so that the light cone does not cause
glare to adjacent properties or on to the street.
5.
At any time, unduly bright lights that create a nuisance to adjacent owners or lighting
complaints received may be re-evaluated.
6.
Utilizing photocell and timers to control switching of site lighting is highly encouraged.
7.
Architectural accent lighting includes appropriately spaced, recessed lighting strategically
placed to enhance architectural elements such as columns. Architectural accent lighting
shall not flash, or change colors, etc.
8.
Exterior lighting that lights an outdoor living space (such as a patio, porch, or
deck) shall light only the livable space and not extend beyond that area.
9.
Exterior eave/rake lighting systems such as Gemstone, Jellyfish, or other similar
companies/products are not permitted.
b.
Decorative Lighting. This type of lighting is installed to provide low-level lighting to create ambiance
for rear outside use areas.
1.
Lighting must consist of café, globe, or lit rope style lights. LED string lights/cords,
"holiday decoration style" string lights, and other forms of lighting are not allowed.
2.
Lighting must be strung under or on structural elements such as pergolas, gazebos,
decks/patio covers or comparable structural items in the rear yard with a limited
number of lights so as not to over light the area or impact surrounding property owners.
3.
Decorative lighting does NOT require DRC approval if:
i.
It is located under a roofed cover above a rear deck or rear patio;
ii.
Light cone does not cause glare to adjacent properties or onto the street; and
iii.
It is a warm white light, with a color temperature of 3,000 Kelvin or less (2,700
Kelvin preferred).
4.
All outdoor decorative lighting must be turned off by 10:00 p.m.
c.
Landscape lighting. This type of lighting is intended to provide low-level illumination at ground level

documents.title: Sec. 21-22. - General community standards.
documents.text:
to landscaping features, sidewalks or other similar low improvements.
1.
Landscape lighting in general should only be used to provide such a level of illumination
as necessary to provide for safe movement through outdoor areas of the property such
as walking paths, retaining walls, steps, etc. All landscape lights should be kept
to a minimum.
2.
Up-lighting is not an approved Dark Sky lighting type and is not permitted.
3.
Lighting must be warm white with a color temperature of 3,000 Kelvin or less (2,700
Kelvin is preferred). Colored lighting is not allowed.
4.
Solar in-ground lighting is permitted in front and rear yards without DRC approval
provided that:
i.
No light fixture shall exceed 36 inches in height.
ii.
Placement of fixtures is limited to edges of walks, driveways, and planting beds.
iii.
The light "cone" is downward facing and does not cause glare onto surrounding properties
or the street.
iv.
No more than eight such fixtures shall be permitted in the front yard.
5.
In the rear transition zone, solar in-ground down lighting provided that it is less
than 36 inches in height, is placed along edges of walks or planting beds and cone
of light is downward facing not causing glare off of property is allowed. See section 9-176 (2) for additional transition zone guidelines.
6.
All landscape lighting, with the exception of solar in-ground lighting, must be turned
off by 10:00 p.m.
d.
Seasonal decorative lighting. This type of lighting is temporary string lighting intended to be a tasteful display
of seasonally appropriate decoration.
1.
Holiday lighting should be installed in a manner that does not create any light trespass
beyond the property boundaries or glare onto surrounding properties.
2.
Use low wattage string lights, LED preferred.
3.
Holiday lighting may be of various colors and patterns and is permitted to blink,
flash, chase, or strobe.
4.
Install and energize holiday lighting from October 15 through January 25 after which
all lighting and light installation clips are required to be removed.
5.
At the sole discretion of the CAB, removal dates for seasonal decorative lighting
may be extended due to extreme weather conditions or other factors. During this time
lighting may not be energized.
6.
All holiday lighting must be turned off by 10:00 p.m.
e.
Security Lighting. This type of lighting is installed for area lighting for security purposes. It includes
wall-mounted fixture lighting, as well as floodlights and spotlights to illuminate
portions of the lot for security purposes.
1.

documents.title: Sec. 21-22. - General community standards.
documents.text:
Security lighting must be directed at the ground and house, whereby the light cone
stays within the property boundaries and the light source does not cause glare toother
properties.
2.
Lighting, except for that on the front of the home and facing the public street, cannot
be on 24/7, must be on photocell control and motion activated. Once activated by motion,
the lighting setting must be adjusted so it cannot stay on longer than five minutes.
3.
Spotlights, floodlights, or other similar lights used for security applications may
only be used on front porches, over garage doors, or over rear porches/decks.
(57)
Mailboxes. All mail is delivered to neighborhood box units (NBUs), which are owned and maintained
by the United States Post Office. Your initial keys for a mailbox can be obtained
from your builder's sales representative. Please do not use the NBUs for signs or
advertising. Replacement keys may need to be purchased at USPS.
(58)
Motorcycles. See section 1-37 .
(59)
Motor homes. See section 1-37 .
(60)
Motor vehicles. See section 1-37 .
(61)
Motor vehicle repairs and maintenance. See sections 1-37 (e)(2) and 9-74 (a)(1)a.
(62)
Open space, access and maintenance. See chapter 17 , article III, for park and open space rules.
(63)
Outdoor decorative objects. DRC approval is not required for yard or lot ornamentation provided such items are
in the rear yard only, and do not exceed three feet in height. A maximum of three
front yard ornaments are permitted without DRC approval, provided the items are placed
on the ground, do not exceed 12 inches in height or width and are integrated into
the landscape design. See also subsection (b)(56) of this section, Lighting.
(64)
Painting, exterior.
a.
DRC approval is required, even if repainting is being done with the same colors as
the original or previous paint color. The submittal must include manufacturer's paint
chips indicating color number and locations where the color will be used (body, trim,
eaves, etc.). Paint must be flat or low luster (e.g., satin). Photos of the immediately
adjacent homes must also be included with the submittal. In some cases, if it is not
clear to the DRC how the paint color will appear, the DRC may request larger samples
or may require that a paint sample be placed on the house for viewing. Notwithstanding
the previous conditions, the DRC reserves the right, at any point in time, to limit
paint colors to certain preapproved colors and combinations for any specific area
or Village of Sterling Ranch.
b.

documents.title: Sec. 21-22. - General community standards.
documents.text:
DRC approval is not required for touch-up on small sections of the home, such as repainting
railings, shutters, or columns which may have faded or otherwise need maintenance.
(65)
Patios.
a.
Patios should be compatible and harmonious with the structure and surrounding neighborhood
and must be an integral part of the landscape architectural design.
1.
Patios shall not be closer than five feet from the rear property line when adjacent
to another single-family lot.
2.
A covered patio shall not exceed two-thirds of the width of the home.
3.
Enclosing covered patios shall not be permitted.
b.
DRC approval is not required provided that the patio meets all the following conditions.
All other patios must be submitted for approval. The patio:
1.
Is constructed of concrete, pavers, flagstone, stepping stones, or other appropriate
outdoor materials;
2.
Is constructed on the ground immediately adjacent to the home (e.g., is not an unconnected
slab in another part of the yard), and does not exceed 12 inches in height from ground
level at any point;
3.
Is a color complementary to the home;
4.
Does not disturb the general drainage pattern of the rear yard; and
5.
Does not cover more than 25 percent of the rear yard.
(66)
Patio covers. See subsection (b)(24) of this section, Deck covers.
(67)
Patios, enclosed. See subsection (b)(25) of this section, Decks, enclosed.
(68)
Paving. See subsection (b)(31) of this section, Driveways, subsection (b)(65) of this section,
Patios, and subsection (b)(78) of this section, Retaining walls. Any additional paving
or concrete installation requires DRC approval and must be incorporated into the landscape
plan either as part of the rear yard submittal or as a renovation of any part of the
landscaping.
(69)
Pets. See section 1-33 (6)—(11).
(70)
Play equipment, sports equipment.
a.
DRC approval is not required provided that:
1.
The equipment does not exceed six feet in height;
2.
Its footprint does not exceed 60 square feet; and
3.
Is placed in the rear yard at least five feet from any property line.
Exception. All trampolines require DRC approval.
b.
Any play equipment not meeting these conditions is required to have DRC approval.
(71)
Play house. DRC approval is required except as noted in subsection (b)(1) of this section, Accessory
buildings.
(72)
Ponds. DRC approval is required.
(73)
Pools. See subsection (b)(95) of this section, Swimming pools.
(74)
Radon. Radon system components external to the home, including all piping, are required
to be painted to match the approved house color.
(75)

documents.title: Sec. 21-22. - General community standards.
documents.text:
Rain barrels. Residents are allowed two 55-gallon rain barrels to collect rainwater for irrigation
of their personal gardens and landscaping.
a.
Rain barrels shall appear natural and blend in with the surrounding landscape and
architecture of the home. Colors shall be earth tones or wood tones; primary colors
are not permitted.
b.
Rain barrels are not permitted to fall into disrepair.
c.
Rain barrels installed behind the wing fence in the rear or side yard of the home
do not require approval if ALL of the following conditions are met:
1.
Rain barrels are installed so as not to be immediately visible to adjacent properties,
street, or open space;
2.
55-gallon capacity or less per barrel, maximum of two barrels;
3.
Precipitation is collected only from the rooftop of the residence via a downspout;
and
4.
The rain barrel has a minimum setback from all property lines of five feet and is
not located within an easement;
d.
Rain barrels are allowed in front of the front wing fence in the front yard, but require
DRC approval.
1.
Nothing herein shall relieve any Owner from compliance with any plumbing or building
requirements, whether local, state or federal.
(76)
Recreational vehicles. See section 1-37 .
(77)
Re-modeling of home or garage. DRC approval is required. See subsection (b)(2) of this section, Additions/expansions.
(78)
Retaining walls. DRC approval is required for material and aesthetic aspects only; the DRC does not
review or approve structural elements of or drainage changes cause by retaining wall
installation or repair. No stacked timber walls are permitted above grade. Walls shall
not prohibit the installation of fencing at property lines. Builder-installed retaining
walls shall not be removed or altered without DRC approval. Approval of a retaining
wall by the DRC does not constitute approval of alteration of existing drainage patterns
resulting from the installation of the retaining wall. Any adverse drainage condition
created by the proposed improvement is the sole responsibility of the Property Owner.
(79)
Roofing materials and roofing replacement. DRC approval is not required if replacement is made with the same material and color
as is currently on the home. Any change to the color or the material requires DRC
approval. Samples illustrating color, style, and material is required as part of the
submittal. New roofing materials are always under development. The DRC reserves the
right to determine appropriate materials and may allow or limit certain materials
in specific areas or Villages of Sterling Ranch.
(80)

documents.title: Sec. 21-22. - General community standards.
documents.text:
Rooftop equipment. DRC approval is required.
(81)
Satellite dish. See subsection (b)(6) of this section, Antennas.
(82)
Sauna. See subsection (b)(48) of this section, Hot tubs, spas, and saunas.
(83)
Screen door and security door. See subsection (b)(28) of this section, Doors.
(84)
Shutters. DRC approval is required. Shutters must be compatible with the architectural style
of the home. The applicant must submit type of material, color, and rendering or photo
of the shutters and a rendering or photo of the exterior wall on which the shutters
are proposed to be attached.
(85)
Siding. DRC approval is required if siding is to be replaced with a material other than what
is currently installed on the home. Repair work replacing small portions of siding
with identical siding does not require DRC approval.
(86)
Signs and other advertising. All signs must be located within property boundaries and not in the right-of-way
which includes the tree lawn. The following signs are permitted and all other signage
or placement requires DRC approval:
a.
One temporary sign of not more than five feet in height, and two feet by three feet
in size, advertising the property for sale. (For requirements for political signs
related to candidates and ballot issues see section 1-34 .)
b.
One sign not exceeding 144 square inches from a bona fide security provider notifying
the public that the home has a security system monitored by the security provider.
c.
One temporary trade sign pertaining to contractor or tradesman only while the work
is in progress or three months, whichever is less. The sign shall not exceed four
feet in height, or two feet by three feet in size.
d.
One dog warning sign not more than 80 square inches in size placed in a window near
the front door or the mulch bed nearest the front door or side yard gate.
e.
There shall be no moving parts or lights attached to any signage on a residential
lot. Signage is not permitted to be attached or hung from fencing, or placed on any
Open Space or landscape tract.
(87)
Skylights. DRC approval is required. The applicant must submit a rendering or photo of the proposed
skylight, plus material specifications and colors.
(88)
Snow removal.
a.
Property owners are responsible to remove snow from the sidewalk in front of their
home and, on corner lots, to the side of their home, in accordance with Douglas County
Rules and Regulations.
b.
Douglas County is responsible for snow removal on all public streets; their policies
on snow removal can be found on the County's website.
c.

documents.title: Sec. 21-22. - General community standards.
documents.text:
Snow removal on certain CAB-owned vehicle access areas will be performed by the CAB
when snow depth on the street has reached four inches, and snow has stopped falling.
d.
Snow removal on walks or trails contained within CAB-owned landscape tracts, parks,
or other common areas will be performed by the CAB when snow depth has reached four
inches and snow has stopped falling.
(89)
Solar energy devices and systems. DRC approval is required for any solar installation or system on the exterior of
the home or on the Lot.
(90)
Sport courts. DRC approval is required. Submittals shall include a drawing showing the court on
the lot, setbacks from property lines, any type of safety fencing to be used, and
samples of colors and materials, with identification of where each will be used on
the court. This includes basketball, volleyball, tennis, shuffleboard, pickleball,
and any and all other similar sport-related surfaces. Courts are not permitted to
be lighted. See also subsection (b)(12) of this section, Basketball backboards, rear
yard.
(91)
Storm and security doors. All storm door and security door additions must complement the architectural style
and colors of the house. If other than full glass is proposed, a photograph of the
proposed door, location on the home, and material sample/color specification is required
for DRC approval. White storm doors are not permitted.
(92)
Statuary. See subsection (b)(63) of this section, Outdoor decorative objects.
(93)
Sunshades. DRC approval is not required provided the sunshade is a freestanding fabric or non-reflective
fixture in conjunction with an outdoor seating, eating, or play area. Any other sunshade
requires DRC approval. See also subsection (b)(8) of this section, Awnings, subsection
(b)(24) of this section, Deck covers, and subsection (b)(66) of this section, Patio
covers.
(94)
Swamp coolers. See subsection (b)(4) of this section, Air conditioning.
(95)
Swimming pools.
a.
All in-ground pools require DRC approval. Plans shall include a drawing showing the
pool on the lot, setbacks to property lines, type of safety fencing to be used, and
samples of colors and materials of finished surfaces, clearly identifying where each
will be used.
b.
Aboveground pools are prohibited with the exception of a splash pool which is defined
as less than eight feet in diameter, does not exceed 18 inches in height and is placed
in the rear yard only.
(96)
Swing set. See subsection (b)(70) of this section, Play equipment.
(97)
Temporary structures.
a.

documents.title: Sec. 21-22. - General community standards.
documents.text:
Roll-off containers include, but are not limited to, tents, shacks, huts, PODS, dumpsters
and portable toilets.
1.
All roll-off containers are required to be placed within property boundaries and are
not allowed in the right-of-way, including the sidewalk or tree lawns.
2.
Temporary fencing is not permitted.
3.
Additional standards or statutes may be imposed by Douglas County and/or the State
of Colorado. Please check with Douglas County and the State of Colorado prior to placement.
b.
DRC approval is NOT required but the following conditions must be followed:
1.
Stored within property boundaries so as not to be in the right-of-way which includes
the sidewalk and tree lawn.
2.
Dumpsters are only allowed during construction, remodeling, and moving. If it is determined
the dumpster is not necessary, or that the construction, remodeling, or moving is
not proceeding in a diligent manner, then the dumpster will need to be removed.
3.
Dumpsters must be emptied regularly so unsightly debris does not exceed top edge of
dumpster and to prevent debris from flying out.
4.
Application for improvement must be submitted via residentsubmit@sterlingranchcab.com
with the location of the roll-off container and the time frame the container will
be on the property.
5.
Temporary moving containers and portable storage.
6.
"PODS" are permitted for no more than 14 days. If needed for longer an application
for general architectural improvement must be submitted for DRC review and approval.
Property owners should contact Douglas County for any additional permit or engineering
requirements.
(98)
Trailers. See section 1-37 .
(99)
Trampolines. DRC approval is required. Consideration will be given to adjacent properties, so
as not to create an undue disturbance.
a.
Trampolines should be installed in a way so as not to be immediately visible to adjacent
property owners and must be a minimum of five feet from all property lines.
b.
Tall plant material is required between the trampoline and all property lines, preferably
including evergreen trees and shrubs, intended to provide for a visual barrier of
the trampoline from adjoining property.
c.
Preference is that these items not be located in a side yard adjacent to a corner
sidewalk, street, common area or open space—instead should be sited on the interior
side of the yard.
d.
Trampolines are required to be anchored per manufacturer specifications and kept in
good repair.
(100)
Transition zone, landscaping. Required on lots adjacent to open space.
(101)
Trash and recycling containers.
a.

documents.title: Sec. 21-22. - General community standards.
documents.text:
Containers for pickup must be returned to an appropriately screened location by the
end of the pickup day. Owners and occupants will keep all equipment for the storage
or disposal in a clean and sanitary condition. No owner or occupant will permit any
garbage or trash cans or receptacles to be maintained in an exposed or unsightly manner.
b.
Trash shall not be stored or allowed to accumulate on any property except within appropriate
containers, an enclosed structure or structure appropriately screened from view. Trash
includes, but is not limited to, garbage, lumber, grass clippings, plant clippings,
plant waste, pet waste, compost, metal, bulk materials, scrap, refuse, automotive
fluids, paint or stain, hazardous materials, or debris of any kind.
(102)
Trash enclosure/screening.
a.
DRC approval is not required if ALL of the following conditions are met. Any trash
enclosure/screening not meeting ALL of these conditions must be submitted for DRC
approval.
1.
The trash enclosure/screening is installed behind the wing fence in the side yard;
2.
It must be attached to the side of the house;
3.
It has a minimum setback from the side property line of five feet;
4.
It is not located within any easement;
5.
It is constructed of top-grade redwood or cedar, or high grade Trex material or an
equivalent in a color complementary to the home or painted to match the fence stain
color of Sherwin Williams #3002 "Belvedere Tan"; and
6.
It may not exceed 4½ feet in height from ground level at any point.
b.
Trash and recycling enclosures will be considered based on size, height, color, relationship
to size of lot, relationship to landscaping, and setbacks from property lines. Material,
style and color, including roofing, are appropriate for the architectural style of
the home unless otherwise approved. No vinyl or resin enclosures will be approved.
(103)
Treehouses. Treehouses are not permitted.
(104)
Tree lawn. DRC approval is required for design changes to the tree lawn. Please refer to chapter 9 , article III, of these Rules.
a.
Property owners are required to replace dead or dying materials with like materials,
or as may otherwise be approved by the DRC. Replacement trees shall be a minimum of
two-inch caliper as measured six inches above grade.
b.
Maintenance of the tree lawn is the responsibility of the property owner, except tree
lawns that are CAB maintained.
c.
A minimum 60 percent live coverage is required.
(105)
Utility equipment. Exterior pipes, conduits, wires, poles, meters, venting, and other equipment require

documents.title: Sec. 21-22. - General community standards.
documents.text:
DRC approval. Screening may be required depending on the nature of the equipment.
This subsection does not apply to equipment installed as part of the initial construction
of the home, including, but not limited to, gas meters, water meters, air conditioning
connections, venting, chimneys, and the like. See subsection (b)(54) of this section,
Landscape Screens.
(106)
Unsightly conditions. No lot or home shall be permitted to fall into disrepair, which includes, but is
not limited to, fading or peeling paint, missing or torn roofing materials, torn or
loose screens, dead or dying landscape materials, weeds, unsecured trash, trash cans
left in view more than 24 hours after pickup, bulk landscape materials left on the
lot or on the street for more than three days, bulk remodeling material left on the
lot or on the street for more than three days, accumulated pet waste, abandoned toys,
tools or equipment not in use, and all other such conditions which result from neglect,
carelessness, and lack of maintenance.
(107)
Venting. See subsection (b)(105) of this section, Utility equipment.
(108)
Watercraft. See section 1-37 .
(109)
Water features. DRC approval is required for all outdoor water features, including, but not limited
to, ponds, fountains in excess of three feet in height, streams, play surfaces, or
other facilities with a water component, whether re-circulating or otherwise. All
such structures or equipment shall be incorporated into the landscape plan.
(110)
Water wells. Water wells are not permitted.
(111)
Weathervanes. DRC approval is not required, provided that only one decorative weathervane is mounted
on the roof, is a color and style compatible with the home, and does not exceed 36
inches in any direction.
(112)
Weather stations. All exterior weather monitoring stations with antenna and exterior sensors require
DRC approval.
(113)
Window replacement. DRC approval is not required for the replacement of glass only, provided the replacement
glass is identical to the previous glass. See also subsection (b)(28) of this section,
Doors and windows.
(114)
Window coverings and tinting.
a.
Window coverings are not required; however, any window coverings installed must be
of appropriate materials such as draperies, curtains, blinds, or interior shutters,
(e.g., blankets, sheets, cardboard, foil, and similar materials are not considered
appropriate window coverings).
b.
Highly reflective or darkly tinted glass is considered too commercial for residential
applications, and is not permitted. Frosted, etched, and colored glass may be used

documents.title: Sec. 21-22. - General community standards.
documents.text:
in small quantities as accents and must be complementary to the architectural style
of the home.
(115)
Wind turbines. DRC approval is required.
(116)
Wood storage. See subsection (b)(34) of this section, Firewood.
(117)
Xeriscape. DRC approval is required. The term "xeriscape" means the combined application of
seven principles of landscape planning and design: soil analysis, soil improvement,
hydro-zoning, practical turf areas, mulching, irrigation efficiency and appropriate
maintenance.
Variances may be approved by the DRC, or by the CAB if the applicant is appealing
the DRC's decision. Any request for a Variance must be submitted in writing, with
appropriate supporting material pertinent to the request. Each request for a variance
is reviewed on its own merit, and approval may be granted or withheld based on the
specific and unique characteristics of each request for a variance.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(1), § VI; Res. No.
2022-08-02
, § 1, 8-26-2022; Res. No.
2023-04-02
, § 1, 4-19-2023

documents.title: Sec. 21-23. - Fencing standards.
documents.text:
(a)
Style 1, Perimeter fencing—Open-rail colored concrete fencing.
(1)
This is an open-rail fence consisting of three concrete rails and concrete vertical
posts. It will be installed inside the residential lot lines, not on tracts or in
Open Space (defined below). The color selected for concrete fencing is Solomon #338
"Earthen."
(2)
If a fence section is less than eight feet wide, the installer will need to cut to
the appropriate length in the field.
a.
It is the responsibility of the home builder and/or installer to determine the amount
of material to be purchased at any one time.
b.
Please consider how material will be stored on lots.
(3)
This fence may not be changed or removed. In the event a Property Owner, or any person
on the property of the Property Owner, damages the fence, the Property Owner must
notify the CAB. The CAB will make the replacement and the cost of replacement will
be assessed against the Property Owner's account.
(4)
No double fencing is permitted, and no additional pickets or rails are permitted to
be installed on this fence. If privacy in the yard is desired, this can be accomplished
through landscaping applications adjacent to a patio or deck or enclosed outdoor living
spaces.
(5)
Approval must be obtained from the DRC prior to any construction or landscaping.
(6)
Additional gates on perimeter fencing are considered on a case-by-case basis and require
DRC approval.
Signature Stone Split-Rail Fence
(b)
Style 2, Wing fencing—Open-rail colored concrete fencing with wood gate.
(1)
A wing fence is the portion of fence that faces the street between homes. This will
also be open rail colored concrete. It will have one wood gate stained to match the
concrete and will be installed by the home builder. If additional gates are desired,
DRC approval is required.
(2)
This fence and gate is the obligation of the Property Owner to maintain. If repair
or replacement is needed on the concrete components, the CAB can supply the names
of installers who can obtain materials and perform the work.
(3)
The gate must be kept stained and in good repair at all times. The approved stain
color on the gate is Sherwin Williams #3002 "Belvedere Tan," which matches Style 3
Fencing described in subsection (c) of this section.
Gate Elevation
Fencing Map
(c)
Style 3, Interior lot line fencing between homes—Open-rail wood fencing, stained.
(1)
Single-family detached homes are not required to have fencing between homes defining
the side and rear yards. Two fencing styles are approved for use on the interior lot
lines between homes:
a.

documents.title: Sec. 21-23. - Fencing standards.
documents.text:
Three-rail cedar dimensional lumber fence stained in the approved color to match the
concrete perimeter fence. The specifications of this fence, including the approved
stain color, are shown below.
b.
Homeowners may also elect to purchase the perimeter concrete style fencing for use
on interior lot lines. This shall match Style 1 specifications in subsection (a) of
this section in all respects.
Additional gates on interior lot line fencing between homes require DRC approval.
(2)
It is customary for adjacent neighbors to share in the cost of installing lot line
fencing between the residences and to place the fence exactly on property lines. It
is up to the neighboring parties to determine which side of the fence will face each
property.
(3)
All interior lot line fencing must be stained and kept in good repair. The approved
stain color is Sherwin Williams #3002 "Belvedere Tan."
Fencing Diagram
(Rules of 8-26-2020(1), § VIII)

Landscaping and irrigation application for homeowners.

Application for approval of general architectural improvements.

documents.title: Sec. 21-25. - Rock mulch guidelines.
documents.text:
Large expanses of uninterrupted rock mulch are to be avoided where possible. Rock
mulch areas greater than eight feet in width shall include one or more of the following
techniques to help mitigate visually monotonous mulch area:
(1)
Addition of plant material. Break up large expanses of rock mulch with planting. Consider pockets of low water
use plants, and/or ornamental grasses.
(2)
Mix of rock size. Supplement 1½-inch rock mulch with larger rocks and boulders to visually break up
large expanses. The use of larger rock (four inches plus) in swales is an acceptable
application to break up expanses of rock mulch, as is the placement of larger boulders.
Planting in conjunction with boulders is preferred.
(3)
Other. The design review committee is happy to consider additional design solutions to mitigate
large expanses of mulch, for example, bocce ball courts, seating areas or paths surfaced
with different hardscape materials such as pavers, flagstone, crusher fines, etc.
Rock Mulch Design
(Rules of 8-26-2020(1), att. H)
