documents.title: Sec. 25-21. - General scope of article.
documents.text:
This article outlines requirements for several key solutions in Sterling Ranch. These
solutions will help Sterling Ranch develop and market a core identity that resonates
with potential buyers. The solutions in this article are intended to help builder
teams understand and articulate the value these key solutions provide for potential
homeowners. Additional resources and training are available to the builder team to
help them articulate the value proposition of these solutions. Labeling in this article
will not match one to one with the execution guides outlined in article III of this
chapter.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(2), app. 10.1(intro. ¶))

documents.title: Sec. 25-22. - Value proposition.
documents.text:
(a)
Every community needs elements that make it unique and give homeowners a reason to
purchase there instead of resale.
(b)
The key solutions outlined in this article will help differentiate homes in Sterling
Ranch from surrounding communities.
(c)
We expect these solutions to add up to $5,000.00 in cost, but add far more significant
value to the sales price.
(d)
Builders who effectively educate their teams on these solutions will drive significant
value for their potential home buyers.
(e)
Sterling Ranch, Lumiere, and Siemens are happy to work with builder teams to help
them maximize the value of these solutions.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(2), app. 10.1(intro. ¶))

documents.title: Sec. 25-23. - Home automation.
documents.text:
(a)
Solution overview.
(1)
Home automation has become an expectation for new home buyers.
(2)
Sterling Ranch has partnered with Lumiere and Siemens to offer a leading edge solution
to whole home automation.
(3)
This solution combines a wide array of functionalities into one intuitive app that
will continue to evolve over time.
(4)
This article lays out a minimum standard for home automation in Sterling Ranch.
(5)
Home builders are encouraged to add additional compatible devices to their base home
to maximize their value proposition.
(b)
Solution description. Home automation requirements in Sterling Ranch include:
(1)
Home Automation Hub.
(2)
Home Automation Tablet.
(3)
Thermostat Control.
(4)
Lighting Control (five Zones).
(5)
Mobile App Based Security System Control.
(6)
Smart Irrigation System Control.
(7)
Water Shutoff Valve Control.
(8)
Real Time Utility Data and Analytics.
(9)
Notification of Community Events and Announcements.
(10)
Wireless mesh networking system.
(c)
Logistics and support.
(1)
Home automation components will be purchased through technology packages offered by
Siemens.
a.
Packages are broken out by trade (low voltage, line voltage, HVAC, etc.).
b.
Builder subcontractors will purchase and install the package corresponding with their
trade.
c.
Siemens will be responsible for activating the home automation package components
after subcontractor installation is complete.
d.
Trade-specific technology packages are further detailed elsewhere.
(2)
Homeowners will have access to home automation customer support.
a.
After move-in, homeowners will be provided with two years of customer support through
Siemens and Lumiere.
b.
Homeowners can access customer support by visiting https://Lumiere.technology/help.
c.
Homeowner support is further detailed in section 25-27 .
(d)
Suggested additions.
(1)
Suggested additions to base homes include:
a.
Connected Door Lock.
b.
Connected Garage Door Opener.
c.
Connected Doorbell Camera.
d.
Additional Zones of Lighting.
e.
IP Camera Pre-Wire.
(2)
Suggested homeowner options include:
a.
Shade Control.
b.
Audio/Visual Control.
c.
IP Cameras and Additional Security Devices.
d.
Connected Flood Sensors.
e.
Connected Smoke and Carbon Monoxide Detectors.
If you would like to discuss adding compatible devices to your base home or upgrade
packages, help is available.
Contact us at help@lumierefiber.com.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(2), app. 10.1(A))

documents.title: Sec. 25-24. - Utilities and conservation.
documents.text:
(a)
Solution overview.
(1)
Sustainability and conservation is important to the Sterling Ranch home buyer and
central to the community.
(2)
Sterling Ranch has partnered with Lumiere and Siemens to offer a leading edge solution
for utility monitoring, sustainability, and conservation.
(3)
This solution will help homeowners save money on their utility bills while conserving
the beautiful nature of Sterling Ranch.
(b)
Solution description.
(1)
Water metering and conservation.
a.
Homes in Sterling Ranch will each have two water meters: one for indoor water usage
and one for outdoor water usage.
1.
This allows the Community Authority Board to bill separate rates for indoor and outdoor
water usage.
2.
These separate rates more accurately reflect system costs and are important to incentivize
conservation of outdoor water usage.
3.
These water meters will also enable feedback to homeowners regarding water usage and
enable homeowners to remotely shut off their water in case of a leak.
b.
Homes in Sterling Ranch will also utilize a smart irrigation controller.
1.
The smart irrigation controller automatically adjusts watering schedules based on
real-time weather data.
2.
This will allow homeowners to conserve water and save money without additional effort.
(2)
Real time utility feedback and smart home integration.
a.
Homes in Sterling Ranch will utilize cutting-edge utility monitoring technology to
provide homeowners with feedback about their utility usage.
1.
Two utility monitoring devices will be used to collect real-time utility information
for gas, water, and electric.
2.
Homeowners will have the ability to access their data and view usage patterns.
3.
This will allow homeowners in Sterling Ranch to adjust their usage over time to save
money and conserve resources.
b.
Utility data will also be connected with the home automation system.
1.
This allows homeowners to view utility usage directly in their home automation app,
create notifications and usage alerts, and automate certain functions in their home
based on utility data.
2.
This will also enable future updates to the home automation software that will help
homeowners conserve even more with less effort.
(c)
Logistics and support.
(1)
Utility and conservation components will be available through technology packages
offered by Siemens.
a.
Packages are broken out by trade (plumbing, landscaper, etc.).
b.
Builder subcontractors will purchase and install the package corresponding with their
trade.
c.
Siemens will be responsible for activating the smart irrigation controller and utility

documents.title: Sec. 25-24. - Utilities and conservation.
documents.text:
monitoring devices after installation.
d.
Landscapers will be responsible for programming watering schedules for the smart irrigation
controller.
e.
Trade-specific technology packages are further detailed in elsewhere.
(2)
Homeowners will have access to customer support.
a.
After move-in, homeowners will be provided with two years of customer support through
Siemens and Lumiere.
b.
Homeowners can access customer support by visiting https://Lumiere.technology/help.
c.
Homeowner support is further detailed in section 25-27 .
(Rules of 8-26-2020(2), app. 10.1(B))

documents.title: Sec. 25-25. - Internet and networking.
documents.text:
(a)
Solution overview.
(1)
A great Internet experience is a differentiator in Sterling Ranch.
(2)
Lumiere, in partnership with CenturyLink, is proud to provide gigabit Internet to
every home in Sterling Ranch.
(3)
The Internet in Sterling Ranch is among the fastest in the country and nearly 20 times
faster than the speeds in neighboring Highlands Ranch.
(4)
In addition, every home in Sterling Ranch is equipped with a best-in-class wireless
mesh system, providing homeowners with the best whole home Internet experience possible.
(b)
Solution description.
(1)
Fiber Internet.
a.
Every home in Sterling Ranch is provided with gigabit Internet, among the fastest
residential Internet speeds available in the country.
b.
Lumiere builds and maintains the physical fiber network in Sterling Ranch while CenturyLink
leases Lumiere's fiber to provide gigabit service to homeowners.
c.
Homeowners will see the name CenturyLink on their monthly bills but Lumiere's fiber
network is a differentiator.
d.
Lumiere's network is built with the future in mind, boasting some of the lowest split
ratios and highest fibers to home ratios in the country.
e.
This means homeowners will continue to receive best-in-class Internet even as technology
evolves, preserving and increasing home values in the process.
f.
Contrast this with neighboring Highlands Ranch, where Internet speeds have stagnated
due to an antiquated Internet infrastructure.
(2)
In-home wireless mesh network.
a.
Every home in Sterling Ranch is equipped with a best-in-class wireless mesh networking
system.
b.
Wireless mesh networking systems are state of the art technology, designed to provide
the best Wi-Fi experience available.
c.
This solution currently consists of:
1.
One wireless access point that will be hardwired into the CenturyLink ONT.
2.
Two auxiliary access that can be placed without a CAT 6.
d.
This solution will provide great whole-home Wi-Fi coverage for the vast majority of
homeowners, but, if needed, homeowners can easily add additional beacons to their
mesh system after move-in.
(3)
In-home cabling.
a.
Homes in Sterling Ranch have CAT 6 cables to enable hard-wired connections.
b.
Each home shall have a minimum of three CAT 6 drops and one Coaxial drop.
c.
One CAT 6 drop must be to a central location on the main floor where a wireless access
point can be installed to enable the home's wireless network.
d.
One CAT 6 and one Coaxial drop must be to an entertainment location within the home.
e.
Each builder is also encouraged to run bendable fiber optic cables alongside each

documents.title: Sec. 25-25. - Internet and networking.
documents.text:
CAT 6 drop to help future-proof homes for their buyers.
(c)
Logistics.
(1)
Fiber Internet installation from the back of the lot to the home is a builder responsibility.
a.
Builder is responsible for paying for fiber Internet installation from the back of
the lot to the home.
b.
This process includes running an 18 mm microduct from the back of lot to the home,
mounting a fiber box on the side of the home, pulling fiber, and installing an ONT.
c.
Article III of this chapter provides additional details including recommended contractors,
method, and approach.
(2)
Wireless mesh networking devices and activation will be available through technology
packages offered by Siemens.
a.
Siemens will install and activate mesh networking devices during final commissioning.
b.
Trade-specific technology packages are further detailed in article III of this chapter.
(3)
Cabling will be performed by low voltage provider and is not included in the technology
packages offered by Siemens.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(2), app. 10.1(C))

documents.title: Sec. 25-26. - Solar and electric vehicle readiness.
path: Sec. 25-26. - Solar and electric vehicle readiness.
documents.text:
(a)
Solution overview.
(1)
Demand for solar panels and electric vehicle chargers continues to increase.
(2)
In many communities, the need to tear out drywall to install these systems is a significant
barrier to adoption.
(3)
As a truly 21st Century community, every home in Sterling Ranch will be equipped with
pre-wire for solar panels and electric vehicle chargers.
(4)
This will allow homeowners to easily install these systems if they desire while increasing
the resale value of the home even if they do not.
(b)
Solution description.
(1)
Solar pre-wire.
a.
Homes must have conduit placed from the roof to the electric load center.
b.
The offering of a solar opt-out program, in which the builder provides homeowners
the option to opt out of a zero down payment Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) or zero
down payment lease option for residential solar, is strongly encouraged.
(2)
Electric vehicle pre-wire.
a.
Homes must have conduit placed from the garage to the electric load center to enable
easier installation of an electric vehicle charging station.
b.
Builders are strongly encouraged to offer a Siemens electric vehicle charging station
as an available upgrade for their homes.
(c)
Logistics.
(1)
Builders will be responsible for installation of conduit in order to meet requirements
outlined in this section.
(2)
The Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board reserves the right to inspect homes for
these conduit runs and enforce their placement.
(3)
If a home is found to be out of compliance, the builder will be subject to consequences,
including being responsible for all costs associated with bringing the home into compliance,
resulting from violating the Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board's Rules and
Regulations set forth in this Code.
(4)
Because of this, builders are strongly encouraged to make sure conduit is placed before
drywall has been hung.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(2), app. 10.1(D))

documents.title: Sec. 25-27. - Homeowner support.
documents.text:
(a)
Solution overview.
(1)
Homeowner support is critical to providing a great technology experience in Sterling
Ranch.
(2)
Homeowners need resources to introduce them to the technology as well as help them
diagnose and solve any issues.
(3)
Builders have strongly indicated they do not want to be responsible for performing
this function.
(4)
As a result, Sterling Ranch and its partners have developed a solution to provide
comprehensive support for homeowners.
(b)
Solution description.
(1)
Lumiere's help website provides the first level of homeowner support.
a.
Lumiere's help website (https://Lumiere.technology/help) is the go-to resource for
homeowners looking for answers to Sterling Ranch technology questions.
b.
It provides everything from high level overviews and FAQs to troubleshooting guides
and help ticket submission for Internet, home automation, and smart irrigation controllers.
c.
The website allows homeowners to quickly answer their own questions while simplifying
the escalation process for technology issues.
d.
The website is also a great resource to help sales agents educate potential buyers
on the value of technology in Sterling Ranch.
(2)
The homeowner support solution includes in-person move-in support.
a.
Sterling Ranch Technology Consultants meet with new homeowners during their move-in
process to provide additional support.
b.
During this meeting, homeowners are provided with:
1.
A technology welcome packet that includes important information about their Internet
and home automation systems.
2.
Help activating their Internet and home automation systems if they have not already.
3.
A basic introduction to the technology in their home.
4.
Instructions on how to get help with technology issues.
c.
This education during move-in reduces homeowner questions back to the builder team
while improving homeowner experience.
(3)
Homeowners receive free technology support for two years after closing on their home.
a.
Not every problem can be solved with a website.
b.
This is why the homeowner support solution includes two years of on-going support
at no charge to homeowners.
c.
Sterling Ranch Technology Consultants help homeowners diagnose and solve more complex
issues related to Internet and home automation.
d.
This allows homeowners to reach out to technology consultants who can help and frees
up the builder team to continue focusing on what they do best.
(c)
Logistics.
(1)
Builders need to provide the Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board, Sterling Ranch,
and Lumiere with accurate closing schedules.
a.

documents.title: Sec. 25-27. - Homeowner support.
documents.text:
Closing schedules should include closing walkthrough date, closing walkthrough time,
and homeowner contact information.
b.
Among other things, this allows our technology consultants to coordinate meetings
with new homeowners.
(2)
Builders need to direct homeowners to the Lumiere help website first.
a.
Whether homeowners have technology questions or specific issues that need to be addressed,
builders need to direct homeowners to the Lumiere help website first.
b.
If a homeowner is experiencing Internet issues and is unable to access the website,
have them call CenturyLink On at 866-872-0238.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(2), app. 10.1(E))

documents.text:
(a)
This article details specific procurement processes and installation details to assist
builders in meeting the design guidelines outlined in article II of this chapter.

Packaging and labeling in this article will not match one to one with the design guidelines
outlined in article II of this chapter.
(c)
Packaging and labeling in this article is broken out by trade in order to improve
ease of execution by site supervisors and their subcontractors.
(d)
Additional resources and training are available to site supervisors and their subcontractors

Reach out to help@lumierefiber.com for additional help and information.

documents.title: Sec. 25-44. - Process overview.
documents.article: ARTICLE III. - KEY SOLUTION EXECUTION GUIDELINES
path: ARTICLE III. - KEY SOLUTION EXECUTION GUIDELINES
documents.text:
(a)
High level process overview. Below are the critical steps in the home technology activation process:
(1)
Builders must provide accurate and updated build schedules to Lumiere and/or Lumiere's
contractors to enable proper scheduling and inventory levels.
(2)
Lumiere will install fiber to a meet-me point at the back of finished lots and builders
will be responsible for running conduit from the meet-me point to the home.
(3)
Builder contractors will order and install applicable technology packages at least
four weeks prior to scheduled home close.
(4)
The builder site supervisor will inspect technology installations using the checklist
provided by Siemens and have contractors fix any defects two weeks prior to scheduled
home close.
(5)
Lumiere or its contractor will pull fiber from the meet-me point into the home and
mount the Optical Network Terminal (ONT/Fiber Modem).
(6)
Siemens will commission/activate all smart devices as well as the wireless mesh Internet
network.
(7)
A Sterling Ranch Technology Consultant will meet with the homeowner during the move-in
process to provide critical information and education.
(b)
Ordering process.
(1)
Technology solutions must be ordered through Siemens on behalf of the Sterling Ranch
Community Authority Board (CAB).
(2)
When ready to order, the home builder/subcontractor must contact the Siemens project
coordinator for Sterling Ranch at sterlingranchorders.us@siemens.com to receive ordering
instructions.
(3)
The home builder/subcontractor must provide a purchase order at the time of ordering
showing the home address for each kit being ordered.
(4)
Accurate order lead times will be provided shortly after the order has been placed.
(5)
Estimated lead times can be between three to six weeks and may vary depending on quantities
and technology packages being ordered.
(6)
Invoicing will be provided at the time of the order.
(7)
Packages will be delivered to a Siemens-certified installer chosen by the home builder.
(c)
Installation overview. Home builder responsibilities are as follows:
(1)
Purchase technology packages as required by the Design Guidelines for:
a.
Low Voltage.
b.
Line Voltage.
c.
Plumbing.
d.
Landscape.
e.
HVAC.
(2)
Home builders are encouraged to schedule an appointment with their subcontractors
and Siemens so that subcontractors are informed of the installation methodologies.
(3)
Home builders and their installers should follow the wiring specifications that are
shown in section 25-45 .
(4)
Site supervisors must complete the Siemens Pre-Commissioning Installation Checklist

documents.title: Sec. 25-44. - Process overview.
documents.article: ARTICLE III. - KEY SOLUTION EXECUTION GUIDELINES
path: ARTICLE III. - KEY SOLUTION EXECUTION GUIDELINES
documents.text:
to ensure all packages are installed properly at least two weeks prior to home closing.
(d)
Commissioning overview. Home builder responsibilities are as follows:
(1)
Home builders must provide Lumiere and Siemens with updated build and closing schedules.
(2)
Home builders must install the equipment as depicted in section 25-45 at least two weeks prior to scheduled closing.
a.
Home builders are recommended to have their subcontractors complete installation four
weeks prior to home close.
b.
This leaves time for site supervisors to check for proper installation and fix any
issues prior to the installation deadline two weeks before closing.
(3)
If Siemens attempts their commissioning and installation is not completed properly,
Siemens will distribute a report with all known issues.
(4)
Home builders will be required to complete any necessary repairs at least one week
prior to home closing and notify Siemens following completion.
(5)
Trip charges will be assessed for builders who have repeatedly require a notification
of improper installation.
(6)
Please reach out to Siemens to train your subcontractors on installation and avoid
trip charges.
(7)
Siemens commissioning must be complete prior to obtaining a Certificate of Occupancy.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(2), app. 10.2(A))

documents.title: Sec. 25-45. - Technology packages by trade.
documents.article: ARTICLE III. - KEY SOLUTION EXECUTION GUIDELINES
path: ARTICLE III. - KEY SOLUTION EXECUTION GUIDELINES
documents.text:
(a)
Technology package overview.
(1)
Many of the key solutions discussed in article II of this chapter reference technology
packages offered by Siemens and Lumiere.
(2)
These packages are outlined in this section and broken out by trade/contractor type.
(3)
Contractors are responsible for contacting Siemens to order packages for their specific
trade and house addresses then picking up those packages from the Siemens warehouse
for installation.
(4)
Contractors will complete install of their packages at least four weeks prior to scheduled
home close.
(5)
Siemens will commission/activate all smart devices within the two-week period prior
to scheduled home close.
(b)
Low voltage overview. Low Voltage contractors will be responsible for the following:
(1)
Ordering the Low-Voltage Technology Package.
(2)
Installation of the Steward Panel.
(3)
Wiring of Steward to CenturyLink Optical Network Terminal (ONT/Fiber Modem).
(4)
Wiring and install of security system devices.
(5)
Completion of installation at least four weeks prior to scheduled close.
Low Voltage Installation Diagram
Steward Panel Installation Diagram
(low voltage responsibility)
(c)
Line voltage overview. Line Voltage contractors will be responsible for the following:
(1)
Ordering the Line Volt Technology Package.
(2)

path: ARTICLE III. - KEY SOLUTION EXECUTION GUIDELINES
documents.text:
(a)
Installation Steps for Home builders.
(1)
Lumiere will install the fiber backbone, network components, and 18 mm microduct to
Xcel's electric pedestal in the back of the lot easement.
(2)
The home builder must install 18 mm microduct pathway from the Xcel electric pedestal
to the connection point (Demarcation Point) on the side of the house.
a.
Builders may contract with SiteWise (who Xcel has contracted for the electrical lateral
installation) for the installation of the microduct only.
b.
Lumiere has shared the specifications for the microduct with SiteWise and will make
the specifications known to any subcontractor that a builder may choose to use for
the installation of the microduct.
(3)
The home builder must install microduct from the network demarcation point to a structured
wiring box within the home.
a.
If desired, Lumiere will provide this installation for a fee which includes: installation
of the 30-inch structured wiring box, Carlon tube with string, single RG6 and communication
penetration and flashing.
b.
Home builders are not required to use Lumiere for this conduit installation.
(4)
Home builders will contract with Lumiere or a Lumiere-recommended fiber contractor
to install fiber from the back of the lot to the home.
a.
This will include:
1.
Pulling a fiber drop through the 18 mm microduct to a demarcation point on the side
of the house.
2.
Pulling fiber from that demarcation point through to the structured wiring box within
the home.
3.
Mounting and connection of the Optical Network Terminal (ONT) inside the structured
wiring box.
b.
Home builders are required to use Lumiere or Lumiere's recommended contractor for
this installation.
(5)
The home builder must proactively provide Lumiere Fiber and/or its relevant contractors
with updated build schedules.
a.
This facilitates fiber installation scheduling and material procurement.
b.
This helps make sure Internet is ready for activation the day homeowners move in.
(b)
Additional footnotes.
(1)
SiteWise. In order to keep all communications duct similar and to utilize a joint trench from
electric pedestal to the utility DMARC on the side of the home, home builders are
encouraged to use SiteWise to couple and bury an 18 mm microduct for the fiber to
the side of the home.
(2)
Lumiere. In order to keep all pathway and wire consistent between the backbone fiber network
and the structured wiring box where the ONT ("Fiber Modem") is located inside the
home, home builders are encouraged to use Lumiere to install the structured wiring
box, microduct inside the home, RG6, penetration and flashing.

documents.title: Sec. 29-1. - Definitions.
documents.text:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the
meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates
a different meaning:
Act or The Act means the Federal Water Pollution Control Act, also known as the Clean Water Act,
as amended, 33 USC 1251 et seq.
Amalgam Separators means a type of Wastewater treatment equipment that is designed to remove amalgam
particles and dissolved mercury from the Wastewater discharged by Dental Facilities.
Amalgam Waste includes any waste containing mercury or residues from the preparation of amalgam.
This includes, but is not limited to, any waste generated or collected by chair-side
traps, screens, filters, vacuum system filters, amalgam separators, elemental mercury,
and amalgam capsules.
Authorized or Duly Authorized Representative of the End User means:
(1)
If the user is a corporation:
a.
The president, secretary, treasurer, or a vice-president of the corporation in charge
of a principal business function, or any other person who performs similar policy
or decision-making functions for the corporation; or
b.
The manager of one or more manufacturing, product, or operating facilities, provided
the manager is authorized to make management decisions which govern the operation
of the regulated facility including having explicit or implicit duty of making major
capital investment recommendations, and initiate and direct other comprehensive measures
to ensure long-term environmental compliance with environmental laws and regulations;
can ensure that the necessary systems are established or actions taken to gather complete
and accurate information for control mechanism requirements; and where authority to
sign documents has been assigned or delegated to the manager in accordance with corporate
procedures.
(2)
If the user is a partnership or sole proprietorship: A general partner or proprietor,
respectively.
(3)
If the user is a federal, state, or local government facility: a director or highest
official appointed or designated to oversee the operation and performance of the activities
of the governmental facility, or their designee;
The individuals described in subsections (1) and (3) of this definition may designate
another authorized representative if the authorization is in writing, the authorization
specifies the individual or position responsible for the overall operation of the
facility from which the discharge originates or having overall responsibility for
environmental matters for the company, and the written authorization is submitted
to the CAB.

documents.title: Sec. 29-1. - Definitions.
documents.text:
Best Management Practices or BMPs means schedules or activities, prohibitions of practices, maintenance procedures,
and other management practices to implement the general or specific prohibitions listed
in Section 29-167 , 29-168 or 29-169 (40 CFR 403.5(a)(1) and (b)). BMPs also include treatment requirements, operating
procedures, and practices to control plant site runoff, spillage or leaks, sludge
or waste disposal, or drainage from raw material storage.
Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) means the quantity of oxygen utilized in the biochemical oxidation of organic matter
under standard laboratory procedure over a period of five days at 20 degrees centigrade,
expressed in terms of milligrams per liter (mg/L).
Categorical Industrial User means an Industrial User subject to a Categorical Pretreatment Standard or Categorical
Standard as defined in 40 CFR Chapter I, subchapter N (40 CFR 405—499).
Categorical Pretreatment Standard or Categorical Standard means any regulation containing Pollutant discharge limits promulgated by the EPA
in accordance with Section 307(b) and (c) of the Act (33 USC 1317(b), (c)) that apply
to a specific category of End Users and that appear in 40 CFR 405—471.
Colorado Discharge Permit System (CDPS) means the permit issued by the State of Colorado pursuant to the Clean Water Act
and the Water Quality Control Act.
Contractor means any Person, firm, association, corporation, local government or agency performing
work or furnishing materials to or for the CAB, directly or indirectly.
Cross-connection means any physical connection or arrangement of piping or fixtures between two otherwise
separate piping systems, one of which contains Potable Water and the other Nonpotable
Water or water of questionable safety, through which or because of which backflow
or back-siphonage may occur which would contaminate the Potable Water system.
Current Service Agreements means those Service Agreements listed in section 29-15 , which will be updated from time to time by Resolution of the CAB upon execution
of a new Service Agreement.
Customer or End User means any person, firm, corporation, association or agency who is authorized, or
who desires, to obtain services from the CAB and is a connector to or user of the
Retail Facilities.
Dental Facility means any facility used for the practice of dentistry or dental hygiene, which discharges
Wastewater containing amalgam.
Dental Facility BMP (Best Management Practice) means the requirements and standards established by Dominion to manage the discharge

documents.title: Sec. 29-1. - Definitions.
documents.text:
of Amalgam Waste to the POTW. This may include incorporating all or part of the Best
Management Practices for Amalgam Wastes issued by the American Dental Association
(ADA), September 2005 and revisions thereto. The Dental Facility BMP provides recommendations
on technology, equipment, and management practices for controlling mercury discharges
from Dental Facilities. Dominion's Dental Facility Pretreatment Requirements are included
in these Rules and Regulations as Section 29-169 .
District Engineer means any Person authorized by the CAB to act as its Engineer.
Domestic Sewage means sewage which can be treated without Pretreatment and within normal operating
procedures; which does not contain Pollutants that Pass Through or interfere with
the POTW; which, when analyzed, shows, by weight, a daily average of not more than
300 parts per million of Suspended Solids and not more than 250 parts per million
BOD; and which does not contain any other constituents above levels normally found
in solely residential Wastewater, as determined by the General Manager.
End User means a connector to or user of the Retail Facilities of the CAB.
Engineer means a duly qualified, Registered Engineer in the State of Colorado.
Environmental Protection Agency or EPA means the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency or where appropriate, the administrator
or other duly authorized official of said agency.
Exhibit A means the Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board Rules and Regulations—Utilities
Exhibit A which contains the current Utility Rates, Charges and Restrictions, as adopted
and amended by Resolution of the CAB from time to time and which is included herein
as section 29-244.
Food Waste means the animal and vegetable waste resulting from the handling, preparation, cooking
and serving of foods.
Industrial User means a nondomestic source regulated under Section 307(b), (c), or (d) of the Clean
Water Act that introduces Pollutants into the POTW.
Industrial Wastewater Discharge Permit means a Permit issued by the CAB allowing the conditional discharge of industrial
Wastewater into the Retail Facilities, pursuant to 40 CFR 403 of the Act.
Interference means the inhibition or disruption of the POTW treatment processes or operations
that contributes to a violation of any requirement of Dominion's CDPS and NPDES Permit.
The term "interference" includes prevention of sewage sludge use or disposal by the
POTW in accordance with Section 405 of the Act (33 USC 1345) or any criteria, guidelines,
or regulations developed pursuant to the Solid Waste Disposal Act (SWDA), the Clean

documents.title: Sec. 29-1. - Definitions.
documents.text:
Air Act, the Toxic Substances Control Act, or more stringent state criteria (including
those contained in any state sludge management plan prepared pursuant to Title IV
of SWDA) applicable to the method of disposal or use employed by the POTW.
Local Limits means any regulation containing Pollution Discharge limits promulgated by Dominion
in accordance with 40 CFR 405.5(c) and (d), which are deemed to be enforceable as
Pretreatment Standards in accordance with Section 307(d) of the Act and which, once
approved, are on file in the offices of the CAB.
NPDES Permit means the National Pollution Discharge Elimination Systems Permit issued pursuant
to Section 402 of the Act (33 USC 1342).
New Source.
(1)
The term "new source" means any building, structure, facility or installation from
which there is or may be a discharge of Pollutants, the construction of which commenced
after the publication of proposed Pretreatment Standards under Section 307(c) of the
Act which will be applicable to such source if such Pretreatment Standards are thereafter
promulgated in accordance with that Section, provided that:
a.
The building, structure, facility or installation is constructed at a site at which
no other source is located;
b.
The building, structure, facility or installation totally replaced the process or
production equipment that causes the discharge of Pollutants at an existing source;
or
c.
The production of Wastewater generating processes of the building, structure, facility
or installation are substantially independent of an existing source at the same site.
In determining whether these are substantially independent, factors such as the extent
to which the new facility is integrated with the existing plant, and the extent to
which the new facility is engaged in the same general type of activity as the existing
source should be considered.
(2)
Construction on a site at which an existing source is located results in a modification
rather than a New Source if the construction does not create a new building, structure,
facility or installation meeting the criteria of subsection (1)a or c of this definition
but otherwise alters, replaces, or adds to existing process or production equipment.
(3)
Construction of a new source, as defined under this definition, has commenced if the
Owner or Operator has:
a.
Begun, or caused to begin as part of a continuous on-site construction program:
1.
Any placement, assembly, or installation of facilities or equipment; or
2.
Significant site preparation work including clearing, excavation, or removal of existing

documents.title: Sec. 29-1. - Definitions.
documents.text:
buildings, structures, or facilities which is necessary for this placement, assembly,
or installation of new source facilities or equipment; or
b.
Entered into a binding contractual obligation for the purchase of facilities or equipment
which is intended to be used in its operation within a reasonable time. Options to
purchase or contracts which can be terminated or modified without substantial loss,
and contracts for feasibility, engineering, and design studies do not constitute a
contractual obligation under this section.
Nondomestic Sewage means sewage which is not Domestic Sewage.
Pass
Through means a discharge which exits the POTW into waters of the United States in quantities
or concentrations which, alone or in conjunction with a discharge or discharges from
other sources, is a cause of a violation of any requirement of the POTW's NPDES Permit
(including an increase in the magnitude or duration of a violation).
Permit means Industrial Wastewater Discharge Permit.
Person means any individual, firm, company, association, society, corporation, group, government,
governmental agency or other legal entity.
Photographic Processing Facility means a facility which processes images from silver-sensitized films and papers.
This includes, but is not limited to, commercial photographic and film processing
facilities, in-house photographic processing facilities, microlabs, printers, X-ray,
and other medical/dental/industrial/institutional diagnostic facilities which use
silver-based imaging materials the processing of which produces a silver-rich solution.
Photographic Processing Facility Best Management Practices (BMPs) means the Requirements and Standards established by Dominion to manage the discharge
of silver wastes to the POTW. This may include incorporating all or part of the Code
of Management Practice for Silver Dischargers, issued by The Silver Council and the
Association of Metropolitan Sewerage Agencies (AMSA), September 1995, and revisions
thereto. The Photographic Processing Facility BMPs provide recommendations on technology,
equipment and management practices for controlling silver discharges from facilities
that process photographic materials. Dominion's Photographic Processing Facility Pretreatment
Requirements are on file in the offices of the CAB, once adopted by Dominion.
Pollutant means any dredged spoil, solid waste, incinerator residue, sewage, garbage, sewage
sludge munitions, chemical wastes, biological materials, radioactive materials, heat,
wrecked or discarded equipment, rock, sand, cellar dirt, and industrial, municipal,

documents.title: Sec. 29-1. - Definitions.
documents.text:
and agricultural waste discharged into water.
Pollution means the manmade or man-induced alteration of the chemical, physical, biological,
or radiological integrity of water.
Pool Tap Fee means a charge imposed by CAB and remitted to Dominion for a residential or commercial
swimming pool.
Potable Water means that water furnished by Dominion which conforms to requirements of the Safe
Drinking Water Act or any other applicable standards.
Pretreatment means the reduction of the amount of Pollutants, the elimination of Pollutants, or
the alteration of the nature of Pollutant properties in Wastewater to a less harmful
state prior to or in lieu of discharging or otherwise introducing Pollutants into
a POTW.
Pretreatment Requirements means any substantive or procedural requirement related to Pretreatment other than
National Pretreatment Standards, imposed on an Industrial User.
Pretreatment Standard, National Pretreatment Standard, or Standards means any regulation containing Pollutant discharge limits promulgated by the EPA
in accordance with Section 307(b) and (c) of the Act, which applies to Industrial
Users. The term "pretreatment standard," "National Pretreatment Standard," or "standards"
includes Prohibitive Discharge limits established pursuant to 40 CFR 403.5.
Prohibitive Discharge Standards means the National Prohibitive Discharge Standard or regulations developed under
the authority of Section 307(b) of the Act of 40 CFR 403.5.
Public Sewer means a sewer which is controlled and maintained by a public authority.
Publicly Owned Treatment Works (POTW) means a treatment works, as defined by Section 212 of the Act (33 USC 1292), which
is comprised in part of the Wholesale Wastewater Facilities and in part by the Retail
Wholesale Facilities.
Retail Facilities means:
(1)
The Retail Water Facilities, the Retail Wastewater Facilities and the Retail Stormwater
Facilities, as defined in sections 29-108 , 29-171 and 29-199 ; or
(2)
Retail Water Facilities, the Retail Wastewater Facilities and the Retail Stormwater
Facilities operated and maintained by the CAB that connect with the Wholesale Facilities.
Retail Provider means a governmental entity that provides retail water and Wastewater service to
an End User through the Wholesale Facilities pursuant to a Current Service Agreement
with Dominion. The CAB is a Retail Provider.
Retail Services means the services provided by the CAB to the End User through the Retail Facilities.
Retail Stormwater Facilities means the Retail Stormwater Facilities as defined in section 29-199 .

documents.title: Sec. 29-1. - Definitions.
documents.text:
Retail Wastewater Facilities means the Retail Wastewater Facilities as defined in section 29-171 .
Retail Water Facilities means the Retail Water Facilities as defined section 29-108 .
Retail Water Services means the services provided by the CAB by way of its Retail Water Facilities.
Retail Stormwater Facilities means the Retail Stormwater Facilities as defined in this Code.
Retail Wastewater Facilities means the Retail Wastewater Facilities as defined in this Code.
Retail Water Facilities means the Retail Water Facilities as defined in this Code.
Retail Services means the services provided by the CAB to the End User through the Retail Facilities.
Rules and Regulations means the Rules and Regulations adopted by Dominion in June of 2015, as amended in
December 2016, and any amendments approved thereafter by Dominion from time to time.
Sanitary Sewage means any combination of liquid and water-carried wastes from residences or nondomestic
sources.
Sanitary Sewer means a sewer which carries liquid and water-carried wastes from residences or nondomestic
sources.
Service Agreement means the written agreement between Dominion and the CAB pursuant to which Dominion
shall provide Wholesale Services to the CAB by way of Dominion's Wholesale Facilities.
Service Charges means all fees and charges other than Tap Fees, set forth in Exhibit A (chapter 13).
Service Lateral means the Sanitary Sewer line from the wye connection on the CAB's Sewer Main to
the End User building to be served, but not including the wye, all as more specifically
described in the Technical Specifications.
Sewer Main means the principal Sanitary Sewer to which Service Laterals are tributary.
Sewer Tap Fee means the Sewer Tap Fee in the amount set forth in Exhibit A (chapter 13) for connection
to or access to the Retail Wastewater Facilities.
Significant Industrial User (SIU).
(1)
Except as provided in subsections (2)a, b, c and (3) of this definition, the term
"Significant Industrial User" means:
a.
An End User of a Retail Provider subject to Categorical Pretreatment Standards; or
b.
An End User that:
1.
Discharges an average of 25,000 gallons per day or more of process Wastewater to the
POTW (excluding sanitary, noncontact cooling, and boiler blowdown wastewater);
2.
Contributes a process wastestream which makes up five percent or more of the average
dry weather hydraulic or organic capacity of the POTW Treatment Plant; or
3.
Is designated as such Dominion on the basis that it has a reasonable potential for
adversely affecting the POTW's operation or for violating any Pretreatment Standard

documents.title: Sec. 29-1. - Definitions.
documents.text:
or requirement.
(2)
Dominion may determine that an Industrial User subject to Categorical Pretreatment
Standards is a Non-Significant Categorical Industrial User rather than a Significant
Industrial User on a finding that the Industrial User never discharges more than 100
gallons per day of total categorical wastewater (excluding sanitary, non-contact cooling
and boiler blowdown wastewater, unless specifically included in the Pretreatment Standard)
and the following conditions are met:
a.
The Industrial User, prior to Dominion's finding, has consistently complied with all
applicable Categorical Pretreatment Standards and Requirements;
b.
The Industrial User annually submits a certification statement as found in 40 CFR
403.3, together with any additional information necessary to support the certification
statement; and
c.
The Industrial User never discharges any untreated concentrated wastewater.
(3)
Upon finding that a user meeting the criteria in subsection (1)b of this definition
has no reasonable potential for adversely affecting the POTW's operation or for violating
any Pretreatment Standard or requirement, Dominion may, at any time, on its own initiative
or in response to a petition received from an End User, and in accordance with procedures
in 40 CFR 403.8(f)(6), determine that such user should not be considered a Significant
User.
Stormwater Tap Fee means the Stormwater Tap Fee in the amount set forth in Exhibit A (chapter 13) for
connection to or access to the Retail Stormwater Facilities.
Surcharge means any charge imposed by the CAB for the provision of a special service not normally
provided by the CAB.
Suspended Solids means the total suspended matter that floats on the surface of, or is suspended in,
water, wastewater or other liquids, and which is removable by laboratory filtering.
Tap means the right of a Single-Family Equivalent (SFE) to connect for Retail Services.
Tap Fee means the Sewer Tap Fee, the Water Tap Fee and the Storm Sewer Tap Fee imposed by
the CAB as set forth in Exhibit A (chapter 13) for obtaining access, respectively,
to the Retail Water Facilities, Retail Stormwater Facilities and Retail Wastewater
Facilities.
Technical Specifications means the Water and Wastewater Standards and Specifications for Water and Sanitation
District, as adopted in April 13, 2015, and as may be amended from time to time.
Toxic Pollutant means any Pollutant or combination of Pollutants listed as toxic in regulations promulgated
by the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency under Section 307(a) of

documents.title: Sec. 29-1. - Definitions.
documents.text:
the Clean Water Act or other acts.
Treatment Plant means that portion of the POTW or any portion thereof designed to provide treatment
of wastewater.
User means any Person who contributes, causes or permits the contribution of wastewater
into the POTW or any portion thereof.
Wastewater means the liquid and water-carried domestic or nondomestic wastes together with Pollutants
which may be present, whether treated or untreated, which are contributed into or
permitted to enter the POTW.
Water Distribution Main means the principal water conveying conduit owned by the CAB.
Water Distribution System means individually or collectively, any water facility or facilities owned by the
CAB. Water Distribution Systems shall include all fire hydrants.
Water Quality Control Act means the Colorado Water Quality Control Act (C.R.S. § 25-8-101 et seq.).
Water Service Line means:
(1)
The water line from the downstream end of the corporation stop to the water main (but
not including the corporation stop) the meter, all as more specifically described
in the Technical Specifications.
(2)
That portion of the water system from the distribution main to the point of connection
within the building.
Water Treatment Works means an arrangement of devices and structures used to produce potable water.
Water Tap Fee means the Water Tap Fee in the amount set forth in Exhibit A (chapter 13) for connection
to or access to the Retail Water Facilities.
Wholesale Facilities means the Wholesale Wastewater Facilities, Wholesale Stormwater Facilities and Wholesale
Water Facilities.
Wholesale Services means the services provided to the CAB by Dominion by way of its Wholesale Facilities.
Wholesale Stormwater Facilities means the stormwater facilities more specifically described in Section 33-303 .
Wholesale Stormwater Services means the services provided to the CAB by Dominion by way of its Wholesale Stormwater
Facilities.
Wholesale Wastewater Facilities means the structure, equipment and processes required to collect, carry away and
treat domestic and industrial wastes and dispose of the effluent which includes, but
is not limited to, the POTW.
Wholesale Wastewater Services means the services provided to the CAB by Dominion by way of its Wholesale Wastewater
Facilities.
Wholesale Water Facilities means the water facilities more specifically described in Section 33-303 .
Wholesale Water Services means the services provided to the CAB by Dominion by way of its Wholesale Water
Facilities.
Wildfire Management Plan means the Sterling Ranch Wildfire Management Plan as revised from time to time by

documents.title: Sec. 29-1. - Definitions.
documents.text:
the CAB Board.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § 2.1)

documents.title: Sec. 29-2. - Relationship of CAB and Dominion.
path: Sec. 29-2. - Relationship of CAB and Dominion.
documents.text:
The CAB operates as the provider of Retail Services to End Users while the Dominion
Water and Sanitation District ("Dominion") is the provider to the CAB of Wholesale
Services.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § 1.2)

documents.title: Sec. 29-3. - Availability of service.
documents.text:
Retail Services shall be available to End Users in accordance with this chapter and
based on the charges established therefor and subject to all penalties and charges
for violation thereof, or any statutes applicable and subject to the availability
and capacity of Retail Facilities.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § 1.3)

documents.title: Sec. 29-4. - Service agreement with Dominion.
documents.text:
The CAB receives Wholesale Services pursuant to a Service Agreement with Dominion.
All End Users shall be subject not only to this chapter but also to the Dominion Rules
and Regulations.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § 1.4)

documents.title: Sec. 29-5. - More restrictive rules and regulations.
path: Sec. 29-5. - More restrictive rules and regulations.
documents.text:
Notwithstanding any other provision of this chapter, the Rules and Regulations of
the CAB, to the extent they are more restrictive than the Dominion Rules and Regulations,
shall apply except as otherwise provided in the Service Agreement.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § 1.5)

documents.title: Sec. 29-6. - Compliance with plumbing, building requirements or regulations.
path: Sec. 29-6. - Compliance with plumbing, building requirements or regulations.
documents.text:
Nothing herein provided shall be deemed to relieve any Person from compliance with
the plumbing code or building code of Douglas County or any other state, federal,
or local plumbing or building requirements. Nothing herein shall be deemed to relieve
any Person from compliance with any other County, State of Federal regulation or requirement
that would apply to the Wholesale Facilities or the Retail Facilities.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § 1.6)

documents.title: Sec. 29-7. - Amendments.
documents.text:
The Rules and Regulations contained in this chapter may be amended by the CAB from
time to time in the same manner as the Rules and Regulations herein were adopted.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § 1.7)

documents.title: Sec. 29-8. - Severability.
documents.text:
If any section, subsection, sentence, clause or phrase of this chapter is for any
reason held to be invalid or unconstitutional, such provision shall not affect the
remaining portions of this chapter.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § 1.8)

documents.title: Sec. 29-9. - Control and operation of facilities.
path: Sec. 29-9. - Control and operation of facilities.
documents.text:
(a)
All Retail Facilities shall be under the management of the General Manager and the
control of the CAB; provided, however, that management and administration of the Retail
Facilities may be provided by a Contractor.
(b)
No other Person shall have any right to enter upon, inspect, operate, adjust, change,
alter, move or relocate any portion of the Retail Facilities without the CAB's written
consent.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § 1.9)

documents.title: Sec. 29-10. - Control of works.
documents.text:
If, for any reason, the CAB deems it necessary to delay or stop work on any water
or sanitary sewer facilities to be connected to the CAB's facilities, a stop order
by the General Manager shall be issued and delivered to the Customer or Person on
the job. Work shall cease in an orderly manner with proper safety measure and protection
for materials, equipment, property and other phases of the job. Work shall not be
resumed until issuance of a proceed order. Such decision shall not be the basis of
any claim by the Customer or Person of concern for direct, indirect, consequential
or other damage by reason of any such action, but may be appealed to the CAB for review.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § 1.10)

documents.title: Sec. 29-11. - Other charges.
documents.text:
(a)
Whenever any Person, Owner or Customer fails to perform any act required by this chapter,
performs any such act in a negligent manner or performs any act prohibited by this
chapter, the CAB may, at its discretion, correct any problem created thereby. In such
event, all costs incurred by the CAB shall be charged and paid pursuant to article
VI of this chapter. Such charge shall be a lien against the property until paid.
(b)
Except in cases of an emergency, notice shall be given pursuant to article II of this
chapter and the Customer or Person may appeal the necessity for the charge and the
amount therefor pursuant to Sections 29-42 , 29-43 and 29-44 .
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § 1.11)

documents.title: Sec. 29-12. - Special conditions.
documents.text:
Any presently installed water distribution facility or sanitary sewer collection facility
which does not meet the requirements of this Article but was in compliance with the
Rules and Regulations at the time of installation and which has been properly maintained
shall, except for the inspection and maintenance requirements, need not be upgraded,
so long as the General Manager is assured that said facilities will satisfactorily
protect the CAB's facilities and the public. Whenever the existing facilities are
moved from their present location or require replacement as determined by the General
Manager or when the General Manager finds that the device constitutes a hazard to
health, the facilities shall be replaced by meeting the current requirements of this
chapter.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § 1.12)

documents.title: Sec. 29-13. - Application for service by retail provider.
path: Sec. 29-13. - Application for service by retail provider.
documents.text:
Water and sanitary sewer service outside of the boundaries of the Districts shall
only be provided when such service is in the best interest of the CAB, Dominion and
the Districts. Such service shall be provided pursuant to a contract approved by the
CAB only if Dominion has confirmed that it has the capacity to provide such service.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § III)

documents.title: Sec. 29-14. - List of current service agreements.
path: Sec. 29-14. - List of current service agreements.
documents.text:
Following is a list of current service agreements:
(1)
Water and Wastewater Service Agreement by and between the Sterling Ranch Community
Authority Board and Dominion Water and Sanitation District dated January 6, 2014.
(2)
First Amended and Restated Water, Wastewater and Stormwater Operations Intergovernmental
Agreement (for service to Sterling Ranch), dated October 17, 2017.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), exh. B)

documents.title: Sec. 29-15. - Retail facilities.
documents.text:
The CAB's Retail Facilities include:
(1)
Streetlights and associated wiring, controls and safety appurtenances.
(2)
Parks and open space including associated landscaping, irrigation devices, benches,
lighting, structures, artwork, playgrounds, signage, entry monuments, trails, etc.
(3)
Certain tracts, alleys, motor courts, sidewalks, medians, traffic circles, and other
road and transportation improvements not owned and maintained by Douglas County.
(4)
Recreation sites, tracts and facilities.
(5)
Software licenses, including Desigo CC and Software as a Service (SAAS) services.
(6)
Underdrain lines, appurtenances, and outfalls that are approved and accepted by the
CAB for ownership and maintenance.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), exh. D)

documents.title: Secs. 29-16—29-35. - Reserved.
documents.text: Secs. 29-16—29-35. - Reserved.

documents.title: Sec. 29-36. - Notice of violations.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - VIOLATIONS, PENALTIES, AND COMPLAINTS
path: ARTICLE II. - VIOLATIONS, PENALTIES, AND COMPLAINTS
documents.text:
When the General Manager has reason to believe that any Person or Customer is not
in compliance with any provision of this chapter, that Person or Customer shall be
served a written notice stating the nature of the violation, the amount of any penalty
assessed, that service may be suspended, the right to appeal to the CAB, and providing
a reasonable time limit to correct the violation. Written notice shall be served by
delivery to the Person or Customer reasonably believe to be the violator, by the method
set forth in the Colorado Rules of Civil Procedure, Section 4(e), or by mailing to
the service address by first class mail. Mail shall be deemed to be received within
three business days of mailing. The violator shall, within the period of time stated
in such notice, permanently cease all violations and pay all penalties assessed.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § 8.1)

documents.title: Sec. 29-37. - Violations and penalties of article IV, division 2, of this chapter.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - VIOLATIONS, PENALTIES, AND COMPLAINTS
path: ARTICLE II. - VIOLATIONS, PENALTIES, AND COMPLAINTS
Sec. 29-37. - Violations and penalties of article IV, division 2, of this chapter.
documents.text:
(a)
Any Customer violating the provisions of article IV, division 2 of this chapter, pertaining
to the water conservation requirements, shall be issued a written notice to correct
the violation. If the condition is not corrected upon receipt of the notice, it shall
constitute a first violation. If within six months of the issuance of a first notice
a second notice is issued for the same violation to the same Customer, it shall constitute
a second violation. Violators will be subject to the following actions and penalties:
(1)
In the event the Customer does not correct the violation, as set forth in the notice,
the Customer will be advised in writing and a charge will be assessed in accordance
with the fee schedule in chapter 13 and added to the water bill.
(2)
In the event of a second violation within six months of the first violation, the Customer
will be advised in writing and a charge will be assessed in accordance with the fee
schedule in chapter 13 and added to the water bill.
(3)
For each subsequent violation occurring within six months of the first violation,
the CAB may, upon written notice, suspend water service to the premises at which said
violation occurred, but only after the Customer has had a hearing, as provided for
in Section 29-42 , and a charge will be assessed in accordance with the fee schedule in chapter 13 and added to the water bill.
(b)
All Customers who receive warning or notice of violation pursuant to this section
may appeal as set forth in Section 29-44 .
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § 8.2)

documents.title: Sec. 29-38. - Violations and penalties of section 29-107.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - VIOLATIONS, PENALTIES, AND COMPLAINTS
path: ARTICLE II. - VIOLATIONS, PENALTIES, AND COMPLAINTS
Sec. 29-38. - Violations and penalties of section 29-107.
documents.text:
(a)
Any Customer who has not installed a proper backflow prevention device pursuant to Section 29-107 shall be issued a written warning of the violation with notice to correct the violation.
If a proper device is not installed, service will be suspended. A notice of suspension
of service shall be delivered to or posted at the premises. A proper device must be
installed within five days after delivery or posting of the notice of suspension or
service will be disconnected. All customers who receive a notice of suspension may
appeal as set forth in Section 29-43 .
(b)
In the event service is suspended, it will be reinstated only if a proper device is
installed and inspected, and such inspection results are approved by the CAB, and
all penalties for failure to install a proper device are paid in full.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § 8.3)

documents.title: Sec. 29-39. - Suspension of service for nonpayment.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - VIOLATIONS, PENALTIES, AND COMPLAINTS
path: ARTICLE II. - VIOLATIONS, PENALTIES, AND COMPLAINTS
Sec. 29-39. - Suspension of service for nonpayment.
documents.text:
(a)
When payments for service are not received by the due date set forth on the bill,
which shall be no less than 25 days from the date the bill is prepared, the account
will be considered past due.
(b)
Payments not received within five days after the due date will be considered delinquent.
A penalty will be imposed in accordance with chapter 13 and a notice of delinquent account will be mailed. Owners or Customers who receive
such a notice may appeal as set forth in Section 29-43 .
(c)
Payment for service, penalties, charges, rates, fees, and tolls must be paid by the
date set forth in the notice of delinquent account. If payment is not received, a
notice of suspension of service will be mailed advising that payment must be made
within ten days or service will be disconnected. All Owners or Customers who receive
a notice of suspension may appeal as set forth in Section 29-43 .
(d)
In the event a notice of suspension is sent and whether or not service is actually
suspended, arrangements satisfactory to the CAB shall be made for the payment of all
fees, rates, tolls, penalties or charges due.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § 8.4)

documents.title: Sec. 29-40. - Suspension and disconnection of service.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - VIOLATIONS, PENALTIES, AND COMPLAINTS
path: ARTICLE II. - VIOLATIONS, PENALTIES, AND COMPLAINTS
Sec. 29-40. - Suspension and disconnection of service.
documents.text:
(a)
For violation of any applicable portion of this chapter or the terms and conditions
of an Industrial Wastewater Discharge permit, the CAB may suspend or disconnect service
upon proper notice.
(b)
In conjunction with its Industrial Pretreatment Program, the CAB recognizes the right
of Dominion to enforce its Rules and Regulations by disconnection of Retail Wastewater
Service to those who violate industrial effluent standards of the CAB or Dominion,
whichever are more stringent, and that neither shall interfere with the other in the
enforcement of their respective industrial effluent standards. The CAB will not reconnect
any service connection which shall have been disconnected by Dominion, except upon
the written request of Dominion. The CAB shall notify Dominion of any connection or
disconnection of a sanitary sewer to End Users, at times and in a manner so as to
cause a minimum of inconvenience to either party.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § 8.5)

documents.title: Sec. 29-41. - Informal resolution.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - VIOLATIONS, PENALTIES, AND COMPLAINTS
path: ARTICLE II. - VIOLATIONS, PENALTIES, AND COMPLAINTS
documents.text:
(a)
Any Customer, upon receipt of a notice of violation or penalty of other than Article
V of this chapter, may, within five days from receipt, request a conference with the
General Manager to discuss the violation or penalty. Said conference shall be held
within ten days of receipt of request. After such a conference, the General Manager
shall render an opinion, and notify the Customer by first class mail within five days.
(b)
Any Customer may, within five days from receipt of the General Manager's opinion,
request reconsideration of said opinion. Within five days of the request, the General
Manager shall hold a conference with the Customer and CAB staff. The General Manager
shall accept and consider any relevant evidence. Within ten days from the conference,
the General Manager shall make written findings and an order disposing of the matter
and shall provide the Customer with a copy of such decision. Said decision may be
appealed to the CAB.
(c)
During the informal resolution procedure, as set forth herein, service will be suspended
unless the General Manager determines that there is no danger to the environment,
the POTW, or to any Person or property.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § 8.6)

documents.title: Sec. 29-42. - Suspension hearing.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - VIOLATIONS, PENALTIES, AND COMPLAINTS
path: ARTICLE II. - VIOLATIONS, PENALTIES, AND COMPLAINTS
documents.text:
(a)
Except as provided in an Industrial Wastewater Discharge Permit, as a result of a
violation of Article V of this chapter or in any emergency situation, any Customer
who has received notice of suspension of service may receive a formal hearing prior
to suspension by submitting a written request. Such request shall be submitted within
five business days of receipt of said notice. The hearing shall be held within five
business days of receipt of the written request.
(b)
The General Manager shall designate a hearing officer who may be an officer, agent
or employee of the CAB, provided that said hearing officer shall not have participated
in any manner in the decision to suspend such service.
(c)
At the hearing, the Customer and any representative of the CAB shall be permitted
to appear in person and shall have the right to present evidence and argument, the
right to confront and cross examine any witness. The Customer may be represented by
any Person of his choice or by legal counsel. The hearing officer may receive and
consider any evidence which has probative value and is commonly accepted by reasonable
and prudent Persons in the conduct of their affairs.
(d)
The hearing officer shall determine whether reasonable grounds exist to support the
suspension of service. The hearing officer's decision shall be based upon evidence
adduced at the hearing. The burden of showing that reasonable grounds exist to support
the suspension shall be upon the CAB. The burden of showing mitigating circumstances
shall be upon the Customer.
(e)
Subsequent to the hearing, the hearing officer shall make written findings and an
order disposing of the matter and shall provide the Customer with a copy of such decision
within ten days after the hearing. Said decision may be appealed to the CAB.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § 8.7)

documents.title: Sec. 29-43. - Appeal to the CAB.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - VIOLATIONS, PENALTIES, AND COMPLAINTS
path: ARTICLE II. - VIOLATIONS, PENALTIES, AND COMPLAINTS
documents.text:
(a)
Except as provided in an Industrial Wastewater Discharge Permit or as a result of
a violation of Article V of this chapter, a Customer may appeal the decision of the
hearing officer or the General Manager by filing with the General Manager a written
notice of appeal within ten days after the decision has been received. Such notice
shall set forth in detail the grounds therefor. In the event of failure to file such
written notice of appeal within said ten-day period, the decision of the hearing officer
or General Manager shall become final. Service shall be suspended unless the notice
of appeal is accompanied by payment of all charges, including arrearages, disputed
amounts, and any penalties, charges, rates, fees, and tolls. In the event the decision
is reversed, appropriate refunds will be made. The CAB shall consider such appeal
at the regularly scheduled or special board meeting to be held within 30 days of the
filing of the notice of appeal.
(b)
The General Manager shall submit to the CAB a summary of the proceedings. The Customer
may present evidence to the CAB at the meeting where the appeal is being considered.
The CAB shall then consider all evidence submitted to it by the General Manager, the
Customer, and any other witnesses who may be called. The CAB shall have the right
to reasonably limit the time and manner of any presentation hereunder. Within 15 days
after the CAB hears and considers the appeal, the CAB shall enter a written ruling
based thereon, a copy of which ruling shall be delivered to the Customer. In the event
that the decision is adverse to the Customer, all administrative remedies shall be
deemed to have been exhausted.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § 8.8)

documents.title: Sec. 29-44. - Emergency situations.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - VIOLATIONS, PENALTIES, AND COMPLAINTS
path: ARTICLE II. - VIOLATIONS, PENALTIES, AND COMPLAINTS
documents.text:
If an emergency situation exists which constitutes an imminent threat to the health
or safety of Persons or which may be potentially dangerous to the environment or to
the POTW as determined at the sole discretion of the General Manager, the Customer's
service may be terminated immediately without notice and such termination of service
shall continue for a long as the emergency situation continues to exist.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § 8.9)

documents.title: Sec. 29-45. - Penalties not exclusive.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - VIOLATIONS, PENALTIES, AND COMPLAINTS
path: ARTICLE II. - VIOLATIONS, PENALTIES, AND COMPLAINTS
documents.text:
The penalties set forth in this article are not exclusive and the CAB may prosecute
to the fullest extent of the law any Person engaged in any illegal activities and
may institute whatever civil actions it deems necessary to ensure compliance with
this chapter and to recover any damages, including attorney's fees, caused by any
violations of this chapter.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § 8.10)

documents.title: Sec. 29-46. - Customer complaints.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - VIOLATIONS, PENALTIES, AND COMPLAINTS
path: ARTICLE II. - VIOLATIONS, PENALTIES, AND COMPLAINTS
documents.text:
Any Customer having any complaint with respect to the conduct or action of any employee
of the CAB in connection with the operation of the water and sanitary sewer system
or in connection with the administration or implementation of any rules, regulation
or policy related to the operation of said systems, unless specifically provided for
elsewhere in this article, shall follow the complaint process described hereafter:
(1)
The Customer shall contact the General Manager to register any complaint. The General
Manager will investigate the Customer's complaint and, upon completion of said investigation,
shall contact the Customer and relate all information associated with said complaint
within 15 days. If the investigation yields evidence of actions or conduct contrary
to the operations, policies, rules, regulations or other procedures of the CAB, the
General Manager shall initiate appropriate corrective action and shall promptly report
such action to the complainant.
(2)
The Customer can appeal the General Manager's decision to the CAB. The decision of
the CAB or its representative will be given in writing to the Customer within 30 days
after the receipt of the appeal by the CAB. In the event the decision is adverse to
the Customer, all administrative remedies in connection with the appeal shall be deemed
to have been exhausted.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § 8.11)

documents.title: Sec. 29-47. - Billing-related complaints.
documents.article: ARTICLE II. - VIOLATIONS, PENALTIES, AND COMPLAINTS
path: ARTICLE II. - VIOLATIONS, PENALTIES, AND COMPLAINTS
documents.text:
Any Customer having a billing complaint shall contact the accounting department in
person, by phone or by letter. The accounting department will investigate the Customer's
concerns and, upon completion of this investigation, shall contact the Customer relating
all information associated with said complaint. If an error is discovered during the
investigation, the succeeding bill shall reflect all adjustments. The Customer may
appeal any decision as set forth in this Article.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § 8.12)

documents.title: Sec. 29-68. - General conformance to design and installation of construction.
documents.article: ARTICLE III. - CONSTRUCTION OF WATER DISTRIBUTION AND SANITARY SEWER COLLECTION FACILITIES
path: ARTICLE III. - CONSTRUCTION OF WATER DISTRIBUTION AND SANITARY SEWER COLLECTION FACILITIES
Sec. 29-68. - General conformance to design and installation of construction.
documents.text:
(a)
All of the Retail Facilities shall be designed and installed so as to provide an acceptable
level of service to the Applicant's specific parcel as well as to all Customers of
the CAB.
(b)
All Retail Facilities shall conform to the Technical Specifications. Prior to the
construction of any Retail Facility, the CAB shall review and approve the plans for
the Retail Facility. The plans shall include a description of all necessary sites
and rights-of-way.
(c)
All sites and rights-of-way reasonably required by the CAB shall be conveyed, free
and clear of all liens, to the CAB. Sites and rights-of-way shall include sufficient
property to ensure the CAB will have a sufficient interest in the property to relocate
or reconstruct Retail Facilities if required.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § 4.1)

documents.title: Sec. 29-69. - Extension and sizing of facilities.
documents.article: ARTICLE III. - CONSTRUCTION OF WATER DISTRIBUTION AND SANITARY SEWER COLLECTION FACILITIES
path: ARTICLE III. - CONSTRUCTION OF WATER DISTRIBUTION AND SANITARY SEWER COLLECTION FACILITIES
Sec. 29-69. - Extension and sizing of facilities.
documents.text:
If, in the opinion of the District Engineer, an increase in line size in a Retail
Facility to be installed by an End User is necessary to serve another End User's property,
the applicant End User shall be required to upsize the subject Retail Facility and
the additional/incremental cost in labor and materials resulting from the upsize shall
be the responsibility of the CAB (to be reimbursed to the CAB from the benefiting
End User). If the increase in line size of a Retail Facility is necessitated due to
the particular applicant End User's needs, or design required to meet such needs,
of the applicant End User, the entire cost of the upsized Retail Facility shall be
the responsibility of the applicant End User.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § 4.2)

documents.title: Sec. 29-70. - Acceptance of facilities.
documents.article: ARTICLE III. - CONSTRUCTION OF WATER DISTRIBUTION AND SANITARY SEWER COLLECTION FACILITIES
path: ARTICLE III. - CONSTRUCTION OF WATER DISTRIBUTION AND SANITARY SEWER COLLECTION FACILITIES
documents.text:
The CAB will assume responsibility for providing Retail Services to individual lots
within a development only upon transfer to the CAB of the ownership of all facilities
and any necessary easements. All such Retail Facilities shall be warranted for two
years after acceptance by the CAB.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § 4.3)

documents.title: Sec. 29-71. - Inspection.
documents.article: ARTICLE III. - CONSTRUCTION OF WATER DISTRIBUTION AND SANITARY SEWER COLLECTION FACILITIES
path: ARTICLE III. - CONSTRUCTION OF WATER DISTRIBUTION AND SANITARY SEWER COLLECTION FACILITIES
documents.text:
The CAB shall have a right to inspect at all times all facilities connected to, or
to become connected to, the Retail Facilities. Authorized employees and representatives
of the CAB shall be allowed free access at all reasonable hours to any End User's
property to ensure compliance with this chapter. The CAB shall have the right to inspect
all businesses to determine if pretreatment may be necessary, whether all pretreatment
systems are operating in compliance and to take all necessary actions if said business
is found to be out of compliance. The CAB shall have the right to assess its costs
for enforcement and corrective actions, levy fines and collect penalties to any business
that is not in full compliance with the Pretreatment Requirements or other CAB rules.
(Rules of 8-26-2020(4), § 4.4)

documents.title: Secs. 29-72—29-100. - Reserved.
documents.article: ARTICLE III. - CONSTRUCTION OF WATER DISTRIBUTION AND SANITARY SEWER COLLECTION FACILITIES
path: ARTICLE III. - CONSTRUCTION OF WATER DISTRIBUTION AND SANITARY SEWER COLLECTION FACILITIES
