path: Chapter 33 - UTILITIES—DOMINION WATER AND SANITATION RULES AND REGULATIONS
Sec. 33-300. - Fats, oils and grease (FOG) pretreatment requirements.
documents.text:
(a)
Applicability.
(1)
Nondomestic users. This section applies to any nondomestic user where preparation, manufacturing, or
processing of food occurs. These users shall install and maintain a gravity grease
interceptor (GGI).
(2)
Domestic users. This section does not apply to domestic users.
(b)
GGI requirements.
(1)
Plan reviews.
a.
Any nondomestic user subject to this section shall obtain a plan review from Dominion
prior to any new or modified operation.
b.
The plan review shall determine the need, size, location, and other requirements of
the GGI necessary to control discharges.
c.
Written approval must be obtained prior to installation of the GGI.
d.
Plan reviews shall be conducted and approval obtained prior to the construction of
a new building, sale or transfer of ownership of the business, change in the nature
of the services provided, change in building use, or remodeling of the facility.
(2)
GGI criteria.
a.
Sinks, floor drains, floor sinks, mop sinks, disposals, dishwashers and other plumbing
fixtures in kitchens, bars, busing stations, and other food service areas into which
wastewater is likely to or has the potential to contain FOG must be connected to the
GGI.
b.
Water closets, urinals, and other plumbing fixtures conveying human waste shall not
drain into or through the GGI.
c.
Each business establishment for which a GGI is required shall have a GGI serving only
that business except where shared GGIs are specifically approved by Dominion.
d.
All GGIs and associated plumbing shall be installed by a licensed plumber or contractor.
e.
All GGIs must have two compartments separated by a baffle wall. The primary compartment
shall have a volume equal to two-thirds of the total capacity, and the secondary compartment
shall have a volume equal to one-third of the total capacity. Each compartment shall
be accessible by a traffic-rated manhole above the inlet and outlet piping with a
minimum diameter of 24 inches. Manhole covers shall not be locked, or otherwise fastened
in place such that access is restricted.
(3)
Exceeding limits.
a.
If a facility's discharge exceeds the imposed limits for oil and grease or contributes
to an excess build-up of FOG in the sanitary sewer line, the user may be required
to install an appropriately-sized GGI.
b.
The user may be charged for any fees associated with sampling, including labor costs,
travel time, sampling supplies, and analytical costs.
(4)
GGI maintenance.
a.
GGIs shall be maintained, at the expense of the user, by regularly scheduled pumping

remain on the premises and accessible for review by Dominion at any time for a minimum
of three years. Dominion may require a user to submit all copies of all records, receipts,
and manifests of GGI and/or WGB maintenance, removal of GGI and/or WGB contents, and
off-site hauling of FOG waste.
e.
In the event a GGI is not properly maintained by the user, Dominion may authorize
and require such maintenance work to be performed on behalf of the user. The costs
of such maintenance shall be billed directly to the user and shall become part of
the charges due.
f.
Biological treatment or enzyme treatment shall not be substitute for the servicing
of the GGI. Use of enzymes to emulsify FOG is prohibited. The direct addition of any
enzyme, chemical, microbial agent to a GGI is prohibited.
(Rules of 7-17-2019(9), att. C-3)

documents.title: Sec. 34-2. - Definitions.
documents.chapter: Chapter 34 - UTILITIES—DOMINION WATER AND SANITATION DISTRICT STANDARDS AND SPECIFICATIONS FOR POTABLE WATER, SANITARY SEWER, AND NONPOTABLE WATER
path: Chapter 34 - UTILITIES—DOMINION WATER AND SANITATION DISTRICT STANDARDS AND SPECIFICATIONS FOR POTABLE WATER, SANITARY SEWER, AND NONPOTABLE WATER
documents.text:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the
meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates
a different meaning:
Approved documents means construction documents, including plans and specifications prepared by the
Customer's Professional Engineer and approved by the DWSD Engineer.
Board means the Board of Directors for the District.
CAB means Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board.
Commercial development means Multifamily dwelling units and all other development including offices, schools,
and restaurants, except residential development.
Contractor means any person, firm corporation, association or agency constructing facilities
which are to be connected to the District's facilities.
Customer means any person, firm, corporation, association or agency who is authorized, or
who desires, to obtain water, sewer, or nonpotable water services from the District.
District Manager means the person designated to act as District Manager for DWSD. The District Manager
administers and supervises the affairs of and operations and maintenance of facilities
of the District.
DWSD or District means Dominion Water and Sanitation District, their Successors or Assigns.
DWSD Engineer means the person designated to act as DWSD Engineer for Dominion Water and Sanitation
District. The DWSD Engineer oversees plan reviews, site inspections, and administers
the Standards in this chapter.
DWSD Representative means a person designated by the DWSD Engineer to conduct plan review, site inspection
and other duties with respect to any Project.
Fire Marshal means the person designated by the fire department (South Metro Fire Protection District)
for the jurisdiction in which the system construction occurs. The Fire Marshal shall
have sole authority over fire protection matters.
Open Space means any area not intended to receive future development.
Paving means concrete or asphalt pavement.
Project means a facility or portion thereof which is to be connected to the District's facilities
as described in the Application for Service in Section 34-32 .
Residential Development means single-family dwelling units.
Representative. See DWSD Representative.
Utilities Director means the person who oversees the operations of DWSD.
(Rules of 7-17-2019(7), § 1.05)

(b)
The approval is only valid for one year. If construction has not begun within one
year, the Construction Documents must be resubmitted, and, in case of any change of

documents.title: Sec. 34-35. - Easements.
documents.chapter: Chapter 34 - UTILITIES—DOMINION WATER AND SANITATION DISTRICT STANDARDS AND SPECIFICATIONS FOR POTABLE WATER, SANITARY SEWER, AND NONPOTABLE WATER
path: Chapter 34 - UTILITIES—DOMINION WATER AND SANITATION DISTRICT STANDARDS AND SPECIFICATIONS FOR POTABLE WATER, SANITARY SEWER, AND NONPOTABLE WATER
documents.text:
(a)
Easements (residential development).
(1)
All water, sanitary sewer, underdrain and nonpotable water facilities which are to
be granted to DWSD shall be located within a dedicated right-of-way or easement.
(2)
Easements shall be dedicated on the plat or granted to DWSD on the DWSD's Grant of
Easement form. All necessary easements shall be executed and recorded prior to the
start of construction. The start of the two-year warranty period is dependent on the
requirements in section 34-76 . Trees shall not be placed in DWSD's easements without written permission of the
DWSD Engineer.
(3)
In the event that trees are placed in DWSD's easements without written permission
of the DWSD Engineer, they shall be removed at the expense of the Customer.
(4)
The minimum width of an easement for a single utility line shall be 15 feet. If two
or more utilities are to be located within the same easement, the minimum width shall
be:
a.
Two utility lines: 30 feet.
b.
Three utility lines: 40 feet.
c.
Four utility lines: 50 feet.
Utilities shall be generally centered in the easement unless otherwise approved by
DWSD.
(b)
Easements/plan approval (commercial development).
(1)
The approval of utilities plans for commercial development within the District where
the District will own and maintain the water, sanitary sewer, underdrain and nonpotable
facilities is contingent on the acceptance of the appropriate easements. Easements
are required to be granted to the District for the purpose of maintaining the utilities
once they have been granted final acceptance by the District. Easements shall be dedicated
on the plat or granted to DWSD on the Dominion's Grant of Easement form. If the easements
are being dedicated on the plat, a copy needs to be submitted with the drawings at
the time of initial submittal for review. Easements granted by separate document will
require the following:
a.
Metes and Bounds legal description.
b.
Exhibit showing the limits of the easements.
c.
Title policy for the property.
(2)
The legal description, exhibit, title policy and executed easement forms will be submitted
for approval to the District prior to the approval of the Construction Documents.
(3)
In the event that the easement cannot be prepared prior to approval of the plans,
a deposit must be made to ensure preparation of all of the required legal documents.
(4)
The amount of the deposit will be based on the following criteria:
Table 34-35 . Deposits
Water & Sewer Lines 500 linear feet or less
$500.00
Water & Sewer Lines between 500 and 1,500 linear feet
$3,000.00

documents.text:
(a)
Any request for a variance from the requirements of the Standards and Specifications
in this chapter shall be submitted in writing to the District Engineer. Each variance
request shall include a detailed description of the proposed variance together with
the Customer's Professional Engineer's analysis of the impact of the variance. The
decision of the District Engineer to grant or deny any variance will be final.
(b)
Each variance request shall include a detailed description of each location of the
variance. For example, a variance to the horizontal separation requirements will not
be granted for the entire project. The request must include a description of each
location that violates the Standards in this chapter and requires a variance.
(c)
The decision of the DWSD Engineer to grant or deny any variance will be final. Variances
will be granted on a per-project basis, and are not to be interpreted as a permanent
change to the Standards in this chapter.
(Rules of 7-17-2019(7), § 2.07)

ARTICLE III. - CONSTRUCTION REQUIREMENTS AND ACCEPTANCE PROCEDURES
documents.text:
Following final approval of the Documents, the Customer may proceed with construction.
In addition to all construction requirements contained in other portions of the specifications
in this chapter:
(1)
A preconstruction conference shall be held prior to the commencement of work with
the District Manager, District Engineer, District's other Representatives, Contractor
who is to perform the work, and the Customer's Professional Engineer.
(2)
The District Engineer shall be notified a minimum of 48 hours prior to the commencement
of work. This notice shall be given for all new projects and for projects that have
been inactive for more than one week.
(3)
Inspections for ongoing work may be scheduled with 24-hour notice.
(4)
Development phasing of any project shall be shown on the initial Document submittal
and made a part of the application procedure. All construction shall be accurately
surveyed and staked in accordance with the Approved Documents.
(5)
Adequate provisions for notification of a service outage must be given by the Customer
prior to the actual isolation of the system by the District. Outages shall be kept
to a minimum. Outages shall be coordinated a minimum of two weeks in advance.
(6)
The District shall be notified whenever it becomes necessary to open or close a valve
on the existing water system. Only District personnel are authorized to operate valves
in the service area. The Customer may operate valves under the direct supervision
of the District or in a life safety emergency.
(Rules of 7-17-2019(7), § 3.02)

documents.text:
(a)
The District shall have a right to inspect at all times all facilities connected to,
or to become connected to, the District's facilities. Authorized employees and representatives
of the District shall be allowed free access at all reasonable hours to any building
or premises receiving water, sanitary sewer, or nonpotable water service to ensure
compliance with the specifications in this chapter.
(b)
Any inspection performed by the District is solely for the purposes of the District
and the District assumes no liability or responsibility as a result of having performed
any such inspection, for having failed to perform any such inspection or for having
collected a fee therefor. Any such inspection shall not be deemed to be an approval
of the size, slope, alignment, materials used in construction, the method used in
excavating, the placing of pipe, jointing, testing, backfilling or any other aspect
of the facility inspected.
(c)
Personnel authorized by the District shall inspect all construction of utilities.
(d)
Inspection shall not relieve the Customer from any obligation to perform the work
strictly in accordance with the Standards in this chapter and the Approved Documents.
Any work, which is not in accordance with the Standards in this chapter and the Approved
Documents, shall be removed and corrected at the Customer's sole expense.
(e)
Approval by the District shall in no manner relieve the Customer from responsibility
for errors or omissions in the plans. Any errors shall be corrected by Customer at
no expense to the District.
(f)
Whenever a conflict occurs in the Standards in this chapter or between the Standards
in this chapter and Approved Documents, the District Engineer shall make the final
interpretation.
(g)
All materials used shall be subject to the inspection and approval of the District
at all times. The District has the right to perform any testing deemed necessary to
ensure compliance of the material with the Standards in this chapter. Failure to condemn
or reject inferior materials or work shall not be construed as acceptance.
(h)
The District shall have the authority to reject defective or inferior materials or
defective workmanship and to suspend work until such time that the Customer has replaced
the materials or corrected the defective work.
(i)
Whenever defective materials or work are rejected, the Customer shall promptly remove
the defective materials and replace all defective work to the satisfaction of the
District. In the event the Customer fails to remove rejected materials within a reasonable

documents.text:
(a)
Shop drawings and engineering data (submittals) covering all equipment and all fabricated
components and building materials which will become a permanent part of the Project
shall be submitted to DWSD for review, as required. Submittals shall verify compliance
with the Standards in this chapter, and shall include drawings and descriptive information
in sufficient detail to show the kind, size, arrangement, and the operation of component
materials and devices; the external connections, anchorages, and supports required;
the performance characteristics; and dimensions needed for installation and correlation
with other materials and equipment.
(b)
All submittals, regardless of origin, shall be approved by Contractor and clearly
identified with the name of the Project, Contractor's name, and references to applicable
paragraphs of the Standards contained in this chapter and Approved Documents. Each
copy of all submittals, regardless of origin, shall be stamped or affixed with an
approval statement of the Contractor. If a project had an Engineer of Record as the
designer, then submittals must be reviewed and approved by the Engineer prior to being
submitted to DWSD. The submittal shall bear their stamp of approval. Each submittal
shall indicate the intended use of the item. When catalog pages are submitted, applicable
items shall be clearly identified and inapplicable data crossed out. The current revision,
issue number, and date shall be indicated on all drawings and other descriptive data.
(c)
Submittals shall be delivered electronically to DWSD in PDF format and with a hard
copy. DWSD's review of submittals covers only general conformity to the Standards
in this chapter, external connections, and dimensions that affect the layout; it does
not indicate thorough review of all dimensions, quantities, and details of the material,
equipment, device, or item covered. DWSD's review shall not relieve the Contractor
of sole responsibility for errors, omissions, or deviations in the drawings and data,
nor of the Contractor's sole responsibility for compliance with the Approved Documents.
DWSD shall review and return comments within 21 days. A list of submittals to be approved
by DWSD shall be provided to the Contractor prior to construction.
(d)
Adequate operation and maintenance information shall be supplied for all equipment
requiring maintenance or other attention. The Contractor shall provide a Project-specific
operation and maintenance manual for each type of equipment installed. Unless otherwise

documents.text:
(a)
Line and grade for water, sewer, underdrain and nonpotable water lines shall be established
by a Professional Land Surveyor licensed to practice in the State of Colorado.
(b)
(1)
Correct alignment and elevation of the utilities as shown on the Approved Documents
is the responsibility of the Customer. Approval of the staked alignment and elevations
by the District does not relieve the Customer in any manner from the responsibility
for field errors. No pipe may be installed without line and grade stakes set by the
Surveyor and approved by the District.
(2)
Exception: If a main is to be extended in an existing street and if the Customer's
Professional Engineer who prepared the plans can show that the finish grade of the
street is to remain unchanged, no grade stakes need be set.
(c)
Hubs and stakes shall be set on an offset line to mark the location of the centerline
of the main. Centerline hubs and stakes may be used in addition to the offset hubs
and stakes; however, they may not be set instead of the offset hubs and stakes.
(d)
All valves, crosses, tees, bends, fittings, fire hydrants, services, manholes, etc.,
shall be staked for line and grade. Points of curvature and points of tangency of
curves, as well as points on the curve, shall be staked for line and grade.
(Rules of 7-17-2019(7), § 3.05)

documents.title: Sec. 34-71. - Traffic control.

documents.text:
(a)
All traffic control shall be in accordance with the requirements of Douglas County
Public Works, Colorado Department of Highways and the law enforcement agency (i.e.,
Douglas County Sheriff, Colorado State Patrol) whose jurisdiction applies or other
governing entity.
(b)
The Customer shall be responsible for the provision of a safe travelway on all dedicated
roadways on and adjacent to the job site. The Customer shall provide for proper traffic
control warning devices around all excavations, embankments and obstructions and shall
provide maintenance of said devices.
(c)
The Customer shall not close any street or portion of a street without receiving an
approved traffic control plan from the agencies that have jurisdiction. It is the
Customer's responsibility to notify Douglas County, DWSD, the Douglas County Sheriff
and South Metro Fire Rescue Authority a minimum of 24 hours prior to closing any street.
The Customer shall also notify Douglas County, DWSD, the Sheriff and Fire Department
immediately after opening of any street.
(Rules of 7-17-2019(7), § 3.07)

documents.text:
In the event that existing water, sanitary sewer, underdrain, or nonpotable water
service will be interrupted as a result of construction, the Contractor shall be responsible
for written notification of all affected customers at least two weeks in advance of
the work. Verbal notification shall be made again the day prior to the service interruption.
Service interruptions for schools, medical clinics and various commercial businesses
shall be conducted at times specified by DWSD. If outages for more than four hours
are necessary, they must be conducted at times to cause the least inconvenience to
other customers. Under all circumstances, work shall be continuous until all customers
are back in service. If, in the process of installing a connection, there exists a
facility that cannot be out of water, as designated by DWSD, such as a hospital, appropriate
temporary means shall be taken to provide and convey water. DWSD, the County and Fire
Department shall approve any such measures prior to their construction.
(Rules of 7-17-2019(7), § 3.08)

documents.title: Sec. 34-73. - Connections to existing mains.

path: Chapter 34 - UTILITIES—DOMINION WATER AND SANITATION DISTRICT STANDARDS AND SPECIFICATIONS FOR POTABLE WATER, SANITARY SEWER, AND NONPOTABLE WATER
ARTICLE III. - CONSTRUCTION REQUIREMENTS AND ACCEPTANCE PROCEDURES
documents.text:
(a)
Where connections are made between new and existing lines, each connection shall be
made as indicated in the Documents. If field conditions make the detailed connection
impossible, then an alternative method may be used with the approval of the District.
(b)
The location of existing stub-outs shown in the District's records is based on the
best available information and may not be exact. The Customer shall be responsible
for determining the exact location and elevation of any stub-out and adjusting the
design or construction of the new facilities as necessary.
(c)
The Customer shall notify the District a minimum of one week in advance of connection
to an existing line or interruption service to an existing line.
(d)
The Customer is responsible for any dewatering necessary which shall be done without
damage to property and as detailed in Section 34-98 (a)(6).
(e)
Special care shall be taken to prevent contamination when draining, cutting into,
or making connections to existing pipes. No trench water, mud, or dirt shall be permitted
to enter the lines as detailed in Section 34-98 (d)(1).
(f)
At the beginning of a construction project, the Customer shall install a watertight
plug in the connection manhole, or first manhole upstream, in order to prevent any
inflow to enter the existing sewer system. The Contractor only, in the presence of
the District, shall remove this plug. All related costs shall be borne by the Customer.
(Rules of 7-17-2019(7), § 3.09)

documents.title: Sec. 34-74. - Existing utilities and structures.

(a)
It shall be the responsibility of the Customer to investigate and verify the existence
and location and elevations of existing utilities.
(b)
The Customer shall be solely responsible for the protection of all existing structures
or utilities, including pipes, cables, fences or similar items. Any existing structures
or utilities disturbed by construction are to be restored to their original location
and condition unless otherwise noted on the drawings. Permission for adjustment of
existing structures, utilities or other items shall be obtained from the appropriate
owners or agencies in written form with items clearly identified.
(Rules of 7-17-2019(7), § 3.10)

documents.title: Sec. 34-75. - Safety.

documents.text:
(a)
The Customer shall be responsible for initiating, maintaining and supervising all
safety programs in connection with the work. It shall be the responsibility of the
Customer to provide all safety measures for the District in order for the District
to perform the required inspections.
(b)
The Customer shall comply with all applicable laws, ordinances, rules, regulations
and orders of any public body having jurisdiction for the safety of persons or property
or to protect them from damage, injury or loss, and shall provide and maintain all
necessary safeguards for the protection of property and utilities. All damage, injury
or loss to any property caused, directly or indirectly, in whole or in part, by the
Customer, or anyone directly or indirectly employed by the Customer or anyone for
whose acts the Customer may be liable, shall be remedied by the Customer.
(Rules of 7-17-2019(7), § 3.11)

documents.text:
The District will accept water, sanitary sewer, underdrain and nonpotable water projects,
as described herein and outlined in other articles of this chapter.
(1)
Pre-warranty inspections.
a.
Testing and reporting. The Contractor shall perform all tests and inspections for water, sewer, underdrain
and nonpotable installations as described in the individual articles of this chapter.
Copies of the test reports shall be provided to the District and shall be performed
in the presence of the District, as required. The following list of the tests and
inspections are required and shall be performed as specified herein and in the individual
articles of this chapter:
1.
Water installations.
(i)
Hydrostatic Test.
(ii)
Disinfection.
(iii)
Fire Hydrant Leak Test.
(iv)
Cathodic Protection System Test.
(v)
Tracer Wire Test.
2.
Sewer installations.
(i)
Alignment and Deflection Tests (Mandrel for straight sections only).
(ii)
TV Inspection with location and the distance from the starting manhole of each tap
called out and provide CD or DVD to DWSD (straight and curvilinear sections).
(iii)
Leakage Tests (Low Pressure Air Test, ASTM 1417).
(iv)
Exfiltration and Infiltration (if applicable).
(v)
Vacuum Test of Manholes (ASTM C1244).
(vi)
Tracer Wire Test.
3.
Nonpotable water installations.
(i)
Hydrostatic Test.
(ii)
Cathodic Protection.
(iii)
Tracer Wire Test.
4.
Other items.
(i)
Compaction of Bedding, Backfill and Subgrade.
(ii)
Concrete and Asphalt Paving (all tests required by Douglas County).
(iii)
Concrete Curb, Gutter, Sidewalk, Motorcourts, etc. (all tests required by Douglas
County).
(iv)
Any required materials testing.
b.
District and Contractor approval. After installation and testing of all water, sanitary sewer, and nonpotable lines
is completed, and the District has accepted the tests, a Pre-Warranty Inspection shall
take place. The District and Contractor shall inspect for approval the following items:
1.
Valve box alignment and accessibility.
2.
Manhole ring alignment and vertical adjustment.
3.
Main line, blowoff assembly and fire hydrant location and operation.
4.
Proper operation of all valves, including air/vac valves.
5.
Proper operation of all meters.
6.
Surface restoration, including asphalt and concrete pavement, sidewalks, motorcourts
and landscaping.
7.
Underdrain Cleanout Alignment.
8.
Surface settlement.
All discrepancies and punchlist items shall be noted on a punch list which shall be
submitted to the Contractor for correction prior to the start of the Warranty Period.
(2)
Record drawings and easements.
a.

documents.text:
The Contractor shall maintain a working set of Construction Record Drawings at the
site. The Construction Record Drawings shall be continuously kept up to date and available
to the District upon request and shall be submitted at the conclusion of the Project.
The Construction Record Drawings shall include the following information, at a minimum:
1.
Surface features including manholes, valve boxes, cleanouts and fire hydrants. Buried
valves shall have top of nut elevation recorded.
2.
New water, sewer, or nonpotable lines installed as part of the Project, including
service connections and underdrains. All service connections, wyes, tees, taps, and
stubs shall be located on the plan view and the invert elevations noted.
3.
Curvilinear pipes shall have centerline and elevation noted at each PC, Mid-Point
& PT.
4.
All manholes shall be provided with elevations for all pipe inverts entering and leaving
the manhole as well as the elevation of the rim. All other structures shall be provided
with elevations of the pipes entering or below the structure and the elevation of
the rim or access cover.
5.
All visible and buried utilities encountered during construction, including those
that may not have been marked on the surface but were discovered during construction.
The top of pipe elevation shall be recorded for all buried utilities (including water,
sewer, underdrain, nonpotable water, storm sewer, gas, electric, cable, fiber optic,
and telephone) as well as the surface elevation above each utility following completed
backfill.
6.
All changes or addenda issued by the District.
b.
All field books, notes, and other data developed by Contractor in performing surveys
required as part of the Project shall be available to District for examination throughout
the construction period. All such data shall be submitted to District with the other
documentation required for initial acceptance of the Project.
c.
The Contractor shall furnish an electronic survey file at the completion of the Project.
Electronic drawing files shall be provided in AutoCAD Land Desktop Civil 3D, Version
2013 or newer. Drawing files shall be developed utilizing multiple layers. Layer names
shall comply with the AIA layer naming convention. Drawings shall be at real world
scale with the appropriate zone and coordinate system established. AutoCAD survey
points and/or blocks shall be inserted at world elevation. Use only AutoCAD colors
1 through 16. Civil 3D styles and entity colors shall be ByLayer unless an exception
is warranted. Shape files not associated with the drawing files are not permitted.

Drawings shall be loadable in Civil 3D without .shx errors. LandXML data shall be
provided as applicable to the site. All horizontal and vertical datum is required

All information required in the Construction Record Drawings as specified herein.

Plat.
3.
Topographic survey to identify contour elevations and all visible surface features

5.
Stream bed and water surface elevations at the crossing of any waterways.
6.
Existing rights-of-way and easements and new permanent easements or temporary construction
easements within 30 feet of each side of the pipeline.
d.
Following the completion of the Project, the following items shall be submitted to
the District:
1.
Completed Construction Record Drawings.
2.
All field books, notes, and other data developed by the Contractor.
3.
A complete electronic survey that shows surface features, utilities, roadways, and
the new system. The survey shall be delivered to the Owner in electronic format on
a DVD.
4.
Easements for water, sanitary sewer, and nonpotable lines which were not dedicated
to the plat.
5.
Grant and Acceptance of Utilities Agreement.

Warranty period. Upon satisfactory completion of the above, the District will accept the utilities
subject to a two-year warranty. During the warranty, the Contractor shall be solely

the District, must be made immediately in order to maintain a reasonable level of
water and sanitary sewer service, the District may make such emergency repairs without
prior notice to the Contractor at the Contractor's cost and expense, but the District
shall give the Contractor notice thereof as soon as reasonably possible. If the District
deems it necessary to flush water mains to maintain water quality control in a portion

Final acceptance. At least 45 days prior to the expiration of the Warranty Period, the District and
the Contractor shall conduct a final inspection of the facilities. The District shall
prepare a list of any defects. At least 30 days prior to the expiration of the Warranty
Period, the District shall submit the list of defects to the Contractor, and the Contactor
shall repair or cause to be repaired those items. Upon completion by the Contractor,
to the reasonable satisfaction of the District, of the items contained on the list,
the District shall accept the facilities. The District agrees that from the date of
final acceptance, the District shall be responsible for all future repairs, maintenance,
operation and use of the facilities, other than any latent defect discovered by the
District after final acceptance.

documents.text:
Water distribution mains are generally defined as pipes sized four inches or more
that serve multiple Customers. Water transmission lines are generally defined as pipes
sized 16 inches or greater that have no direct connections for Customers. These pipe
sizes are not absolute. It is possible to have an 18-inch water distribution main
with service taps for Customers. This article specifies the criteria for water distribution
mains, but transmission mains should also follow these general requirements. Transmission
mains must undergo special review and approval from the District and may be subject
to more stringent requirements.
(1)
Flow design criteria. Water system design shall be based on the hydraulic capacity of the system using
the following criteria:
a.
Domestic demand criteria.
1.
The domestic demand criteria are set forth in Table 34-96.1.

b.
Water line looping.
1.
Water lines shall be looped so that no more than one fire hydrant is out of service
at any time when any repair of the water line or an interruption of service occurs.
No more than one fire hydrant or fire sprinkler system shall be installed on a single
line that is not looped.
2.
In the event that the looping is to be constructed as part of future phases, it shall
be included as part of the pipe network analysis. Upsizing, at the customer's cost,
of distribution lines shall be required when the hydraulic analysis indicates that
upsizing is needed for current or future phases to meet the hydraulic criteria for
all construction phases.
(3)
Location and alignment.
a.
Streets. Water mains shall be located within dedicated rights-of-way along an alignment that
generally follows the roadway six feet inside of the flowline. On streets running
north and south, the water line shall be placed on the east side of the street. On
streets running east and west, the water line shall be placed on the north side of
the street. On roadways which meander in each direction, the water line shall not
zig-zag across the street.
b.
Easements.
1.
When water mains cannot be located within dedicated right-of-way, they shall be located
within a dedicated easement at least 15 feet wide as required in Section 34-35 . Within residential developments, the easement shall be located within an open space
tract. Under exceptional circumstances, the District Engineer may allow the easement
to be located between two residential lots; however, the easement shall be at least
20 feet wide. In some instances, additional width may be required in accordance with Section 34-35 .
2.
The water main shall be placed no more than two feet from the centerline of the easement
with a minimum depth of cover of six feet when located in an easement. Horizontal
deflections or curvilinear alignments in water mains located in easements are not
permitted. Valves may be located in dedicated open space or common areas, but not
between residential lots.
3.
Grading within the District easement is permissible; however, the side slope may not
exceed a 6:1 ratio. The grade along the length of the easement may not exceed five
percent unless otherwise approved by the District Engineer. Vehicle access must be
maintained at all times.
4.

When a water main crosses an existing or future open space drainageway, the line shall
cross perpendicular to the drainageway or as close to perpendicular as feasible. If
the slope of the drainageway downstream from the crossing exceeds a grade of 0.5 percent
within 200 feet of the crossing, a cutoff wall located ten feet to 15 feet downstream
from the crossing shall be required. The cutoff wall shall continue to a minimum depth
of two feet below the water line. A minimum six-foot-wide footing is required at the
bottom of the cutoff wall. The water line shall be concrete encased as required in
Detail SM-2 Concrete Encasement in Section 34-211 for the width of the drainageway plus five feet on each side.
c.
Alignment with other utilities. Water lines shall be designed to adhere to the minimum alignment requirements as
stated herein. Variances may be granted by DWSD to decrease separation within local
roadways where insufficient room is available. Variance requests shall be submitted
as required in section 34-37 . Variances will not be allowed in easements or open spaces. Variances will be reviewed
and approved on a limited basis, and will not be considered when adjusting the locations
of the planned installation can be easily accomplished.
1.
Vertical utility separation; for all utilities. A minimum of 18 inches of vertical separation is required for parallel lines and
when crossing any other utility. All effort shall be made to lay out the system to
meet these minimum requirements. Generally, water lines shall be a minimum of 18 inches
above nonpotable water lines, which shall be a minimum of 18 inches above storm sewers,
which shall be a minimum of 18 inches above sanitary sewers. Dry utilities, such as
gas and electrical, should be generally located above wet utilities, such as water.
Utility crossings shall follow Detail WM-19 in Section 34-211 and other applicable standards depending on the situation outlined in the detail.
2.
Horizontal utility separation; for all utilities.
(i)
Potable water lines shall be designed so that ten feet of horizontal separation, measured
from outside edge of pipe to outside edge of pipe, shall be maintained from sanitary
sewer, nonpotable water, and storm sewer lines. Sanitary sewer lines shall be designed
so that ten feet of horizontal separation, measured from outside edge of pipe to outside
edge of pipe, shall be maintained from potable water, nonpotable water, and storm
sewer lines. Nonpotable water lines shall be designed so that ten feet of horizontal

(ii)
Separation from dry utilities shall be based on the requirements of the owning agency
of the dry utility and to allow enough space for safe construction and future maintenance
of both lines.
(iii)
When horizontal separation of ten feet is not possible, one of the following special
construction measures shall be incorporated into the design in order for the District
to approve the requested variance. All utilities shall be laid in a separate trench,
regardless of which option is used. Note that the separation distance between potable
and nonpotable water lines may be reduced to no closer than six feet, measured outside
of pipe to outside of pipe, without requiring special construction measures. However,
a variance request is still necessary. All efforts shall be made to maintain the ten-foot
minimum separation requirement. Special construction measures for when less than ten
feet of separation is proposed shall be:
A.
Sanitary sewer or storm sewer lines that do not meet the separation requirements to
potable or nonpotable water lines shall be constructed of C900 water pipe grade PVC
pipe, having a minimum pressure rating of 150 psi. All other Standards in this chapter
for water line materials and construction shall apply. The completed section of sewer
(storm or sanitary) shall be pressure tested to 150 psi to ensure there are no leaks.
The pipe shall be continuously marked by means of wrapping utility marking tape indicating
the line's service (sanitary or storm). The C900 material shall be transitioned to
and from at manholes only, no partial reaches are allowed, and shall continue for
the entire length of the pipe that does not meet the separation distance;
B.
Potable water or nonpotable water lines that do not meet the separation requirements
to sanitary sewer or storm sewer lines shall be bored/constructed of fusible HDPE
or welded steel pipe. There shall be no mechanical fittings for the entire length
of the pipe that does not meet separation distance. The specification for the materials
and construction shall be submitted by the Engineer for review by DWSD; or
C.
Potable water, nonpotable water, sanitary sewer, or storm sewer lines that do not
meet the separation requirements to other utilities shall be installed in a casing
pipe or flow fill for the entire length of the pipe that does not meet separation
distance. Casing pipe design shall be submitted for review along with the variance.

over the top of the pipe after final grade has been established. Where the water line
is constructed in an easement between lots, the minimum depth shall be six feet from
final grade to top of pipe. The maximum depth of a water main shall not exceed ten
feet to top of pipe after final grade has been established unless a variance request
is approved.
(6)
Groundwater barriers. Continuity of embedment material shall be interrupted by low permeability groundwater
barriers to impede passage of water through the embedment. Groundwater barriers shall
be soil plugs of three feet in length, extending the full depth and width of granular
material unless otherwise indicated on the drawings. Groundwater barriers shall be
placed at designated locations and indicated on the drawings. The locations may be
adjusted based upon the field conditions encountered. Any change from the locations
indicated on the drawings shall be approved by DWSD and shall be recorded on the record
drawings. Groundwater barriers for water lines shall be used where the trench is below
the groundwater elevation, where a pipe crosses a pond or embankment and concrete
encasement is not used, or any other area where the flow of groundwater in the trench
is possible and must be prevented. When used for water lines, groundwater barriers
shall be spaced not more than 400 feet apart unless otherwise indicated on the drawings.
Materials shall be as specified in Section 34-97 (c)(20).
(7)
Valves.
a.
Placement criteria.
1.
Valves shall be placed in the distribution system in accordance with the criteria
below. These criteria shall be the minimum requirement and additional valves may be
required where the District determines they are necessary.
2.
Valves shall be placed in the distribution system such that:
(i)

break.
(ii)
No more than one fire hydrant or fire suppression system will be out of service as
a result of a single main break. Adjacent fire hydrants or fire suppression systems
shall not be affected.
(iii)
No more than three valves shall be necessary to isolate a single main break.
(iv)
The maximum spacing between valves on a single line shall not exceed 500 feet for
mains in residential or commercial zones. Sixteen-inch and larger mains may have greater
spacings, up to 800 feet, if no laterals or taps are present and the District approves.
(v)
Any connection to the transmission system shall have a means of isolation directly
adjacent to the transmission line. If a connection results in an adjacent service
and fire hydrant being out of service as a result of a transmission main break, an
additional valve will be required on the transmission main.
(vi)
Any future extensions of distribution mains may be accomplished without interruption
of service.
(vii)
When a water line is placed through a side lot easement or tract for the purpose of
looping or connecting to an infrastructure water line, isolation valves shall be placed
at the points of connection. No water services shall be permitted on this portion
of the water line.
(viii)
Valves may not be moved from the location shown on the Approved Documents without
District approval.
b.
Location and alignment. Valve locations shall be determined in accordance with the following:
1.
At intersections, valves shall be located 2.5 feet from the center of the tee or cross
to the center of the valve.
2.
In the middle of blocks, valves shall be located along the projection of a property
line, and adjacent to a fire hydrant.
3.
Valves shall be located within paved areas at a minimum of one foot from the lip of
the curb and gutter or the edge of pan on the street side.
4.
Valves in landscaped or open space areas shall have an 18-inch square, six-inch thick,
reinforced concrete collar poured around the box.
5.
When a water line is placed through a side lot easement or tract for the purpose of
looping or connecting to an infrastructure water line, isolation valves shall be placed
at the connection in the street and on the connection to the infrastructure line.
No water services shall be permitted on this portion of the water line. Exceptions
to the above criteria may be permitted for wet taps or in areas where a valve would
be deeper than ten feet.
c.

Resilient wedge gate valves. Resilient wedge gate valves shall be installed on water mains 12 inches in diameter
and smaller. Resilient wedge gate valves shall be line size, or one nominal size smaller
with reducers on each side. Resilient wedge gate valves shall be no smaller than four
inches. Resilient wedge gate valves shall comply with all provisions of Section 34-97 (c)(5)a.
d.
Butterfly valves. Butterfly valves shall be installed on water mains 16 inches in diameter and larger.
Butterfly valves shall be line size for all locations. Butterfly valves shall comply
with all provisions of Section 34-97 (c)(5)c.
e.
Pressure-regulating valves. The function of the pressure-regulating valve is to reduce an upstream high pressure
to a pre-adjusted lower downstream pressure to vary the rates of flow without causing
shock or water hammer on the system. Pressure-regulating valves shall comply with
all provisions of Section 34-97 (c)(5)d.
f.
Operators. All buried valves shall have a standard AWWA two-inch square operating nut. Buried
valves shall have a position indicator in the valve box that is calibrated to the
valve size and number of turns to open/close. Valves located in vaults or meter pits
shall have a hand-wheel operator. All valve operators shall open the valves by means
of clockwise rotation (OPEN RIGHT) of the nut or hand-wheel. Blowoff assemblies shall
have a two-inch brass nut attached with a brass cotter pin.
g.
Zone valves and other critical valves. Zone valves shall be provided in transition locations between filling zones, pressure
zones or as dictated by DWSD. Zone valves shall have actuators located within a manhole
as shown on Standard Detail WM-21 in Section 34-211 .
(8)
Fire hydrants.
a.
The Fire Marshal shall approve the number, location and spacing of fire hydrants.
The Fire Marshal will determine the required fire flows and locate the appropriate
number of fire hydrants on the water main construction plans. The Fire Marshal shall
have a signature block on the cover of the Approved Documents to confirm that they
have been reviewed and approved.
b.
Fire hydrants shall be located on the same side of the street as the water main. At
intersections, fire hydrants will be located on the northeast corner. If hydrants
are to be installed at locations other than street intersections, they shall be located
along the projection of a property line.
c.
The actual number and spacing of hydrants will depend on access road/parking lot configurations
and the degree of hazard which the new development presents (i.e., sprinkled buildings

Hydrants shall be no more than 500 feet apart in single-family residential areas,
400 feet apart in multifamily developments, and 300 feet apart in commercial or industrial
areas.
d.
Fire hydrants shall be at least five feet from the edge of any driveway. In the event
that fire hydrants are located within parking lots or alleys without curbs, vertical
steel bollard (minimum four-inch diameter) barriers shall be placed around the fire
hydrants. Fire hydrants located behind curbs and sidewalks shall be placed 36 inches
behind the back of curb or sidewalk to the center of the hydrant. The maximum allowable
distance between tracer wire test boxes shall not exceed 500 feet.
e.
Fire hydrant branch lines shall be set at right angles to street mains. The branch
line from the main to the fire hydrant may not exceed 50 feet unless otherwise approved
by the District Engineer. Lines that exceed 50 feet in length may need to be upsized
to the next normal pipe size and reduced adjacent to the isolation valve of the fire
hydrant assembly. The hydrant shall be set at the end of the branch line and shall
face the branch line. No horizontal or vertical bends shall be used in installing
fire hydrant branch lines without approval from the District Engineer. Under no circumstances
shall any size or manner of tap be made on a fire hydrant branch line.
f.
Each hydrant shall be connected to the main with a minimum of a six-inch branch of
ductile iron pipe controlled by an independent gate valve and restrained to the tee
on the main. Tapping saddles will not be permitted. The branch line and hydrant shoe
shall be rodded to the main line tee and fire hydrant shall be thrust blocked. The
entire hydrant shall be wrapped in plastic, including any extension installed on the
hydrant to raise it to final grade.
g.
Any fire hydrant within the District's service area shall be owned and maintained
by the District, whether in a public right-of-way or on private property, except where
master meters are installed for any one or a group of fire hydrants. All hydrants
connected to the mains of the District are provided for the primary purpose of furnishing
water for fire suppression and shall be opened and used only by persons authorized
to do so by the District.
h.
Any other use of fire hydrants shall be allowed by permit issued by the District and
shall require the use of a hydrant meter and regulating valve for the monitoring of
water use. Authorized personnel shall make the connection and disconnection only.

Rates to be charged for water extracted from each hydrant shall be in accordance with
the current fee schedule.
i.
Use of hydrant water shall cease for the duration of any fire within the District,
or for any other reason upon notice by the District. The Customer is responsible to
pay for any damage to the hydrant, hydrant meter, or other District property.
(9)
Fire sprinkler lines.
a.
Fire sprinkler lines shall be installed using ductile iron pipe at right angles to
distribution mains and shall run in as straight a line as possible from the main to
the property line and from the property line to the proposed structure. Horizontal
and vertical bends must be approved by the District and shall only be permitted where
interference prohibits a straight-line installation.
b.
All fire sprinkler lines shall be 100 percent restrained from the main to the proposed
structure by means of restrained joint pipe, restraining rods, or other devices approved
by the District. No taps are permitted on fire sprinkler lines.
c.
Post indicator valves are permissible; however, the District does not require them.
A post indicator valve may be installed on the fire sprinkler line provided it is
designed to operate in an open right position (clockwise) only.
(10)
Pressure-regulating stations. Pressure-regulating valve (PRV) stations are used to control pressures between distribution
zones. When main extension plans are submitted for review, the need for a pressure-regulating
valve station shall be determined based on existing pressure zones and the impact
on the proposed development. Pressure-reducing and -regulating valves shall be of
a type capable of maintaining pre-adjusted downstream pressures with varying rates
of flow and upstream pressure without causing water hammer. Pressure reducing and
regulating valves shall be installed in concrete vaults in accordance with Standard
Details WM-14 & WM-15 in Section 34-211 .
(11)
Air and vacuum valves. Combination air and vacuum release valves shall be installed at each high point on
all water mains 16 inches in diameter and larger. Combination air and vacuum release
valves shall be installed at each high point on all water mains 12 inches and smaller
if there is not a fire hydrant at the high point or if there are no service lines
along the main. Air and vacuum release valves shall be installed in precast concrete
manholes or vaults fitted with air vents in accordance with Standard Details WM-12
& WM-13 in Section 34-211 .
(12)
Blowoff assemblies.
a.
All water mains, which are not looped, shall have a blowoff assembly installed at

lines shall have a two-inch assembly installed on the end plug in accordance with

until future looping shall have a two-inch assembly installed on the main or on the

b.
In instances where the water mains are stubbed out for future phasing, the in-line
valve shall be restrained from the tee to the valve, and pipe placed past the in-line
valve to prevent the valve from blowing off when the main is extended in the future.
Length of pipe required past the valve shall be based on the restrained length required

(13)
Rods, clamps and restraining devices. All bends, tees, plugs, reducers, valves, fire hydrants, and fire suppression systems
shall be fully restrained in accordance with the Standard Detail WM-16 in Section 34-211 . All pipe joints on each side of a bend, tee, plug, or valve shall also be restrained
within the lengths shown in the Standard Details. Rods and clamps shall be used on
ductile iron and PVC pipe systems. Where mechanical joint pipe is used, rods may be
bolted through the joint bolt holes in accordance with the Standard Details. All clamps
shall be covered with an epoxy coating as specified. In all cases where reducers with
a reduction ratio equal to or greater than 2:1 are used, special rodding and clamping
procedures shall be required.
(14)
Thrust blocks. Concrete thrust blocks shall be installed at all bends, tees, plugs, fire hydrants,
and fire suppression systems in accordance with the Standard Detail WM-3 in Section 34-211 . Pipe and fittings shall be separated from concrete by eight mil polyethylene bond
breaker. Size of thrust block, type of concrete, and dimensions shall be in accordance
with the Standard Details.
(15)
Wet taps.
a.
When a connection is required on an existing distribution or transmission main, the
District may require a wet tap. This determination is based on the effect any connection
may have on the interruption of service to customers, the effect on the transmission
system, or the time restrictions involved with working in an existing street.
b.
The minimum size wet tap is four inches in diameter and, generally, the maximum size
wet tap is 12 inches in diameter. The maximum size of the wet tap shall be limited
to 75 percent of the nominal diameter of the distribution or transmission main (i.e.,

(16)
Corrosion protection.
a.
1.
Cathodic protection shall be designed for all sections of DIP in accordance with NACE
International SP0169 and AWWA M41. Drawings shall indicate the location of each anode,
underground reference electrode, buried insulated flange, and field test station complete
with a description of piping connected. Drawings shall be provided with sufficient
information so that each underground galvanic anode and underground reference electrode
can be exactly excavated or replaced.
2.
If borings and geotechnical results indicate non-corrosive soils, a request for omission
of the cathodic protection system may be submitted to DWSD for approval.
3.
Operations and maintenance manual for the cathodic protection system shall be provided.
b.
Wax tape shall be provided in accordance with AWWA C217 for all buried metallic hardware
on pipe fittings, valves and restraints.
c.
Polyethylene encasement shall be provided for all DIP, valves, and fittings in accordance
with AWWA C105.
(17)
Limits of accuracy (allowable error). A limit of accuracy refers to the horizontal and vertical deviation permissible during
the laying of water mains. The allowable error shall be a maximum of plus or minus
0.3 feet in a vertical direction, but no deviation will be allowed which results in
less than five feet of cover. The allowable horizontal error shall be a maximum of
plus or minus 0.3 feet. Any line that does not meet the criteria shall be removed
and re-installed.
(Rules of 7-17-2019(7), § 4.01)

(a)
Furnishing and installation of construction materials. All pipe materials used in the construction of the water system shall conform to
the requirements specified herein. Any material proposed as an equal must be approved
by the District in writing prior to construction. All materials furnished shall be
new and undamaged. All installations shall be constructed in accordance with the specifications
in this chapter. All necessary pipes, joints and appurtenances shall be furnished
and installed whether shown on approved construction drawings or not. All installations
shall be completed as fully operable.
(b)
Applicability to Standards; final interpretation. When materials reference Denver Water Complete Engineering Standards, the requirements
listed in the most recent version of those Standards shall apply. In the event of
a conflict between the Denver Water Standards and the Standards in this chapter, the
District Engineer shall make the final interpretation.
(c)
Materials.
(1)
Ductile iron pipe.
a.
Manufacture. Ductile iron pipe shall be manufactured in strict accordance with AWWA Standard Specification
C151.
b.
Size of pipe. This specification shall cover all sizes of ductile iron pipe 24 inches in diameter
and smaller.
c.
Joint type. All ductile iron pipe joints shall be push-on joint single gasket or mechanical joint
single gasket. The rubber gasket shall conform to the requirements of AWWA C-111.
d.
Pressure class. Pipe furnished shall be Pressure Class 250 for all sizes four inches in diameter
and larger. Where pipe will be direct tapped without the use of tapping saddles, pipe
shall be Special Thickness Class 52 minimum. The preceding classes are minimums and
higher classes may be required. In cases of smaller pipe with larger taps, all pipe
thickness shall be verified with Table AWWA C151 A.1 and shall have at least three
thread engagement for specific pipe thickness classifications.
e.
Laying length. Pipe furnished shall have a normal laying length of 18 feet or 20 feet. Random lengths
are not acceptable.
f.
Cement mortar lining. All pipe furnished shall have standard thickness cement mortar lining with seal coat
in accordance with AWWA C-104.
g.
Exterior coating. All pipe furnished shall have an exterior asphaltic coating in accordance with Manufacturer's
standards.
(2)
Polyvinyl chloride (PVC) pipe.
a.
Manufacture. All polyvinyl chloride (PVC) pipes shall be manufactured in strict accordance with
AWWA Standard C900 or C 905.
b.
Size of pipe. This specification shall cover all sizes of PVC pipe 14 inches and smaller. All pipe

Thickness class. Pipe furnished under this specification shall be Pressure Class 150 or greater.

Laying lengths. Pipe shall have a normal laying length of 13, 18 or 20 feet. Random lengths are not

(4)
Water main fittings.
a.
1.
Mechanical joint restraints shall be in accordance with Denver Water's Complete Engineering

be ductile iron mechanical joint, Class 350 minimum for pipe diameters 24 inches and

2.
Alternative protective coating systems for buried pipe fittings may be considered

b.
All bends shall be restrained in accordance with Denver Water's Complete Engineering

Solid sleeve fittings shall be restrained in accordance with Denver Water's Complete

(5)
Valves.
a.
Resilient wedge gate valves.
1.
All gate valves shall be resilient seated, epoxy coated, cast iron body, with a non-rising
stem. Resilient seated gate valves shall conform to Denver Water's Complete Engineering
Standards with the following additional requirements or exceptions: Valve stems shall
be sealed with two "O" rings, each of which shall be designed as to allow replacement
under full line pressure when the valve is in the full open position.
2.
Gate valves may have flanged or mechanical joint ends. Flanges shall be sized and
drilled in accordance with ANSIB16.1 Class 125 or mechanical joint ends rated for
250 psi, minimum, in conformance with AWWA-C111. Flanges shall be machined to a flat
face with a finish of 250 microinches, AARH maximum or machined to a flat surface
with a serrated finish in accordance with AWWA C-207. Mechanical joints ends shall
be compliant with AWWA C-111. Tee head bolts and hexagon nuts shall be fabricated
from high-strength low-alloy steel.
3.
All gate valves shall have the year of manufacture cast as part of the valve body.
4.
Any valve that is more than two calendar years old shall not be installed unless approved
in writing by the District.
5.
Ferrous surfaces, except machined or bearing surfaces or flange faces, shall be prepared
for coating in accordance with SSPC SP10. These surfaces shall then be coated with
a two-part thermosetting polyamide epoxy in two or more uniform coats or with fusion-bonded
epoxy to a minimum DFT of ten mils. Epoxy coating shall be in accordance with AWWA
C550.
b.
Tapping valves. Tapping valves shall be resilient wedge gate valves with centering ring on flanged
face of valve, for proper alignment. Tapping valves shall conform to this subsection
(c)(5).
c.
Butterfly valves.
1.

All butterfly valves shall conform to Denver Water's Complete Engineering Standards
with the following additional requirements or exceptions: All butterfly valves shall
have a working pressure equal to or greater than the pipe classification where it
is located. In no case shall the valve be rated for less than 150 psi working pressure.
2.
The actuator shall be capable of withstanding an overload input torque of 300 foot-pounds
at full open or closed position without damage to the valve or valve actuator. Torque
limiting devices shall be provided with all butterfly valve actuators. All gearing
shall be totally enclosed and sealed from groundwater. Geared actuators shall be provided
on all valves larger than eight inches, the actuator shall be designed to resist submergence
in water to 25 feet head pressure. The maximum input torque required to fully open
or close the valve for Class 150B conditions shall not exceed 150 foot-pounds when
applied to the operating nut.
3.
All buried butterfly valves shall have mechanical joint ends in conformance with AWWA
C-111. Tee-head bolts and hexagon nuts shall be fabricated from high-strength low-alloy
steel in accordance with Denver Water's Complete Engineering Standards. Flanged ends
may be approved by the District if necessary. When specified, butterfly valves shall
have flanged ends sized and drilled in accordance with ANSI-B16.1 Class 125. Flanges
shall be machined to a flat face with a finish of 250 microinches, AARH maximum or
machined to a flat surface with a serrated finish in accordance with AWWA-C-207.
d.
Pressure-reducing and -regulating valve.
1.
Pressure-regulating valves shall conform to Denver Water's Complete Engineering Standards
with the following additional requirements or exceptions: Components shall be suitable
for exposure to chlorinated water.
2.
Material for valve body shall be cast iron. Flanges and covers shall conform to ASTM
Standard Designation A48 Class 35. Bronze castings or parts for internal trim shall
conform to ASTM Standard B61 and B62. The valve shall be fully bronze mounted and
all packing shall have rubber seals to provide tight closure and prevent metal to
metal friction.
3.
The pressure-reducing valve shall be hydraulically operated with a free-floating guided
piston having a seat diameter equal to the size of the valve. An indicator rod shall
be furnished as an integral part of the valve to show the position of the piston within
the valve body. The valve shall be provided with a check feature to prevent backflow.
4.

documents.text:
All pressure-reducing and -regulating valves shall be installed in concrete vaults,
as per Subsection (c)(14) of this section, and as shown in Standard Details WM-14
and WM-15 in Section 34-211 .
5.
All pressure-reducing and -regulating valves shall be certified by the manufacturer
that the assembly has been inspected and all of the specified tests have been performed.
A copy of the certification shall be sent to the District upon request.
e.
Swing check valves. Swing check valves shall conform to Denver Water's Complete Engineering Standards
with the following additional requirements or exceptions:
1.
All check valves shall be installed in vaults in a horizontal position with exterior
lever and adjustable spring operation. See Subsection (c)(14) of this section.
2.
The operating pressure shall be 175 psi or equal to the operating pressure of the
pipe.
(6)
Fire hydrants. Fire hydrants shall conform to Denver Water's Complete Engineering Standards with
the following additional requirements or exceptions: Hydrants shall have an underground
six-inch connection, two 2½-inch hose connections and one 4½-inch pumper connection.
Threads on the pumper and hose connections shall conform to the requirements of the
"National Standard Screw Threads for Fire Hose Couplings and Fittings," published
by the Insurance Services Office. Fire hydrants shall be cast iron with bronze seat
mountings and shall have a traffic breakaway feature incorporated into the barrel
and operating shaft at the finished grade elevation. The operator nut shall be National
Standard pentagon shape and measure 1½ inches from point to opposite flat. The fire
hydrant assembly shall include the hydrant, an auxiliary six-inch gate valve and a
six-inch diameter lateral pipe.
(7)
Valve boxes.
a.
Valve boxes shall be the three-piece adjustable screw type six inches in diameter
and conform to Denver Water's Complete Engineering Standards with the following additional
requirements or exceptions: All extensions to a valve box shall be coal tar coated,
and wrapped in eight mil polyethylene plastic (see Subsection (c)(25) of this section).
b.
Valve box covers shall be marked with lettering that indicates the type of utility,
"WATER," "SEWER," and "NONPOTABLE WATER." All valve boxes shall have a lip or flange
extending into the valve box shaft. No slip-type boxes will be allowed. The valve
box shall be of a design which will not transmit shock or stress to the valve and
shall be centered and plumb over the operating nut of the valve with the box cover
one-quarter inch below the surface of the pavement.
c.

d.
Valve boxes shall be provided as described herein and Section 34-98 (f) and as shown in Standard Detail WM-2 in Section 34-211 .
(8)
Combination air relief-vacuum breaker assemblies.
a.
Air release valves.
1.
Air and vacuum release valves shall have cast iron bodies, stainless-steel float and
working parts and shall conform to Denver Water's Complete Engineering Standards with
the following additional requirements or exceptions: Except as modified or supplemented
herein, all valves furnished under this section shall conform to the applicable performance
requirements of AWWA C512 and NSF 61. All pipe and fittings used in the relief valve
system shall be copper and/or brass and connections shall be threaded. See Standard
Detail WM-12 in Section 34-211 . Components shall be suitable for exposure to chlorinated water.
2.
The manufacturer shall furnish a sworn statement that the inspection and all specified
tests have been completed and that results comply with the requirements of the Standards
in this chapter. A copy of the Certification, including compliance with NSF/ANSI 61,
shall be provided to Dominion Water and Sanitation.
b.
Vault. The vault shall be a 60-inch diameter precast concrete manhole with 24-inch manhole
grade rings, frame and cover. Grade beams shall be precast concrete with dimensions
of 12 inches by six inches by eight feet long. See Detail WM-12 in Section 34-211 .
c.
Vent piping. Vent piping below ground shall be six-inch nominal diameter, PVC pipe, Schedule 40.
Above-ground piping shall have an exterior with a black anodized finish, and be sized
per Standard Detail WM-13 in Section 34-211 .
(9)
Tapping sleeves and saddles. Requirements for fabricated carbon steel and stainless steel tapping sleeves and
saddles are as follows:
a.
Tapping sleeves and saddles shall conform to Denver Water's Complete Engineering Standards
with the following additional requirements or exceptions: Components shall be suitable
for exposure to chlorinated water.
b.
The manufacturer shall furnish a sworn statement that the inspection and all specified
tests have been completed and that results comply with the requirements of the Standards
in this chapter. A copy of the Certification, including compliance with NSF/ANSI 61,
shall be provided to Dominion Water and Sanitation.

Rods and clamps. Harness rods shall be mild steel conforming to ASTM A-36 with hex nuts conforming
to ASTM A-307, Grade A or B, Hexagon heavy series. The number and size of rods shall
be as indicated in the Standard Details. All rods and clamps shall be covered with
wax tape.
(11)
Pipe restraint.
a.
Joint restraint devices. Joint restraint devices shall be used at bends and fittings where joint restraint
devices are specifically required. Joint restraint devices shall be required for the
following installations:
1.
Fire hydrants.
2.
Fireline connections.
3.
Domestic line connections three inches and larger.
4.
Vertical bends.
5.
Reducers.
6.
Vertical and horizontal offsets.
7.
Horizontal bends, line valves, plugs, and fittings.
8.
Bulkheads and plugs.
9.
Bored casings.
10.
When the bearing capacity of the soil is not sufficient to provide adequate restraint
in the opinion of the District.
11.
When the District identifies potential future development that may utilize or connect
to the water main to be installed.
b.
Horizonal and vertical offsets and reducers. Horizontal and vertical offsets and reducers shall be restrained on each side of
the fitting. For other fittings, the length of tied pipe shall be in accordance with
Standard Detail WM-16 in Section 34-211 .
c.
Bends, fittings, thrust blocks. Bends, fittings, tees, fire hydrant tees, and service taps three inches and larger
shall be restrained by using mechanically tied joints and thrust blocks. Thrust blocks
shall be placed against undisturbed soil, have sufficient clearance from adjacent
interference, and meet all other requirements as described in subsection (12) of this
section. Vertical bends on pipe sizes 12 inches and smaller are not required to have
thrust blocks.
1.
Ductile iron pipe. Mechanical joint restraint for ductile iron pipe shall conform to Denver Water's
Complete Engineering Standards.
2.
PVC pipe. Mechanical joint restraint for PVC pipe shall conform to Denver Water's Complete
Engineering Standards with the following additional requirements or exceptions.
3.
Bolt through restraint. Bolt through MJ restraints may be used in the jointing of two MJ fittings when a
combination of two fittings is required and shall conform to Denver Water's Complete
Engineering Standards with the following additional requirements or exceptions. Adaptors
shall be manufactured of Ductile-iron conforming to ASTM A536-80.
4.
Solid sleeves. Two solid sleeves shall be used when making a connection to an existing water main
to install a branch line either the same size or smaller.
(12)

documents.text:
Thrust blocks. Concrete thrust blocks shall be installed at all tees, plugs, bends greater than
five degrees, fire hydrants or where designated on the plans in accordance with the
Standard Detail WM-3 in Section 34-211 . Thrust blocks are not required for vertical bends of less than 45 degrees. Size
of thrust block and dimensions shall be in accordance with Standard Details (usually
twice the diameter of the pipe used). Thrust blocks shall be constructed of "Class
B" concrete as defined in the specifications in this chapter.
(13)
Bedding material.
a.
Definition. Pipe bedding shall be defined as that portion of the pipe zone which extends from
six inches below the bottom of the pipe to six inches above the top and along the
sides of the pipe.
b.
Certifying test results. The Customer shall provide, upon request, certified test results of the bedding material
confirming compliance with the following standards and a sample of the bedding material:
1.
Pipe bedding. Bedding for water, sewer and nonpotable water mains constructed of PVC and DIP shall
be in accordance with Denver Water Engineering Standards for Squeegee Sand. Bedding
shall be placed in layers not more than six inches deep and shall be compacted around
the pipe as specified.
2.
Flowable fill.
(i)
Flowable Fill shall conform to the following mix proportions per cubic yard:

(ii)
The type of cement used shall be ASTM Type II, the class of fly ash in CLSM shall
be Air entraining agent can be used to increase flowability. Flowable fill shall have

3.
Granular fill. Granular fill material for use as base for structures or stabilization of trench
bottoms shall be crushed rock or pea gravel coarse aggregate in accordance with CDOT
gradation No. 67 and per ASTM C33. Material shall be placed in layers not more than
six inches deep and compacted as specified.
4.
Job-excavated materials. Job-excavated material shall be free from debris, organic matter, and stones, placed
in uniform layers not more than eight inches thick, and compacted to 95 percent maximum
density as determined by ASTM D698.
5.
Graded backfill. Graded Backfill shall replace job excavated material where the job-excavated material
is deemed unsuitable. Graded backfill shall be a gravel mixture with no clay lumps
or organic material. It shall be uniformly graded from in size from three-quarter-inch

size to No. 200 sieve. The fraction passing the No. 4 sieve shall have a liquid limit
not greater than 25 and a plasticity index not greater than five. Materials shall
be compacted as outlined in the trench backfill section and shall be covered with
six inches of topsoil where outside of roadways.
(14)
Precast concrete vaults and manholes. Precast vaults and manholes shall conform to the size, shape, form, and details shown
on the plans and shall conform to Denver Water's Complete Engineering Standards.
(15)
Concrete.
a.
Class A concrete shall be used for all cast-in-place and precast concrete structures.
The concrete shall have a maximum allowable water/cement (w/c) ratio of 0.50 by weight.
The w/c ratio may be increased to 0.56 by weight by the addition of an approved water-reducing
agent (WRA) conforming to ASTM Designation C-494—Type A. The WRA, in suitably diluted
form, may be added to water containing an air-entraining agent for the batch providing
the materials are compatible with each other. If the two are incompatible, they shall
be introduced separately.
1.
The concrete shall have a minimum 28-day compressive strength of 3,000 psi for cast-in-place
structures and a minimum 28-day compressive strength of 4,000 psi for precast structures.
2.
Fine aggregates shall be between 34 percent and 38 percent by volume of the total
aggregates.
b.
Class B concrete shall be used for all thrust blocks, protective pads, and encasements.
The Class B concrete shall have a maximum w/c ratio of 0.63 by weight. The w/c ratio
may be increased to 0.70 by the addition of a WRA as specified above. Class B concrete
shall have a minimum 28-day compressive strength of 2,000 psi.
c.
A minimum of ten days prior to starting concrete work, the Customer shall submit to
the District Engineer for approval samples of the various aggregates to be used in
the final mix and the concrete mix proposed to be used. The source of each sample
of aggregate shall be stated. After approval of the aggregates and concrete mix, neither
the source of aggregate nor the mix of the concrete shall be changed without written
approval of the District Engineer.
(16)
Concrete reinforcement. All deformed reinforcing bars shall conform to ASTM Standard A-615, Grade 40 or 50,
or ASTM Standard A-617, Grade 40 or 60. All welded steel wire fabric shall conform
to ASTM Standard A-185 except that the weld shear strength requirement shall be extended
to include a wire size differential up to and including six gauges.
(17)
Manhole rings and covers.
a.

documents.text:
Manhole rings and covers shall be cast iron in accordance with ASTM A-48, Class 35
B. Twenty-four-inch diameter assemblies shall be the Denver Heavy style with a combined
weight of not less than 400 pounds, or as approved by DWSD (approximate distribution:
Frame—235 lbs., Lid 165 lbs.). All bearing surfaces shall be machined to the tolerances
shown on the construction drawings. Manhole lifting holes shall be manufactured with
an elongated oval hole per Standard Details SM-3, SM-4 & SM-5 in Section 34-211 . Manhole lids with more than one lifting hole shall not be accepted. Rim elevation
shall be four inches to eight inches above grade in open space and shall be flush
to one-quarter inch below grade of any finished surface.
b.
Manhole rings, covers, and risers shall be heavy duty and designed, manufactured,
and tested in accordance with AASHTO M306. HS-20 rated manhole rings and covers shall
be provided.
c.
The manufacturer shall furnish a sworn statement that the inspection and all specified
tests have been completed and that results comply with the requirements of the Standards
in this chapter. A copy of the Certification shall be provided to Dominion Water and
Sanitation. The report shall include material data that is traceable to the originating
foundry, traceable test bars that match, the name of the manufacturer, and the date
of the pour.
d.
The horizontal seating and vertical facing surfaces common to the ring and cover shall
be machine finished to ensure non-rocking and full bearing for the entire width and
circumference of the bearing surface to permit interchangeability with castings of
the same design. The vertical face common to the ring and cover shall be beveled.
e.
Covers shall be labeled with the name or symbol of the manufacturer, country of origin,
and date of manufacture to be located at the manufacturer's option. In addition, the
cover shall contain the owner's name, "DWSD," and the respective utility contained
in the manhole "WATER," SEWER," "UNDERDRAIN," "NONPOTABLE WATER," all in three-inch-high
lettering that is centered and recessed on the exposed face.
(18)
Flexible plastic joint sealing compound. Preforming flexible plastic joint sealing compound shall meet Federal Specification
SS-S00210 and AASHTO M198 75 1, Type B. The sealing compound shall show no visible
deterioration when immersed separately in a solution of acid, alkalize and saturated
hydrogen sulfide for a period of 30 days. The plastic gasket shall be "Ram-Nek" as
manufactured by K.T. Snyder Company or an approved equal.
(19)
