documents.text:
Service connections to manholes. Residential sewer service lines shall not be connected directly to a manhole. The
end of a sewer main shall always be a cleanout manhole. All services shall be connected
downstream from that.
(8)
Grade adjustments. Manholes shall be constructed to permit grade adjustments by use of precast concrete
adjusting rings not to exceed a total height of eight inches. In dedicated open space
or landscape areas, manhole rims shall be set four inches above grade to prevent infiltration
from surface runoff. A concrete collar shall be placed around the ring and cover in
all landscaped tracts and dedicated open space areas as shown in the Standard Detail
SM-3, SM-4, SM-5 and SM-6 in Section 34-211 .
(f)
Underdrain systems.
(1)
Underdrains, roof drains and other surface water collection systems shall not discharge
into the sanitary sewer system.
(2)
Underdrains shall not be considered part of the sanitary sewer system and are not
required by, nor are they the responsibility of, the District.
(3)
If an underdrain is designed as part of the Customer's requirements and is located
in the same trench as the sanitary sewer, the type, capacity, and sizing shall be
submitted to the District for approval. Additionally, a detailed drawing of any underdrain
cross-section shall be included on the sanitary sewer plans.
(4)
An underdrain system shall be designed and constructed as a groundwater conveying
system independent of the sanitary sewer line foundation and bedding material. No
allowance shall be taken for the porosity of the sewer main bedding material in calculating
the underdrain capacity. Along the trench where the underdrain system and the sewer
foundation bedding meet, filter fabric shall be installed around all sides of the
underdrain bedding in order to prevent the migration of the foundation material into
the underdrain trench. Underdrains shall be bedding with Graded Gravel Fill material
as specified in article IV of this chapter.
(5)
Underdrain systems shall have adequate daylight points to permit the groundwater to
drain freely from the system. When a daylight line leaves the underdrain trench a
groundwater barrier shall be constructed immediately downstream, in the underdrain
trench. A groundwater barrier shall follow the requirements of Section 34-136 (15).
(6)
When passing around or below manholes, underdrain systems shall be constructed of
a solid wall pipe to prevent water from accumulating around the manhole. Under no
circumstances shall a sump condition exist below the manhole base. Groundwater barriers

(7)
Cleanouts shall in no case be installed inside of a sanitary sewer manhole, but are
allowed to be installed on the outside of a manhole. Unless agreed by the District,
cleanouts shall not be the responsibility of the District to maintain and shall be
constructed in accordance with Standard Detail UD-1, UD-2, UD-3 and UD-4 in Section 34-211 .
(g)
Sewer main cleanouts. The use of sewer main cleanouts shall not be permitted. The manhole of a dead-end
sewer shall be a cleanout manhole as shown in Standard Detail SM-12 in Section 34-211 .
(h)
Special applications. Special applications or designs of sanitary sewer systems, such as lift stations,
siphons, elevated pipelines, etc., are generally not permitted. Any situations which
dictate the need for such an application shall be presented as a variance prior to
design and permitting.
(i)
Limits of accuracy (allowable error). Limits of accuracy shall refer to the horizontal and vertical deviation from the
approved construction plans permissible during the laying of sewer mains. The allowable
error shall be a maximum of plus or minus 0.02 feet for lines designed at one percent
or less in a vertical direction. Lines designed at greater than one percent shall
be a maximum of plus or minus 0.1 feet in a vertical direction. Vertical deviation
limits shall apply to the entire Project, not each reach. No bellies or low points
in the sewer will be allowed as a way to adjust slope to get within allowable deviation
limits. In a horizontal direction the allowable error shall be a maximum of 0.3 feet.
Any line that does not meet the criteria shall be removed and reinstalled. On curvilinear
mains, the maximum horizontal deviation shall not exceed plus or minus 0.3 feet.
(Rules of 7-17-2019(7), § 5.01)

documents.text:
All pipe materials used in the construction of the sanitary sewer system shall conform
to the requirements specified herein. Any other material proposed as an equal must
be approved by the District in writing prior to construction. All materials furnished
shall be new and undamaged. Everything necessary to complete all installations in
accordance with the specifications in this chapter shall be furnished and installed
whether shown on approved drawings or not. All installations shall be completed as
fully operable.
(1)
Polyvinyl chloride pipe—SDR 35 and 26.
a.
All PVC pipe four inches to 24 inches in diameter furnished under this specification
shall be manufactured in strict accordance with ASTM Standard D 3034 and ASTM D 1784.
b.
All PVC plastic shall have a minimum cell classification of 12354 in accordance with
ASTM D 1784.
c.
Joints shall be made using a bell and spigot joint with integral bell push-on type
elastomeric gaskets in accordance with ASTM D3212.
d.
Pipe furnished under this specification shall have a DR ratio of 35 or 26. SDR 35
shall be used in applications with less than 20 feet of cover. For applications where
the pipeline is deeper than 20 feet, SDR 26 shall be used.
(2)
Polyvinyl chloride pipe—C900.
a.
All polyvinyl chloride pipe furnished under this specification shall be manufactured
in strict accordance with AWWA Standard C900.
b.
Joints shall use a standard elastomeric joint.
c.
Pipe furnished under this specification shall have a Pressure Class/Pressure-Rating
of 150 psi minimum.
d.
C900 PVC pipe shall be used where indicated for horizontal separation variances.
(3)
Polyvinyl chloride fittings. PVC fittings shall only be permitted for service connections such as tees and wyes.
PVC fittings shall be manufactured in strict accordance with ASTM D-1784, ASTM D-3034,
ASTM F-477 and ASTM F-679. Joint type shall be identical to that of the pipe. Solvent
weld fittings are allowed only for sand and grease interceptors.
(4)
Precast concrete vaults and manholes. See Section 34-97 (c)(14).
(5)
Pipe encasement. See Section 34-97 (c)(19).
(6)
Concrete. See Section 34-97 (c)(15).
(7)
Concrete reinforcement. See Section 34-97 (c)(16).
(8)
Manhole rings and covers. See Section 34-97 (c)(17).
(9)
Bedding material. Bedding for sewer mains constructed of PVC shall be CDOT Gradation No. 7, per ASTM
C33. Bedding shall be placed in layers not more than six inches deep and shall be
compacted around the pipe as specified.
(10)
Nonshrink grout. Grout shall be non-shrink consisting of Portland cement, sand and admixtures required

to meet the site conditions. Nonshrink grout shall be precision cementitious grout
with demonstrated non-shrinking properties; L&M "Crystex," BASF "Masterflow 713 Plus"
or "Masterflow 928," Sika "SikaGrout 328," Hilti "CB-G PG Precision Grout," or Five

(11)
Flexible plastic joint sealing compound. See Section 34-97 (c)(18).
(12)
Resilient manhole to pipe connectors. Pipe shall be connected to manholes with A-Lok Premium manhole pipe seal or equal.
Connector shall be cast into the manhole during fabrication. Straps shall be stainless
steel.
(13)
Coal tar epoxy dampproofing. See Section 34-97 (c)(21).
(14)
Corrosion-resistant epoxy lining.
a.
Corrosion-Resistant Epoxy shall be installed on the interior of each drop manhole,
cleanout manhole, waste metering manholes and all manholes within 1,000 feet of lift
stations or as shown on the approved construction plans. The coating may be applied
at the precast factory or in the field. If the product is installed at the factory,
a can of touch up material shall be supplied and the joints striped with two coats
of the material following installation of the manhole. Any visible pinholes or damage
shall be repaired. The manufacturer's installation specifications shall be followed.
b.
Product shall be a 100 percent solids epoxy, spray or trowel applied product with
documented chemical resistant to H2S and other common wastewater corrosive chemicals.
Product shall be Environmental Coatings "Sewer Shield," SpectraShield," "SpectraShield,"
Tnemec "Perma-Shield 436," Warren Environmental "S-301," or equal.
(15)
Groundwater barriers. See Section 34-97 (c)(20).
(16)
Tracer wire. See Section 34-97 (c)(23).
(17)
Marking tape. See Section 34-97 (c)(24).
(18)
Open channel flow meters. Ultrasonic open channel flow meters shall be a microprocessor-based electronic unit
consisting of a sensor assembly, a signal converter/transmitter, and an interconnecting
cable. The transmitter output shall be an isolated 4-20mA dc signal linearly proportional
to flow. The transmitter shall be mounted and provided per Standard Detail SS-7 in Section 34-211 . The manufacturer shall be Flo-Dar/Flo Station by Marsh-McBirney or approved equal.
(Rules of 7-17-2019(7), § 5.02)

Excavation.
(1)
Limit of excavation. See Section 34-98 (a)(1).

Trench width. See Section 34-98 (a)(2).

Pipe foundations and bedding.
(1)
Pipe foundation. See Section 34-98 (b)(1).
(2)

(c)
Trench backfilling and compaction. See Section 34-98 (c).
(1)
Procedure within the pipe zone. See Section 34-98 (c)(1).
(2)
Compaction above the pipe zone. See Section 34-98 (c)(2).
(3)
Compaction tests. See Section 34-98 (c)(3).
(4)

(d)
Installation of sanitary sewer main.
(1)
Pipe shall be laid without break and upgrade from structure to structure, with the
bell ends of pipe upgrade. Pipe shall be laid to the line and grade given so as to
form a close concentric joint with the adjoining pipe and prevent sudden offsets of
the flowline. Deflections of pipe joints shall be within no more than 80 percent of
the pipe manufacturer's deflection tolerances for curvilinear sewers. The pipe and
appurtenances shall be survey staked as required by the District and the interior
of the sewer pipe shall be cleaned of all dirt and superfluous materials as the work
progresses.
(2)
At all times when pipe laying is not in progress, the open end of the pipe shall be
closed with a tight-fitting cap or plug to prevent the entrance of foreign matter
into the pipe. This provision shall apply during all work breaks, including the noon
hour, as well as overnight. Under no circumstances shall sewers be used as drains
for removing water which has accumulated into the construction trenches. At the beginning
of a construction project, a watertight plug shall be installed in the connection
manhole, or first manhole upstream, in order to prevent any inflow into the existing
sewer system. This plug shall be removed by the Customer only in the presence of the
District. All related costs shall be borne by the Customer.
(3)
All sewer lines shall have a minimum of five feet of cover from the finished grade.
All pipes and fittings shall be carefully examined for cracks and other defects before
installation. All lumps, blisters and excessive coating shall be removed from the
bell or coupling and spigot ends of each pipe. Defective pipes or fittings shall be
set aside for inspection by the District who may require repairs or reject the pipe.

documents.text:
Polyvinyl chloride pipe shall be installed in accordance with ASTM D-2321, Uni-Bell
Standard UNI B-5, the manufacturer's recommendation and the specifications in this
chapter. All pipes and fittings shall be carefully lowered into the trench in such
a manner as to prevent damage to the materials. Under no circumstances shall sewer
main materials be dropped or dumped into the trench. PVC pipe stored outside and exposed
to sunlight for more than 30 days shall be covered with an opaque material. Clear
plastic sheets shall not be used to cover pipe. Both ends of the pipe shall be clear
to allow for air circulation under the covering.
(5)
Immediately before joining two lengths of sanitary sewer pipe, the inside of the bell
or coupling, the outside of the spigot and the gasket shall be thoroughly cleaned
to remove all foreign material. Lubrication of the joint and rubber gasket shall be
done in accordance with the pipe manufacturer's specifications.
(6)
Care shall be taken that only the correct gasket, compatible with the annular groove
of the bell, is used. Insertion of the gasket in the annular groove of the bell or
coupling must be in accordance with the manufacturer's recommendations. Pipe that
is not furnished with a depth mark shall be marked before assembly to assure that
the spigot end is inserted to the full depth of the joint. The spigot and bell or
coupling shall be aligned and pushed until the reference line on the spigot is flush
with the end of the bell or coupling. Pushing shall be done in a smooth, steady motion.
(e)
Installation of tracer wire. See Section 34-98 (e). The tracer wire shall be brought to grade at intervals not exceed 500 feet. Test
stations shall be located at the nearest manhole to the 500-foot interval, but shall
not exceed 500 feet.
(f)
Installation of marking tape. See Section 34-97 (c)(24).
(g)
Installation of manholes.
(1)
Excavation and backfill. See Sections 34-98 (a) and 34-97 (c)(13).
(2)
Manhole base.
a.
The manhole base shall be set over a six-inch base of (minimum) Granular Fill, as
specified in article IV of this chapter, and shall be either poured in place concrete
or an approved precast manhole base. The manhole stubs and sewer main shall be set
with water stop gasket before the concrete is placed and shall be rechecked for alignment
and grade before the concrete has set. The various sized inlets and outlets to the
manhole shall be located as shown in the Standard Details SM-7 and SM-8 in Section 34-211 . The base shall be extended eight inches below the bottom of the lowest pipe. Invert

of all pipes shall be the same as the crown elevation of the largest pipe.
b.
All transitions shall be smooth (free of edges and burs) and of the proper radius
to give an uninterrupted transition of flow. The concrete shall be Class "A" concrete
with three-quarter-inch maximum size aggregate and shall have a slump not greater
than two inches. The concrete base shall be shaped with a wood float and shall receive
a hard steel trowel finish before the concrete sets. In the event additional mortar
is required after initial set has taken place, the surface to receive the mortar shall
be primed with a concrete binding agent, in order to secure as chip-proof a result
as possible. No mortar lifts less than two inches in thickness shall be permitted.
The base shall set a minimum of 24 hours before the manhole construction is continued.
c.
The accumulation of water on the surface of the concrete due to water gain, segregation,
or other causes during placement and compacting shall be prevented as much as possible
by adjustments in the mixture. Provisions shall be made for the removal of such accumulated
water so that under no circumstances will new concrete be placed in such accumulations.
d.
When concrete is placed, the temperature of the concrete mix shall not be lower than
50 degrees Fahrenheit nor higher than 80 degrees Fahrenheit. Concrete shall not be
placed on a substrate which is frozen or has standing water. If freezing temperatures
are expected during the cure time, the concrete shall be kept at a temperature no
less than 50 degrees Fahrenheit for five days. Heaters and blankets may be necessary.
e.
When concrete is deposited against ground or aggregate, it shall be covered with eight
mil polyethylene sheeting to prevent the ground from drawing water from the concrete.
f.
The upstream side of each manhole shall have a groundwater barrier installed in order
to break continuity of the embedment material. Material shall meet ASTM 2487 soil
clarification GC, SC, CL, or ML-CL and shall be compacted to 95 percent of a low strength
concrete mix. The barrier shall be three feet wide and extend the entire width of
the trench and effectively break the bedding material.
(3)
Precast manhole sections. Each manhole section shall be placed in accordance with the manufacturer's recommendations
in a perfectly plumb position. Each joint between the manhole sections shall have
a layer of flexible plastic joint sealing compound on both the tongue and groove part

manhole centered over the pipe. Exterior dampproofing and interior corrosion-resistant
epoxy lining, as required herein, shall be placed in accordance with the specifications
in this chapter for all sanitary sewer manholes.
(4)
Manhole frames and covers. Manhole frames and covers shall be set to the proper elevations and shall match final
grades. Manhole frames shall be set one-quarter inch below to flush with the final
grade of the asphalt or concrete roadway and shall be securely attached to the manhole
shaft unit with a grout bed and fillet. After the frames are securely set, the frames
and covers shall be cleaned and scraped to ensure a satisfactory fit. In the event
the manholes are placed in open space areas, the ring and cover shall be placed a
minimum of four inches above final grade in an 18-inch wide collar of reinforced concrete
the depth of the ring and cover, or 12 inches minimum.
(5)
Watertightness of manholes. Manholes and appurtenances shall be watertight and free from infiltration. The District
Engineer shall determine the adequacy of manholes and appurtenances as to watertightness.
(6)
Connection to existing manholes. New connections to existing manholes wherein stubs have not been provided shall be
made by core drilling through the base or as approved by the District. Connection
shall be as shown on Standard Detail SM-9 in Section 34-211 .
(7)
Installation of grout. Grout shall be applied to all surfaces in accordance with the manufacturer's recommendations.
Grout shall have a troweled finish and shall be protected from a rapid loss of moisture
with a covering of wet rags or polyethylene sheets. The temperature of the grout and
the surfaces receiving the grout shall be maintained between 65 degrees Fahrenheit
and 85 degrees Fahrenheit until after setting.
(h)
Alignment and deflection testing.
(1)
General inspection. After the sewer main and all appurtenances have been installed and have passed the
compaction test, the line shall be inspected for alignment and deflection.
(2)
Debris and dirt removal; installation of plug. Prior to any testing of the sewer mains, the lines shall be thoroughly flushed and
balled to remove debris and dirt. The lowest manhole (or manholes) within the Project
shall be plugged with an approved watertight plug (Pollard or approved equal) on the
downstream outlet of the manhole and all water, silt and debris shall be pumped from
this manhole and disposed of properly. The plug shall be installed once the base for

documents.text:
the lowest manhole has been constructed and shall not be removed at any time without
the consent of the District.
(3)
Mandrel testing and T.V. inspection. All mains shall be mandrel tested and T.V. inspected 14 days after installation of
the reach has been completed.
a.
Mandrel testing. The Customer shall supply all necessary equipment and personnel to perform the testing.
Testing consists of pulling an approved calibrated mandrel equal to 95 percent of
the inside diameter, through the pipe from manhole to manhole. If excessive deflection
does not allow the mandrel to pass through the line, the defective section shall be
removed and replaced.
b.
T.V. inspection. The Customer shall provide the T.V. equipment and give 24 hours' notice prior to
such inspection. The District shall receive a copy of the video following completion
of the inspection. The Customer shall correct any defective portions. All costs for
the T.V. inspection and any repairs shall be borne by the Customer.
(i)
Leakage testing. Once the pipe has passed the alignment and deflection tests, the pipe shall be tested
for leakage and infiltration. All materials and associated costs for such tests shall
be at the Customer's expense.
(1)
Exfiltration test.
a.
The water exfiltration test may be conducted if groundwater was not encountered during
installation and the invert of the lower manhole is not greater than 25 feet below
the invert of the upper manhole. Such testing shall be conducted by plugging the inlet
of the lower manhole and the inlet of the upper manhole with an approved watertight
sewer plug. The segment shall then be filled with water to a point two feet above
the crown of the open sewer in the upper manhole. The segment shall remain filled
for at least two hours. The leakage shall not exceed 100 gallons per inch of nominal
diameter per mile.
b.
The length of service connection shall not be used in computing the length of the
sewer main being tested.
c.
If the leakage is greater than allowed, further inspection shall be conducted by a
T.V. inspection. The defective area shall be repaired, and the process shall be repeated
until the test section meets the allowable limits. All costs for the testing and repair
shall be borne by the Customer.
(2)
Low pressure air test.
a.
Low pressure air testing may be used in lieu of exfiltration testing for 24-inch diameter
and smaller pipe. Air testing shall not be used for manholes, or for pipe larger than
24 inches in diameter.
b.
Low pressure air testing shall comply with ASTM F1417 for PVC and composite pipe.

documents.text:
The schedule of testing shall be submitted to District prior to starting the tests.
c.
The time elapsed for a one psi drop in air pressure shall be not less than, nor shall
the air loss exceed, the limits set forth in the governing standard.
d.
If the length of sewer to be tested is fully or partially submerged in groundwater,
the test pressure shall be increased if necessary to overcome the actual static pressure
exerted by the groundwater. If a test pressure greater than eight psi results, air
testing shall not be used, and exfiltration testing will be required.
e.
Leaks shall be located by testing short sections of pipe. Leaks shall be repaired,
and the reach of sewer retested. If the leakage is greater than allowed, further inspection
shall be conducted by a T.V. inspection. The defective area shall be repaired, and
the process shall be repeated until the test section meets the allowable limits. All
costs for the testing and repair shall be borne by the Customer.
(3)
Infiltration and inflow test.
a.
If groundwater is present, the end of the sewer at the upper manhole shall be plugged
with an approved watertight plug and the section shall be tested for infiltration.
The infiltration shall not exceed 100 gallons per inch of nominal diameter per mile.
The length of house laterals entering that section are not to be used in computing
the length of the sewer main being tested.
b.
The amount of infiltration shall be measured through the use of a pipe weir, flume
or other approved apparatus in the presence of the District Engineer.
c.
If the leakage is greater than allowed, further inspection shall be conducted by a
T.V. inspection. The defective area shall be repaired, and the process shall be repeated
until the test section meets the allowable limits. All costs for the testing and repair
shall be borne by the Customer.
(4)
Vacuum test of manholes.
a.
Manholes shall be tested before the ring and cover and concrete adjustment collars
have been installed. All pipes entering the manhole shall be plugged and braced and
a vacuum of ten inches of mercury shall be drawn. The vacuum pump shall be turned
off and the time monitored as the vacuum drops one inch. The vacuum must not drop
more than one inch in 60 seconds for a four-foot diameter manhole, or one inch in
75 seconds for a five-foot diameter manhole.
b.
For manholes that fail the vacuum test, defects shall be repaired, and the tests repeated.
Repair and repeat testing shall be continued until the testing requirements have been
met.
(Rules of 7-17-2019(7), § 5.03)

Each single-family residential detached or attached dwelling unit shall have a separate

Service lines shall follow a straight horizontal alignment between the outlet of the

Materials. All materials for sanitary sewer service lines shall be in accordance with Sections 34-136 and 34-139 .
(g)
Underdrain systems. Underdrain systems that are installed in conjunction with sanitary sewer service
lines shall comply with all provisions of Section 34-135 (f). The only exception to the Standard Specifications of this chapter is that a barrier
material is not required between the sewer service line bedding and the underdrain
trench provided that both materials are of the same gradation.
(h)
Sewer service cleanouts. Cleanouts shall be installed on sewer service lines within three feet of the exit
point of the service line from the structure, every 100 feet thereafter, and at all
points of horizontal deflection. Cleanouts shall be spaced a maximum of 100 feet apart.
The cleanout diameter shall match the nominal diameter of the service line and shall
be constructed in accordance with the Standard Details in Article VII of this chapter.
Cleanouts shall be located so that surface water does not accumulate. When cleanouts
are located in existing or future landscape areas, the cleanout cover shall be four
inches to six inches above finished grade. See Section 34-135 (e)(8).
(i)
Sand/oil and grease interceptors.
(1)
All restaurants, cafeterias or other food preparation facilities shall have a grease
interceptor installed on the sewer service line. The sizing of the grease interceptor
shall be determined by the Customer's Professional Engineer and submitted to the District
Engineer for approval. The grease interceptor shall be owned and maintained by the
Customer. Bypasses around grease traps shall not be permitted.
(2)
Services which discharge any quantities of sand, oil or other inert debris into the
sanitary sewer system shall have a sand/oil interceptor installed. Examples of such
services include, but are not limited to, automobile service stations, mechanical
repair shops, car washes, garden nurseries, warehouses and garages with floor drains.
The sizing of the sand/oil interceptor shall be determined by the Customer's Professional
Engineer and submitted to the District Engineer for approval. The sand/oil interceptor
shall be owned and maintained by the Customer. Bypasses around sand/oil interceptors
shall not be permitted.
(3)
Although a facility may not have been originally constructed with a sand/oil or grease
interceptor, the District may require that one be installed in the event of a change
in the type of use of the facility. All costs shall be borne by the Customer.

Lift stations shall not be permitted to provide service to individual buildings. Lift
stations may be used to serve multiple buildings or a small service area in the event
that gravity service is not possible for that area, but should not be considered until
other options have been investigated. Lift stations shall not be used as an alternative
to extending a gravity service line, which may be longer or deeper than "normal."

Lift stations shall be designed by the Customer's Professional Engineer and shall

Polyvinyl chloride (PVC) pipe. Sanitary sewer service lines may be constructed of polyvinyl chloride pipe in compliance
with Section 34-136 (1), (2) and (3).
(b)
Bedding material. Pipe bedding for all types of sanitary sewer service lines shall comply with Section 34-136 (9).
(c)
Sanitary sewer service fittings. Pipe fittings for PVC service lines shall be PVC, bell and spigot joint in compliance
with Section 34-137 (d). No solvent weld fittings may be used except for sand and grease interceptors.
(d)
Tapping Saddles. Sanitary sewer service tapping saddles shall be constructed of PVC manufactured in
strict accordance with ASTM D-1784, ASTM D-3034, ASTM F-477 and ASTM F-679. Tapping
saddles shall consist of: a rubber gasket attached to the flange of the saddle which
will seal against the outside wall of the main, a bell and spigot gasket in the bell
of the service outlet and a minimum of two stainless steel straps which secure the
saddle to the main line. Solvent welded saddles shall not be used.
(e)
Precast concrete sand/oil and grease interceptors. Precast concrete sand/oil and grease interceptors shall be constructed in the same
manner as Precast Concrete Vaults; see Section 34-97 (c)(14) and the Standard Details in Article VII of this chapter. All piping within
these interceptors shall be solvent weld PVC. Interceptors installed in a parking
lot or a roadway shall be raised to grade by using precast concrete riser rings that
are a minimum of six inches wide (see Standard Details in Article VII of this chapter).
(f)
Manhole rings and covers. Manhole rings and covers for sand/oil and grease interceptors shall comply with Section 34-97 (c)(17).
(g)
Pipe adaptors/couplings.
(1)
Pipe adaptors, couplings or bushings shall be used to connect pipes of different materials
or dimensions. Adaptors, couplings and bushing shall provide a secure, leak-proof
joint that shall meet or exceed the leak testing requirements of the pipe.
(2)
Adaptors, couplings and bushings shall be secured to the pipe by means of a mechanical
connection such as stainless-steel clamps or a positive bell and spigot gasketed joint.
The nominal diameter of the adaptor, coupling, or bushing shall match the nominal
diameter of the pipes being connected. Field modifications of these items shall not
be permitted. Couplings shall be Fernco—Strong Back Couplings or an approved equal.
Concrete collars with diapers shall not be permitted.

documents.text:
(a)
Excavation.
(1)
Excavation for sanitary sewer service lines shall be in accordance with Section 34-98 (a).
(2)
In the event that a joint trench is specified for both a sewer and water service line,
the subgrade bench for the water service line shall have a minimum width of 12 inches.
This bench shall be excavated from undisturbed soil at an elevation no less than 18
inches above the top of the sanitary sewer service.
(b)
Pipe foundation and bedding. Pipe foundation and bedding for service lines shall be in accordance with Sections 34-98 (b) and 34-136 (9).
(c)
Trench backfilling and compaction. Trench backfilling and compaction of sewer service lines shall be in conformance
with Section 34-98 (c).
(d)
Installation of sanitary sewer service lines.
(1)
Installation of service lines shall be in accordance with Section 34-137 (d).
(2)
Sewer services shall be connected to the main by means of a wye fitting or tapping
saddle entering the main at an angle of 45 degrees vertically above the spring line
of the main. Service lines shall be extended from the main using a combination of
no more than three eighth bends (45 degrees) or sixteenth bends (22½ degrees). All
service lines shall be plugged at the end of the line with a watertight plug manufactured
for use with the service line material, and shall not exceed 15 feet in depth at the
plug.
(3)
End plugs must be able to withstand the internal pressure of leakage testing required
by the specifications in this chapter.
(e)
Installation of service line taps.

documents.text:
The purpose of this article in conjunction with Article IV of this chapter is to provide
guidelines for the planning, design, construction, and operation of the District's
Nonpotable Water System. These Standards apply to nonpotable water facilities under
the control of the District and its Customers.
(Rules of 7-17-2019(7), § 6.01)

ARTICLE VI. - NONPOTABLE WATER SYSTEM SPECIFICATIONS
documents.text:
Standards listed in Article IV of this chapter that apply to four- through 24-inch
potable water mains shall apply to nonpotable water systems along with the supplemental
requirements and exceptions stated in this article. This includes, but is not limited
to, pipe, meters, valves, service lines, backflow prevention, and easements. In the
event of a conflict with any other article of this chapter, this article shall govern
for nonpotable water.
(Rules of 7-17-2019(7), § 6.02)

documents.title: Sec. 34-166. - Water quality.

documents.article: ARTICLE VI. - NONPOTABLE WATER SYSTEM SPECIFICATIONS

documents.text:
(a)
Recycled water that is intended for irrigation use shall be in accordance with applicable
water quality regulations including those established by the CDPHE under Regulation
84. The District will maintain a system of records for water quality analyses performed
on recycled water that confirms compliance with water quality regulations.
(b)
Nonpotable water that is from a raw water supply such as a reservoir or river intake
shall not have the initial quality of the water degraded by the system. This water
shall not contaminate the nonpotable water for irrigation use and cause violation
of Regulation 84 requirements.
(c)
For the purpose of the specifications of this chapter, both shall be referred to unless
otherwise noted.
(Rules of 7-17-2019(7), § 6.03)

documents.text:
If nonpotable water is unavailable for irrigation, only the District may substitute
potable water as a backup. The potable water system shall be protected by an approved
backflow prevention device or air gap as described in Section 34-177 .
(Rules of 7-17-2019(7), § 6.04)

Sec. 34-168. - Conversion from a potable line to a nonpotable line.
documents.text:
Facilities converted from a potable water supply to a nonpotable water supply shall
be approved by the District prior to the design commencing. Once construction is complete,
only the District may make the switch over.
(Rules of 7-17-2019(7), § 6.05)

Sec. 34-169. - Protection of the potable water system.
documents.text:
(a)
Backflow prevention and cross-connection control. The potable water system shall be protected from contamination by nonpotable water
through the physical separation of the two systems; the District will perform inspections
to ensure this separation. See section 34-177 for BFPA specifications and requirements.
(b)
Operating pressures and head loss criteria. When possible, the operating pressure for nonpotable water conduits, transmission
mains, distribution mains, and service lines shall be five to ten psi less than operating
pressure in potable water conduits, transmission mains, distribution mains, and service
lines. The nonpotable water system may be operated at a higher pressure than the potable
water system depending on location.
(Rules of 7-17-2019(7), § 6.06)

documents.title: Sec. 34-170. - Discharges from the system.

documents.text:
Discharges from blowoff assemblies or other appurtenances on the nonpotable water
system once operational or during construction shall be contained or discharged in
a manner approved by Dominion Water and Sanitation and applicable regulations. Discharging
into a watercourse, including a storm sewer that is not specifically approved by Dominion
Water and Sanitation and the regulatory authorities having jurisdiction, is prohibited.
(Rules of 7-17-2019(7), § 6.07)

documents.text:
Customers must obtain written authorization for nonpotable service in accordance with
the Rules and Regulations of Dominion and the CAB. Connections to the nonpotable water
system can only be made after applying for and obtaining a Nonpotable Water Supply
License from Dominion and the CAB. Fees shall be in accordance with the Rules and
Regulations of Dominion and the CAB.
(Rules of 7-17-2019(7), § 6.08)

documents.text:
Design of the main shall proceed only after approval to design and/or construct the
main is received from Dominion Water and Sanitation. The design, size, location, and
any other pertinent details will be reviewed by Dominion Water and Sanitation prior
to the formal submittal of plans and specifications in accordance with the Standards
of this chapter.
(1)
Valves. Valves in the nonpotable water system shall open in a counterclockwise direction
(open left). Valve operators shall have a pentagonal-shaped operating nut. The valve
body, including the operating nut, shall be coated with a factory-applied epoxy, purple
in color. Valve flanges and bolts that are not coated with epoxy shall be wrapped
in wax tape in accordance with article IV of this chapter. The outer tape wrap shall
be purple. The maximum spacing of line valves for conduits and mains on the nonpotable
water system shall be 2,500 feet. Variances to the spacing will be evaluated on a
case-by-case basis by Dominion Water and Sanitation.
(2)
Valve boxes. Valve boxes shall meet the requirements of Article IV of this chapter with the following
exceptions:
a.
Boxes shall be fitted with triangular covers that are cast with the words NONPOTABLE
WATER. Round covers may be accepted following review and approval by the District.
b.
Both the top and bottom surfaces of the cover shall be coated with a 16—20 mil DFT
fusion-bonded epoxy or liquid epoxy applied in accordance with AWWA C210, Pantone
2577U in color.
(3)
Appurtenances in vaults or manholes. Nonpotable pipeline appurtenances in vaults or manholes shall be labeled as belonging
to the nonpotable water system. Labels shall be inert plastic formulated for prolonged
exposure. The labels shall have white lettering a minimum of one-half inch high on
a purple background that reads NONPOTABLE WATER FACILITIES and be attached with heavy-duty
nylon fasteners. Where applicable, exposed metal surfaces shall be protected from
corrosion by wax tape wrapping in accordance with the requirements of article IV of
this chapter. The outer tape wrap shall be purple.
(4)
Manhole covers. Manhole covers shall meet the requirements of Article IV of this chapter for potable
water lines with the following exceptions:
a.
Covers shall be coated with a 16—20 mil DFT fusion-bonded epoxy or liquid epoxy applied
in at least two coats and in accordance with AWWA C210, purple in color.
b.
Covers shall be cast with the words NONPOTABLE WATER.
(5)
Blowoffs. Blowoff assemblies for nonpotable water mains shall be provided in accordance with

Pipe separation. Nonpotable water pipes shall be separated from potable water, sanitary sewer and

documents.text:
The exterior of nonpotable water piping and fittings shall be colored purple. A warning
label that reads CAUTION: NONPOTABLE WATER—DO NOT DRINK shall be located on the exterior
of the pipe.
(1)
PVC pipe shall have the Pantone 2577U color integral to the PVC material. The warning
shall be stamped on the pipe or fixed by means of a separate label applied to the
pipe. The warning label shall be a minimum of three inches high and visible on both
sides of the pipe.
(2)
Buried ductile iron pipe and fittings shall be wrapped in polyethylene encasement
material in accordance with the requirements of article IV of this chapter, except
that it shall be purple in color and include the warning information printed on the
wrap.
(Rules of 7-17-2019(7), § 6.10)

Sec. 34-174. - Nonpotable water service lines and appurtenances.
documents.text:
Nonpotable water service lines are for the conveyance of water from mains to the plumbing
of licensed premises. The design and construction of service lines and appurtenances
that carry nonpotable water shall be in accordance with this article and article IV
of this chapter and the following supplementary requirements:
(1)
Service lines that convey nonpotable water shall be placed in a separate trench from
the potable water service and the sanitary sewer service. A minimum separation of
ten horizontal feet is required between nonpotable water lines, potable water lines,
and sanitary sewer lines. Potable water lines must be 18 vertical inches above nonpotable
water lines. Nonpotable water lines must be 18 vertical inches above sanitary sewer
lines.
(2)
Fittings shall be such that an interconnection cannot be made between the potable
and the nonpotable systems. Hoses shall not be interchanged between the systems. Signs
shall be used to identify nonpotable water quick coupling connections.
(3)
Covers for curb stop boxes and meter pits in the nonpotable water system shall be
cast with the words NONPOTABLE WATER. Covers shall be coated with a fusion-bonded
epoxy, Pantone 2577U in color. Covers shall be painted on the top and the bottom and
be triangular. Four-inch roadway type covers shall be used for service line valves
that are larger than two inches. Meter pit lids and manhole covers shall match those
used for potable water, except they shall be Pantone 2577U in color and shall have
the words NONPOTABLE WATER cast or molded on the top. Composite lids shall have the
color integral to the material. Cast iron lids shall be colored with a fusion-bonded
epoxy.
(4)
Dominion Water and Sanitation will meter users of nonpotable water. The meter shall
be of the size and type specified by Dominion Water and Sanitation. Meters and meter
installations shall be in accordance with the Standards of this chapter. Meters shall
be identified as nonpotable water and painted purple before being used for nonpotable
water service. For meters purchased directly from a vendor by the Owner, the purchase
specifications must indicate the meter is to be used for nonpotable water. If available
from the manufacturer, the meter register box and dial shall be intended for use with
nonpotable water and purple in color.
(5)
Meters and control valves shall be installed in separate vaults. Control valve vaults
shall have locking, metal door-type hatches. Meter vaults shall have standard water
meter manhole covers, Pantone 2577U in color.
(6)

documents.title: Sec. 34-174. - Nonpotable water service lines and appurtenances.

Sec. 34-174. - Nonpotable water service lines and appurtenances.
documents.text:
Buried nonpotable water service lines shall be required to have purple marking tape
located 18 inches above the service line in the trench with the words CAUTION: NONPOTABLE
WATER—DO NOT DRINK. The marking tape for service lines shall be a minimum of three
inches wide. Marking tape material for service lines shall be as outlined in article
IV of this chapter. Conversions of existing potable water service lines for use in
the nonpotable water system may require the replacement of the service line up to
the curb stop box or first valve on the customer's premises. This requirement will
be evaluated on a case-by-case basis by Dominion Water and Sanitation.
(7)
On-site nonpotable water pumping and storage systems are not allowed unless approved
and the systems permitted by Dominion Water and Sanitation. On-site nonpotable water
storage systems must meet a leakage rate of 1x10
-6
cm/sec.
(8)
Backflow prevention on nonpotable water systems is required on nonpotable water connections
if any of the following conditions occur:
a.
Chemicals are injected directly into the private system.
b.
Nonpotable water is pumped to a higher pressure on the private system.
c.
Hazards exist on a private system that pose an additional risk of contamination to
Dominion Water and Sanitation's nonpotable water system (e.g., sprinkler heads installed
below the level of a surface water feature).
(9)
Backflow prevention shall be required at the discretion of Dominion Water and Sanitation's
Cross-Connection Control Section. See Section 34-137 for further information on the prevention of backflow and cross-connection.
(10)
PRVs in service lines may be required as determined by Dominion Water and Sanitation.
Modifications to the potable water service line may be necessary when a new nonpotable
water irrigation system is installed or modified. PRVs shall meet the requirements
of this article and article IV of this chapter.
(11)
A nonpotable water system shall not be connected to a potable water system as a backup
source for nonpotable water. A connection such as this is only allowed if permitted
and designed by DWSD.
(Rules of 7-17-2019(7), § 6.11)

documents.title: Sec. 34-175. - Nonpotable water customer guidelines.
documents.chapter: Chapter 34 - UTILITIES—DOMINION WATER AND SANITATION DISTRICT STANDARDS AND SPECIFICATIONS FOR POTABLE WATER, SANITARY SEWER, AND NONPOTABLE WATER
documents.article: ARTICLE VI. - NONPOTABLE WATER SYSTEM SPECIFICATIONS
path: Chapter 34 - UTILITIES—DOMINION WATER AND SANITATION DISTRICT STANDARDS AND SPECIFICATIONS FOR POTABLE WATER, SANITARY SEWER, AND NONPOTABLE WATER
ARTICLE VI. - NONPOTABLE WATER SYSTEM SPECIFICATIONS
documents.text:
(a)
A nonpotable water customer shall comply with applicable regulations regarding the
use of recycled water including CDPHE Regulation 84 if the water source meets the
criteria.
(b)
Additionally, the customer shall adhere to the following guidelines for using nonpotable
water:
(1)
The nonpotable water customer shall designate an on-site supervisor that shall be
responsible for compliance with regulations regarding the use of nonpotable water.
(2)
The District may assign a specific nonpotable water usage schedule for the customer
to follow.
(3)
The nonpotable water customer shall obtain prior approval from Dominion Water and
Sanitation and the regulatory authorities having jurisdiction for proposed changes
or modifications to nonpotable water facilities.
(4)
Signage indicating the use of nonpotable water is required on site at the point of
use to notify workers and/or the public.
(5)
Nonpotable water piping shall not be extended to or supported from any residential,
domestic, or commercial structure. At least one exterior hose bibb supplied with potable
water shall be provided at each structure.
(6)
Irrigation sprinklers that are used in on-site nonpotable water systems shall have
an exposed surface that is purple. The exposed surface may be purple by the use of
dyed plastic or rubber or weatherproof paint. Sprinklers that do not meet these requirements
shall be identified with purple nonpotable warning notification tags.
(7)
On-site nonpotable water facilities shall have restricted public access so the public
cannot draw water from the system. Wash down hydrants, blowoff hydrants, blowoffs
on strainers, and other such facilities shall be restricted from public access. These
facilities, both above and below grade, shall be housed in an approved locking container
that is purple. A sign with black lettering on a purple field with the words CAUTION:
NONPOTABLE WATER—DO NOT DRINK shall be installed on the container.
(8)
Exposed service piping in the nonpotable water system, including piping inside the
buildings, shall be spirally wrapped with warning tape with the words CAUTION: NONPOTABLE
WATER—DO NOT DRINK.
(9)
Customer systems planned for nonpotable water use shall be marked as belonging to
the recycled water system. Pipes and tubing shall be purple with the words CAUTION:
NONPOTABLE WATER—DO NOT DRINK or wrapped with warning tape with the words CAUTION:
NONPOTABLE WATER—DO NOT DRINK.
(10)
Customer systems converted from potable water to nonpotable water shall mark modifications

to or replacements of the system and/or its components as belonging to the nonpotable
water system. This includes the use of purple caps on sprinkler heads and purple pipe
with the words CAUTION: NONPOTABLE WATER—DO NOT DRINK or spiral wrapping of the pipe
with the words CAUTION: NONPOTABLE WATER—DO NOT DRINK.
(11)
The nonpotable water customer shall ensure that on-site nonpotable water facilities
remain in compliance with applicable regulations and the guidelines established by

may result in the termination of service until the appropriate corrective actions
are taken.
(Rules of 7-17-2019(7), § 6.12)

documents.title: Sec. 34-176. - Dual supply systems.
documents.chapter: Chapter 34 - UTILITIES—DOMINION WATER AND SANITATION DISTRICT STANDARDS AND SPECIFICATIONS FOR POTABLE WATER, SANITARY SEWER, AND NONPOTABLE WATER

documents.text:
Dual supply systems are not allowed. Distribution mains, water systems, and private
systems may not have dual water supplies. This includes:
(1)
A single system that would allow for the introduction of potable or nonpotable water
without the use of an air gap.
(2)
Parallel systems used to provide dual water supply service at the same point of use
(e.g., the availability of potable and nonpotable water to serve the same garden plot,
water feature, etc.). During the plan review process outlined in Section 34-36 , Dominion Water and Sanitation will review the segregation of potable and proposed
nonpotable water pipes to determine the risk of cross-connection and approve or reject
plans based on the risk assessment.
(Rules of 7-17-2019(7), § 6.13)

Sec. 34-177. - Cross-connection control and backflow prevention.
documents.text:
(a)
Cross-connection control.
(1)
Dominion Water and Sanitation is responsible for protecting its public water system
from contamination due to backflow occurrences through residential, multifamily, irrigation,
and/or commercial property water service connections (i.e., cross-connections). Dominion
Water and Sanitation needs the assistance and the cooperation of the public and licensees
to ensure this responsibility is met. Dominion Water and Sanitation may request access
to a property or facility to conduct an on-site cross-connection control audit.
(2)
A properly designed air gap is the most effective method of protecting the public
water supply from high hazard cross-connections. When an air gap cannot be used, a
RP BFPA shall be installed. Dominion Water and Sanitation requires the installation
of a containment assembly on commercial property service lines. In high hazard applications,
a RP BFPA shall be installed. In low hazard applications, a DC BFPA may be installed
at the discretion of Dominion Water and Sanitation's Cross-Connection Control Section.
(3)
Failure to comply with the installation and annual testing requirements may result
in suspension of service.

(2)
A USC FCCCHR approved RP BFPA is required when:
a.
High-level security or restricted commercial properties do not allow Dominion Water
and Sanitation to gain access to conduct a cross-connection control audit of the property
and/or facility. An approved RP assembly shall be installed five feet downstream from
the existing meter pit in an above-ground, heated enclosure.
b.
A landscape irrigation system is designed for the direct injection of chemical additives
into the system. An approved RP assembly shall be installed on the designated service
line to the premises five feet downstream from the meter pit or ten feet for irrigation
installations with the use of a stop and waste valve.
c.
A temporary construction water license is issued by the Sales Administration Section
for construction use. An approved RP assembly shall be installed on the temporary
water service line entering the building or above ground, downstream from the meter
pit before any connections.
d.
A low hazard DC BFPA, used as containment, is installed on a water service line downstream
from the meter and a high hazard RP BFPA, used as isolation, is installed on internal
plumbing to protect the public water supply. Both containment assemblies shall be
tested and the report sent to Dominion Water and Sanitation's Cross-Connection Control
Section annually.
e.
A RP BFPA is required for irrigation system installations that are two inches in diameter
or less:
1.
An approved USC FCCHR RP BFPA shall be installed on the irrigation water service line
five feet downstream from the meter pit or ten feet with the use of a stop and waste
valve; the line must be above ground before any connections.

A DC BFPA is required when:

There is an auxiliary water supply (e.g., raw water, a well, a pond, or a ditch) on

b.
Fire protection systems are installed without chemical additives or pumps. An approved
DC BFPA shall be installed on the designated water service line entering the building
(i.e., the Mechanical Room or the Pump Room).
(e)
Examples of commercial properties supplied with nonpotable water or auxiliary water
sources that require a RP or DC BFPA.
(1)
Where a nonpotable water irrigation system is designed to inject chemical additives
and the use of pumps installed downstream from the meter and/or the proposed irrigation
system poses a risk to the integrity of the nonpotable water system, an approved USC
FCCCHR RP assembly shall be installed on the designated service line to the premises
five feet downstream from the meter pit or ten feet with the use of a stop and waste
valve.
(2)
Where auxiliary water is used for irrigation on a commercial, multifamily, or residential
premises, an approved USC FCCCHR BFPA shall be installed five feet downstream from
the meter pit on the domestic water service line. The type of BFPA will be determined
by Dominion Water and Sanitation's Cross-Connection Control Section based on the degree
of hazard encountered downstream of the meter.

If the BFPA fails and cannot be repaired on the day of its failure, the Cross-Connection
Control Section must be notified by the certified ABPA or ASSE tester within 24 hours.
A copy of the failed test report must be submitted to the Cross-Connection Control
Section within three days.
2.
The Property Owner is responsible for coordinating the necessary repairs to the BFPA

(g)
Exemptions. Single-family residential customers are exempt from Dominion Water and Sanitation's
cross-connection control requirements unless the premises is served by an auxiliary
water supply (e.g., raw water, a well, a lake, a pond, or a ditch). Auxiliary water
supply conditions require a Dual Water Supply Agreement to be in effect between Dominion
Water and Sanitation and the Property Owner. Multifamily residential customers are
exempt from Dominion Water and Sanitation's cross- connection control requirements
unless the premises fall under the criteria listed in this section.

DISTRICT WATER NOTES. THESE NOTES SHALL BE ADDED TO THE GENERAL NOTES SHEET OF ALL CONSTRUCTION DOCUMENTS.
(1)
THE INSTALLATION OF ALL WATER LINES AND APPURTENANCES SHALL COMPLY WITH THE DOMINION
WATER AND SANITATION DISTRICT STANDARD SPECIFICATIONS (DWSDSS), LATEST VERSION.
(2)
EXISTING UTILITIES AND STRUCTURES (UNDERGROUND, SURFACE, AND OVERHEAD) ARE INDICATED
ONLY TO THE EXTENT THAT SUCH INFORMATION WAS MADE AVAILABLE TO THE SURVEYOR, UTILITY
LOCATOR, OR ENGINEER, FOR CONTRACT DOCUMENT PREPARATION. NOT ALL LOCATIONS, CONFIGURATIONS,
AND ELEVATIONS OF EXISTING UNDERGROUND POWER, TELEPHONE, FIBER OPTIC CABLE, DUCT WAYS,
SPRINKLER SYSTEMS, SEPTIC SYSTEMS, WATER, GAS, SEWER AND SERVICE LINES ARE INDICATED.
OTHER UTILITIES AND STRUCTURES NOT DISCOVERED MAY BE PRESENT. UNDERGROUND LOCATIONS
AND ELEVATIONS OF EXISTING UTILITIES AND STRUCTURES AS FURNISHED BY THE OWNER OF EACH
UTILITY OR STRUCTURE, ARE APPROXIMATE AND ARE NOT TO BE CONSTRUED AS AN ACCURATE LOCATION
OF THEIR UTILITY. THE ENGINEERING INVESTIGATIONS, LOCATIONS, AND DESIGNATIONS OF SUBSURFACE
UTILITIES INDICATED IN THESE CONTRACT DOCUMENTS HAS BEEN PERFORMED TO QUALITY LEVEL
'C' IN ACCORDANCE WITH GENERALLY ACCEPTED ENGINEERING PRINCIPLES AND PRACTICES AS
OUTLINED IN ASCE STANDARD AND GUIDELINE BULLETIN CI/ASCE 38-02, UNLESS OTHERWISE DESIGNATED.
WHERE SUCH ACTIVITIES HAVE BEEN TO A HIGHER LEVEL OF QUALITY, THE HIGHER QUALITY LEVEL
FOR THE AFFECTED AREAS ARE INDICATED IN THE CONTRACT DOCUMENTS.
(3)
WATER LINES SHALL BE C-900 CLASS 150 MINIMUM, PVC UNLESS OTHERWISE NOTED. ALL DIP

documents.text:
MEMORANDUM
Dominion Water and Sanitation District
B&V Project 196849
Rainwater Harvesting Standards
B&V File 40.0000
Interim Standards Memo
5 October 2017
To:
Mary Kay Provaznik, Utility Director
Sarah Stone, Manager of Operations
From:
Brian Jessee
Black & Veatch is currently developing the Design and Construction Standards (Standards)
for the Rainwater Harvesting program for Dominion Water and Sanitation District (District).
Until such time as the Standards are published and adopted by the District, this Rainwater
Harvesting Interim Standards Memorandum (Memo) is intended to be a list of requirements
that must be followed by all designers and developers of Filings for Sterling Ranch.
The requirements included in this Memo are very basic in nature and are only intended
to ensure that design of stormwater ponds is not performed in such a way that would
prevent them from having a dual purpose in the future as Rainwater Harvesting ponds.
These requirements are not to be considered comprehensive in nature or to take the
place of future Standards. All stormwater ponds that are under design now or will
be designed prior to the adoption of the Standards must be reviewed by the District
at the preliminary and final design phase of the work to ensure that the design meets
the requirements both outlined in this Memo and any other necessities of the District
that will allow future implementation of the Rainwater Harvesting program. It is the
District's sole responsibility to waive or modify these requirements. Modifications
to these requirements may not be considered unless reviewed and approved by the District.
This Memo is focused on the physical infrastructure for a stormwater pond that could
also be utilized as a Rainwater Harvesting pond. The actual hydraulic and hydrologic
design and sizing of the pond to account for capture volume will be defined by Leonard
Rice Engineers in separate requirements. Both sets of requirements will be enforced
by the District until Standards are published. The final Standards document will combine
both the requirements for pond sizing and capture as well as the infrastructure to
direct the rainwater to the nonpotable water system that the District will operate.
The following items shall be considered as the minimum interim requirements for the
Rainwater Harvesting program and shall be followed by all designers and developers
working in Sterling Ranch:
•
Pond Sizing. Sizing of stormwater ponds to account for Rainwater Harvesting shall be as required

documents.text:
by Leonard Rice Engineers. The storage volume for rainwater shall be completely useable,
and the outlet structure that will connect to the pump station shall be placed such
that the full volume of the rainwater harvesting portion and stormwater portion can
be pumped out of the pond.
•
Outlet Structure. The outlet structure shall allow the pond to function as a stormwater detention pond
and release water in the quantity as required by the county while also allowing a
specific volume of water to be retained for rainwater harvesting. The outlet structure
shall prevent the transport of sediment into the connection piping to the rainwater
harvesting pump station. If an outlet structure for the rainwater harvesting connection
piping is necessary to be separate from the stormwater outlet structure, the rainwater
harvesting outlet structure should be maintainable in a similar fashion as dictated
for the stormwater outlet and prevent sediment transport to the connection piping.
•
Outlet Structure Measurement. A measurement device shall be provided at the outlet structure to measure and record
the amount of water that leaves the pond (both for the stormwater and rainwater harvesting).
The device shall be capable of taking measurements at increments as small as one minute
or as large as 60 minutes. The range of measurement shall provide accurate recording
for all flows expected to discharge from the pond for storms up to the 100-year type.
The equipment shall be of a type that is robust and rated for outdoor installation
and shall be common in the industry for measuring pond discharge or stream flow. This
device shall be linked to the District's SCADA system by way of a radio that is compatible
with their current system and can transmit the measurement data to the central SCADA
system. The on-site equipment shall measure and record data. Local storage shall be
provided for up to seven days' worth of measurements. A local uninterruptable power
supply shall be provided that can power the measurement and recording equipment and
radio for up to six hours following loss of utility power. All electrical and control
panels shall be NEMA 4X, stainless steel.
•
Pump Station Suction Connection Piping. Connection piping shall be brought from the outlet structure to a square vault a
minimum of 25 feet outside the top of the slope of the pond. This is to allow the
pipe to be exposed and connected to without disturbance to the pond. The pipe shall
be 24-inch minimum diameter and shall end in a square vault. Connection piping shall
have a minimum cover of 4.5 feet.
•

documents.text:
Pump Station Suction Connection Vault. A four-foot by four-foot connection vault shall be the termination point for the
connection piping. The vault shall be topped with a four-foot by four-foot aluminum
hatch to allow access to the vault. The invert of the vault shall be a minimum of
two feet below the invert of the connection piping. Each side of the vault shall be
designed to allow any or all sides to be field cored for future 24-inch connection
piping.
•
Pump Station Site. An area next to the pond shall be dedicated to be used for the construction of a
raw water pump station. The optimal site shall be down grade of the pond to permit
gravity flow without making the pump station wetwell needlessly deep. The site shall
be at least level with the top of the top, and shall not be up a slope. A minimum
of one-half acre of land, generally square in shape, shall be located next to the
pond, and the connection vault shall be located in this site. The site shall be generally
flat and have no trees or landscaping (other than grass) planted in the area dedicated
to the future pump station. One edge of the site shall be accessible from the nearest
public street. The nearest raw water pipeline in the road that operates at the same
pressure as the nearby irrigation and other nonpotable points of use shall be able
to receive supply from the pump station and shall be no smaller than eight-inch diameter.
A power supply transformer able to supply 480-volt, three-phase power shall be located
no farther than one-quarter mile from the site.
•
Land Ownership/Easements. Easement dedication for pond access and maintenance shall be as required by Douglas
County. All Douglas County easements shall also name Dominion Water and Sanitation.
The Pump Station Site shall have a permanent easement dedicated to Dominion Water
and Sanitation, and shall be extended as necessary to encompass connecting utilities
from the pond or to the street.
(Rules of 7-17-2019(7), ch. 8)

Subject:
Interim Standards—Hydrology, Hydraulics, and Monitoring Standards
_____
At the request of Dominion Water & Sanitation District (District) Leonard Rice Engineers,
Inc. is currently developing the hydrology, hydraulic, and monitoring Standards (Standards)
for the Rainwater Harvesting program. The purposes of the Standards are to preserve
the options for District to develop rainwater as viable water supply and allow for
the opportunity for the District to be included in the design of stormwater facilities.
Until such time as the Standards are published and adopted by the District, this Rainwater
Harvesting Interim Standards Memorandum (Memo) is intended to be a list of requirements
that must be followed by all designers and developers of Filings for Sterling Ranch.
The requirements included in this Memo are very basic in nature and are only intended
to ensure that design of stormwater ponds is not performed in such a way that would
prevent them from having a dual purpose in the future as Rainwater Harvesting ponds.
These requirements are not to be considered comprehensive in nature or to take the
place of future Standards. All stormwater ponds that are under design now or will
be designed prior to the adoption of the Standards must be reviewed by the District
at the preliminary and final design phase of the work to ensure that the design meets
the requirements both outlined in this Memo and any other necessities of the District
that will allow future implementation of the Rainwater Harvesting program. It is the
District's sole responsibility to waive or modify these requirements. Modifications
to these requirements may not be considered unless reviewed and approved by the District.
This Memo is focused on pond sizing, pump sizing, as well as monitoring requirements
for stormwater facilities utilized as Rainwater Harvesting sites. The actual physical
infrastructure for a stormwater facility will be defined by Black & Veatch in a separate
requirements document. Both sets of requirements will be enforced by the District
until Standards are published. The final Standards document will combine both the
requirements for pond sizing and capture as well as the infrastructure to direct the
rainwater to the nonpotable water system that the District will operate.
The following items shall be considered as the minimum interim requirements for the

Rainwater Harvesting program and shall be followed by all designers and developers
working in Sterling Ranch.
District has identified a goal of 75 percent capture as an interim standard. The following
steps outline the procedure for determining pond size, pump size, and yield of the
rainwater system meeting this goal. The following information must be provided to
Dominion to evaluate the:
1.
Total Effective Impervious Area (Acres). Utilizing the total effective percent impervious area from Colorado Unit Hydrograph
Procedure (CUHP) and the total basin area (acres) from CUHP. Calculate the total effective
impervious area in acres contributing to the stormwater facility. Total effective
percent impervious area includes the percent of directly connected impervious areas
(DCIA) and the percent of the unconnected impervious area (UIA) that contribute to
the stormwater facility.
2.
Provide Proposed Stormwater Facility Design Capacities. Provide the proposed stormwater facility design capacities including the water quality
capture volume (WQCV), excess urban runoff volume (EURV), and the 100-yr detention
volume in acre-feet.
3.
Pump Sizing. To reach a goal of capturing 75 percent of available rainwater a minimum unit pumping
rate of ten GPM/impervious acre is required. To calculate the required pump size multiply
ten GPM/impervious acre by the total effective impervious area calculated in step
1.
4.
Pond Sizing. To reach a goal of capturing 75 percent of available rainwater a minimum unit stormwater
storage capacity of 0.13 AF/impervious acre is required. To calculate the required
pond size of 0.13 AF/impervious acre by the total effective impervious area calculated
in step 1.
5.
System Yield. The average annual yield of the system associated with capturing 75 percent of available
rainwater would result in 0.68 AFY/impervious acre. To calculate the system yield,
multiply 0.68 AFY/impervious acre by the total effective impervious area calculated
in step 1.
Based on the information provided above, Dominion will assess the water supply potential
of each stormwater facility and determine if any modifications to the stormwater design
or infrastructure are required to preserve the option for District to develop rainwater
as viable water supply. Any recommended variances in the stormwater facility design
or infrastructure will be developed in consultation with Sterling Ranch CAB engineers.
Monitoring and Sensors:
All inflows, outflows, and changes in storage of a stormwater facility are required

documents.text:
to be monitored and recorded. Sensors installed at these facilities need to meet the
following minimum standards:
•
Pump Station Meter. All withdrawals from the stormwater pond to a defined use or regional system must
be metered. The meter must include outputs allowing for the data to be collected manually
and connected to a Campbell Scientific CR-1000, or similar data logger. The meter
must also include a totalizer that is visible to administrators. The accuracy of the
meter must allow for low flow measurements of rates of ten gpm or less.
•
Open Channel Sensors. All inflows and outflows from the stormwater pond must be recorded. An ultrasonic
sensor that measures depth (level) and velocity is required. The sensor must have
the ability to measure partially filled and surcharged pipes as this is the preferred
installation for monitoring inflows and outflows from a facility. The sensor selected
must meet or exceed the specification of the Grayline AVFM 5.0 Area-Velocity Meter
(http://greyline.com/index.php/products/water-wastewater/open-channel-flow/avfm-5-0-area-velocity-flow-monitor-detail)
and include outputs allowing for the data to be connected to a Campbell Scientific
CR-1000, or similar data logger. Upon completion of the stormwater facility the final
specifications of the inflow and outflow structures are required to be provided to
Dominion.
•
Stage Sensors. A pressure transducer is required at all stormwater facilities where operational/active
storage is being maintained. If water is retained at the facility for longer than
24 hours, the measurement and quantification of storage is required. The pressure
transducer selected will need to maintain calibration when not submerged or frozen.
The selected sensor must meet or exceed the specification of the OTT PLS sensor (http://www.ott.com/en-us/products/water-level-1/ott-pls-pressure-level-sensor-959/).
The sensor must include outputs allowing for the data to be connected to a Campbell
Scientific CR-1000, or similar data logger. Upon completion of the stormwater facility
the final stage-area-capacity curves are required to be provided to Dominion.
